title: Democratic Integration Conference in Zurich discusses democratic transformation, equal coexistence
content:
The Kurdish Social Research Association (Akademî Kurd) is holding a conference titled “Democratic Integration” in Zurich, Switzerland. The conference, taking place at the Kirchgemeindehaus, is examining the concept of democratic integration from various perspectives within the framework of LAbdullah Öcalan’s Manifesto for a Democratic Communal Society.




The conference, attended by academics, politicians, legal experts, and researchers, focuses on the theoretical foundations of democratic integration as well as its social, political, and cultural dimensions. Legal reforms necessary for a democratic resolution of the Kurdish question, equal citizenship, the democratic republic, and the democratic communal economy are also among the main topics of discussion.




Dilan Çetinkaya: The process places significant responsibilities on all of us




The conference began with a minute of silence in memory of the martyrs of the revolutionary struggle, followed by an opening speech delivered by Dilan Çetinkaya, Co-Chair of the Democratic Kurdish Council of Switzerland (CDK-S).




Dilan Çetinkaya began her speech by commemorating the martyrs of the Kurdish Freedom Struggle and drew attention to the Kurdish people’s struggle for freedom spanning more than half a century. Stating that this struggle has brought significant gains to the Kurdish people, Çetinkaya emphasized the historical importance of the peace and democratic society process initiated under the leadership of Abdullah Öcalan.




Çetinkaya stated that the ongoing process places significant responsibilities not only on political actors but also on all segments of society, stressing that democratic transformation must be reflected in every aspect of life. “Change must not remain merely in words; it must take place in every sphere. We must thoroughly understand Leader Öcalan’s concept of democratic integration and carry out our reconstruction accordingly,” she said.




Veysi Aktaş: Democratic integration is based on the democratic transformation of all peoples




Following the opening speech, the conference proceeded to its first session, titled “The conceptual and theoretical framework of democratic integration.” Moderated by Gülistan Arslan, the session featured Kurdish politician Veysi Aktaş and sociologist, academic, and author Nazan Üstündağ as speakers.




Veysi Aktaş began by thanking Akademî Kurd for organizing the conference. Stating that democratic integration is one of the fundamental concepts of the peace and democratic society process, Aktaş said that the concept points not only to the resolution of existing problems but also to the building of a democratic future in which peoples can live together in equality and freedom.




Aktaş explained that democratic integration is based on different identities and social groups creating a shared democratic life while preserving their distinct identities. “Democratic integration is a concept based on the democratic transformation of all peoples, not just the Kurds. It is founded on coexistence with differences, equality, equal negotiation as a method, and democratic participation,” he said.




Emphasizing that democratic integration does not mean assimilation or the elimination of differences, Aktaş stated that the concept is fundamentally based on the recognition of different identities, social pluralism, and democratic participation. In this respect, he explained that democratic integration entails not only the recognition of the political and social rights of Kurds but also the restructuring of society as a whole on a democratic basis.




‘The fundamental principle is equal citizenship’




Remarking that democratic integration rests on several fundamental principles, Aktaş said that equal citizenship is foremost among them. He emphasized that equal citizenship cannot be understood merely as formal equality before the law, highlighting the importance of enabling different identities and social groups to participate in political and social life while preserving their distinct characteristics.




Aktaş stated that democratic integration is directly linked to the perspective of a democratic republic and stressed the need to establish legal guarantees to ensure that democratic transformation becomes lasting.




“Democratic integration is also based on the Democratic Republic. Achieving this is possible through the implementation of a legal process. Certain legal reforms are necessary for it to become a reality in everyday life,” he said.




Stating that discussing democratic integration solely at the theoretical level would not be sufficient, Aktaş emphasized the importance of safeguarding principles such as equal citizenship, democratic participation, and the recognition of different identities through concrete legal and political arrangements.




‘The process is not limited to laying down arms’




Aktaş also addressed the question of why the concept of democratic integration was chosen, stating that this approach is important for understanding the scope of the peace and democratic society process.




Emphasizing that the process cannot be viewed as limited to laying down arms or ending armed conflicts, Veysi Aktaş explained that democratic integration also encompasses the participation of Kurds in political life with their own identity, language, and social existence.




In this context, Aktaş stated that democratic integration aims to create the conditions for Kurds to pursue their democratic struggle within the existing political and social system without abandoning their identities, adding that this also requires the democratic transformation of both the state and society.




Nazan Üstündağ: Kurds were forced to live as ‘smugglers’ in every sphere of life




Following Veysi Aktaş, sociologist, academic, and author Nazan Üstündağ took the floor, examining the concept of democratic integration through the historical experiences of the Kurdish people, their relationship with the state, and the discrimination they have faced in social life.




Üstündağ stated that the Kurdish people have historically faced various prohibitions, policies of denial, and discrimination in political, cultural, and social spheres, emphasizing that this situation has directly affected their daily lives and their relationship with the state.




Explaining that Kurds have often been forced to live outside the boundaries of the official system in order to exist with their own identities, Üstündağ described this historical condition using the term “smuggler.”




Nazan Üstündağ pointed out that the Kurdish people have faced various obstacles not only when crossing borders but also when speaking their language, preserving their culture, and expressing their political identity. The Kurds, she added, have been forced to live almost like “smugglers” in many spheres of life.




Üstündağ stated that one of the most important aspects of democratic integration is the creation of a social and political order in which Kurds no longer face such constraints simply to exist with their own identity. In this regard, she emphasized that democratic integration cannot be understood as the unconditional adaptation of Kurds to the existing order. Rather, she said, the essential issue is to create democratic conditions in which Kurds can live freely and equally while preserving their identities.




‘I understand democratic integration as a struggle against the state’




Nazan Üstündağ stated that democratic integration has become more important today than ever before, emphasizing that the concept should not be approached solely through legal reforms or political compromises.




She pointed out that democratic integration also entails redefining the relationship between the state and society, and cannot be considered independently of the democratic struggle. “I understand democratic integration as a struggle against the state,” Üstündağ said, adding that democratic integration should be viewed as a process involving the questioning of existing power relations and the expansion of society’s democratic rights. Highlighting the importance of democratic integration in overcoming the exclusion and discrimination historically experienced by Kurds, Üstündağ said, “In this context, democratic integration is linked not only to enabling Kurds to participate in public and political life with their own identity but also to the transformation of state-society relations on a democratic basis.”




The conference will continue with sessions featuring Syrian Presidential Advisor Mazlum Abdi, sociologist Engin Sustam from Paris 8 University, TJK-E (Kurdish Women’s Movement in Europe) member Zîlan Diyar, DEM Party Central Executive Board member Derya Arslan, İmralı Delegation member and lawyer Özgür Erol, lawyer Hüsnü Yılmaz, researcher and economist Ahmet Pelda, and sociologist and anthropologist Neşe Özgen. The sessions will address the political, sociological, cultural, legal, and economic dimensions of democratic integration, as well as the democratic resolution of the Kurdish question.

author: Unknown
title: KOMAW calls for international action against death sentence for Varisheh Moradi
content:
The Association of Families of Martyrs and the Disappeared (KOMAW) called on international institutions to intervene against the renewed death sentence imposed on Kurdish activist Varisheh Moradi. In a statement, the organization condemned the Iranian regime’s execution policy and the ongoing repression of women, political activists, and opposition groups. KOMAW has submitted a dossier on Moradi’s case and other human rights violations in Iran to international institutions.




In November 2024, Branch 15 of the Revolutionary Court in Tehran sentenced Moradi to death on charges of “rebellion against the state.” The Supreme Court overturned the ruling in December 2025 due to serious deficiencies in the investigation. Instead of conducting the additional investigations ordered by the Supreme Court, the same court branch once again imposed the death penalty in mid-October. The defense has described the proceedings as unlawful and rejected the accusations against Moradi. The new verdict is not yet final.




KOMAW views the proceedings as another manifestation of the systematic oppression of the Kurdish population in particular, as well as other communities in Iran. “Women who fight for freedom, equality, and democratic rights are particularly vulnerable to persecution and severe punishment. However, human rights must not be sacrificed to political power interests or ideological conflicts.”




Dossier submitted to international institutions




Through the dossier, KOMAW aims to prompt the United Nations (UN) human rights mechanisms, as well as international women’s and human rights organizations, to take action against Moradi’s threatened execution and the ongoing violations of rights in Iran. The documents are intended to initiate independent investigations and diplomatic initiatives. The association announced that it would monitor responses to its submissions and keep the international public informed of further developments.




Six demands to the international community




In its statement, KOMAW outlined six specific demands. The first is the immediate annulment of the death sentence against Moradi and the prevention of its enforcement. The association also calls for independent investigations into executions, allegations of torture, arbitrary arrests, and politically motivated judicial proceedings in Iran. The relevant UN bodies and international human rights organizations are urged to continuously monitor developments.




At the same time, KOMAW calls for stronger diplomatic measures against Tehran to halt executions and ensure the protection of fundamental freedoms. It also calls for political, diplomatic, and economic relations with Iran to be reviewed from a human rights perspective. As its sixth demand, the association calls for effective protection of women’s rights activists and human rights defenders against persecution, ill-treatment, and the threat of execution.

author: anred
title: De Stonewall a  la Argentina que gobierna Milei
content:
El ajuste, los discursos de odio y el debilitamiento de las políticas públicas ponen en tensión derechos conquistados por décadas de lucha. En este contexto mundial de vanzada de la ultraderecha, la organización de la Comunidad LGBTIQ+ vuelve a las calles el próximo 7 de noviembre para realizar la 35 Marcha del orgullo. «Cuando el odio avanza, el orgullo en las calles es resistencia». 

Por Rocío Cisterna para ANRed 







Hay momentos históricos en los que luchar por existir deja de ser solamente una reivindicación y se convierte en una disputa política contra el orden establecido. Cuando el hambre, el ajuste, la discriminación, la persecución y la violencia institucional amenazan las condiciones de vida, los derechos conquistados dejan de parecer garantizados y las calles vuelven a ser escenario de resistencia.




La 

rebelión de Stonewall

 fue uno de esos momentos. Hoy, en la Argentina gobernada por Javier Milei, su historia adquiere una renovada vigencia: cuando el Estado debilita las políticas de protección, desfinancia derechos y promueve discursos estigmatizantes, la resistencia se convierte en una necesidad colectiva.




Pero esta disputa no se limita a nuestras fronteras. También se inscribe en un escenario internacional marcado por el avance de las ultraderechas, las alianzas geopolíticas y las confrontaciones en torno a la libertad, la democracia, la soberanía y los derechos humanos.




Stonewall: cuando la resistencia rompió el silencio




En junio de 1969, las personas homosexuales, lesbianas, trans y otras identidades disidentes sufrían distintas formas de criminalización, hostigamiento y persecución en Estados Unidos. Las redadas policiales contra los bares frecuentados por estas comunidades formaban parte de un sistema que buscaba controlar los cuerpos, las identidades y los afectos que desafiaban la norma dominante.




La madrugada del 28 de junio, quienes estaban en el Stonewall Inn, en Greenwich Village, Nueva York, se negaron a someterse pasivamente a la violencia policial. El hartazgo frente a años de persecución se transformó en una rebelión que se extendió durante varias jornadas y se convirtió en un símbolo internacional de las luchas por la liberación sexual y los derechos de las diversidades.




Stonewall no fue solamente una revuelta contra una redada policial. Fue una ruptura con el silencio impuesto y con la idea de que las personas LGBTIQ+ debían aceptar la violencia como una condición inevitable de su existencia.




Su legado recuerda que los derechos no fueron concesiones generosas del poder, sino conquistas de quienes se organizaron y resistieron. Esa memoria sigue presente cada vez que una persona trans encuentra obstáculos para acceder a la salud, cuando se produce una situación de discriminación o cuando un gobierno pretende convertir el odio en sentido común.




Argentina: del avance de derechos al ajuste




Argentina construyó una historia de conquistas en materia de derechos humanos, diversidad y ampliación de derechos civiles. El Juicio a las Juntas, el Nunca Más, la Ley de Educación Sexual Integral (ESI), el matrimonio igualitario y la legalización de la interrupción voluntaria del embarazo forman parte de un recorrido colectivo que demuestra que las transformaciones sociales son posibles mediante la organización popular.




Ninguna de esas conquistas fue resultado de una concesión espontánea. Todas fueron producto de décadas de militancia, debate público y movilización. Por eso, tampoco pueden darse por garantizadas.




Desde la asunción de Javier Milei, las organizaciones feministas, transfeministas, LGBTIQ+ y de derechos humanos denuncian un escenario de retroceso, ajuste y debilitamiento de las políticas públicas. La eliminación del Ministerio de las Mujeres, Géneros y Diversidad y los recortes presupuestarios expresan un cambio en las prioridades del Estado nacional.




También preocupan el financiamiento y la implementación de la ESI, las políticas vinculadas con la interrupción voluntaria y legal del embarazo (IVE e ILE) y el acceso efectivo a la salud integral de las personas trans y no binarias.




No se trata de discusiones abstractas ni de diferencias meramente ideológicas. Se trata de recursos, profesionales, tratamientos, acompañamiento y prevención. Cuando las políticas públicas desaparecen o pierden capacidad de respuesta, las consecuencias recaen sobre vidas concretas y profundizan desigualdades que ya existen.




El ajuste no impacta de la misma manera en todos los sectores. La pobreza, la precarización laboral, la discriminación y la falta de redes de acompañamiento agravan la exclusión de quienes enfrentan mayores obstáculos para ejercer sus derechos.




La batalla cultural: del discurso de odio a la violencia institucional




El gobierno nacional impulsa una confrontación política y cultural contra buena parte de las agendas feministas, de diversidad y de ampliación de derechos. Sus intervenciones públicas y sus decisiones presupuestarias deben analizarse en conjunto, atendiendo tanto a sus efectos materiales como a los discursos que contribuyen a legitimarlos.




Los dichos de Milei en el Foro Económico Mundial de Davos, en enero de 2025, provocaron el rechazo de organizaciones feministas, LGBTIQ+ y de derechos humanos, que denunciaron la estigmatización de las diversidades sexuales y de género. El 19 de febrero de ese año, las movilizaciones antifascistas y antirracistas expresaron una respuesta colectiva frente a esa avanzada.




El racismo, la xenofobia, la homofobia y la transfobia no pueden analizarse por fuera de las relaciones de poder. Cuando se naturaliza el desprecio hacia determinados grupos sociales, se debilitan las condiciones para una convivencia democrática basada en la igualdad.




La batalla cultural no se libra solamente en los medios de comunicación, las redes sociales o los discursos oficiales. También se disputa en las escuelas, los hospitales, los barrios y los lugares de trabajo: cuando defendemos la ESI, exigimos el acceso al aborto legal, reclamamos políticas para prevenir las violencias o acompañamos a una persona trans frente a la discriminación.




La violencia estatal tampoco se limita a la acción directa de las fuerzas de seguridad. Las decisiones y omisiones que obstaculizan el acceso a derechos, reducen los recursos de protección o dejan sin respuesta a quienes necesitan asistencia también producen consecuencias.




Frente a las denuncias de violencia institucional y crímenes de odio, se necesitan mecanismos de denuncia accesibles, investigaciones eficaces, acompañamiento integral y una justicia que comprenda las desigualdades estructurales que atraviesan a las víctimas. La democracia no se mide únicamente por la existencia de elecciones, sino también por la capacidad del Estado para proteger a quienes históricamente fueron perseguidos.




No vamos a regalarle la palabra libertad a quienes pretenden convertirla en un privilegio de mercado ni aceptar que la batalla cultural se transforme en una herramienta para justificar la discriminación.




La salud y las identidades trans no son variables de ajuste




Una de las preocupaciones urgentes de las comunidades trans y no binarias es el acceso a tratamientos de hormonización y a una atención sanitaria integral. En un contexto de restricciones presupuestarias y cuestionamientos políticos a las políticas de diversidad, las denuncias sobre recortes, faltantes y obstáculos deben ser atendidas con seriedad.




El acceso a la hormonización forma parte del derecho a la salud integral reconocido en el marco normativo argentino, incluida la Ley de Identidad de Género. Garantizarlo requiere presupuesto suficiente, continuidad de los tratamientos, medicamentos, turnos y respuestas institucionales concretas.




No alcanza con que un derecho esté escrito en una ley si después no hay profesionales, insumos ni acompañamiento. La salud sexual, la ESI, la IVE y la ILE forman parte de una misma discusión política: quiénes pueden acceder a una vida digna y quiénes quedan expuestos a las desigualdades económicas, territoriales y sociales.




Sin oportunidades laborales, políticas de inclusión y acceso efectivo a la justicia, las personas trans y no binarias quedan todavía más expuestas a la violencia y la exclusión.




Las identidades trans no son una variable de ajuste. Nuestros cuerpos no son un campo de batalla para la ultraderecha. Nuestra salud no puede quedar subordinada a una disputa ideológica.




La ultraderecha también se organiza a escala global




El gobierno de Milei no puede analizarse de manera aislada del escenario internacional. Su alineamiento político y diplomático con Estados Unidos e Israel plantea una discusión sobre el modelo de sociedad que promueve, los intereses que prioriza y el lugar que ocupan la soberanía de los pueblos, la justicia social y los derechos humanos.




Ese alineamiento no demuestra, por sí solo, que todas las políticas de esos países sean idénticas ni que exista una relación causal directa entre cada decisión de política exterior y los retrocesos internos. Sin embargo, permite discutir las alianzas ideológicas y las concepciones de libertad y derechos humanos que los gobiernos deciden priorizar.




Desde una perspectiva internacionalista, la defensa de los derechos humanos no puede aplicarse de manera selectiva. La solidaridad con el pueblo palestino y la defensa de sus derechos nacionales, civiles y humanos forman parte de esa posición. Denunciar las violaciones de derechos humanos contra la población palestina no significa justificar el antisemitismo ni responsabilizar colectivamente a las personas judías por las decisiones del Estado de Israel.




Cuestionar las políticas de un gobierno no puede convertirse en una excusa para discriminar a una comunidad religiosa o nacional. La defensa de los pueblos, la autodeterminación, la igualdad y la dignidad humana no puede depender de conveniencias geopolíticas.




Mientras se reivindica una determinada concepción de la libertad en el escenario internacional, dentro de Argentina se cuestionan políticas públicas de igualdad, diversidad y protección social. Esa contradicción merece ser discutida.




¿Qué libertad puede defenderse si se desatienden las condiciones materiales que permiten ejercerla? ¿Qué democracia puede sostenerse si se deslegitima a quienes reclaman igualdad? No hay derechos humanos a conveniencia ni solidaridad internacional si elegimos qué pueblos merecen ser defendidos y cuáles pueden ser abandonados.




El Orgullo como memoria y resistencia




La Marcha del Orgullo no es una celebración vacía ni un acontecimiento separado de la realidad política. Es una expresión histórica de resistencia, memoria y organización colectiva. En ella conviven la celebración de la diversidad, el recuerdo de quienes abrieron camino, la denuncia de las violencias y la exigencia de políticas públicas que garanticen una vida digna.




El Orgullo también es un territorio en disputa. Frente a los sectores conservadores, clericales y antiderechos que buscan recuperar influencia sobre las decisiones políticas y sociales, las comunidades LGBTIQ+ tienen el desafío de sostener una agenda propia, independiente y democrática.




No se trata de atacar las creencias personales, sino de impedir que determinadas convicciones religiosas o morales se conviertan en herramientas para restringir derechos civiles, sanitarios y sexuales. La libertad de culto es un derecho democrático; la imposición de una moral religiosa sobre el conjunto de la sociedad es otra cosa.




Por eso, defender un Estado laico, plural y respetuoso de la autonomía de las personas es parte de la lucha por la igualdad. Los derechos conquistados no pueden quedar sujetos a las expectativas de los sectores conservadores ni depender de que las diversidades permanezcan en silencio.




La ESI, la IVE y la ILE son conquistas fundamentales para la autonomía corporal, la salud pública y la prevención de las violencias. Su implementación requiere información, profesionales capacitados, insumos y servicios que garanticen una atención oportuna y sin discriminación.




Defender esos derechos implica exigir las condiciones materiales para ejercerlos, así como sostener las políticas públicas que permitan que la igualdad no sea solamente una declaración formal.




De Stonewall a nuestras calles




La historia no se repite de manera idéntica. Las condiciones políticas, sociales y jurídicas de la Argentina actual son diferentes de las que existían en Nueva York en 1969. Sin embargo, Stonewall y las luchas presentes comparten una pregunta fundamental: ¿qué hacen las comunidades cuando las instituciones que deberían protegerlas se convierten en obstáculos para ejercer sus derechos?




La historia argentina demuestra que los derechos humanos, la educación pública, el matrimonio igualitario y el aborto legal fueron posibles gracias a generaciones que se organizaron frente a las resistencias del poder. Ninguna conquista está asegurada para siempre y cada generación tiene la responsabilidad de defender los derechos alcanzados y enfrentar nuevas formas de exclusión.




El ajuste y el hambre golpean a las familias trabajadoras. La precarización profundiza las desigualdades. Las personas trans y no binarias siguen reclamando acceso efectivo a la salud, al trabajo, a la educación y a la justicia. Frente a esta realidad, no alcanza con indignarse: hacen falta organización, solidaridad, participación y presencia en las calles.




La resistencia también consiste en 

sostener espacios comunitarios

, acompañar a quienes atraviesan situaciones de violencia, construir redes de cuidado y defender la educación y la salud públicas. Consiste en no dejar a nadie atrás.




La rebelión es la negativa colectiva a aceptar la injusticia como algo natural y la decisión política de no obedecer cuando lo que se pretende imponer es la discriminación, el silencio y la pérdida de derechos.




Argentina no puede resignarse a abandonar la historia que construyó. El país del Nunca Más, del Juicio a las Juntas, de la ESI, del matrimonio igualitario y del aborto legal no puede aceptar que los derechos humanos se conviertan en una cuestión secundaria frente al ajuste económico y la avanzada conservadora.




Frente a un gobierno que confronta con las agendas feministas y de diversidad, la respuesta es más organización, más solidaridad y más democracia. Frente a los discursos de odio, más derechos humanos. Frente a la precarización, más justicia social. Frente al intento de devolvernos al silencio, más voces en las calles.




Y frente a una ultraderecha que construye alianzas internacionales mientras cuestiona las políticas de igualdad dentro de nuestras fronteras, la respuesta debe ser internacionalista, soberana, antifascista y solidaria con todos los pueblos que luchan por su dignidad.




Porque nuestros derechos no son una concesión del poder: son conquistas de las luchas populares. Porque la libertad no existe sin igualdad, y la igualdad no existe sin justicia social. Porque la defensa de los derechos humanos no puede tener fronteras ni dobles estándares.




De Stonewall a la Argentina de Milei, cuando el poder pretende convertir la opresión en norma, la organización popular abre el camino de la resistencia.




No vamos a retroceder en nuestros derechos. La batalla cultural continúa. La resistencia es colectiva. La rebelión sigue viva.




Nos vemos en las calles.

author: Bruno Malheiro
title: The Destruction of the Amazon Is Central to the Bolsonaros’ Vision for Brazil
content:
Flávio Bolsonaro may revive his father’s program to transform the Amazon into ranches, strip mines, and plantations.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

Bolsonarismo wasn’t born at the ballot box. Before it became an electoral force, it had already been taking shape along the frontiers of Brazilian capitalism, through the expansion of a territorial logic that subordinated land, nature and social relations to private accumulation. That logic legitimized the destruction of common resources and delegitimized other ways of organizing life. In 2018, maps of soy production, cattle ranching and mining overlapped with the maps showing where Jair Bolsonaro won his strongest electoral results. That wasn’t a cartographic coincidence. These frontiers were tied to political and cultural circuits, ranging from agribusiness fairs to shooting clubs to religious networks, that spread an unrestricted defense of private property, the promise of prosperity and the ideology of individual entrepreneurship. As commodity production homogenized landscapes, it also homogenized behavior and social narratives, weakening people’s ties to the land, to memory and to collective life. In the end, “agro” became “pop,” taking a central place in how meaning gets produced in Brazil.

The destruction of the Amazon is the most brutal expression of this territorial logic. Felled forests, poisoned rivers, invaded territories, and people driven out or killed: none of this is a side effect of development. These are the direct results of processes that subordinate life to private accumulation and delegitimize other ways of organizing territory. These processes sustain power relations that have expanded the far right’s strength, reach and legitimacy, and the 2018 election gave it a path into the Brazilian state.

Between 2019 and 2022, these geographies scaled up to the level of state policy, turning the Amazon into a laboratory for authoritarian experimentation. Relaxed environmental regulations, weakened enforcement, attacks on territorial rights, and the legitimization of violence in defense of private property all expanded the conditions for destruction. During this period, accumulated deforestation in the Legal Amazon reached 45,612 square kilometers, according to Brazil’s National Institute for Space Research (Inpe) and its Amazon deforestation monitoring program, known as Prodes, in 2022. The Bolsonaro administration’s agricultural policy encouraged bringing more land into the market and drove land re-concentration, while Funai, Ibama and ICMBio, Brazil’s Indigenous affairs, environmental protection and biodiversity conservation agencies, were all weakened, and environmental policy became increasingly militarized. Illegal mining expanded into Indigenous territories, linked to organized crime and enabled by the state’s tolerance. The Yanomami crisis captured this policy in its starkest form: more than 20,000 illegal miners invaded Yanomami territory, worsening river contamination and spreading disease, hunger and death, all while the government looked away.

In the Amazon, this offensive brought together sectors of traditional oligarchies with new political actors tied to predatory economic interests, including illegal ones connected to organized crime. These actors converted their economic interests into electoral power under the banner of bolsonarismo. Brazil’s so called secret budget strengthened local groups and leaders, expanding the far right’s reach across the region’s interior. This consolidation also relied on political violence, attacks on the press and the intimidation of opponents, all of which restricted critical thought and made it harder for left wing forces to organize. The Amazonian experience shows how the Bolsonaro project reshaped Brazilian patrimonialism, brought private interests closer to an authoritarian agenda and narrowed the conditions under which democracy could function.

Lula won the 2022 election by a narrow margin. His government rebuilt institutions, restored public policies, rebuilt state capacity and put Amazon protection back on the federal agenda. Brazil also regained ground in multilateral diplomacy, working to defend its interests across different blocs without aligning itself with a single center of power, a significant stance in an international landscape marked by wars and geopolitical disputes. In the Amazon, deforestation fell from 9,064 square kilometers in 2023 to 5,731 square kilometers in 2025, according to Inpe and Prodes data from 2025. Environmental enforcement resumed, operations to remove illegal occupiers confronted invasions of Indigenous lands, and territorial rights returned to the public agenda. Ibama, ICMBio and Funai also went through institutional rebuilding. Destruction, in other words, was slowed.

Despite this progress in protecting the Amazon, the first round of the 2026 election made clear that bolsonarismo‘s electoral and territorial strength has persisted. In both 2018 and 2022, the areas expanding soy production, cattle ranching, mining and deforestation overlapped geographically with the areas where Jair Bolsonaro won the most votes. In the Amazon in 2022, he won in counties that together accounted for 70% of the deforested land from the previous three decades. In 2026, separate studies once again identified these same geographies of bolsonarismo. Marcela Vecchione and Rafaella Pinto linked land concentration, properties larger than 1,000 hectares, to a drop in Lula’s vote share compared with 2022, especially along soy’s expanding frontiers. Marco Antônio Faganello, meanwhile, found sharper losses for Lula in smaller municipalities, where agribusiness carries more economic weight. Together, these studies reinforce an understanding of bolsonarismo as an electoral force sustained by a territorial logic that remains active in Brazilian society.

The rebuilding of institutions and environmental protection policies under the Lula government showed that slowing the Amazon’s destruction is possible. But this progress hasn’t dissolved the territorial foundations that sustain bolsonarismo. The 2026 election puts the country at a territorial, geopolitical and climate crossroads. The possible return of a political project that made destroying the Amazon a form of governance threatens the forest and its peoples, threatens national sovereignty given the risk of subordination to the United States, and threatens the planet’s climate balance, which the Amazon helps regulate through key biogeochemical cycles.

This election is decisive in preventing bolsonarismo from tightening its grip on the Brazilian state. Recent mobilizations by students and workers, in the streets and online, have signaled a new political force, one that needs to outlast this election’s urgency and become a lasting collective force. In the Amazon and in other biomes affected by environmental destruction, peoples and communities continue confronting the territorial forces that sustain bolsonarismo. It’s in the convergence of these different forms of mobilization that resistance to the far right can grow stronger, confronting both its territorial base and the mindset that sustains it.

Bolsonarismo turned the destruction of the Amazon into a tool for exercising power and organizing the state. But Indigenous, Quilombola, peasant, riverine and extractivist struggles, in dialogue with broader movements for rights and democracy, point toward other ways of conceiving the state, politics and our relationship with the world. It’s through the territorial experience of these forms of resistance that we can do more than confront the geographies of death that sustain bolsonarismo. We can also find geographies capable of imagining other worlds, and keep open the horizons we still need to build.

This article originally appeared in LeMonde Diplomatique Brasil, and has been translated by Panamerican Dispatch with express authorization of the editor-in-chief. Read it in its original Portuguese here.

author: Jessica Corbett
title: Trump Claims Ignorance as His Ambassador Threatens Strikes on Iran This Weekend
content:
“We may do another little Epic Fury,” Trump said after previously pledging to halt strikes until after the midterms.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

When President Donald Trump landed in Florida for a Friday campaign rally, he dismissed comments from one of his own ambassadors that the US could strike Iran this weekend as part of his illegal nearly eight-month war — but once the commander-in-chief took the stage, he changed his tune, threatening more bloodshed.

In an interview with online commentator Mario Nawfal published earlier Friday, US Ambassador to Turkey Tom Barrack, who is also Trump’s special envoy to Syria and Iraq, said: “Could there be a strike this weekend? Absolutely.”

“The president is very clear. He’s open and available and accessible to a deal. And we’ve been at the table for months and months and months,” he continued, noting that in addition to the nuclear priorities and aiming to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, the US is “in a bargain for unfreezing assets, releasing sanctions, no more kinetic engagement, [and] supplying the needed help to Israel, our ally.”

🇺🇸🇮🇷 BREAKING: AMB. TOM BARRACK WARNS U.S. STRIKE COULD HAPPEN THIS WEEKEND I asked Trump's Special Envoy, Tom Barrack: “Could there be a strike on this this weekend? His answer was direct: "Absolutely.” Amb. Barrack laid out exactly where things stand with Iran right now.… pic.twitter.com/upe7UlgGvb

Trump had said on his Truth Social platform earlier this month that “we are having productive discussions with the Islamic Republic of Iran. I want to make it clear to everybody that, while Iran is in very bad condition, both Economically and Militarily, and while the Blockade will remain in full force and effect, with Oil flowing in Record Numbers of Barrels through the Hormuz Strait (22 Million Barrels, last night alone, with not one barrel coming from, or going to, Iran!), we will not be attacking Iran at any time prior to the Midterm Elections to be held in the United States on November 3rd.”

Asked about Barrack’s suggestion that a US attack could come soon while on a Florida runway, and whether it meant Trump was rethinking that position, the president responded: “That was my ambassador? He’s a pretty powerful man, I guess. Well, if that’s the case. I don’t know anything about it.”
