The government recently adopted the IHRA definition of antisemitism while escalating its ethnic cleansing of Haitians.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

On August 24, the Dominican government adopted the International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance (IHRA) working definition of antisemitism, infamous for equating opposition to Israeli apartheid and Zionist colonialism with antisemitism. President Luis Abinader made the announcement in Santo Domingo, while speaking at an event organized by the U.S. Zionist organization Combat Antisemitism Movement. Subsequently, a statement from the Dominican Foreign Ministry justified the decision by invoking a supposed official policy against hate and discrimination dating back to 1938 when, according to the text, “the Dominican State was the only one to offer asylum in Sosúa to a significant number of Jewish refugees fleeing the war crimes perpetrated by the Nazi regime”.

In 1938, the racist and genocidal Trujillo dictatorship was in power. Just as the Israeli regime pushes for the redefinition of antisemitism to shield itself, in Orwellian fashion, Abinader is rewriting the past to accommodate the neo-Trujilloist present.

It is not surprising that the Dominican government, led by Abinader, would uphold the Trujilloist legacy. This is a government that has denied the significance of slavery during the Spanish colonial period that preceded the formation of the Dominican state, that does not officially commemorate the genocide against Haitians in 1937, known as the Parsley Massacre, and that denies the existence of widespread racism in the Dominican Republic while keeping more than 200,000 Dominicans of Haitian descent stateless. President Abinader boasts of following the ideas of dictator Joaquín Balaguer, one of the Trujillo era’s main ideologues. Abinader follows in Trujillo’s footsteps regarding what Dominican racists dub “the Haitian problem,” as shown by his policy of mass deportations and the construction of a border wall — an aggiornamento of the Trujillo-era political program known as the “Dominicanization of the border.”

Today’s neo-Trujilloist regime, with its apartheid policies of racial mass deportations, denationalization and statelessness, is coherent in its support of the genocidal Israeli regime and in claiming the legacy of the dictatorship. This is the true significance of the Dominican endorsement of the IHRA definition through a statement that upholds the legacy of a totalitarian regime that extorted and killed Jewish refugees.

In the context of the ongoing genocide in Gaza, the Dominican government has signed agreements with Israel on issues such as water management and has acquired Israeli weapons. By adopting the IHRA’s working definition of antisemitism, Abinader now threatens to further erode the weak democratic rights that still exist in this Caribbean country by moving in the direction of weaponizing accusations of antisemitism to criminalize solidarity with Palestine.

Abinader’s total subordination to Trump is another key driver of his support for Israel. The Dominican government has aligned itself with the pro-Trump “Shield of the Americas” regional coalition and has made its airports available for U.S. military operations in the Caribbean and against Venezuela; it has even agreed to accept deportees from third countries arriving from the U.S.

The Dominican government’s alliance with Israel is part of this broader trend, and one of the clearest indicators of the region’s shift to the right is the intensification of ties with Israeli apartheid.

Due to a combination of strong U.S. interference and the decline of center-left parties, elections over the past year have brought right-wing governments to power in Bolivia, Chile, Honduras, and Colombia. In the cases of Bolivia and Colombia, which had no diplomatic relations with Israel, these were immediately reestablished. In Chile and Honduras, where relations had been degraded by the withdrawal of ambassadors, there was a full diplomatic normalization.

The Venezuelan government’s capitulation to Trumpism, following the U.S. military attack on January 3, 2026, and the kidnapping of Nicolás Maduro, is also part of this regional shift to the right. Interim president Delcy Rodríguez reestablished diplomatic relations with Israel in August, following a campaign of “disaster diplomacy” by Netanyahu, who took advantage of the twin earthquakes in northern Venezuela that left more than 6,500 dead and tens of thousands injured. Relations had been broken since 2009.

In turn, the adoption of the IHRA’s definition of antisemitism has become an indicator of how closely Latin American regimes align with the objectives of Israeli foreign policy and their willingness to criminalize solidarity with Palestine. The definition in question was drafted in 2004 and adopted by the IHRA in 2016, after which it was promoted by Israeli foreign policy as part of its “new antisemitism” doctrine, which views opposition to Israel as the most significant form of antisemitism. Its text includes questioning the democratic character of the State of Israel among its examples of antisemitism. The definition was referenced in a Trump executive order in 2019 and in Latin America it has been adopted by right-wing governments in Argentina, Colombia, Costa Rica, Panama, Guatemala, and Uruguay before being adopted by the Dominican Republic.

Over the past two years in Argentina, legal proceedings have been initiated, using the IHRA definition, against Alejandro Bodart, Vanina Biasi, and Mariano Soria, leaders of the Left and Workers’ Front-Unity, a Trotskyist coalition that holds four seats in the National Congress. In Brazil, socialist leader Zé María of the PSTU and the Jewish journalist Breno Altman have been criminalized for criticizing the Israeli state and calling for Palestinian freedom “from the river to the sea.” Zé María was sentenced to two years in prison, Altman was fined, Bodart won an appeal that overturned his conviction, and the cases against Biasi and Soria remain open.

Kenneth Stern, the main drafter of the IHRA definition, who describes himself as a liberal Zionist, has criticized its use by right-wing Jewish sectors to limit freedom of expression and foster a McCarthyist environment, citing the case of Germany, where authorities have used it to label Jewish people as “anti-Semites” for opposing Israeli crimes in Gaza. Stern recommended the U.S. Senate in 2025 to not adopt the IHRA definition.

Dominican legal scholar Jaime Rodríguez has pointed out that, within the Dominican legislative framework, the Abinader administration’s endorsement of the IHRA definition is not yet legally binding, though he has warned of the risks of censorship and persecution that would result from moving forward with enshrining it into law. Democratic guarantees and freedoms in the country are already fragile, and the alliance with Israel has contributed to their weakening, as evidenced by the Dominican government’s use of the Israeli spyware Pegasus against journalists.

But the peril is an even greater one. There is a clear affinity between the Neo-Trujillista regime led by Abinader and the Zionist project, as Israel is viewed by the Dominican right as a blueprint for Dominican apartheid. Neonazi organizations regularly wield Israeli flags at racist marches against Haitians. Much like Trujillo in 1938, Abinader is unconcerned about antisemitism or discrimination more broadly, as the regime he leads is carrying out a brutal crackdown on Haitian migrants and Dominicans of Haitian descent, conducting a campaign of more than one million deportations over the past six years during which dozens of people have been killed and many more subjected to horrific violence. Normalizing genocide abroad is a way of normalizing apartheid and ethnic cleansing it at home.

Truthout is one of only a few platforms for justice-oriented, grassroots journalism. Today, we face an existential threat.

Due to Google’s launch of AI search, we’ve seen a drastic plunge in our site traffic and, as a result, our revenue. We lost 15 percent of our readership overnight. This was a readership we painstakingly built over decades, and it vanished because Google chose corporate greed over a healthy democracy.

We are fundraising right now to meet our basic operating expenses. If you can support Truthout with a one-time or monthly donation, you will make a significant impact on our work. Anything you can do makes a difference — we appreciate your support.

author: David Swanson
title: Leaving Borders Behind Us
content:
By David Swanson, World BEYOND War, October 24, 2026




Remarks at 

#NoWar2026







Welcome to #NoWar2026 Beyond Borders. Welcome to people from the other sides of countless borders from where I am — borders often effortlessly and thoughtlessly crossed by live images and audio of us, yet sometimes absurdly turned into barriers to some of our physical bodies — turned into such absurdities at enormous financial and environmental and cultural costs. Might there be another way, slightly or radically different from the current way? This will be our topic for these three days.




Thank you to the sponsors and endorsers of #NoWar2026. Our sponsors at the level of War Abolishers are Dr. Michael D. Knox and the U.S. Peace Memorial Foundation. At the level of peace champion is War Prevention Initiative. At the level of Peacemakers, our sponsors are Ann Wright, World Service Authority, Conscience Canada, Just Peace Advocates, and Women’s International League for Peace and Freedom – U.S. Congratulations to that last one for being the recipient this year of the U.S. Peace Prize from the aforementioned U.S. Peace Memorial Foundation. At the level of Supporters, our sponsor is Josette Wier. Our endorsers are far too numerous to name, but you can find them at worldbeyondwar.org/nowar2026.




Thank you to our staff who have all had a role in putting this conference together, and especially to Greta Zarro, its primary organizer.




Thank you to our board and advisory board and chapter organizers and online course facilitators and affiliate organizations and all of you who take part in these annual gatherings and support our work throughout the year.




One of my favorite things about our annual conferences is how many different corners of the world people attend from. It makes it very difficult for anyone to say the sorts of things that peace activists often say, at least where I live, things like “We just threatened to obliterate Iran” or “We just sent troops to Panama.” Of course no peace activists ever, ever actually do such things. But they speak as if they are the military or the ruler of a nation. That’s hard to do when we, the people taking part in an event like this, are from dozens of different nations.




From early on in the existence of World BEYOND War we have sold and encouraged the wearing of sky blue scarves symbolizing the sky we all share. The idea for them came from peace activists in Afghanistan who created what they called 

the Border-free Blue Scarves project

.




When we created World BEYOND War 12 years ago it was to create what World BEYOND War is, an organization not based in any nation, but with Board, Advisory Board, Staff, and participants from any corner of the planet possible. From Day 1 we had no use for borders. We’re not just based beyond borders but loyal beyond borders. We don’t support or oppose any particular government. We oppose all warmaking and all weapons making by any governments that do those things, including the ones that do them a lot and the ones that do them a little.




We also created World BEYOND War to be something else that it is, a movement aimed at no particular war or tactic or weapon, but at the entire institution of organized mass killing. We’re not here to examine the war business and decide where it needs tweaking. We’re not upset that an overpriced weapon doesn’t work. We’d love for them all to not work. We can’t provide you with a list of the bad wars and a list of the good wars any more than we can list for you the good cases of any other atrocity. So we’re inclined toward rejecting misleading examples used to justify enormous industries. A claim to have found a just and proper militarized national border is unlikely to win us over to walling off all countries, and more likely to lead us to ask for more information.




In looking at the full picture of war, we see the transformation of borders into war zones as one part of the war problem.




And we point out that in many cases its no transformation, as the borders are products of wars. Our past annual conferences have also looked at particular aspects of war’s destruction. #NoWar2017 looked at what war does to the natural environment, #NoWar2018 at what war does to the rule of law, #NoWar2021 at the business of holding weapons fairs and of preventing them, #NoWar2023 at unarmed defense as an alternative to war, #NoWar2024 at the empires of bases war creates, and #NoWar2025 at abolition — at the project of eliminating something like wars or borders.




Borders is a critical topic when it comes to war and peace because wars are driving more people to cross and to try to cross borders, because the war industry is treating those war victims as another war enemy and turning borders into permanent wars, and because those wars against refugees may evolve into wider wars as the pressures to flee warzones and militarized governments and environmentally devastated climates build on one side, and the fear, greed, bigotry, and war profits grow on the other — unless these vicious cycles are disrupted by wiser behaviors imposed on governments by nonviolent activists who’ve attended good conferences.




At World BEYOND War we often think of our work in terms of education and activism and media, though the three areas cannot always be separated. We want education to drive activism to drive media coverage to drive more education to drive more activism and so forth. Thus we do all sorts of educational events, such as this one.




Borders do so much damage that we think they are everywhere and always have been, a little bit like wars. But borders are a very strange new invention and mostly not there. A lot of things cross borders. Our work crosses borders. This conference crosses borders.







One of the great many things that cross borders is weapons.




Weapons cross borders when they’re resold, when they’re stolen, when they’re used, but especially when they are first purchased. Most places on Earth, including most places with wars, don’t manufacture any significant weapons of war. The few places that do (the U.S., Israel, France, Germany, Italy, Russia, South Korea), sell them almost everywhere. Weapons from one country, the United States, cross U.S. borders to arm dictatorships and so-called democracies across the globe, in quantities equal to the foreign weapons sales of almost all other countries combined. World War II, the Iran-Iraq War, the Mexican Drug War, the Wars on Iraq and Libya and Syria, and many others, large and small, have had U.S. weapons on both sides and weapons from other nations on both sides. One might say that weapons dealers have no respect for borders. They sell on this side and on the other side. I would say that they have the utmost respect for borders. Without the borders they’d hardly be selling anything at all.




The U.S. government itself buys more U.S. weapons than it sells, though it sells them hard. And it buys them mostly based on a pretended fear of China. I say pretended because, among many other reasons, the U.S. famously has invested in a bioweapons lab in China, and because Trump has been trying to sell weapons to China. Again, I think that demonstrates supreme respect for borders. As long as the borders are there, as long as a foreign nation exists, he expects to sell war to his side, even while selling it to the other side. And if he can’t sell a war to the public he might be able to sell it to Congress Members if they’ve been paid enough to believe it. Remember that Reagan wouldn’t give up the Star Wars ancestor of Trump’s Golden Dome, not even to rid the world of nuclear weapons, but he would have sold the same threatening, malfunctioning death missiles to the Soviets and called that peace. I would have called it justification. You can’t militarize a border until you’ve militarized the other side of it.




But what about the countries that buy weapons or allow the basing of weapons because they’re ordered to. Are they countries or pawns? Do they have borders or just lines on a game board? Or do they just have borders on some sides for some people?




Another thing that crosses borders is weapons technology. A nuclear war, no matter who fought it, would be fought with technology invented in New Mexico. The resulting nuclear winter would cross borders. The world could quite possibly be rendered lifeless or close to it even by a unilateral nuclear assault. For a second government to join in on the so-called other side would be superfluous. This rather severe limitation to a nuclear second strike is what makes some of us scratch our heads at demands for no first strikes as opposed to immediate unilateral abolition. Nuclear and other weapons testing and nuclear power catastrophes cross borders. We’ve all been impacted. Diseases cross borders. So do propaganda and corporations and hurricanes and islands of plastic garbage.




Culture crosses borders. Music crosses borders. So do friendships and love and family bonds and social movements and birds and wildlife. Everything but people. And even then, it’s only some people and some borders. Which people and which borders is determined by, or at least popularly supported by, bigotry. This includes the openly fascist, hateful, pseudoscientific, racist sort of bigotry largely or entirely rejected by many. It also includes the less obvious, such as the acceptance of different values for people with different passports, the thought that it’s simply natural for the 2% of the casualties of a war who lived near you to get most of the news coverage, or the unthought belief that (without placing anything above anything else) a culture needs to be protected in an imaginary frozen state, cut off from all fantastic enrichment and creative influences — or even just the steadfast refusal to notice that the places from which people are fleeing in large numbers are the same places that are being bombed and militarized.




“I have nothing against anyone, but people should obey the law and not cross borders without legal permission.” Is that right?




Should so-called colored people not drink from the water fountains of so-called white people now that those laws have been changed? What about before they were changed? Are there not unjust laws? If it is unjust to discriminate based on random demographic features you’re born with, is it just to discriminate based on where you were born or to what parents you were born? Is it true that you can consider such a thing to be just and have nothing against anyone? When we read medieval so-called just war theory discussing the killing and respecting of the enemy in war, do we stop and ask whether you can truly respect someone while killing them? When my neighbor Thomas Jefferson is said to have had kind feelings for his enslaved mistress or his enslaved look-alike son, we sometimes question how full and deep such kindness can have been while enslaving its objects. Maybe we should begin asking how completely we respect or even tolerate the person we tell not to cross a line where ignorant armies once grew tired and stopped.




There are policies that change at borders. This is why people claim they can see a few exceptional borders from space, and not just borders that are approximated by rivers even though rivers move. Some borders exist between a country lit up like a Christmas tree at night and a country where people can still see stars, or between a country covered in forest and one by irrigated farmland, or between the latter and a country turned to desert sand. But those aren’t borders we’re seeing exactly; they’re public policy decisions made at levels too large to be democratic, too small to be sustainable, and too selfish to be accepted.




If national borders were no more than provincial or regional borders, a lot of media pundits would find it hard to identify which places they currently hated. They wouldn’t instantly lose any racism or religious bigotry. But they’d struggle to apply their nationalism. And it is nationalism — along with the demonization of national dictators by the same government that was arming them six months earlier — that is essential for selling wars. And the quixotic crusade of protecting the rich from the poor, even while rendering swaths of the Earth uninhabitable through war and through the environmental destruction exacerbated by war, are essential for borders. And the combination of wars and borders is essential for the profiteers. We can add to that the militarization of police everywhere as the borders spread inward. Yesterday’s New York Times has a story about AI video cameras on towers in towns near the U.S.-Mexico border that can record detailed images from two-miles away including through people’s windows. This is about two days after stories that the Pentagon would have the Department of so-called Homeland Security test near borders a weapon that makes people feel like they are burning. These things creep inward in a country, but also outward to other countries’ borders and capitals.







The good news is how many more of us there are than there are profiteers.




We don’t profit from borders or from the MICIMATT or, if you’ll allow me to add two more letters, the MICIMATT-BS, the Military Industrial Congressional Intelligence Media Academia Think Tank – Borders and Surveillance complex. And we, the great majority, have an obvious solution that could benefit everyone in several ways. Reduce the money going to wars and borders and spend it on people and the environment and all things good and useful, including in those places people are now having to flee in search of a secure or decent life because of wars.




At World BEYOND War we sometimes talk about the hardware and the software of wars, the structures and the cultures. The hardware of borders — the walls and guns and cameras and prisons — separate loved ones and kill and traumatize. They create disputes. If there’s one thing you need to generate a border dispute it’s a border. They prevent cooperation across borders on urgent crises, and they militarize whole nations.




The software of borders is the normalization of borders in the backs of our heads, our mythical imagining that they are organic self-creations by people united by language and culture and perhaps even nonsense we’ve made up like race. In fact, borders are quite new in the grand scheme of things, and the attempts to pair them up with anything other than governments has always been a struggle. Borders have crossed people as often as people have crossed borders. Often, borders have been imposed by brutality and slaughter. Many borders, were they marble monuments of the people who created them, would be torn down and replaced with something less shameful. Borders may, in fact, be the largest, most prominent monuments to racism on Earth, so large we can’t see them. But we can think free of borders as we work to live free of borders. We can identify with humanity, carry world passports, and organize events like this one globally, not nationally. We can work for the sort of large-scale global cooperation that is needed for survival, as if there were no armed, walled borders, as if the right to move around were ranked up there with the right to speak or the right to self-govern. We can paint a picture of what it would be like to spend trillions of dollars on positive projects rather than on lines that make us pawns in their game.




To demilitarize borders, to deemphasize borders would fit well with democratization of governance and with a shift in power toward the local and the global levels, but it would hardly mean the complete elimination of borders, much less of countries — only of borders and countries as they are now conceived. It isn’t hard to imagine what that could look like.




At former president Jimmy Carter’s funeral, the current and past U.S. presidents and staff and families, some of the biggest boosters of wars and borders on Earth, listened solemnly to a rendition of John Lennon’s 

Imagine

: Imagine there’s no countries. It isn’t hard to do. Nothing to kill or die for. And no religion too. Imagine all the people living life in peace. One hears that song in churches and government functions around the world, not purely due to obliviousness or hypocrisy, but also because huge numbers of people know that positive change has always started with imagining it. Somebody had to imagine ending slavery or Apartheid, child labor or serfdom, lynching or human sacrifice, trial by ordeal, dueling, cannibalism, women as property, capital punishment, public tortures and executions. At last year’s annual conference of World BEYOND War, #NoWar2025, we tried to imagine eliminating or utterly transforming all kinds of institutions, including police or prisons. Unless you can imagine a world without our current incarnations of oligarchs, corporate power, armed drones, robots manufacturing biological weapons, Zionism, fascism, capitalism, or agnotologism, you’ll never create anything else.




Do you know that word, agnotology? According to it, you shouldn’t know it or anything else.




Agnotology is the manufacturing of ignorance. Wars protect you. Immigrants harm you. Massive walls and rows of weapons are basic necessities for the rule of law. Cheerfully thanking people for treating you as a criminal suspect for going on a trip is as much a civic duty as shopping, waving a flag, or beating up a protester. When it comes to reconceiving of something like wars or borders, education begins with unlearning countless things you’ve learned, before moving on to learning something new. I’m hoping to unlearn and learn many things over these next three days.







Here is a bit about what is coming.




First we are going to hear some quick reports from a sampling of World BEYOND War chapters around the world. These are volunteer-run and organized groups doing incredible educational, activist, and media work toward the abolition of war, with help from World BEYOND War’s staff and Board. We have 56 active chapters and growing and are eager to work with you to create a new one if there’s not one near you. See our annual reports on the World BEYOND War website, and the webpages for each chapter, for more on what chapters do each year.




We also have 125 affiliates; those are independent organizations that work with us toward the common goal of ending all war.




Next, following a break, we will have a musical performance, followed by our first panel, on the topic of the Militarization of Borders and the Criminalization of Migrants. Then we’ll have a chance to get together in breakout rooms and discuss.




Tomorrow, we will open with a poetry performance, so make sure you’re not late! That will lead into a panel on Case Studies of Militarized Borders and Demilitarized Zones. This promises to inform us on all kinds of history and impacts of militarized borders, as well as on what scholars, organizers, communities, and governments can do to work toward demilitarization, self-determination, and a world with fewer walls.




Following a break, we’ll next be going into a hybrid session, meaning a session that is here on Zoom for most of us but via video from a live event happening in-person in Amsterdam. The focus will be on borders and the military budget of the European Union. Fourteen years ago, the European Union was given a Nobel Peace Prize for making peace within its borders, in fact for doing to its internal borders between countries just what the world might benefit from doing to all national borders. Yet, Europe remained a major supplier of weapons to elsewhere, continued to pursue militarism towards elsewhere, and has heavily militarized its external borders. We’ll learn exactly what people are doing to reverse this trend.







Tomorrow’s closing panel, after a break, and prior to discussions in breakout rooms, will look into How War and Militarism Fuel Displacement, but also what individuals, communities, civil society, and governments can do to prevent displacement, promote peace, and contribute to building a world beyond war.




On the third day of #NoWar2026, we will open with poetry, followed by a workshop called “Nonviolent Communication: Breaking Free from Limiting Beliefs.” We all need to do more of that! And if we can do it as individuals, maybe we can do it as governments too.




The final panel of the conference will make the case for all that is to be gained from open borders. The panelists will explore how border regimes operate, whose interests they serve, and how they might be dismantled. Most importantly, the discussion will invite participants to imagine what a border-free world could look like.




Then we will be privileged to hear Closing Words by World BEYOND War’s President Kathy Kelly, followed one last time by discussion in breakout rooms. I hope that those discussions will be some of the most valuable sessions for you. It’s important to recognize how diverse and contrasting we are, how we approach this from infinite perspectives, and yet how we can find a consensus, unite, and act effectively.




I’d like to close with words from Percy Bysshe Shelley, worth remembering if you’re ever feeling beat down or walled in:




‘Rise like Lions after slumber 




In unvanquishable number, 




Shake your chains to earth like dew 




Which in sleep had fallen on you- 




Ye are many-they are few.   

 







##




The post 

Leaving Borders Behind Us

 appeared first on 

World BEYOND War

.

author: Randi Beers
title: News quiz Oct. 24 | Time for an education
content:
It’s time for another news quiz. You ready? Let’s go!




1.

 Gjoa Haven’s Emerald Hatkaittuq travelled to Manitoulin Island in September as part of her journalism studies. What was out of the ordinary about the trip?




A.

 Her group encountered a black bear while on the island but luckily they were equipped with bear spray.




B.

 Hatkaittuq’s flight back was delayed by weather, leaving her stranded in Yellowknife for a week.




C.

 She had the chance to interview Tom Selleck, who owns a home near Manitoulin Island.




2.

 A man in Qikiqtarjuaq forfeited his right to a jury trial in September. What happened?




A.

 He slept in and did not showed up late to the first day of his trial, causing a mistrial.




B.

 He heckled the jurors.




C.

 He simply stated he no longer wanted a jury trial, so the judge scheduled a new trial by judge alone.




3.

 People in Iqaluit might hear blasting this month as workers make room for what potential development?




A.

 A new movie theatre




B.

 A new Ampere building




C.

 A mall
















4.

 Cst. Jerry Patterson is Nunavik Police Service’s newest Inuk recruit. Why did he decide to become a police officer?




A.

 He loves detective movies.




B.

 The pay is good, and the work allows for travel.




C.

 His father was an officer, and he wanted to follow in his footseps.




5.

 Nunavut classrooms look different this year, says Justin Matchett, president of the Nunavut Teachers’ Association. Why?




A.

 All classrooms are fitted with brand new smart boards.




B.

 There are fewer student support assistants, causing stress and burnout among teachers.




C.

 There are many more Inuit teachers thanks to a new recruiting initiative.




Alanna Dean, left, interviews fellow student Emerald Hatkaittuq while testing audio recording equipment during an in-person intensive for Carleton University’s Certificate in Journalism in Indigenous Communities on Manitoulin Island, Ont., in September. (Photo by Cedar Grace Photography)




Answers:
















1.

 B — Hatkaittuq was 

stranded

 in Yellowknife on her way back to Gjoa Haven. Her Carleton University program director Duncan McCue noted how far Hatkaittuq had to travel to get to Manitoulin Island, but was happy the university was able to support her trip.




2.

 A — Ronald Aulakiak did not set an alarm, 

slept in

, and failed to make it to his own trial. He tried to argue he hadn’t forfeited his right to a jury trial, but the judge sided with the Crown, saying sleeping in is not a reasonable excuse to miss your own trial.




3.

 B — Ampere is hoping to 

build

 an expanded Makerspace Economic Development Hub along the Road to Nowhere. The not-for-profit provides educational programming for people of all ages.




4.

 C — Allen Patterson 

served as an officer

 with the Kativik Regional Police when his son Jerry Patterson was a child. “I spent my entire youth watching my dad be a cop,” Jerry Patterson said. “It inspired me to pursue that path.”




5.

 B — Thanks to a 

change

 in how Inuit Child First Initiative funding requests are approved, there are fewer student support assistants working in Nunavut classrooms. It’s causing stress, says Justin Matchett, president of the Nunavut Teachers’ Association, because teachers have to manage their own curriculum and have less help with students who have special needs.

author: Shahad Ali
title: Netanyahu May Lose Israeli Elections. That Won’t Save Gaza From Occupation.
content:
As living conditions here in Gaza deteriorate, we have little hope that Israel’s elections will ease our suffering.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

Israel is scheduled to hold general elections on October 27, with a fierce contest between incumbent Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, leader of the Likud party, and former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, leader of the Yashar party. These will be the first elections since Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza began following the Hamas-led October 7, 2023, attacks on Israel.

The continuation of suffering in Gaza has been exploited as a political tool to attract more votes in Israel’s electoral struggle. The Likud party, led by Netanyahu, has cited ongoing military operations and the assassinations of Palestinian faction leaders in Gaza as evidence that its military strategy is working, warning that its opponents would end the war without fully destroying Hamas. It also frames the election as a decisive battle to protect Israel from the establishment of a Palestinian state and prevent the Palestinian Authority from returning to govern Gaza. The party argues that an opposition victory would mean yielding to international pressure and accepting a two-state solution.

Likud’s campaign rhetoric has unfolded alongside calls from its far right coalition partners for the “voluntary emigration” of Palestinians from Gaza and the re-establishment of Israeli settlements in the Strip. Both Bezalel Smotrich, Israel’s finance minister and leader of the Religious Zionism party, and Itamar Ben-Gvir, Israel’s national security minister and leader of the Jewish Power party, have championed rebuilding Israeli settlements in Gaza since October 7, 2023, framing the war as an opportunity to reverse the 2005 disengagement. Moreover, as part of his election campaign, Ben-Gvir has proposed a seven-year plan, which he calls “Disengagement 710,” to relocate approximately 1.86 million Palestinians from Gaza.

On the other hand, Gadi Eisenkot, the main challenger to Netanyahu and leader of Israel’s Yashar party, pledged to remove Hamas from power in Gaza and destroy its military wing within 18 months of becoming prime minister. Speaking near the Gaza border, he said he would work to end Hamas’s rule in the Strip, either by implementing U.S. President Donald Trump’s plan, which Netanyahu’s government had approved, or through military force.

In Gaza, most people see no real difference between Benjamin Netanyahu and rivals such as Gadi Eisenkot. In our view, Gaza’s future will not be determined at the Israeli ballot box. Both Netanyahu’s and Eisenkot’s parties and members of their coalition are likely to pursue similar policies toward our cause. Although the leading parties may have different ideas and methods, their policies ultimately serve the same goal: destroying Gaza and reshaping its reality and culture to give it an Israeli character.

As the election approaches, humanitarian conditions in Gaza continue to deteriorate. Israeli forces are intensifying their military operations across the Strip through airstrikes, artillery fire, and the expansion of the area under their control, known as the Yellow Line. Since the ceasefire agreement was announced on October 10, 2025, ongoing Israeli attacks have killed 1,522 Palestinians and injured 5,421 others. Israeli forces now control an estimated 63 percent to 70 percent of the Strip and continue to seize additional land. Recently reported expansion into more areas of eastern Gaza City has forced many families to flee without a suitable place to go.

The International Organization for Migration warns that approximately 1.8 million people in Gaza face a fourth winter without adequate protection from rain, flooding, and cold. Meanwhile, Israeli authorities continue to block the entry of emergency shelter supplies, timber for repairs, heating equipment, and winter clothing through the crossings.

In addition to this, the Israeli Coordinator of Government Activities in the Territories (COGAT) announced in a statement on October 15 that coordination for the entry of commercial goods into Gaza had been suspended. COGAT claimed that the decision was made by local merchants in Gaza, who had grown frustrated with Hamas’s imposition of taxes on their trucks. However, Jihad Esleem, deputy head of the Private Transport Association in Gaza, announced on October 19 that an official agreement had been reached with the Israeli side to resume operations at the Kerem Shalom crossing, allowing truck movements to resume and commercial goods to enter the Gaza Strip.

Although the closure of the crossing did not last long, it heightened Gazans’ concerns that such closures could happen again at any moment, with Hamas used as a pretext. The closure led to shortages of food and other basic necessities, including clothing and essential shelter materials, as well as significant price increases.

The price of a 25-kilogram bag of flour has risen from 70 shekels to 150 shekels, putting it beyond the reach of many families in Gaza.

Humanitarian aid alone cannot meet the needs of the entire population. Commercial goods must also be allowed into Gaza to ensure that essential supplies are available at affordable prices. We are already beginning to see the effects of the closure. Take flour, for example: the price of a 25-kilogram bag of flour has risen from 70 shekels to 150 shekels, putting it beyond the reach of many families in Gaza, where the war has caused widespread poverty and unemployment. Moreover, vegetables, fruits, eggs, and chicken have become increasingly scarce because Israel continues to restrict their entry, even after resuming commercial operations through the Kerem Shalom crossing.

Beyond these immediate concerns, what we fear most is that the upcoming Israeli elections could trigger a resumption of the war. Netanyahu might use a renewed war to postpone the vote and salvage his political future, especially as polls have suggested the possibility of his electoral defeat. According to Haaretz military analyst Amos Harel, Netanyahu views losing the election as a serious personal threat. Harel added that people who have spoken with Netanyahu in recent years believe he is convinced that electoral defeat would lead to his conviction in his criminal trial.

Ranya Hammouda, a 45-year-old mother of five children in Gaza whom I met while she was trying to light a fire to cook for her children, told me she had no hope that her family’s conditions would improve if the Israeli government changed. She told me:

The Board of Peace plan for Gaza will remain ink on paper, as I do not believe that either Netanyahu or Eisenkot will move forward with it. From the beginning, I saw this plan as an illusion that we desperately clung to in the hope that our suffering might end one day and we could return to our normal lives.

We will continue to live under the same harsh conditions in flimsy tents, deprived of the most basic human dignity and struggling to obtain even food and water. I believe that the suffering we endured last winter will be repeated this winter. Our tent is now torn after two years of use, and I fear that strong winds and rain will cause it to collapse. On top of that, we do not have enough winter clothes or blankets. My only wish now is that winter would not come at all, because I know the suffering that awaits us … I fear that we might pay with our blood for the promises Benjamin Netanyahu makes to appease extremists. I fear that he might order vicious attacks against us simply to win more votes and bolster his election campaign.

Mohamed Abu Raylah, a 29-year-old programmer who is currently living in what remains of his home in Al-Shati Camp also told me that he no longer follows the Israeli elections or hopes that Netanyahu’s defeat might ease Palestinians’ suffering. He said he believes all the leading Israeli parties are the same, differing only in name:

The policies of killing, displacement, and destruction, passed down through Israeli generations since 1948, will continue until they achieve their goal of taking control of all Palestinian land and expelling its inhabitants…. Whether Netanyahu leaves and Eisenkot takes his place, each will use an escalation of military operations in Gaza to convince the Israeli public that he is building on past achievements rather than destroying them. The same scenario will continue: siege, suffocation, and war. Their mentality will not change. It is the mentality of an occupying power that believes we must be wiped out.

For Abu Raylah and many others in Gaza, the rivalry between Israeli politicians means nothing when Palestinians continue to be denied their rights and freedom regardless of who holds power in Israel.

“None of them will come along and give us our rights,” Raylah concluded. “Change won’t come from them. It will come from our own steadfastness.”

Truthout is one of only a few platforms for justice-oriented, grassroots journalism. Today, we face an existential threat.

Due to Google’s launch of AI search, we’ve seen a drastic plunge in our site traffic and, as a result, our revenue. We lost 15 percent of our readership overnight. This was a readership we painstakingly built over decades, and it vanished because Google chose corporate greed over a healthy democracy.

author: Mike Ludwig
title: Courts Reject Trump’s Attempt at Deploying ICE to Intimidate Voters
content:
A judge ordered Homeland Security to stop sending agents door to door in nine key states to hunt for “voter fraud.”

A judge ordered Homeland Security to stop sending agents door to door in nine key states to hunt for “voter fraud.”

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

The Trump administration is attempting to intimidate Latino voters and naturalized citizens with the threat of Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) raids and arrests ahead of the midterm elections, democracy advocates are warning.

The Department of Homeland Security (DHS), which oversees ICE, has deployed federal agents in multiple states to knock on doors and demand voters verify their identities and registration as part of an “Unlawful Voter Initiative” launched in August. In response to a lawsuit filed on October 19 by labor and voting rights groups, a federal judge in California ruled the DHS initiative violates the Voting Rights Act and ordered federal agents to halt “elections-related field operations and field interviews” in California, Wisconsin, New York, Missouri, Connecticut, Nevada, Georgia, Pennsylvania, and Washington.

“I look at this list of states, and I can think of some high-profile races that may be anticipated to be close in a lot of those jurisdictions,” said David Janovsky, senior policy analyst and acting director of the Constitution Project at the Project On Government Oversight, in an interview. “So, I think there is a reasonable question in all of this about how the federal government is choosing to focus these efforts, and the motivation that is behind that.”

Critical contests in these states include the tight race between Democratic Sen. Jon Ossoff and Republican Rep. Mike Collins in Georgia, which could decide which party has a majority in the Senate. In California, New York, and beyond, multiple races could help to determine control of the House or pad a Democratic majority.

Janovsky said sending agents door-to-door in states where Republicans face headwinds could suppress turnout. Indeed, since the 2024 election, polls suggest that Latinos and many other voters turned against the GOP as ICE invaded major cities such as Chicago and Minneapolis, causing chaos, fear, and death.

By deploying federal immigration agents to go door-to-door hunting for so-called “voter fraud” ahead of Election Day, the Trump administration may also be preparing the ground for meddling with election results and suppressing dissent if Republicans perform poorly and lose their congressional majority.

With billions of dollars in funding from Congress, the Trump administration has transformed ICE into a powerful tool of intimidation. ICE agents have injured and killed people in multiple high-profile cases since Donald Trump took office again. Under Trump’s mass deportation campaign, ICE has detained at least 506 U.S. citizens as well as many legal permanent residents. People arrested by ICE are often jailed in facilities where dozens have died amid complaints of medical neglect, including a lawful permanent resident who was found dead in a Texas ICE jail last week.

Trump’s Justice Department has been trying for over a year to get voter rolls from every state and hand them over to DHS investigators searching for evidence of widespread fraud that experts say does not exist. DHS uses voter data to create “target lists” of potentially fraudulent voter registrations, according to Wednesday’s court order.

“With Homeland Security agents knocking on people’s doors asking them if they are properly registered to vote, there is a very real concern, and it’s pretty well known, that the federal government doesn’t have accurate data,” Janovsky said. “It could freak people out, like, ‘maybe I don’t want to register to vote and put myself on this list.’”

Under an executive order issued in May 2025, the Department of Justice demanded voter rolls from states to share with DHS so agents could scour for non-citizens attempting to vote, which is exceedingly rare. States run elections, not the federal government, but many red states handed voter data over voluntarily. Another 26 states, including those named in Wednesday’s order, saw lawsuits filed by the Justice Department over voter rolls dismissed by federal courts.

“That effort has largely been rejected by the courts, because basically the federal government has no real business micromanaging every state’s voter rolls,” Janovsky said.

Unable to force states to hand over voter data, DHS gathered more than 48 million voter records through independent and commercial sources “of questionable provenance” in order to search for potential fraud, according to Wednesday’s ruling. DHS records obtained by Democracy Forward under the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) link these efforts to Heather Honey, a prominent 2020 election denier who has supplied Trump with conspiracy theories and is currently serving as a senior advisor to DHS and ICE.

The FOIA records also reveal that the Trump administration considered sending undercover agents to investigate pro-democracy groups that register people to vote, particularly in Pennsylvania and New Jersey.

Critically, the court order halting the DHS door-knocking initiative highlights the significant likelihood that such investigations would result in errors and the misidentification of citizens as non-citizens, potentially preventing them from voting, according to Elizabeth Laird, director of equity at the Center for Democracy & Technology.

“This decision continues to establish the legal basis that it is not only unethical but illegal to weaponize personal data in ways that lead to irreparable harm to individuals who are wrongly targeted,” Laird said in a statement on Thursday.

While Laird said the initial ruling is a promising step forward, the case underscores the “significant dangers” of the Trump administration’s “ongoing efforts to compile and weaponize personal information from across federal and state agencies.”

“That is the high-level problem,” Janovsky said of the administration’s exploitation of voter data. “Then you have these targeted enforcement operations happening in a handful of states, including California.”

California may be a testing ground of sorts, Janovsky said. Immigrant advocates have confirmed a rapid increase of ICE arrests in the Central Valley and beyond, with more than 100 farmworkers arrested last week alone. As California’s KQED reports, fear and rumors spread whenever ICE conducts large enforcement operations. People stay home as a result, causing Latino businesses to suffer, schoolchildren to miss classes, and patients to forgo seeing the doctors.

Advocates warn the Trump administration is betting that ICE could keep Latino voters away from the polls as well, but Democratic California Rep. Lateefah Simon says the intimidation campaign will not work. Indeed, election officials are seeing a surge of interest in early voting, with 21 million people casting early ballots as of Friday morning, NPR reports.

“We know what Republicans are trying to do — intimidate Latino citizens so they stay at home and don’t exercise their right to vote,” said Simon in a statement to local media on October 16.

Activists are preparing for the potential deployment of ICE agents to the polls, which Trump officials have said is not a priority but also could not be ruled out. In Arizona, the grassroots LUCHA coalition has trained hundreds of volunteer “constitutional defenders” to respond to federal intimidation if it were to occur on Election Day, according to communications director César Fierros.

“Masked agents in tactical gear threatening people in line or attempting to raid polling locations would be an assault on democracy itself, and it’s the greatest threat facing our nation,” Fierros told Truthout in an email. “We are preparing, but hoping for the best.”

On Monday, the Justice Department announced it was charging 28 non-citizens in California with election crimes, a development Janovsky is watching closely. On October 15, the Justice Department filed a lawsuit against California that asks a federal court to order California officials to stop processing ballots from thousands of people the Trump administration identifies as “likely non-citizens.”

Before filing the lawsuit, federal officials delivered a flash drive to Los Angeles County that contained 20,000 names and a 48-hour deadline to investigate them for fraudulent voter registrations. When local and state officials refused to do so, citing security concerns and potentially faulty data, Trump wrote online that, “They will all go to jail for a long period of time!!!”

The administration’s data has already proven to be faulty in the neighboring state of Nevada, where DHS officials recently claimed to have identified nearly 16,000 non-citizens registered to vote on state rolls. However, that number fell to 185 after further inquiry, and then to zero after state officials confirmed that those individuals were all U.S. citizens.

While Janovsky said the circumstances surrounding the charges of election crimes against 28 individuals are unclear, the Trump administration has consistently claimed to be fighting widespread voter fraud that does not exist — but such enforcement backs up bogus claims about fraud that Trump has made since losing the 2020 election.

“It’s entirely possible that some of these folks are citizens who were properly registered to vote and the feds have bad data — and that is the basis for the court injunction issued on Wednesday,” Janovsky said.

title: Рикардо Флорес Магон - Проснись, пролетарий!
content:
Автор

: Рикардо Флорес Магон

Название

: Проснись, пролетарий!

Дата

: 24 декабря 1910

Источник

: Regeneración




 Вставай, сознательный пролетарий; вставай, брат! В эти мгновения многие пролетарии взялись за оружие; но они не знают, что делают, или, вернее, не знают, на кого работают, как говорит вульгарная поговорка. Ты, кто знает интересы своего класса; ты, кто знает, что нужно бедным, – беги и скажи им: 

Товарищи, чтобы завоевать свободу и счастье, нужно нечто большее, чем храброе сердце и оружие в руках: нужна идея в мозгу

. 




 Корабль без компаса в безбрежности океана – вот что такое революционер, который рассчитывает только на своё оружие и свою отвагу. Корабль может бороться с волнами, может держаться против ветров; но как ему ориентироваться, чтобы добраться до порта, если нет компаса? Так и революционер может держаться в мятеже, может сеять смерть; но если ему недостаёт направляющей идеи для его действия, он будет не более чем корабль без компаса. Тогда революционер не знает, за что убивает, как топор не знает, зачем валит дерево. 




 Вставай, сознательный пролетарий: вставай, брат! Нужно, чтобы ты летел к своим несознательным братьям, чтобы сказать им: 

Товарищи, до сегодняшнего дня вы были рукой и резаком; теперь нужно, чтобы вы стали мозгом, рукой и резаком

. 




 Пролетарий: не позволяй больше другому думать за тебя, чтобы ты был лишь исполнителем. Резак ценой своего лезвия отрывает куски от мрамора, не зная, что получится от его действия. Революционер ценой своей крови атакует бастионы деспотизма, не зная, какова будет форма здания, которое поднимется над дымящимися развалинами. 




 Если другой думает за тебя, не удивляйся, видя, как вслед за тобой – словно вновь прорастает чёрное здание, которое ты сокрушил, – поднимается другое, ещё чернее, ещё тяжелее, откуда выглядывают ещё более зловещие защитники, и среди этих новоявленных защитников будущего деспотизма ты узнаешь тех, кто сегодня советует тебе взять винтовку и восстать; но не дает тебе понять, в чем твои интересы как бедняка, – и всё для того чтобы ты отдал жизнь за их интересы, а не за твои собственные. 




 Открой глаза, вечный пария; истекай кровью, пушечное мясо, обитатель казармы и тюрьмы. Пойми, каков твой интерес; неси в своём мозгу идею – и так пойдёшь прямо к своей цели, и из хаоса революции сумеешь извлечь благословенную формулу своего освобождения с той же точностью, с какой скульптор пробуждает в куске каменной глыбы фигуру, позу, жест произведения искусства, которое без него проспало бы ещё миллионы лет в недрах Земли; и тогда, если ты падёшь смертельно раненным в бою, ты сможешь с гордостью сказать то, что сказал тот поэт, который, идя на плаху, поднёс руку ко лбу и воскликнул перед палачом и перед народом: 

Здесь что-то есть!




 Не вступай в борьбу как стадо, но как боевая единица, которая складывается с другими равными единицами – сознательными и мятежными, – чтобы выкопать могилу политической тирании и капиталистической эксплуатации. 




 Разрушай, но позаботься разобрать развалины и вырвать фундамент. Сокрушай действием так называемое право собственности; но не для того, чтобы ты индивидуально завладел тем, что удерживают твои хозяева, ибо тогда ты превратишься в хозяина, будешь угнетать своих братьев и станешь таким же вором и таким же злодеем, как те, кто эксплуатирует тебя сейчас. Твоё освобождение должно быть включено в освобождение всех людей. Земля, которую нужно отнять у буржуа, не должна быть для тебя одного или для немногих, но для всех, без различия пола. 




 Подними потную голову; смотри прямо в лицо своим хозяевам, которые дрожат, предчувствуя твой гнев; овладей им и поставь на его место разум. Гнев ослепляет; разум освещает. Так ты лучше увидишь свой путь среди теней страшной борьбы; так ты сможешь отдать себе отчёт в том, что среди тех, кто хочет тобой руководить, много волков в овечьей шкуре; много таких, кто на мгновение утоляет твой голод, давая тебе несколько монет, чтобы ты дал их своей семье перед тем, как броситься в борьбу. Несколько монет за то, чтобы ты пошёл отдать свою кровь, чтобы он поднялся на твоих плечах! Достойно ли это? Ты солдат свободы или наёмник, нанятый честолюбцем? 




 Нет, товарищ: отвергни деньги. Недостойно человека просить денег, чтобы идти завоёвывать свободу и благосостояние. Если бы ты сделал это, чем бы ты отличался от шпика, который стреляет из оружия в своих братьев за полученную плату? 




 Винтовка наёмника куёт цепи, потому что её держит эгоистичное сердце; винтовка либертария куёт свободу, потому что её держит самоотверженное сердце. Тот, кто поднимается с оружием за плату, несёт идею личной выгоды с исключением чужой; тот, кто поднимается с оружием из любви к свободе, несёт идею довольства для всех. Разве просили денег, чтобы стать героями, Идальго, 

Пипила, человек-клин

? Разве можно вообще представить героя за плату? Представьте себе 

героя Накозари

, торгующегося о цене своих геройств; представьте себе Хуареса, требующего платы за декрет об экспроприации имущества духовенства; представьте себе Христа, требующего золота за то, чтобы быть принесённым в жертву. 




 Проснись, пролетарий! Иди в борьбу с намерением бороться за свой класс. Того, кто даёт деньги, чтобы ты взял винтовку, презирай, смотри на него с недоверием, потому что он даёт тебе несколько монет, чтобы ты отдал за него свою жизнь; он хочет твоей жертвы, чтобы сделать своё счастье; он хочет твоей гибели и несчастья твоей семьи для своей личной выгоды. Иди в борьбу, пролетарий; но не для того, чтобы возвысить кого-либо, а чтобы возвысить свой класс, чтобы придать ему достоинство; раз уж представился случай, что у тебя в руках оружие, возьми землю, но не только для себя; для себя и для всех остальных, ибо она принадлежит всем по естественному праву. 




...

author: Solange Guimarães
title: Nunes Marques faz TSE pender para Flávio Bolsonaro ao priorizar decisões e conduzir pautas
content:
O Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) sob o comando do atual presidente, ministro Kassio Nunes Marques, tem garantido à campanha eleitoral de Flávio Bolsonaro tratamento diferenciado. Mas para isso, precisou abrir mão de sua isonomia, segundo quatro especialistas ouvidos pela 

Agência Pública

: o advogado e professor de Direito Eleitoral da Fundação Getulio Vargas (FGV-SP), Fernando Neisser, a professora de Direito Eleitoral na Universidade de Brasília (UnB), Caroline Lacerda, o constitucionalista e professor da PUC-SP Pedro Serrano e Aldo Fornazieri, coordenador do curso de pós-graduação em Estratégia e Liderança Política da Fundação Escola de Sociologia e Política de São Paulo (FESPSP). 




O funcionamento da Corte apresenta “um desequilíbrio no tratamento [entre os candidatos]”, “assimetria [na comparação entre as campanhas]”, “uma postura claramente anti-isonômica” e “um viés em favor da candidatura de Flávio Bolsonaro evidente”, dizem os entrevistados, respectivamente.




O responsável pelo quadro, na visão tanto de Neisser como de Fornazieri, é o atual presidente do TSE. “Não tenho dúvida alguma que está havendo um desequilíbrio no tratamento, fundamentalmente por parte da Presidência [do TSE] e algumas vezes também por parte do ministro André Mendonça”, afirma Neisser.




“E mais grave, está havendo o uso estratégico da pauta por parte do presidente [Nunes Marques]. Decisões que beneficiariam o Lula, às vezes em plenário virtual, já com maioria formada, Ele apresenta destaque, retira de pauta”, complementa o professor da FGV.




Kassio Nunes Marques foi indicado ao Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF) pelo então presidente Jair Bolsonaro, em novembro de 2020. Já ministro, em março de 2025, votou contra O ministro Nunes Marques, do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), votou contra recursos do ex-presidente e do general Braga Netto para impedir os ministros Alexandre de Moraes, Flávio Dino e Cristiano Zanin de atuarem em seus julgamentos por tentativa de golpe de Estado. O julgamento ocorreu e ambos foram condenados.




Atualmente, Nunes Marques está envolvido em várias denúncias de envolvimento com o caso Master e o ex-banqueiro Daniel Vorcaro. Entre elas, a denúncia da 

revista piauí

 de mudar votos em processos no STF que beneficiaram negócios do Banco. Uma outra 

reportagem da revista piauí

 também indica que Vorcaro teria organizado uma festa em seu apartamento de luxo em São Paulo para receber o ministro.  




Outra forma de beneficiar a campanha de um candidato é segurar as decisões referentes a outra campanha. 

“As representações propostas pela campanha do Lula têm demorado a ser julgadas, independentemente do tema, mais do que as propostas pelo Flávio”

 diz Neisser. 




Uma pesquisa do professor de Direito Celso de Oliveira Santos, da Universidade do Estado do Rio de Janeiro (Uerj), divulgada pelo 

Estadão

, identificou que 25,7% das ações apresentadas por Flávio Bolsonaro receberam decisão em até três dias no segundo turno, contra 19,8% das movidas por Lula.




O gabinete de Nunes concentrou 43,3% das ações de Lula contra Flávio, mas apenas 16,8% das apresentadas pelo candidato do PL contra o petista. Entre as 38 ações de Lula que já haviam completado três dias de tramitação, nenhuma tinha recebido decisão nesse intervalo. Das 15 ações de Flávio nas mesmas condições, uma havia sido decidida.




A diferença ganha importância porque, numa eleição disputada nas redes sociais, uma decisão que chega tarde pode não ter qualquer efeito. Uma publicação retirada do ar durante os últimos dias da campanha pode perder seu alcance mesmo que a proibição seja revogada depois.




“A ação judicial virou ferramenta de comunicação”, explica Lacerda. Para a professora, durante uma campanha eleitoral, a demora ao analisar um caso “tem efeito prático de indeferimento.

 Se o pedido só é analisado depois que o conteúdo já circulou, ou depois da eleição, quem pediu perdeu, mesmo sem nenhuma decisão contrária”, explica. “Então a diferença de ritmo produz, sim, desequilíbrio entre as campanhas”, complementa.




Para ela, o resultado político de uma liminar pode ser mais importante do que a decisão definitiva: “Numa eleição apertada, deixar um vídeo forte fora do ar por alguns dias pode valer mais do que ganhar o processo depois”.




A dimensão dessa disputa aparece também nos números do 

Núcleo Jornalismo

. Com base em dados abertos do TSE, o veículo identificou, até 20 de outubro, pelo menos 353 processos relacionados a reclamações digitais ou desinformação envolvendo os dois presidenciáveis. Desse total, 165 foram apresentados diretamente por uma campanha contra a outra: 92 pelo campo de Flávio Bolsonaro e 73 pelo de Lula.

contato@apublica.org

 ou doe em 

apoie.apublica.org

.




O canal que colocou em campos opostos o presidente e o corregedor do TSE 




Criado pelo deputado André Janones (Rede-MG) para mobilizar apoiadores da reeleição de Lula, o canal “

Exército do Lula”

 virou alvo de uma ofensiva judicial da campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro. O PL acusou a ferramenta de disseminar desinformação e pediu sua suspensão. Em 10 de outubro, o corregedor-geral eleitoral, Ricardo Villas Bôas Cueva, responsável pelo processo, solicitou informações adicionais antes de decidir sobre a retirada do canal.
















Deputado federal André Janones (REDE-MG), ao lado do presidente Lula; Janones é o coordenador do canal “Exército do Lula” no WhatsApp




No dia seguinte, apenas 41 minutos depois de uma manifestação do corregedor, a campanha de Flávio apresentou um pedido administrativo diretamente à presidência do TSE. Kassio Nunes Marques determinou então a suspensão do canal. Cueva derrubou a ordem e questionou a atuação da presidência em um assunto já submetido à análise judicial.  




A partir daí, o canal passou por sucessivas suspensões, reativações e exigências de regularização, enquanto os dois ministros divergiam sobre quem tinha competência para decidir. A disputa não terminou com a reativação da ferramenta. Na quinta-feira, 22 de outubro, três dias antes da eleição, Kassio voltou a atender a um pedido da campanha de Flávio. 




Determinou que a Meta, responsável pelo WhatsApp, apresentasse em 24 horas um relatório técnico sobre o funcionamento do canal. A empresa deveria esclarecer, entre outros pontos, se havia atividades coordenadas entre contas, amplificação artificial de mensagens, impulsionamento pago e eventuais falhas no cumprimento do plano de conformidade firmado com a Justiça Eleitoral.




O presidente do TSE também solicitou informações a outras plataformas sobre a circulação coordenada de conteúdos associados ao canal. A medida foi apresentada como fiscalização do cumprimento das obrigações assumidas pelas empresas, não como uma nova ordem de suspensão. 




Nesta sexta-feira, 23 de outubro, a controvérsia ganhou outro capítulo. Ao examinar um mandado de segurança apresentado pela coligação de Lula, o ministro Floriano de Azevedo Marques decidiu que a presidência do TSE não pode determinar administrativamente uma nova suspensão do canal. Eventuais restrições deverão ser analisadas judicialmente, com apreciação pelo colegiado.




Para Neisser, a sequência de decisões sobre o “Exército do Lula” expõe uma questão institucional grave: o uso das atribuições da presidência para interferir em controvérsias que já estão sob responsabilidade de outros ministros. O professor defende uma reação do próprio TSE ou, se necessário, do Supremo Tribunal Federal. Em sua avaliação, é preciso “colocar um freio em condutas que colocam em dúvida o equilíbrio das decisões da presidência do TSE”. Fornazieri também cita o episódio entre os exemplos que sustentam sua acusação de favorecimento à campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro. 




Kassio, por sua vez, sustenta que o canal “Exército do Lula” apresenta uma situação jurídica distinta da ferramenta de mobilização de apoiadores de Flávio Bolsonaro, denominada “Tropa do Flávio”. Segundo o presidente do TSE, as diferenças envolvem a vinculação formal dos canais às respectivas campanhas.




Risco para o resultado das eleições




O cientista político George Avelino vê no embate entre Kassio Nunes Marques e Ricardo Villas Bôas Cueva, no caso do “Exército do Lula”, um exemplo da capacidade da própria Justiça Eleitoral de reagir a possíveis excessos. 

“O que aconteceu naquele tribunal foi que a instituição desautorizou o próprio presidente”

, afirma. Para ele, a atitude do corregedor demonstra que decisões questionáveis não passam necessariamente sem contestação dentro da Corte.




Avelino admite, no entanto, a possibilidade de equívocos e vieses em decisões individuais, mas considera precipitado concluir que a eleição esteja sendo manipulada. “Eu não vou dizer que estão roubando a eleição, seria um absurdo, uma leviandade minha”, ressalta.




Sua preocupação também se volta para os efeitos políticos das acusações contra o tribunal. O cientista político lembra que a confiança nas instituições é indispensável para que o resultado das urnas seja reconhecido, inclusive por quem perder a disputa. “Se você desconfiar do processo eleitoral, a democracia acaba no dia seguinte”, adverte.




A professora Caroline Lacerda também afirma que uma decisão judicial desfavorável a determinada campanha não significa, necessariamente, tratamento desigual. Ela ressalta que o pedido de destaque, utilizado pelo ministro André Mendonça no julgamento envolvendo o vídeo sobre os cortes de R$ 200 bilhões propostos por Flávio Bolsonaro, chamado de “tesouraço” pela campanha de Lula, é um instrumento previsto nas regras do tribunal. O problema, em sua avaliação, está nos efeitos práticos de sua utilização durante uma campanha que se aproxima do fim.




Neisser considera graves as controvérsias envolvendo a presidência do tribunal, mas não afirma que elas sejam suficientes para comprometer o resultado da votação. Para ele, eventuais distorções podem ser corrigidas pelo plenário do TSE ou, em determinadas circunstâncias, pelo Supremo Tribunal Federal.




Já Pedro Serrano admite que “se comprovado um tratamento desigual com potencial para interferir em uma disputa apertada, as consequências podem atingir a própria legitimidade do resultado”. O professor da PUC-SP, entretanto, também distingue a existência de decisões que considera desiguais, de uma demonstração de que tenham alterado a vontade dos eleitores. 

Uma eventual contestação da legitimidade do resultado exigiria, segundo Serrano, provas concretas da gravidade das condutas e de seus efeitos sobre a disputa.




Justiça caiu nas redes
















Presidente do TSE, ministro Nunes Marques, se reúne com representantes da Meta na sexta-feira, 23 de outubro




Para Gustavo Roberto, pesquisador de pós-doutorado na USP e professor de Direito Eleitoral, a crise expõe um outro problema que ultrapassa os gabinetes dos ministros: a dificuldade de acompanhar uma campanha que se desenvolve em tempo real nas plataformas digitais. A combinação entre polarização, inteligência artificial, aplicativos de mensagens, influenciadores e multiplicação de ações judiciais “parece ter gerado um colapso da capacidade de funcionamento da Justiça Eleitoral”, avalia.




Segundo o professor, as campanhas perceberam as limitações do sistema e passaram a explorá-las. “As campanhas, sentindo a fragilidade também do Judiciário, estão jogando com e contra ele próprio”, afirma.




Roberto considera que tanto a circulação de notícias fraudulentas quanto o impulsionamento irregular exigem respostas rápidas. Mas faz uma ressalva importante: afirma que não dispõe de dados empíricos suficientes para afirmar que o tribunal esteja priorizando um tipo de infração em detrimento de outro.




A velocidade das redes também preocupa Avelino, embora o cientista político questione a tendência de atribuir à comunicação digital um peso determinante na escolha do presidente. Avelino lembra que televisão, debates e outras formas de comunicação continuam influenciando o eleitorado. 




Para ele, os tribunais enfrentam dificuldades permanentes para compreender tecnologias e estratégias que mudam rapidamente. “O que é novo ontem é velho amanhã. Às vezes, o que é novo hoje de manhã é velho hoje à tarde”, observa.




Pedro Serrano também considera que a tecnologia agravou uma crise mais antiga, com a transferência dos conflitos políticos para Poder Judiciário, que passa a decidir questões antes resolvidas no debate e na própria disputa política.




“A política tem resolvido de forma cada vez pior os seus próprios conflitos, terceirizando para o Poder Judiciário a solução de conflitos que deveriam ser solucionados no âmbito da política”, afirma. O resultado, segundo Serrano, é a crescente politização da Justiça, fenômeno que não começou em 2026, mas se tornou especialmente visível nesta eleição.




O que acontece com as ações depois da votação?
















 Corregedor Ricardo Villas Bôas Cueva tem questionado atitudes do presidente da Corte, ministro Nunes Marques no processo eleitoral de 2026




A proximidade do segundo turno faz com que parte das controvérsias possa perder sua finalidade prática quando a votação terminar. Caroline Lacerda explica que representações destinadas exclusivamente à retirada de propaganda ou à concessão de direito de resposta tendem a perder o objeto depois da eleição. Já processos que envolvem multas podem continuar, assim como ações de investigação judicial eleitoral destinadas a apurar abuso de poder ou uso indevido dos meios de comunicação.




Essa distinção é fundamental. Uma liminar que determina a remoção de conteúdo não equivale a uma condenação definitiva, e uma representação sobre propaganda não tem, por si só, o mesmo alcance de uma ação capaz de discutir a validade de um mandato.




Enquanto isso, o TSE continua recebendo demandas sobre a atuação das plataformas. Nesta quinta-feira, 22 de outubro, o 

corregedor Ricardo Villas Bôas Cueva determinou

 que Meta e a rede social X (antigo Twitter) prestassem esclarecimentos técnicos sobre distribuição de conteúdos, anúncios eleitorais, inteligência artificial e possíveis diferenças de tratamento entre candidaturas, em uma investigação apresentada pela coligação de Lula.

title: Έκθεση: Ο μυστικός Τύπος της αντίστασης στη ναζιστική κατοχή
content:
Έκθεση για τον μυστικό Τύπο της Εθνικής Αντίστασης




Φέτος, συμπληρώνονται 82 χρόνια από την απελευθέρωση της Θεσσαλονίκης, στις 30 Ὀκτωβρίου1944, από τα γερμανικά στρατεύματα Κατοχής, με την καταλυτική επέμβαση των ανταρτικών δυνάμεων του ΕΛΑΣ, που έσωσαν και τις υποδομές της πόλης από την καταστροφὴ.




Η Εταιρεία 

Διάσωσης ι

στορικὡν 

Αρχεἱων Μακεδονίας

 

(EΔΙA) 

1940-1974, 

τιμώντας την επέτειο ’απολὐτρωσης’ της πόλης από το ναζιστικό ζυγό, διοργανώνει, από τις 19-29|1Ο|2026͵στο χώρο του φουαγιέ του Δημαρχείου Θεσσαλονίκης, 

έκθεση για τον μυστικὸ Τύπο της Εθνικἠς Αντίστασης

, που κυκλοφόρησε την περίοδο 1941-1944 στη Θεσσαλονίκη και την υπόλοιπη Βόρεια Ελλάδα.




Στα μαύρα χρόνια της χιτλερικής σκλαβιᾶς τηνπερίοδο 1941—1944, κυκλοφὀρησαν περισσότερες από 220 μυστικές εφηµερίδες στους νομούς της Μακεδονίας και της Θράκης. ‘Εναςπραγµατικός’άθλος’, αν σκεφτεί κανείς τις ανείπωτες δυσκολίες και τους θανάσιμους κινδύνους της Κατοχής, όταν και μόνο ηανάγνωση κάποιας αντιστασιακής εφημερίδας μπορούσε να καταλήξει στο εκτελεστικό απόσπασμα των Ναζί κατακτητών.




Το αρχειακό υλικό που εκτίθεται, προέρχεται από τη συλλογή του δημοσιογρἀφου-ιστορικού ερευνητή Σπύρου Κουζινόπουλου. Η έκθεση πραγματοποιείται υπό την αιγίδα του ΔήμουΘεσσαλονίκης και μετην ευγενική υποστήριξη του Οργανισμού Μεγάρου Μουσικής Θεσσαλονίκης.




Η έκθεση είναι ανοιχτή στο κοινό όλες τις μέρες της εβδομάδας, από τις 10π.μ. έως τις 8.30μ.μ.͵Σάββατο-Κυριακἠ έως τις 6.30μ.μ.




Σημειώνεται ότι η 30η Ὀκτωβρίου, ημέρα απελευθέρωσης της πόλης από τα χιτλερικά στρατεύματα κατοχής, καθιερώθηκε ως “δηµόσια εορτἠ τοπικής σημασίας για τον Δἠμο Θεσσαλονίκης’ με το Προεδρικό Διάταγμα 50|9-5-2016.

Έκθεση: Ο μυστικός Τύπος της αντίστασης στη ναζιστική κατοχή

 first appeared on 

infolibre

.
