author: Julius Gavroche
title: The “enemy” isn’t in the streets. It’s what sends you there
content:
by Leonardo Caffo




from 

The Anarchist Library




From France to Albania, from Belgium to Turin, the protests of these days stage a clash between metaphors. Young people (the people) and police officers (the State), equally precarious, face each other as if the other were the enemy. But the enemy stopped living where we look for it long ago. And that is precisely where it organizes the anger, makes it visible and summons it into the street.




Let me say this right away, to leave no room for misunderstanding: the young people who have been filling the streets of Europe in recent weeks have every right to do so. This is not a rhetorical concession, one of those premises you write only to take back three lines later. They have reasons to spare: schools falling apart, overcrowded classrooms, a future shrinking like a room whose walls someone moves at night while we sleep. Anyone who dismisses them as vandals, as spoiled children of a prosperity they no longer know, or as puppets of some hidden director, has understood nothing. Or pretends not to understand, which is worse. But precisely because they are right, and precisely because their distress is real, it is worth asking the question nobody seems willing to ask these weeks. Not because it is difficult, but because it is uncomfortable for everyone: for governments, for movements, for newspapers, for commentators. The question is simple. Against whom are they protesting? In favor of what?




There is no point asking against 

what

. The what is clear, even too clear: the cuts, the cost of living, the decrees, the war that swallows resources, the idea that school should serve the labor market rather than people, impossible rents. But where does the power that produces all this live, if it lives anywhere at all? Because a protest without an addressee is not an absence of politics: it is a politics someone else is doing in your place, using your body, your time, your anger.







I. The scene: a Europe that always ends up in the same frame




Let us look at the images before interpreting them. In France the mobilization began in September in Brittany, in the schools, against staff shortages and the decay of public education, and spread across the whole country. On October 6, according to the Interior Ministry, more than 250,000 people were in the streets; according to the organizers, almost twice that. The toll of weeks of protest runs to thousands of arrests and hundreds injured, among students, teachers and officers. In Lens a fifteen-year-old boy lost a hand after coming into contact with a police grenade. In Brussels, on October 9, unions striking against budget cuts were joined by hundreds of students inspired by what was happening in France. A few dozen masked protesters threw stones at the police; the police responded with tear gas and water cannons; twenty-one people were detained, thirteen of them minors. In Albania, the student protest outside the Ministry of Education on October 13 turned within hours into a revolt against the Rama government: the Ministry of Justice in flames, attacks on public buildings, banks and businesses, 89 injured, 61 of them officers.




And then Italy. On October 16 thousands of students marched in every city against the school decree, the cap on foreign pupils in classrooms, the 4+2 model for technical institutes, the cost of living, military spending. In Milan, a river of second-generation young people, born here or arrived as children, forming a shield against those who would like to count them. In Rome, bottles and firecrackers outside the ministry. In Bologna, shields in front of the station. In Turin, stones against officers, water cannons against students, and in between some teachers who placed themselves between the two lines, as their French colleagues had done a few days earlier. You don’t need to be a sociologist to notice that the causes are different, and so are the contexts, and yet the final frame is always the same. A kid in a hood facing a kid in a helmet. The protest is born against something enormous and undefined, a social model, a stolen future, a politics that does not listen. And it ends, with almost mechanical regularity, in hand-to-hand combat between two people who have never met and have no personal reason to hate each other.




This frame is the real political subject under discussion today. Not because the clash is the heart of the matter: on the contrary, I argue that it is peripheral. But because that frame is a symptom, in the precise sense the word has in psychoanalysis: a compromise formation that shows and hides at the same time. It shows that there is a conflict. It hides who is really party to it. And the media, who love that frame because it brings in viewers, only amplify its function as a screen. Even the mayor of Turin said so, with unexpected lucidity: there are those who use those images to talk only about the clashes, leaving the problems the young people raise in the background.




II. Two metaphors facing each other in a mirror




Let us return to those two bodies. The student in the street is a metaphor: he stands for a generation whose future has been taken away, for a school turned into the antechamber of employment, for an existence that discovers itself precarious before it has even begun. But the police officer is a metaphor too. In fact, if you look closely, he embodies it even better. He is often young as well, almost always from the peripheries and the South, poorly paid for a hellish job that asks him to stand for hours under a hail of bottles to defend a ministry whose minister he will never meet. He too has watched his future shrink; he too is the product of a social model that offers a uniform as the only possible stability. The difference between the two is not one of class. It is one of position: one has been put in front, the other behind a shield.




Pier Paolo Pasolini understood this in 1968 when, after the clashes at Valle Giulia, he wrote that his sympathies lay with the police officers, sons of the poor, and not with the students, children of the bourgeoisie. It was a heresy, and he was treated as a reactionary (and hardly anyone has ever read how that line continues, something Ascanio Celestini does very well in his new book on Pasolini). But Pasolini’s gesture was not a defense of the police: it was an attempt to shift the gaze from the choreography to the structure, to remind us that within that clash stood bodies socially closer than the flags let on. Today that intuition has become even truer, and at the same time more tragic. Truer, because the social distance between the student and the officer has narrowed further: the kids in the streets of Milan are the children of workers, migrants, precarious laborers. More tragic, because in the meantime the master those officers once shielded has disappeared. In 1968 behind the cordon there was still the State, there was the bourgeoisie, there was an enemy with an address. Today behind the cordon there is a palace often empty of real power.




Hegel, in the 

Phenomenology of Spirit

, describes the struggle for recognition as the moment when two self-consciousnesses confront each other at the risk of their lives, and from which the relationship between master and servant arises. The decisive point, the one Alexandre Kojève would make famous in his Paris lectures, is that the struggle only makes sense if there is a master by whom to be recognized. But what happens when the struggle takes place between two servants? When both contenders seek recognition from a third party who is not present, and who has no interest in recognizing anyone? The dialectic jams. There is no synthesis, no overcoming, no history. There is only repetition: the same scene, every week, in a different city.




René Girard gave this mechanism a name. In 

Violence and the Sacred

 and then in 

The Scapegoat

, Girard shows how communities in crisis discharge accumulated violence onto a substitute victim, who is not the cause of the crisis but becomes its symbol. The sacrifice solves nothing, but it temporarily restores order: the violence is discharged, the tension drops, everything can start again as before. The street clash works exactly like this, and it works in both directions. For the student, the police officer is the scapegoat of the system: striking him is symbolically striking power. For the State, and for the public reading the next day’s papers, the violent student is the scapegoat of disorder: punishing him reaffirms order. Each sacrifices the other. No one touches the cause.




That is why I speak of a clash between metaphors. Not to diminish the pain, which is all too real: the hand lost in Lens is no figure of speech, nor are the 61 officers injured in Tirana. But because what confronts itself in those streets is not the subjects of the conflict but their representations. Two figures of distress set against each other, each convinced the other is the obstacle. And while they stare into each other’s eyes, neither looks up from the screen.




III. Power has changed address




If we look up, what do we see? We see that what is at stake in the streets of Paris, Tirana, Brussels, Madrid and Turin is no longer, or no longer only, a matter of States. Local governments, with their budgets and decrees, are the visible target: the one you can name in a slogan, the one outside whose ministry a march can stop. But the organization of society that produces the distress now has little to do with ministries. Governments administer ever-narrower margins within constraints decided elsewhere: by the financial markets that rate the debt, by the platforms that control the infrastructure of information, by the large corporations that decide where to move capital, production, labor.




Michel Foucault, back in the 1970s, taught us to distrust the idea that power resides in a place. Power, he wrote, is not a thing one possesses; it is a network of relations running through bodies, institutions, forms of knowledge. It is not at the top of the pyramid; it is everywhere. But Foucault was still thinking of disciplinary institutions: the school, the barracks, the factory, the prison. Closed places, with walls and timetables, where power shaped individuals. Gilles Deleuze, in a short 1990 text that now reads like a prophecy, the 

Postscript on the Societies of Control

, had already announced the end of that model. Disciplinary societies, he said, are giving way to societies of control, in which power no longer confines but modulates, no longer watches within an enclosure but follows everywhere, continuously and without boundaries. Man, Deleuze observed, is no longer man enclosed but man in debt. And he added a detail that sounds chilling today: in the society of control, school would be replaced by lifelong training, and the corporation would take the factory’s place as the soul of the system. Reread that text thinking of the 4+2 model, of work-study schemes, of school as one segment in a human-capital supply chain, and you realize that this autumn’s students are protesting precisely against what Deleuze described. But they do so with the tools of another era: the march, the occupation, the siege of the ministry. Tools designed for a power that had a center, a palace, a door to break down. Control power, by contrast, has no doors. You cannot besiege it, because it is nowhere.




Michael Hardt and Antonio Negri (who knows how pleased he would have been today), in 

Empire

, described this form of sovereignty as a decentered and deterritorializing apparatus, with no territorial center and no fixed boundaries. One can argue at length about their political conclusions, but the diagnosis stands: sovereignty no longer coincides with the nation-state. Power has evaporated into the global space of flows, while politics has remained local. Power without politics on one side, politics without power on the other. In between, the streets. And here we understand why the young people’s anger, even when it finds a precise target, such as the Italian decree or the Rama government, always ends up seeming a little disproportionate, a little out of focus. Not because it is unjustified, but because the addressee is not equal to the message. A minister is being asked to give back a future it is not in his power to give back. A national government is being asked to reverse processes that national governments have, for decades, merely managed. The street shouts at the palace, but the palace is only the switchboard of a power that answers from another number. The ministry, in this scene, is as much a metaphor as the student and the police officer: it is the visible face of decisions it does not make.




IV. The paradox of the medium: what moves you is what you are fighting




There is, however, something deeper, and more disturbing, than the simple evaporation of power upward. And it is the real news of this autumn, the news no newscast will report. The protests are organized on the very platforms that embody the power they protest against. The chats where the meeting point is decided, the social networks that call for mobilization, the algorithms that circulate videos of the clashes: these are all private infrastructures, owned by a few corporations, fueled by an economic model that lives on attention, data, conflict. What moves the young people and what they would like to fight coincide. The medium of the revolt is its target.




Marshall McLuhan put it in a phrase that has become a cliché and that, for this very reason, no one takes seriously anymore: the medium is the message. What matters is not only what is said, but through what it is said, because the medium alters the very form of experience. A protest organized on a platform is not the same as a protest organized in an assembly. It inherits the platform’s grammar: speed, fragmentation, the hunt for the image, polarization. Above all it inherits its economic logic. Every shared video of clashes is monetized attention. Every call to mobilize is a data point. Every expression of rage online is engagement. The platform is not neutral toward the conflict: it lives off it. And it has every interest in the conflict taking its most spectacular form, namely physical confrontation, because that is what generates the most views.




It is a telling detail that in France a fact-checking organization identified fake videos circulated to inflate the chaos and violence of the protests. It does not matter here who produced them. What matters is that the ecosystem rewards them. Guy Debord, in 

The Society of the Spectacle

, wrote that the spectacle is not a collection of images but a social relationship between people mediated by images. And there it is: today’s street is exactly that. A social relationship, the one between the student and the police officer, entirely mediated by the images that will be drawn from it. People take to the streets partly to be seen, and they are seen only if the clash happens. The spectacle has absorbed the contestation of the spectacle, as Debord feared and as the Situationists, in the end, could not prevent.




Byung-Chul Han added a decisive piece. In 

Psychopolitics

 he observes that contemporary power does not repress freedom; it exploits it. It does not force us to be silent; it encourages us to speak, to express ourselves, to share. It is a seductive power, working through our desire rather than against it. That is why, Han says, it is so hard to rebel: because rebellion itself becomes a form of participation in the system. Shoshana Zuboff, in 

The Age of Surveillance Capitalism

, gave this mechanism a precise economic anatomy: human experience turned into free raw material, extracted, analyzed and resold as behavioral prediction. The anger of a generation is an extraordinary mine of behavioral data. And it is extracted as it is being expressed.




The result is a paradox reminiscent of the knot in certain ancient myths, where the hero flees his fate and, by fleeing, fulfills it. The young people are fighting a model of society governed by financial and digital flows, using those very flows as their only means of organization. This is not a fault, not naivety: it is the condition of anyone living today. There is no available outside, no uncontaminated place from which to organize resistance. But precisely for this reason it should be named. Because as long as it goes unnamed, that paradox works in silence, and it always works in the same direction: it turns protest into content, content into clashes, clashes into ratings. And power, the real one, thanks you for your cooperation.




V. Simulacra of struggle




All this leads to a conclusion that must be stated carefully, because it is easy to misread. This autumn’s struggles risk becoming simulacra. Not in the sense that they are fake: the pain is real, the reasons are real, the bruises are real. But in the precise sense Jean Baudrillard gave the word. In 

Simulacra and Simulation

 Baudrillard describes a sequence: first the image reflects a reality, then it masks it, then it masks its absence, and finally it bears no relation to any reality whatsoever and is its own pure simulacrum. The street clash passes through every one of these phases. At first it represents a real conflict, between a generation and a social model. Then it masks it, because it replaces it with another conflict, between students and police. Then it masks its absence, because the real adversary is not present and the scene serves to make us believe it is. Finally it becomes autonomous: people take to the streets for the clash, the clash produces images, the images produce the next protest.




Baudrillard wrote a provocative book titled 

The Gulf War Did Not Take Place

. Obviously he did not deny the bombs and the dead. He argued that what the Western public had seen was not a war but its televised simulation, an event built to be watched. One could write an equally provocative book today: the revolt is not taking place. Not because there are no people in the streets, but because the event we call revolt is increasingly its own representation, a coded sequence of gestures, slogans, images and reactions everyone knows in advance. The minister will say the violence is unacceptable; the opposition will say the young people must be listened to; the police union will demand more protection; the papers will headline the clashes. And the next day nothing structural will have changed.




Mark Fisher, in 

Capitalist Realism

, described the condition of a generation for whom it is easier to imagine the end of the world than the end of capitalism. Fisher’s point was not that capitalism was invincible, but that it had colonized the imagination to the point of making any alternative unthinkable. Protest too, in this picture, is precoded: there is a space set aside for dissent, a format, a genre, with its own rules and outcomes. Fisher spoke of gestural anti-capitalism: critique of the system expressed as style, as pose, without touching the mechanisms. I am not saying the young people of Turin or Paris are posing. I am saying the system they move within has already anticipated their anger and prepared a stage for it.




The enormous political problem today is that the individual can no longer represent to himself the totality of the system he lives in. Global capitalism is too vast, too abstract, too distributed for anyone to draw its map and locate themselves within it. Without that map, political action is blind: you strike what you see, not what matters. The police officer is visible. The ministry is visible. The capital flow that decided a school’s closure, the algorithm that decided which protest to show and which not, the investment fund that owns the platform on which the protest was called: these cannot be seen. And what cannot be seen cannot be fought. This is the heart of the simulacrum: the struggle takes place between sections of the population equally in distress, while the distress itself is produced elsewhere. The student who will never have a pension and the officer who barely makes it to the end of the month. The precarious teacher who steps in to protect his pupils and the shopkeeper whose window is smashed. The second-generation immigrant marching against the cap on foreigners and the pensioner watching him fearfully from the window. All in difficulty, all convinced they have the problem in front of them. None of them truly in a position to solve it.




VI. Infiltrators, clashes, legitimacy: the wrong questions




I already know what objections will come, because they are the same ones repeated every hot autumn. There are infiltrators, professional troublemakers, those who in Turin seemed a little too old to be students. According to the Albanian police, of the dozens detained after the Tirana clashes only a few were students. The police, on the other side, use disproportionate force, and human rights organizations have been denouncing it in France for weeks. Burning a ministry is not legitimate; or it is, if the ministry is deaf. Throwing a stone is violence; or it is the response to a greater, structural, invisible violence.




These are serious discussions, and I do not intend to dismiss them. Twentieth-century political philosophy left us refined tools for tackling them. Walter Benjamin, in his 

Critique of Violence

, distinguished between law-making and law-preserving violence, and showed how every legal order is born of a violence it then forgets. Hannah Arendt, in 

On Violence

, argued the opposite: that violence and power are opposites; where power is real, that is, grounded in consent and acting in concert, violence is unnecessary; violence appears where power is waning, and it can destroy power but never create it. Frantz Fanon, in 

The Wretched of the Earth

, saw in the violence of the colonized a moment of detoxification, a way of reclaiming a denied subjectivity. These are three incompatible positions, and each illuminates something.




But it is Arendt who gives us the key to understanding why these questions are secondary today. If violence appears where power is waning, then the violence in these streets is the sign of a power vacuum. Not of an excess of state power, as those throwing stones believe. Not of an excess of youthful disorder, as those repressing them believe. But of a vacuum: real power, the power that decides, is not present, and the two bodies left in the street collide because they have nothing else to hit. Street violence is the shape politics takes when politics no longer has an interlocutor.




That is why the debate over who is infiltrating, over how far it is acceptable to make use of a mobilization that destroys everything, over what the acceptable threshold of force might be, is a debate about the choreography, not the music. Every hour spent establishing who threw the first stone is an hour not spent talking about where the money missing from schools ends up. Every editorial on student violence, or on police brutality, is one editorial fewer on who owns the infrastructures through which we think, on what form of life we are accepting without ever having chosen it. I am not saying those questions should not be asked. I am saying they are the questions the system prefers us to ask, because they keep us busy arguing about the perimeter while the center remains intact.




There is, indeed, a suspicion worth formulating, even if it cannot be proven. Street violence benefits everyone except those who suffer it. It benefits governments, which can shift the conversation from the reasons for the protest to security. It benefits the most radical groups, which gain visibility. It benefits the media, which gain viewers. It benefits the platforms, which gain traffic. It does not benefit the students, who see their reasons buried under the images. It does not benefit the police officers, who risk their bodies for a miserable salary. An economy of violence in which the gains are distributed at the top and the costs at the bottom: is that not the most precise definition of the system being protested against?




VII. The enemy exists, and it is shared




Carl Schmitt identified the distinction between friend and enemy as the very criterion of the political. To do politics, for Schmitt, means being able to name the enemy. It is a dangerous thesis, one that has justified horrors, and I do not propose it as a model. But it contains a truth that today’s streets make evident by contrast: whoever cannot name their enemy does not do politics, they endure it. And whoever gets the enemy wrong is doing someone else’s politics. The student who sees the police officer as the enemy, and the police officer who sees the student as the enemy, are both applying Schmitt’s criterion in the worst possible way: they have identified their own kind as the enemy.




The enemy exists. It is shared: shared by students and police officers, by the teachers who step in between and the parents watching the news, by the second-generation kids of Milan and the pensioners who fear them. It is an organization of society founded on extraction: of value from labor, of data from lives, of attention from emotions, of future from the generations to come. It has no face, because it is made of flows. It has no headquarters, because it is distributed. It has no name, because every name we give it, finance, platforms, corporations, capital, captures only one aspect. But it has precise, measurable effects that the young people in the streets know very well: collapsing schools, impossible rents, fixed-term contracts, a climate in collapse. The enemy, then, is not in those streets. It is what sends you into those streets. It is what organizes your anger, lays it out, makes it go viral, turns it into content and then channels it into the one outlet that costs it nothing: having you tear each other apart. While, outside the frame, the world crumbles, work dissolves, school becomes a supply chain, and those who profit from all this have never needed to put on a helmet or a balaclava.




This is not an invitation to stay home. That would be the most convenient advice for the system I have described, and the most unjust toward young people who are right. It is an invitation to protest better. To turn the street from a stage into a place of thought: assemblies, inquiries, maps of power drawn together. To seek unexpected alliances, even with those on the other side of the shield, who have a union, a salary and a child attending the same crumbling school. To hold governments to account, of course, but also those above them: the platforms, the funds, the supranational institutions that decide without ever setting foot in the street. And not to forget that the phone you use to organize the next march also belongs to someone: try disconnecting all at once, all of you, stop posting and go back somewhere else, and see how suddenly everything would collapse.

author: Unknown
title: « La comparution immédiate n'était à mon sens pas nécessaire » : premières comparution immédiates suite au 17 ocotbre
content:
Deux jeunes femmes arrivent dans le box. L'une est accusée de vol en réunion (en «

 

récidive légale

 

»). L'autre d'avoir conduit un véhicule alors que son permis est suspendue et d'avoir fait un «

 

refus d'obtempérer

 

».


«

 

Est-ce que quelqu'un est là pour la société 

JD

 sport, partie civile

 

» demande le juge. Pas de réponse.


Le procès commence. Vers 3h du mat', une patrouille de police est positionnée derrière le 

JD

 Sport de la Soie à Vaulx-en-Velin. La porte de la réserve a été fracturée et «

 

un pillage est en cours

 

». Le sol est jonché de vêtements. L'équipage remarque un jeune homme, chargé de vêtements, qui s'engouffre dans une voiture, qui démarre. La police les prend en chasse sur quelques dizaines de kilomètres (30 min de course-poursuite apparemment). Puis la voiture stoppe. Le jeune homme en sort et s'enfuit dans un immeuble. 


La conductrice stoppe la voiture quelques rues plus loin et les deux occupantes sont sorties de force et menottées. La passagère est dépistée au cannabis. La voiture finit au commissariat de Villeurbanne.




Le préjudice des vêtements retrouvés dans la voiture s'élève à 1725 euros. Mais, précise, le juge, des vêtements ont été jeté par la fenêtre durant toute la course-poursuite.




La conductrice raconte : «

 

j'étais posé, je regardais les petits qui sortaient du magasin, y'avait plein de gens qui sortaient les bras chargés. En vrai, je cautionne pas.

 

»


Un type est venu dans sa voiture. Il lui a proposé 50 euros pour le ramener à Vaulx-en-Velin. Le véhicule qui devait le récupérer était parti. Le véhicule de police s'est rapproché. La proposition s'est transformé en menaces («

 

je connais ton blaze, démarre

 

»). Et la course-poursuite s'est lancée.


«

 

En garde-à-vue, j'ai réalisé que j'avais fait de la merde, je ne peux plus revenir en arrière.

 

»




Le juge : à son amie qui a ramassé des vêtements devant le magasin : «

 

vous avez dit que c'était une pulsion dans votre corps

 

?

 

» «

 

Non j'ai jamais dit ça. Les policiers ne m'ont pas laissé relire ma déposition.

 

»
















 







Procureur : «

 

Vous avez un certain nombre de choses qui se sont passées dans le centre, des événements qui ont secoué la ville de Lyon ce week-end. Ces faits sont qualifiés par la loi au préjudice du magasin 

JD

 Sport. On peut se dire que ce ne sont que des atteintes aux biens, que ce n'est pas très grave. Des gens ont profité du chaos, ce qui a donné lieu à des scènes de pillage au préjudice des magasins et des habitants des quartiers.


On est là dans l'expression de comportements asociaux. Ils profitent de l'anonymat de ces rassemblements. Elles ont profité de l'anarchie. L'agglomération a été à feux et à sang, tout le monde regarde la télé et les réseaux sociaux. Les fonctionnaires de police ont été débordé. Elles sont les seules à se faire interpeller, certes. Tant pis pour elles.


Ces dames ont bien vu ce qui se jouait cette nuit-là. Il y avait un pillage en cours. Même ramasser les vêtements par terre, c'est du vol. Elles n'ont pas d'intégration de la loi.

 

»




La proc' demande 10 mois avec mandat de dépôt, dont 6 mois assortis d'un 

TIG

 + interdiction de Vaulx-en-Velin pour 5 ans. Pour la conductrice 9 mois d'emprisonnement + la révocation d'un sursis de 3 mois, le tout avec mandat de dépôt + interdiction de Vaulx-en-Velin pour 5 ans et confiscation de la voiture + interdiction de repasser le permis pour 5 ans.


[Les deux jeunes femmes ont les yeux rougis.]




Avocat : «

 

J'entends qu'on parle d'une nuit de chaos. À chaque fois, c'est un dossier, une personnalité, ce ne sont pas des éléments de contexte qui doivent contraindre cette décision. Quand un pillage est opéré, ce ne sont pas les 20 premiers qui sont interpellés. Ce sont les derniers, ceux qui étaient là parce que c'était noël. Par opportunisme, l'une a ramassé des affaire. Attrapé les dernières n'a pas empêché les 30 premiers de prendre des affaires. La sanction ne doit pas satisfaire le pouvoir politique. Le "refus d'obtempérer" en comparution immédiate, c'est le lot quotidien. Elle n'a pas eu de comportement particulièrement dangereux. La culpabilité a été reconnu.


Mais quand j'entends 9 mois d'enfermement avec mandat de dépôt, est-ce qu'on fait du maintien de l'ordre ici

 

? Non, c'est la justice ici. Je n'ai pas entendu que les règles de droit aient changé dernièrement. J'entends qu'il y a des attentes d'ordre de la part de la population. Prononcer cette peine, c'est complètement disproportionné, ses enfants risquent d'être placés. Elle a une charge de famille, on doit basculer sur du ferme aménageable.


L'interdiction de Vaulx-en-Velin

 

? Toute sa famille habite là-bas, le père de ses enfants. Les interdictions territoriales, c'est pour des infractions liées au territoire.

 

»




Avocate de la deuxième : «

 

Je voudrais que cette jeune femme soit sanctionnée pour ce qu'elle a commis. Vous ne devez pas cédé à la pression, par exemple de cette salle qui est pleine [en vérité, la plupart des gens sont des proches des arrêtés]. Ne rendez pas des décisions qui sont des exemples. Elle ne s'est jamais retrouvée devant la justice.

 

»




Verdict : pour l'une, 

8 mois

 avec sursis, interdiction de Vaulx-en-Velin pour 2 ans.


Pour l'autre, 

6 mois

 + 

3 mois

 de sursis révoqués, 

3 mois

 pour le refus d'obtempérer, le tout sous bracelet. Interdiction du Carré de Soie pour 

2 ans

.




Pour les dommages et intérêts pour 

JD

 Sport, la cour renvoie à plus tard.
















 







***




Un jeune homme passe pour «

 

participation à un groupement en vue de commettre des violences

 

».


Le juge : «

 

On a retrouvé sur vous une cagoule et du sérum physiologique, vous avez été arrêté dans le Monoprix de Bellecour. Vous êtes aussi accusés d'avoir exercé des violences sur Benjamin C., fonctionnaire de police, n'ayant pas entraîné d'

ITT

 de plus de 8 jours, en l'espèce en lui mettant un coup de tête. On a reçu un courrier de constitution de partie civile.

 

»


«

 

Pouvez-vous nous expliquer ce que vous veniez faire

 

? Dans quel contexte vous êtes vous retrouvés là.

 

»


Prévenu : «

 

J'ai bien tenté de voler. En sortant j'ai été interpellé par les 

CRS

. Je n'ai pas tenté de fuir. Ils m'ont fait mal, je me suis débattu. Ils ont considéré ça comme de la violence. En aucun cas je n'en avais l'intention.

 

»


J : «

 

Qu'allez-vous faire dans un monoprix en train de se faire piller

 

?

 

» (le juge précise qu'il a casier vierge). 


P : «

 

J'avais manifesté de manière pacifique.


J : «

 

Justement, on entend dire qu'il faut distinguer les manifestants des pillards. Mettez-vous à la place des 

CRS

, votre tenue, c'est une tenue pour aller manifester

 

? Pourquoi êtes-vous surpris qu'on vous interpelle

 

? Quand on est interpellé on lâche prise, sinon on risque la rébellion. Et vous pouvez blesser des policiers. Et le coup de tête au menton

 

?


J : «

 

Je n'avais pas l'intention de lui faire mal

 

». L'avocat intervient : en réalité, dans sa tentative de fuite, le policier certifie dans sa déposition qu'il a pris un coup de bras involontairement et que c'est le poids de son casque qui l'a blessé. Contrairement à certains 

PV

 du dossier, il n'y a jamais eu de coup de tête…




Bohé, L'avocat de la police prend la parole. Il se met à poursuivre l'interrogatoire du jeune homme. comme si on était encore en garde-à-vue. «

 

À quelle heure êtes-vous arrivés pour la manifestation

 

? Celui-ci habite en Suisse, pourquoi venez-vous à une manifestation à Lyon

 

? («

 

J'ai déjà habité en France, je voulais soutenir la cause

 

»)

 

? Quelles informations avez-vous eu sur le 17 octobre

 

? Êtes-vous sur des groupes telegram

 

? Il y avait de nombreux black block de toute l'Europe, que veniez-vous faire-là

 

? Pourquoi en noir

 

? Pourquoi ne pas être reconnaissable

 

? Vous alliez dormir où

 

? Avez-vous jeté des pierres plus tôt

 

?

 

»


L'avocat de la défense se lève : «

 

Cher collègue, on s'égare, on déborde du dossier, tout cela n'est pas dans la prévention. Il n'a pas d'obligation de vous répondre.

 

»




L'avocat de la partie civile (Monop') demande un renvoi sur intérêt civil pour «

 

chiffrer le préjudice

 

».




L'avocat de la police (de nouveau) : «

 

Je me lève en soutien de la défense des fonctionnaires de police. La 

CRS83

 était là pour du maintient de l'ordre. Première chose : il y avait ce 17 octobre un mouvement social qui devait se dérouler à Lyon et à d'autres endroits. La police avait été déployé pour permettre son bon déroulement. Certains groupes sont venus uniquement pour affronter la police. Je rappelle que 100 policiers ont été blessé au cours de cette journée à Lyon.


La manifestation s'est déroulée sans trop de difficulté [ça c'est le plus gros mensonge de la journée, il n'y a jamais eu à Lyon de manifestation «

 

bon enfant

 

» «

 

revendicative

 

» avec à la marge du pillage. Il y a eu des cortèges sauvages toute la matinée puis une foule qui s'est massée à Bellecour et autour en fin de matinée/début d'aprem, puis sa dispersion par gaz, puis une marée humaine qui a grossi en différents endroits de la presqu'île, des affrontements avec les flics, de l'expropriation de marchandises toute l'après-midi, une mutinerie au 

CRA

 de St-Ex et deux bâtiments incendiés, des répliques à Vaulx-en-Velin, Vénissieux, etc.].


«

 

Les 

CRS

 sont lourdement défendus. Les projectiles lancés pouvaient les tuer s'ils n'étaient pas protéger. 1000 grenades lacrymogène ont été tiré ce jour-là, les stocks locaux étaient presque épuisés.

 

»


«

 

Sur le plan collectif, ça a été très destructif. Quand on participe individuellement à une œuvre aussi destructive, il faut se rendre compte qu'on va devoir assurer les conséquences. La plupart des prévenus ont accepté d'être interpellés. Lui non. Tous n'étaient pas habillés comme lui.

 

»


«

 

Je crains qu'il ne soit venu avec d'autres sur la ville de Lyon pour provoquer des saccages. L'essentiel des blessures aux cervicales de mon client est dû à son casque très lourd. En dépit de son arrêt de travail, ce policier m'a dit qu'il était retourné en mission aujourd'hui. Le prévenu a essayé d'échapper à ses responsabilités. Il y a une sidération par rapport à cette violence que Lyon n'avait pas connu depuis longtemps.

 

»
















 







Procureur : «

 

Il y a eu des exactions particulièrement graves. Un 

PV

 global a été demandé pour se rendre compte de l'ensemble de ce qui s'est passé. Il nous dit si je résume "j'étais seul, qu'est-ce que je pourrais faire de mal

 

?" Il ne pourra pas vous faire croire qu'il a agi de manière décorrélée du contexte de guérilla urbaine. On a tous été sidéré. On a tous suivi pas à pas ce qui se passait. J'attends que votre tribunal prenne en compte ce 

PV

 de contexte. Ce jeune homme a des capacités à s'exprimer. Il a des convictions.

 

» 


«

 

Je vais mettre ma petite cagoule et je vais rentrer dans un magasin pillé. Vous avez un citoyen qui est capable de s'en prendre physiquement à un fonctionnaire de police. L'intéressé a bien participé à un groupement formé. Je vous demande d'entrer en voie de condamnation : 6 mois avec mandat de dépôt + interdiction du Rhône pendant 5 ans.




Avocat de la défense : «

 

Le "coup de tête" se transforme au gré des 

PV

. Benjamin F. (

CRS

] dit que deux personnes étaient à l'intérieur du Monoprix. Mon client a été sorti du magasin par deux fonctionnaires de police. Ils l'ont remis à un troisième qui tenait à la main une grenade. Il a vu l'occasion de se carapater.


Après avoir été maîtrisé, le police enclenche sa caméra piéton et commence une audition sauvage alors que mon client est menotté au sol. Ce n'est pas son office. Mon client reconnaît la tentative de vol mais c'est irrecevable. C'est illégal. Dans sa fuite, son bras a heurté le menton du policier, le poids de son casque a accentué sa "blessure"

 

».


«

 

Le sérum physiologique qu'on a retrouvé sur lui pour caractériser le "groupement"

 

? Tout le monde en a, les manifestants comme les policiers.

 

»


«

 

Le certificat médical du policier

 

? Pour des femmes battues que j'ai défendu avec des bleus sur tout le corps, je n'ai obtenu que 2 jours d'

ITT1

. Il a des acouphènes

 

? Ça n'a rien d'objectif, c'est lui qui le dit. 8 jours pour des «

 

contractures aux cervicales

 

»

 

? On se moque du monde

 

? Je tombe des nues.

 

»


«

 

La comparution immédiate n'était à mon sens pas nécessaire, ça vallait une 

CRPC2

. On est là juste parce qu'il est étranger. Ce qu'il a fait appelle à une simple peine d'avertissement.

 

»


«

 

Porter une cagoule et avoir tenté de voler des chips ne constitue pas un groupement pour commettre des violences.

 

»




L'avocat de la police reprend la parole. Il avait oublié de demander les dommages et intérêt pour son client : 3000 euros.




Verdict : relaxe pour le «

 

groupement de vue de...

 

», 

12 mois

 de sursis + interdiction du Rhône pendant 

3 ans

 + 

500 euros

 pour le policier-blessé-qui-va-travailler-le-lendemain pour ses «

 

souffrances endurées

 

» [sic]. 


Enfin, il est renvoyé sur «

 

intérêt civil

 

» pour indemniser «

 

l'agent judiciaire de l'État

 

»...
















 







***




M. est arrêté avec un sac contenant 6 porte-feuilles, un pantalon, 2 paires de lunettes, un sac en cuir, un en tissu (le tout Louis Vitton). Il serait rentré par effraction par une vitrine cassée. Il est en «

 

récidive

 

».




Juge : «

 

Vous avez été interpellé à 23h40 en marge des pillages. Vous êtes interpellé avec deux personnes (un mineur et un dont l'état s'avérera incompatible avec la poursuite de la garde-à-vue). Il n'y a pas d'inventaire des marchandises. Simplement des photos.Que nous dites-vous aujourd'hui

 

?

 

»


Prévenu : «

 

Je ne suis pas rentré dans le magasin, y'avait trop de trucs par terre. Je ne suis pas rentré, je n'ai rien cassé.

 

»


J : «

 

Pourquoi vous ramassez alors

 

? Qu'est-ce que vous faisiez ici ce soir-là

 

?

 

»


P : «

 

Non je passai par là.

 

»


J : «

 

Que vouliez faire avec ces objets

 

? [narquois] Les payer

 

?


P : «

 

… Je ne sais pas, c'était juste devant le magasin. Y'avait trop de trucs par terre. Je m'excuse.

 

»




Proc : «

 

[narquoise] Est-il si naturel pour vous de voler que vous ne vous en rendez même plus compte

 

? … 


P : «

 

Tout le monde le faisait, c'était par terre.

 

»


P : «

 

C'était à quelle heure

 

? Le magasin était ouvert

 

? [se foutant de sa gueule] Ah non

 

! 


[bis repetita] Vous saviez que les gens qui étaient autour de vous n'étaient pas les services de la ville quand même

 

!




Juge : «

 

Vous avez déjà un sursis pour vol en réunion. Vous êtes Algérien, arrivé en 2020, vous vivez chez votre tante, vous êtes célibataire sans enfant. Vous avez une 

OQTF

 depuis le 10 mai 2026.

 

»




Proc : «

 

Le tribunal appréciera les agissements de l'intéressé. Je ne veux pas être redondante mais vous apprécierez aussi le 

PV

 de contexte qui constate une situation catastrophique de la presqu'île lyonnaise.

 

»


«

 

Il vient vous soutenir qu'il n'avait pas conscience qu'il volait. Le tribunal appréciera. Le tribunal pour enfants l'a déjà condamné à 3 mois avec sursis, on peut se poser la question de savoir s'il n'abuse pas le tribunal. Je ne vais pas alourdir votre audience, il y a encore beaucoup d'individus qui ont commis des exactions.

 

»


«

 

Le centre-ville était une vaste zone de guerre. Pour la vol aggravé, vous le condamnerez, le tribunal le rappellera à ses responsabilités. Je demande 6 mois ferme + les 3 mois de sursis, le tout assorti d'un mandat de dépôt + interdiction du territoire de 5 ans.

 

»


«

 

Il a un gros défaut d'intégration de la loi chez nous. L'autorité administrative le lui a fait comprendre. Mais il faut qu'il comprenne qu'il n'a rien à faire sur notre territoire. Derrière moi se tiennent les citoyens qui veulent qu'on puisse vivre de manière apaisée.

 

»




La défense : «

 

C'est un vol d'opportunité, il était en "tenue bourgeoise" [vocabulaire policier]. Il n'avait pas le sac [il l'a ramassé sur place], pas un élément de préparation.

 

»


«

 

On a pas le temps de faire un inventaire précis des biens volés... Je m'interroge. Tout le monde sait que ce sont des biens de grande valeur. Comme tout le monde j'ai vu les vidéos suspectes de policiers qui semblaient subtiliser des marchandises… Je n'accuse personne. Mais je m'interroge. Attention quand même.

 

»


L'avocat rappelle qu'il y a eu une mutinerie au 

CRA

 de St-Ex le 17 octobre et que certains policiers ont été envoyé en urgence sur place «

 

Si vous voulez lui faire quitter la France, ce n'est pas nécessaire de le mettre en prison.

 

»




Verdict : condamné à 

6 mois

 avec mandat de dépôt + interdiction du territoire français pour 

2 ans

.
















 







***




Nouvel accusé dans le box. Il lui est reproché d'avoir exercé des violences sur des fonctionnaires de police avec une «

 

barre

 

». «

 

Voulez-vous être jugé aujourd'hui ou préférez-vous un délai

 

?

 

» L'homme ne comprend pas complètement ce qu'on lui dit. 


«

 

Monsieur vous n'avez pas demandé d'interprète en garde-à-vue. Il est indiqué que vous ne pouvez ni lire ni écrire le français. Vous le comprenez ou pas

 

? [Silence] Vous voulez un renvoi pour avoir un interprète

 

? [moment de flottement] Vous vivez en France depuis 2017, vous arrivez à échanger avec les gens

 

?

 

» [réponse peu audible] Le tribunal décide alors de renvoyer l'affaire.




Juge : «

 

Vous avez un casier vierge, célibataire sans enfant, avec un titre de séjour jusqu'en 2027. Vous êtes intérimaire dans le 

BTP

, vous gagnez 1700 euros/mois. Vous faites aussi un peu de "Uber"

 

».




Procureur : «

 

En fonction des éléments pénals, il y a des risques de fuite hors de France et qu'il ne se représente pas. Je demande le placement en détention.

 

»
















 







Avocat : «

 

Ces réquisitions, je ne m'y attendais pas, elles ne sont pas raisonnables. Il est "réfugié", il n'y a pas de risque de retour dans le pays qu'il a quitté. Qu'est-ce qu'il faisait dans le quartier

 

? Il y habite. Il n'a pas de casier. Il doit comprendre ce qu'on lui reproche. Avec un interprète, nous serons plus à l'aise pour communiquer avec lui.

 

»




Verdict : il est placé sous contrôle judiciaire jusqu'au 10 décembre, date de l'audience avec interdiction de manifestation dans le Rhône.




***




Nouvel inculpé, renvoyé devant le tribunal pour recel, refus d'obtempérer (il aurait fait mine de s'arrêter, puis redémarrer brusquement sur 20mètres avant d'être bloqué par la circulation, selon les policiers). Il aurait percuté la jambe d'un policier, la voiture serait donc une «

 

arme par destination

 

».




Il demande un délai pour préparer sa défense.




Proc : Elle requiert le placement en détention. «

 

Je crois que sans aller à l'examen du fond de cette affaire, les faits sont suffisamment graves. Il se voit reproché encore une fois des faits de pillages dans un 

JD

 Sport. Un fonctionnaire a été blessé

 

».


«

 

Le tribunal doit avoir à l'esprit que les faits sont graves. Je pose la question de la garantie qu'on a qu'il se représente devant votre tribunal ou qu'il re-commette les mêmes faits.

 

»


«

 

Les promesses d'embauche apparaissent toujours de manière magique alors que les gens déclarent n'avoir ni revenus ni ressources en 

GAV

 [désapprobation dans la salle].

 

»




La défense : les faits sont graves

 

? On en a même pas parlé encore

 

! Ce soir il ne participait pas aux pillages. Il passe devant les policiers, il décide de les filmer, ceux-ci le braquent. La gravité des blessures des policiers

 

? Un seul agent sans 

ITT

, pas de certificat médical, rien.

 

»


«

 

Il s'est exprimé sans avocat en 

GAV

, durant laquelle il a amendé sa version à la fin sous pression des policiers. Là, il n'est pas en étant de s'exprimer. Tous les éléments hormis le contexte permettent de ne pas le placer en détention. Dans ce tribunal, on ne fait pas de politique général, on fait du particulier.

 

»




Verdict : affaire renvoyé le 8 décembre avec jusque là interdiction de conduire un véhicule, interdiction de Vaulx.




***




Nouveau prévenu qui prend place dans le box.




Juge : «

 

Il vous est reproché d'avoir dérobé des bouteilles d'alcool (Monoprix) et un téléphone (Orange), une sacoche Nike, des bijoux, une enceinte provenant d'un vol et dissimulé tout ou partie de votre visage sans motif légitime.

 

»


«

 

Vous êtes interpellé sur la presqu'île avec un sac 

JD

 Sport. Le butin est estimé à 850 euros. On a visionné de courtes vidéos sur votre téléphone : notamment l'incendie de l'office du tourisme, puis la caméra qui se retourne et qui vous filme cagoulé. Des messages ont été trouvé dans des conversations : «

 

c'est la guerre

 

», «

 

on a tout niqué

 

», «

 

je viens de péter la caisse on a tout défoncé

 

», etc.




Prévenu : «

 

Je suis bien allé à la manif mais je n'ai pas...

 

»


Juge [le coupe] : «

 

Alors je veux bien qu'on fasse la différence entre aller manifester et aller piller. 


P : «

 

Je ne suis pas rentré dans le magasin, le téléphone on me l'a donné devant.

 

»


J : «

 

Vous aviez conscience que les vêtements étaient neufs

 

?


P : «

 

Oui.

 

» 


J : «

 

Y'a eu une distribution de téléphones devant Orange

 

?


P : «

 

Oui.

 

»


J : «

 

Vous n'êtes rentrés dans aucun magasin pillé

 

?

 

»


P : «

 

Non. Sauf peut-être Monoprix. "On a pété la caisse", c'était un "on" euphorique.


J : Vous n'étiez pas sidéré

 

? Qu'est-ce qui peut vous rendre euphorique dans un tel contexte

 

? Vous étiez accompagné

 

? Vous vous êtes donnés rendez-vous devant des magasins semble-t-il [exploitation du tel]

 

? Vous aviez une cagoule, une casquette

 

?


P : «

 

Oui je ne savais pas que c'était interdit d'être masqué, c'était plus pour les gaz.

 

»


J : «

 

Vous savez que vous risquez 7 ans de prison

 

?

 

»


P : …


J : «

 

Vous allez manifester sans savoir pourquoi.

 

»


P : «

 

Si pour la hausse des salaires.

 

»


J : «

 

Vous croyez que ça sert votre cause de faire ça

 

? Vous aviez un sac

 

?

 

»


P : «

 

Non je n'en avais pas, je l'ai trouvé sur place.

 

»




Proc : «

 

Vous dites vouloir participer à la manifestation

 

? Mais vos conversations toutes entières [sur le tel] ne parle pas de manifestation. «

 

Le 17/10, on va remplir des sac 

JD

 

» je vois.


Vous assumez que vous n'êtes pas allé manifester mais pour piller

 

?


Elle lit les derniers messages recus : «

 

vous êtes fous, vous aller tous finir à la rate, au heps.

 

» puis «

 

Ramène des pâtes

 

».
















 







Il est en alternance depuis 8 mois.


Proc : «

 

Vous n'avez pas pensé à votre patron

 

? Il va penser quoi de vous

 

? Il peut ne pas y avoir de rupture de confiance. Il s'est fait interpellé dans une configuration qui interroge beaucoup sur sa capacité à se tenir en société. Il est en marge de la société, de la manif, il vient faire son petit commerce. Il n'est pas là pour des destructions de biens mais on peut s'interroger sur ce qu'il a fait avant son interpellation. On a quelqu'un qui était sur la presqu'île pendant 4h, qui était hyper-actif.


Le mouvement lycéen est bien malheureusement invisibilisé par toutes ces actions.


Ces faits signent une personnalité. Il est coupable de faits inadmissibles dans un contexte de guérilla. Tout le monde n'a pas fini dans un magasin à faire n'importe quoi.

 

»


«

 

Je vais requérir pour le recel, le vol aggravé et la dissimulation du visage. 12 mois, dont 6 avec sursis avec du 

TIG

, un mandat de dépôt et une interdiction du 2

e

 arrondissement.




Avocat : «

 

Les vols sont très opportunistes. Il n'est pas rentré dans le 

JD

 Sport, il a trouvé des affaires devant. Est-ce que c'est un vol

 

? Je vous pose la question. Ça devient tellement facile, la barrière morale cède rapidement. C'est dans la rue, à la portée de n'importe quel passant, alors on ramasse.

 

»


«

 

Qu'a-t-on

 

? On a un jeune homme pris dans un effet de groupe. S'il avait été déterminé et prévoyant, il n'aurait pas laissé libre accès à son téléphone avec toutes les informations. La peine demandée est très sévère. Cette peine mettrait un terme à ce qu'il est en train de construire. C'est un âge où les choses ne sont pas encore très claires. Les réquisitions ne sont pas en phase avec les éléments du dossier.

 

»




Verdict : 

12 mois de sursis

 (il part en prison pendant 

5 jours

 jusqu'à ce que le 

JAP

 aménage sa peine) + interdiction de manifestation pendant 

2 ans

.




***




«

 

Il vous est reproché d'avoir frauduleusement soustrait une paire de baskets en pénétrant par effraction dans une enseigne et ceci en "récidive légale"

 

».


«

 

Lors de votre interpellation, vous êtes porteur d'une cagoule et de masques chirurgicaux. Vous n'avez pas reconnu les faits de dégradation. Vous déclarez être rentré dans le magasin sur recommandation d'une personne qui vous aurait dit qu'il y avait "moyen de se faire de l'argent"

 

».




Prévenu : «

 

L'alcool m'est monté à la tête, je suis allé dans le magasin, je me suis fait prendre par la police.

 

»


Juge : «

 

Vous étiez venu sur Lyon pourquoi

 

?

 

»


P : «

 

À la base, j'étais venu signer au commissariat avec un collègue, je descends chaque semaine.


On est passé à coté du 

JD

, on a vu que tout le monde se servait.

 

»


J : «

 

Vous saviez que ça allait se passer comme ça [à Lyon. Il vient de Dijon] et vous venez quand même

 

? Pourquoi vous venez cagoulé

 

?

 

»


P : «

 

Parce que les gens autour son cagoulés.

 

»


J : «

 

On vous voit en photo avec d'autres gens cagoulés sur l'exploitation de votre téléphone

 

» (qui n'a pas été réalisé entièrement, faute de temps).




Proc : «

 

Celui-ci comparait pour ces faits qu'il a l'air de reconnaître, avec un contexte d'opportunité. Il était avec des individus qui étaient très intéressés par l'ambiance («

 

ça nique le rolex

 

»). Il n'était pas venu manifesté contre la vie chère mais il était là pour du vol. Il a été découvert sur lui tout l'attirail pour piller.

 

»


«

 

Pas de chance pour lui, beaucoup de gens ont commis des vols et des délits mais n'ont pas été attrapés, la police étant débordé.

 

»


Elle requiert : 3 mois + 6 mois de sursis révoqués, le tout avec mandat de dépôt + confiscation du téléphone + interdiction du Rhône pendant 2 ans.




Avocate : le pillage est déclarée commencer à 17h22. Il est interpellé à 20h. Il n'est plus alors avec les casseurs. Arrivait-il sur Lyon dans l'intention de manifester, de se livrer à des déprédations

 

? La question se pose. Si ça avait été le cas, il aurait été équipé autrement.


Il m'a demandé s'il pouvait faire sa peine de détention chez lui.


On veut lui prêter des intentions qu'on veut. Mais il n'a rien cassé, il a été interpellé avec une paire de chaussures seulement sur lui.




Prévenu : «

 

J'ai vu la manif. Je n'ai aucune haine de la police. Je n'ai rien fait, à part voler cette paire de chaussures. C'est la seule chose que j'ai faite.

 

»




Verdict : 

4 mois

 + 

6 mois

 révoqués avec mandat de dépôt. Interdiction du Rhône pour 

2 ans

 + confiscation du tel.

title: Sermin Demirdağ’s release delayed for the eighth time
content:
The release of Sermin Demirdağ, who is being held at Kayseri Women’s Closed Prison, has been postponed for six months for the eighth time by the Prison Administration and Observation Board.




Sermin Demirdağ, who has been imprisoned since 13 April 1993, had previously had her release postponed seven times through board decisions at Sincan Women’s Closed Prison, where she was formerly held.




With this latest decision, the total time added to Sermin Demirdağ’s imprisonment has reached four years and three months, as her release has been blocked since 7 March 2023.

author: Unknown
title: Kalkan: The legal and political groundwork for Öcalan’s physical freedom must now be established
content:
Duran Kalkan, a member of the Abdullah Öcalan Academy of Social Sciences, gave an interview to Medya Haber TV, sharing his assessment on the recent developments.




This is an excerpt of the interview. 




You have assessed the past two years of the process. There is also the situation in the prisons. While the release of prisoners under a framework law is being discussed, we see that even those who have served their sentences are not being released. There is complete arbitrariness here. This seems to have sparked serious debate and anger within society…




What I have said applies here as well. Turkey's laws are, in fact, subject to oversight by the European Court of Human Rights (ECHR). Its rulings must be implemented. Yet none of them are being implemented. Under the current Justice and Development Party (AKP) government, Turkey is enforcing neither its own constitution nor its criminal laws. They have now set up some sort of committee, whose members are not even legal professionals. They have brought together prison guards and people from here and there, and these committees decide whether prisoners are released. It is not the law that decides. It is not the courts that decide.




It is not legislation that determines their release. Instead, decisions are made by groups of people whose authority and qualifications are entirely unclear. All these groups are political. They operate under the control of those in power. Consequently, everyone being held in these prisons is effectively a political hostage. They are being held as political hostages. I also want to make a criticism here. So many people have been released after spending 30, 35 or 33 years in prison. They could and should have done much more to expose this situation. Why are they not pursuing this issue more forcefully? Why are they not exposing what is happening? This must be exposed throughout the world. A regime that does not implement its own laws or constitution expects us to do whatever it wants, almost to the point of surrendering to it.




Does that make any sense? Are they the only intelligent ones, and are the rest of us fools? Nobody can treat us that way. Nor should they. The situation in the prisons is particularly striking. There are people who have spent 35 or 36 years behind bars, and nobody knows how much longer they will remain there. A year passes, and their release is postponed for another year. Then it is postponed again. There is no law, no court, nothing. They simply do as they please, as though they have absolute power over people's lives. There have been some protests against this, but they are insufficient. There should be far more. There should be an enormous outcry. Across the world, all kinds of protests are organised against governments that do not even commit a tenth of what is happening here. The response has been too weak. Even those directly subjected to this treatment have not reacted strongly enough. Many of these prisoners are also seriously ill. They have endured every kind of hardship. Many are on their deathbeds. Yet even this has not prompted an adequate response.




They tell us that these releases constitute a step forward. People have finally been released after serving years beyond their original sentences, and they present this as a step towards advancing the process. They even say, “We could have refused to release them if we had wanted to.” Our interlocutors openly say this to us. And we are sharing it with the public. That is the situation. Everyone should see and understand how the people held in these prisons are being treated as hostages. I want to say just one more thing, and I want to make this absolutely clear: if anyone dies in prison under these circumstances, we will regard them as a martyr of war. Our interlocutors should understand this very well. As a movement, we are absolutely determined on this matter. We will regard them as martyrs of war. We will say that the ceasefire was never implemented, that the war was never brought to an end, that the war continued inside the prisons and that this was the consequence. Everyone should know this.




We began our interview by discussing the unfolding Third World War. More recently, the war between Yemen and Saudi Arabia has come to the fore. Discussions suggest that Turkey has also become involved through the Mecca Alliance. There is also talk of growing Sunni-Shia polarisation. To what extent do you agree with these assessments? What is the current situation?




We have been following these developments, waiting for the situation to become a little clearer. But the issue has always been on our agenda. You may remember the questions being raised: What decisions were taken at the NATO meeting held in Ankara in July? Beyond the decisions made public, what other decisions might have been taken behind closed doors? What responsibilities were assigned to Turkey? Many circles were asking these questions. We were asking them too.




These matters were being discussed and investigated. In fact, they deliberately allowed some time to pass to make it harder to follow developments. Then, seemingly out of nowhere, the Mecca Agreement appeared on the agenda, as though it were something entirely new.




Now there is also talk of Turkey sending troops to Saudi Arabia. They are calling the Mecca Alliance a Middle Eastern NATO. This idea had already been raised in previous years, when US administrations held meetings in Israel and Saudi Arabia. At the time, there were discussions about whether a Middle Eastern NATO or an Arab NATO would be established.




Some are now saying that this is precisely what is happening. However, we need to understand that the Mecca Alliance emerged from a decision taken at the NATO meeting held in Ankara in July. This has now become clear. What are they doing with Turkey through the Mecca Alliance? US President Donald Trump had issued a call, saying, “We call on the states of the Middle East, particularly Turkey, to join the Abraham Accords.” The Mecca Alliance agreement is an arrangement through which its participants become part of the Abraham Accords. This is how we should understand it. Turkey is effectively joining the Abraham Accords in this way. It has reached an agreement with the United States. Through this agreement, it is also reaching an agreement with Israel. This is an agreement involving Israel. Now they are sending troops to Saudi Arabia. They will become involved in the war in Yemen. They will fight against pro-Iranian forces in Yemen. Turkey is indirectly entering a war against Iran. This is the position into which it is being drawn. It is both becoming part of the Abraham Accords and, within that framework, becoming involved in the war against Iran.




The US President made another statement just the other day. He said that Erdoğan was fulfilling all his demands concerning Yemen. I do not understand why Turkish society is discussing this so little. The collapse of the Ottoman Empire began in Yemen. So many songs and laments were composed about Yemen. Now the AKP government is preparing to send Turkish soldiers to Yemen once again. Will they go or not? This must be opposed. Can something like this simply be accepted without objection? There is also hostility towards Iran. In one respect, Turkey is approaching the point of going to war with Iran.




Yet we know that, on the other hand, Turkey has reached far-reaching agreements with Iran against the Kurds. We need to follow Hakan Fidan's policies very carefully. He is rather like a tightrope walker. In Saudi Arabia, Yemen and the Gulf, Turkey is fighting against Iran alongside Israel and the United States. But when it comes to the Zagros Mountains, it fights alongside Iran against the Kurds. We do not know exactly what the Iranians have made of this.




Of course, the state has been severely weakened. It is in a very fragile position. It appears unable to demonstrate much political will. But attacking the Kurds cannot be the way to overcome all these weaknesses and contradictions. Everyone needs to understand that. This is where things now stand. We must recognise the situation clearly. It also represents a serious threat. Political forces must be able to intervene, both in Turkey and in Iran. Opposition forces must intervene. Societies must intervene. The Kurds, too, must remain vigilant. The situation is serious. There are threats, serious threats. There are dangers. Some parties and organisations have issued statements drawing attention to these developments. We attach importance to those statements. There really are dangers. There is a genuine threat. We have spoken about democratic unity.




Kurdish democratic unity is of immense importance as the only way to confront all these threats and dangers. It is therefore not enough simply to issue statements warning of the threats. We must develop democracy and build unity to generate the strength needed to overcome them. This is both necessary and essential.




Ecocide and attacks on the environment have become increasingly prominent issues. Most recently, disturbing images emerged from Istanbul. Are these issues being discussed? Are the discussions taking place on the right basis? What kind of mentality and approach do you think lie behind what we are witnessing?




I have not been able to follow the developments closely enough to understand exactly how what they call a disaster unfolded. But I later saw the images and watched the footage. They immediately call it a natural disaster. But is it really natural? They use words like disaster and catastrophe to conceal what is actually happening. They said the same thing when the earthquake struck the Mediterranean region. The AKP government described it in exactly those terms. Many people blame nature and various other factors. But this is not something unique to Turkey. It is happening across the world. If you interfere with the balance of nature to such an extent, nature will inevitably hold you to account. And that is precisely what is happening. Kurdish People's Leader Abdullah Öcalan said that nature would take its revenge. He spoke about nature as a living entity and warned that it could take revenge.




Previous governments in Turkey had already gone too far in this regard. But the AKP government has reached a point where it recognises neither moral nor legal limits. Nature is being destroyed on an enormous scale wherever there is money or profit to be made. This began in the Black Sea region. The people of the Black Sea resisted. Women and local communities protested. We genuinely attached great importance to their resistance. The destruction then spread to the Aegean and other regions, while in Kurdistan it has been pursued without restraint. Across many areas, from Diyarbakır (Amed) to Muş and Varto, awareness has begun to develop, albeit very late. Committees and organisations have emerged. Society is defending its home and the foundations of its existence against the destruction of nature. Nature is the environment in which we live. Without it, humanity cannot exist. 




Developing an awareness of nature is the starting point for human beings and society to understand themselves. The relationship between nature, society and humanity forms an inseparable whole. Öcalan said that an entire mountain was being destroyed for a handful of gold. And that is exactly what is happening. Forests and trees have been devastated. The destruction continues particularly in Kurdistan, from Botan to Dersim. It is taking place openly, before everyone's eyes. They are also involving Kurds in this destruction through village guards and others. The response was insufficient when it was needed most. There is therefore no question of a natural disaster or an unavoidable catastrophe. What we are witnessing are disasters brought about by the misguided policies of those in power. That is how we must understand them. The capitalist modernity system, driven by its insatiable pursuit of profit and its destructive attacks on nature, has disrupted every natural balance. It has disturbed the balance above the ground, beneath the ground and in the atmosphere. It has disrupted the climate itself.




Look at the kind of rainfall we are experiencing. The climatic balance has been completely destroyed. Rainfall now causes devastation comparable to that of earthquakes. This is happening in many parts of the world.




What happened in Istanbul is another example. It was not inevitable. It was not fate, nor was it simply a natural consequence of nature's processes. It was the result of human destruction of the environment, the pursuit of money and profit, and the capitalist modernity system. There is also the question of construction and urban development. How have these cities been built? How were these houses constructed? There has been no proper planning, and such dangers were never taken into account. Houses and other buildings have been constructed directly in riverbeds and along stream banks. They claim there is urban planning and that safety measures are in place. Municipalities are supposedly working, along with all the other relevant institutions. Everyone claims to be doing their job. But the earthquake in Çukurova showed us that none of these safeguards actually existed. We saw the consequences of the AKP government's policies.




The flooding in Istanbul was a second manifestation of the same failure. Everyone in Istanbul had been living with the fear of an earthquake. There was no earthquake, but the flood caused devastation on an even greater scale. Its impact was like that of an earthquake. It swept through and destroyed everything in its path. We must now understand the causes of this destruction and struggle to eliminate them. Expressions of sorrow and regret are not enough. Those responsible must be identified and held accountable. Ecological awareness, ecological struggle and ecological organisation are indispensable. They are essential for life and for the liberation of life itself. An attack on nature must therefore be understood as an attack on society.




There is an old saying: “Those who cut down living trees are no different from those who take human lives.” Look at what is happening in Botan. We are following it closely. Now, apparently, they are doing the same thing in South Kurdistan, throughout Behdinan. In fact, they have been doing this since 1985. We know that the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) reached an agreement back then. There is no need to go into all those details here. How many lives have been taken? Every tree cut down should be regarded as the killing of a human being. If society understands this, it will also come to understand itself. A genuine social consciousness will emerge. Free and democratic life can only be built on the basis of such awareness. It is indispensable.




Left-wing and socialist forces, along with democratic circles, must take this issue much more seriously. Greater importance must be attached to developing ecological awareness, organisation and struggle.




The plunder and destruction of nature are, in fact, grounds for rebellion. They provide every justification for developing all forms of democratic action and mass mobilisation. Indeed, they offer the most legitimate grounds imaginable. Nobody can reasonably ask why people have risen up against such destruction. What greater justification could there be? The damage being inflicted is immense. It threatens life, humanity and the future of humankind. The future itself is being darkened. Those who have suffered losses should receive compensation. But what matters most is learning from what has happened. I call on everyone to act on the principle that experience is the best teacher, to draw lessons from these events and to develop the organisation and struggle necessary to ensure that such disasters never happen again. There is no other way.
