author: Darío Aranda
title: Elecciones en Brasil: deforestación, frontera agrícola y ultraderecha
content:
Por Raúl Zibechi




“La frontera agrícola avanza expropiando, y la expropiación necesita de apoyo político”, escribe el abogado en derechos humanos Diogo Cabral en un trabajo que cruza datos para intentar comprender dónde y cómo se produce el avance de la ultraderecha bolsonarista, concentrado en la selva amazónica. Las conclusiones de su trabajo son tremendas y pueden ser resumidas en el editorial de Eliane Brum, directora del sitio periodístico Sumaúma: si Flávio Bolsonaro vence en la segunda vuelta, describe Brum, “existe una gran posibilidad de que la selva deje de existir como tal, lo que implica que dejará de actuar como reguladora del clima y sumidero de carbono, uno de los gases responsables del calentamiento global”.




El bolsonarismo gobernará siete de los nueve estados de la Amazonia, en tanto más de la mitad de los parlamentarios electos ya han votado en contra de la selva y de los pueblos originarios, según 

la investigación de Sumaúma

.




Esta realidad impone colocar la lupa sobre lo que sucede en la Amazonia Legal brasileña, (Mato Grosso, Pará, Rondônia, Tocantins, Maranhão, Acre, Amapá, Amazonas y Roraima), que ocupa el 60 por ciento del total de la selva amazónica. En las últimas cuatro décadas la territorialidad del conflicto por la tierra se ha movido desde el sureste, donde nació el 

Movimiento de Trabajadores Rurales Sin Tierra (MST)

, migró primero hacia el norte y nordeste, y ahora hacia la Amazonia, siguiendo los pasos de la expansión del agronegocio.




La expansión ha sido geométrica: 

en 1990 había

 

once

 

millones de hectáreas cultivadas de soja, llegando a casi 50 millones en la actualidad

; la producción del grano creció 738 por ciento en los últimos 40 años, en tanto el área sembrada se expandió en un 

322

 

por ciento

 

en el mismo período

. Hacia finales de la década de 1970, más del 80 por ciento de la soja provenía de los estados del sur; en la década siguiente comenzó a extenderse por la región central (Mato Grosso, Goiás y el distrito de Brasilia). Esta región que hace 40 años representaba el dos por ciento de la producción nacional de soja, ahora alcanza el 40 por ciento.




Este cambio notable puede observarse en el mapa 

(ver mapa)

, donde se combinan cuatro variables analíticas: la deforestación, los conflictos agrarios de 2025 registrados por la 

Comisión Pastoral de la Tierra (CPT)

, el monitoreo de la pulverización con agrotóxicos de la Red de Agroecología de Maranhão y los resultados electorales de la primera vuelta.




En color azul los lugares donde ganó Bolsonario. En rojo donde triunfó Lula




A medida que la frontera agrícola se expande, el mapa se va coloreando de azul. 

José de Souza Martino, citado por Cabral

, entiende la frontera agrícola no sólo como la línea de avance de la producción agropecuaria sobre la vegetación nativa, sino como “espacio social de conflictos”. Se trata de una expansión autoritaria, “acumulación por despojo” como la definiera David Harvey, que busca convertir la tierra en mercancía para lo que debe no sólo apropiársela sino expulsar a las comunidades indígenas, quilombolas (negras) y pueblos tradicionales.




Datos crudos e impunidad




Los datos indican que entre 2019 y 2025 Brasil perdió once millones de hectáreas de vegetación nativa, siendo la actividad agropecuaria la responsable del 97 por ciento de esa deforestación. En paralelo, se registra un promedio de 1.500 conflictos en el campo; con 26 asesinatos en 2025, el doble que en el año anterior, y los hacendados fueron responsables de 14 de las 16 muertes en la Amazonia Legal. En los 34 años en los cuales la CPT viene sistematizando datos de conflictos rurales, hubo casi 

2.000

 

asesinatos, pero sólo 120 habían sido juzgados hasta 2018

, según la CPT.




Flávio Bolsonaro tuvo sus mayores votaciones justamente en los estados donde la deforestación fue más intensa: 71 por ciento en Roraima, 67 por ciento en Rondonia, 65 por ciento en Mato Grosso y en Acre. “Ganó en ocho de los diez municipios de la Amazonia Legal que más deforestaron desde 2016”, asegura Cabral, cruzando datos electorales y del Instituto Nacional de Investigaciones Espaciales, que monitorea las áreas deforestadas.




Foto: Pedro Saldanha Werneck - Mídia NINJA




La ciudad de Novo Progresso, en Pará, que en 2019 fue el epicentro del “Día del Fuego” (10 de agosto, cuando los productores rurales iniciaron la quema masiva de áreas de la selva, para “limpiar” y permitir el avance del agronegocio), Bolsonaro obtuvo el 85 por ciento, superando holgadamente la votación de su padre en 2022. Lula ganó, no por casualidad, en municipios donde existen reservas naturales, asentamientos de recolectores y poblaciones ribereñas. Por el contrario, donde se proyecta la explotación minera aurífera de Belo Sun contra la tierra indígena Ituna/Itatá (en Pará), Lula cayó del 52 al 35 por ciento, mientras que Bolsonaro alcanzó el 61 por ciento de los votos.







En los llamados “polos del agronegocio”, en Mato Grosso, Lula perdió el 26 por ciento de sus votos en cuatro años, en tanto Bolsonaro sumó un 24 por ciento más que su padre, superando el 70 por ciento.







Aquellos estados atravesados por la frontera del agronegocio, como Bahía, Pará y Maranhão, son los más violentos del país. El MST denunció el “proyecto Mataiba”, en Maranhão, como un “crimen del agronegocio". El proyecto surgió en 2015 y abarca cuatro estados para “impulsar la expansión de la agroindustria para la producción de productos básicos de exportación”, pero en los hechos es una amenaza “a las comunidades tradicionales y las zonas de asentamiento de la reforma agraria al 

impulsar la invasión de estos territorios

, la reconcentración de tierras y el fomento de la especulación inmobiliaria y la financierización de la agricultura”. Además de la expropiación de tierras por la violencia, enfrentan el uso masivo de pesticidas, con los consiguientes daños a la salud.




La impunidad es la tónica que permite al agronegocio expandirse. Pero la impunidad supone la existencia de redes de complicidades entre empresarios, capataces de las haciendas, sicarios, policías y la justicia estatal; esa alianza que se traduce en el apoyo político a la familia Bolsonaro.




El abogado José Batista Afonso de la CPT esgrime que “la impunidad es la prueba de que el crimen compensa”. Sostiene que no es una cuestión territorial sino que existe un patrón de impunidad que se repite una y otra vez. 

Repórter Brasil

 investigó cinco crímenes (en realidad cinco ejecuciones) con siete víctimas ocurridos en 2009. Once años después sólo un caso fue cerrado, con la condena de un policía que continuó recibiendo su salario hasta que el Repórter Brasil lo denunció.




La impunidad se sostiene en una alianza tejida en base a una abrumadora desigualdad racial, étnica y social, a la que debe sumarse la criminalización judicial y mediática de los movimientos que luchan por la tierra. Es importante tomar nota de este complejo político-social que sostiene al agronegocio, porque no se expresa sólo en Brasil, y será el sentido común del extractivismo en toda la región.







La entrada 

Elecciones en Brasil: deforestación, frontera agrícola y ultraderecha

 se publicó primero en 

Agencia de Noticias Tierra Viva

.

author: Suliman Baldo
title: Why Sanctions Are Not Stifling Sudan’s War Economy and What We Can Do About It
content:
Since the outbreak of the brutal civil war in Sudan in April 2023, the US, British, and Canadian governments, along with the European Union and United Nations, have imposed targeted sanctions on some 32 individuals and 20 companies tied to the bloodshed to restrict their access to assets, international finance, and travel. Three and a half years into the fighting, more than two-thirds of Sudan’s population requires humanitarian aid and almost 14 million people have been forcibly displaced, and the need for effective policy responses has never been more urgent.




These sanctions have had some impact. For example, China, citing international sanctions, refused to authorise the sale of its air defence systems by Pakistan to Sudan in August 2025. Turkey refused a deal to sell drones to the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) because the group was unable to provide an end-user licence. Succumbing to pressure, the UAE has 

distanced itself

 from some shell companies previously operating as covers for the RSF from its soil.




More often, however, it has been easy for sanctioned entities to obfuscate and manoeuvre around sanctions, sometimes in the very capitals that have issued them.




Earlier this year, a business forum convened in London to mobilise capital to rebuild Sudan’s economy showed how those profiting from the conflict continue to evade sanctions. One of the event’s sponsors, the Export Development Group (EDG), presented itself as a leading player in Sudan’s future reconstruction.




A 

new report

 by the Sudan Transparency and Policy Tracker (SPTP) argues that the company is, in fact, a subsidiary of the Defense Industries Systems (DIS), the military conglomerate that operates a web of businesses that finance the Sudan Armed Forces’ (SAF) war machine, which the UK government designated in June 2023. Operating in London and on its website, it obfuscates that connection, scrubbing any reference to its affiliation to its parent company from its website, with the imputed goal of distancing itself from the sanctions. At the same time, it continues to reference it in 

social media posts

 intended for domestic audiences.




The Exports Development Group presents a different image in content for domestic audiences compared to its international profile.




Research published

 by STPT has identified the primary challenge in employing sanctions effectively. The designations issued to date have been drawn narrowly and enforced loosely, targeting specific individuals and companies, with targets adapting faster than the governments that target them.




A prime case is that of Zadna International, a DIS subsidiary sanctioned by the UK, US, and EU between June 2023 and January 2024. Despite this, the report argues that the company has become the primary beneficiary of massive contracts across areas controlled by the Sudanese Army and a conduit for war profiteering. In December 2025, the company was awarded an approximately $7 million contract to resurface a 12-mile road in Gezira state, a cost ten times higher than an estimate for the same work in a 2022 agreement, according to the STPT report.




In the same month, White Nile state reportedly named Zadna as the primary partner for all of its 2026 development projects. The company’s director described the strategy as ‘financial engineering,’ shifting its externally-sanctioned operations domestically.  Such ‘financial engineering’ involves structuring joint-venture trade partnerships in friendly countries—such as Egypt—and using commodity swaps to bypass international currency transactions, a mechanism detailed in a recent 

STPT report

 and investigated by 

The New Arab

.




Red Rock Mining Company, another DIS affiliate company sanctioned by the UK and EU, highlighted its operations in Tanzania, Ethiopia, the UAE, and the Netherlands, an EU member state, 

on LinkedIn

 in November 2025.




LinkedIn post by Red Rock Mining.




Merghani Idriss, the head of DIS, is still alleged to lead major weapons procurements for the army, despite being sanctioned by Canada, the US, and the EU, reportedly leading a delegation to Pakistan to 

sign

 a $230 million arms package, widely reported to have been 

financed by Saudi Arabia

.




The DIS, two years into the conflict, 

showcased

 its domestically manufactured drones and precision weapons at a Turkish defence fair.




Similarly, SAF’s main rival, the RSF, have employed similar tactics and adapted to sanction regimes. One of its primary vehicles, Al-Junaid company, has managed to process and export millions worth of gold via neighbouring countries and onwards to the UAE, according to 

reporting by the New York Times

.




Kenya, one of the key conduits for RSF operations, 

saw its gold exports to the UAE spike

 by almost 30 percent in the first nine months of 2025, a 13-ton increase from 2024 attributed to laundering and not domestic production.




This is not to say that sanctions do not work entirely or that they should be abandoned, but rather a call for using them more effectively. Evidence shows they have worked in isolated examples.




The difference between the cases that worked from the cases that failed is whether the corporate structure was hidden in the first place.




At the same time, the decades of sanctions imposed during the Bashir era that were fully removed by 2020, continue to have an impact. Overcompliance by banks and companies continues to impede banking and commercial transactions, making it difficult for humanitarian and human rights actors to move funds and access corporate services.




The recent exposure of the 

SAF’s use of chemical weapons

 has renewed attention to the need to address weapons supply chains. Despite an arms embargo being in place for Darfur since the start of the conflict both SAF and the RSF have managed to move weapons there that have targeted Sudanese civilians. Both are channelling the country’s natural resources towards arms purchases, including said chemical weapons.




Fixing sanctions evasion requires five elements.




First, more attention needs to be paid to subsidiaries and the joint ventures established to obfuscate sanctions. Under US law, any company more than 50 percent owned by a designated entity, such as the Export Development Group, is included in the designation. The UK adopts a similar standard. However, too little attention is paid to ensuring that there is awareness of these connections and subsidiaries, which impedes enforcement. Explicitly naming subsidiaries more quickly could address this.




Second, expand that scope of the current and future targeted sanctions to network sanctions by targeting the entire supporting ecosystem around those primary bad actors, the commanders of the warring parties and their top revenue earning companies. This would require identifying and sanctioning foreign shell companies, front organisations, procurement agents, financial facilitators, and logistics providers that enable the primary target to evade restrictions or maintain operations.




Third, the UN arms embargo on Darfur should be expanded to cover all of Sudan, 

a call made in August by the US Government

.




Fourth, sanctioning entities should directly engage third-country jurisdictions, including neighbouring countries such as Egypt, Kenya, and the UAE to ensure the logistics hubs facilitating evasion are eliminated, with clear due diligence and secondary measures as warranted.




Fifth, guidance that unwinds overcompliance by banks in areas that are not targeted by sanctions and which hinders humanitarian, legitimate businesses, and individual transfers should be issued to facilitate access to millions in need of aid.




Sanctions can work only if a concerted strategy is put in place to ensure that sanctioned entities cannot continue to operate via subsidiaries in the very capitals that issued them.




The post 

Why Sanctions Are Not Stifling Sudan’s War Economy and What We Can Do About It

 appeared first on 

African Arguments

.

author: Thiago Domenici
title: Hospitais do Rio de Janeiro, Flávio Bolsonaro e a acusação de Lula na Band
content:
“Eu queria fazer a pergunta: se ele [Flávio Bolsonaro] tem noção da destruição que ele fez nos seis hospitais federais do Rio de Janeiro, que nós agora estamos recuperando”. Essa foi a fala do presidente e candidato à reeleição Lula (PT), no último debate realizado pela TV Bandeirantes no domingo, 18 de outubro.




O presidente acusou o concorrente Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) de mandar nos hospitais federais do Rio durante o governo do pai, Jair Bolsonaro. Lula falou de UTIs fechadas, de unidades sucateadas e de um “pedágio” cobrado de funcionários para estacionar no que Flávio respondeu que Lula estava “vomitando um monte de mentiras”.




A informação usada por Lula foi revelada pela 

Agência Pública

 em 1º de outubro, na 

reportagem

 de Caio Briso, que trouxe documentos oficiais e entrevistas que indicam como o senador Flávio Bolsonaro, sem cargo no Executivo à época, exerceu forte influência sobre a rede de saúde entre 2019 e 2022, em plena pandemia de Covid-19.







O Rio é a única cidade do país com hospitais administrados pelo governo federal, herança dos tempos em que era a capital do país. São seis unidades: Bonsucesso, Andaraí, Cardoso Fontes, Ipanema, Lagoa e Servidores do Estado. Com orçamento alto e muitos contratos terceirizados, a rede virou um “feudo” de políticos fluminenses, segundo fontes consultadas sob reserva pela reportagem que traz detalhes de como Flávio Bolsonaro influenciou a saúde do Rio no governo de Jair Bolsonaro.




No debate, Flávio chegou a assumir uma mea culpa sobre o mal resultado da gestão do pai na saúde. “De fato, a saúde não foi uma área que a gente teve o melhor resultado. Eu faço aqui esse mea culpa”, 

afirmou

 o senador. Apesar disso, ele argumentou que Jair comprou as vacinas, sem informar que o presidente deu várias declarações contrárias à compra de vacinas, além de desinformar sobre o efeito delas.







Leia a fala de Lula na íntegra







“Eu queria fazer a pergunta: se ele [Flávio Bolsonaro] tem noção da destruição que ele fez nos seis hospitais federais do Rio de Janeiro, que nós agora estamos recuperando. Fizemos parceria com a iniciativa privada, com a prefeitura, para que a gente dê conta daqueles hospitais. Aquele hospital tem que ser hospital de qualidade, aquele hospital tem que ser referência.










Mas sabe o que ele fazia quando ele tomava conta desses hospitais? Ele cobrava até pedágio dos funcionários, os caras pagavam estacionamento. Então, quem está assistindo pode ir lá perguntar, pode ir lá perguntar, pode ir nos hospitais perguntar para a enfermeira, para médico. Tinha um hospital lá do Rio de Janeiro, federal, que ele tomava conta, que não tinha cozinha (…) Então é o seguinte, rapaz: pelo amor de Deus, quando a gente trata de saúde, você tem que tratar de saúde com respeito, com muito respeito (…)”

author: infolibre
title: Για τις πρόσφατες εξεγέρσεις στις ευρωπαϊκές μητροπόλεις
content:
Από τη λωρίδα της Γάζας μέχρι τους δρόμους των ευρωπαϊκών μητροπόλεων:




Αλληλεγγύη και δύναμη σε όσους και όσες αντιστέκονται, εξεγείρονται, επαναστατούν!




Στην εποχή της παγκόσμιας όξυνσης της καταπίεσης και της εκμετάλλευσης απέναντι στην εργατική τάξη και τα κατώτερα κοινωνικά στρώματα, των συνεχών πολέμων, της ανόδου του φασισμού, των γενοκτονιών και των μαζικών δολοφονιών μεταναστ(ρι)ών στα σύνορα της Ευρώπης, βλέπουμε να ξεπηδούν μια σειρά από δυναμικές κινητοποιήσεις και εξεγέρσεις σε διάφορες γωνιές της ηπείρου, με πυροδότη τη νεολαία και τους φτωχοδιαβόλους, ντόπιους και “ξένους”.




Οι λόγοι πολλοί και διάφοροι, “όλοι οι λόγοι του κόσμου” όπως συνηθίζουμε να λέμε. Η σπίθα φαίνεται να ανάβει από την ευρεία εξάπλωση της φτώχειας και των περικοπών των κυβερνήσεων σε βασικούς πυλώνες του κράτους πρόνοιας, προκειμένου να διαθέσουν όλο και μεγαλύτερα κομμάτια των κρατικών προϋπολογισμών στην πολεμική οικονομία.




Στην Αλβανία, μετά από μήνες κινητοποιήσεων ενάντια στο ξεπούλημα της δημόσιας περιουσίας της χώρας από την Κυβέρνηση Ράμα σε ξένα funds, ήταν η σειρά των φοιτητ(ρι)ών να βγουν στους δρόμους των Τιράνων ενάντια στη διαφθορά, την υποβάθμιση της παιδείας και το υψηλό κόστος ζωής.




Στο Βέλγιο παρόμοιοι λόγοι έχουν βγάλει στους δρόμους τη νεολαία της χώρας, με τα συνδικάτα των εργαζομένων να ακολουθούν με την προκήρυξη απεργιών, ενώ η ακρίβεια και οι κοινωνικές ανισότητες βρίσκονται πάντα στο προσκήνιο.




Στην Ιταλία οι διαδηλώσεις ενάντια στην κυβέρνηση της Μελόνι και τις πολιτικές φτωχοποίησης που ακολουθεί, τις περικοπές στην παιδεία, το αυξημένο κόστος ζωής, έχουν επεκταθεί σε παραπάνω από 40 πόλεις και έχουν λάβει ιδιαίτερα μαχητικά χαρακτηριστικά. Οι διαδηλώτ(ρι)ες προέρχονται κυρίως μέσα από τις μεγάλες μάζες της νεολαίας δίχως μέλλον, ανάμεσα τους ακόμη και ανήλικα παιδιά των φτωχότερων περιοχών της χώρας, που φαίνεται να μην εκφράζονται από καμία επίσημη πολιτική οργάνωση, κάτι που τρομάζει την κυβέρνηση ακόμη περισσότερο. Οι κινητοποιήσεις τους συνδυάζονται με τις απεργίες διαφόρων κλάδων σχετικά με την αύξηση των τιμών των καυσίμων, δημιουργώντας ένα εκρηκτικό κλίμα, με την εθνικιστική κυβέρνηση να απαντά με την ανάπτυξη στρατιωτικών δυνάμεων στις πόλεις.




Στην Γαλλία, με επίκεντρο το Παρίσι αλλά και άλλες μεγάλες πόλεις, όπως η Μασσαλία, η Λιμόζ και η Λυών, οι μαθητ(ρι)ες της δευτεροβάθμιας εκπαίδευσης ξεκίνησαν εκτεταμένες καταλήψεις στα σχολεία τους και βγήκαν στους δρόμους. Τα αιτήματά τους ξεκινούν από την εναντίωση στην ολοένα και αυξανόμενη υποβάθμιση της παιδείας, τη σταδιακά δυσκολότερη πρόσβαση στη δημόσια και δωρεάν πανεπιστημιακή εκπαίδευση, τις ελλείψεις υποδομών και τα σχολικά συγκροτήματα που καταρρέουν, αλλά δεν μένουν μόνο εκεί: Οι Γάλλοι/ιδες μαθητ(ρι)ες εξεγείρονται ενάντια σε ένα εκπαιδευτικό σύστημα που μοιάζει με φυλακή. Που τους/τις κρατάει κλεισμένους/ες μέσα σε τέσσερις τοίχους για 10 ολόκληρες ώρες κάθε μέρα, με ελλειπή διαλείμματα, εμποδίζοντάς τους/τες να έχουν οποιαδήποτε ποιοτική κοινωνική ζωή, να αθληθούν, να διασκεδάσουν, να ζήσουν. Μαζί τους και οι “κολασμένοι” των φτωχών προαστίων, τα κατώτερα στρώματα του προλεταριάτου με το έντονο μεταναστευτικό υπόβαθρο, άνθρωποι με καταγωγή από χώρες διαλυμένες από τη γαλλική αποικιοκρατία, καθώς και μεγάλα κομμάτια του ριζοσπαστικού κινήματος.




Τα κινήματα αυτά έχουν απέναντί τους τις κυβερνήσεις των χωρών τους και τις αστυνομίες τους, που τους επιτίθενται με βία και τους πυροβολούν με πλαστικές σφαίρες στο ψαχνό. Αλλά όχι μόνο: Αντίπαλός τους είναι η παγκόσμια αντίδραση, τα Κράτη και το Κεφάλαιο συνολικά. Οι πολιτικές ηγεσίες όλων των “ανεπτυγμένων” χωρών της “πολιτισμένης Δύσης”, συντονισμένες, δηλώνουν τη “φρίκη” τους απέναντι στις ταραχές και τις λεηλασίες. Οι ίδιοι που επέτρεψαν και ενίσχυσαν πολιτικά και υλικά τη συθέμελη ισοπέδωση ολόκληρης της Γάζας, οι συνένοχοι και συμμέτοχοι στη δολοφονία δεκάδων χιλιάδων ανθρώπων σε όλο τον πλανήτη και στη σύνθλιψη ολόκληρων χωρών κάτω από τις βόμβες τους, χύνουν κροκοδείλια δάκρυα μπροστά στην καταστροφή του ενός ή του άλλου μνημείου σε κάποια ευρωπαϊκή πόλη, αναπαράγοντας αυτούσια την ακροδεξιά, φασιστική ατζέντα που μιλάει για “ισλαμιστές”, για “βαρβάρους λαθρομετανάστες” και “ακροαριστερούς τρομοκράτες”. Οι ίδιοι που πετούν στη φτώχεια και την εξαθλίωση την παγκόσμια εργατική τάξη, φρίττουν όταν αυτοί που έχουν στερηθεί τα πάντα, απαλλοτριώνουν μέσα από τους ναούς του εμπορεύματος μικρό μέρος των αγαθών τα οποία μόνο στα όνειρά τους είχαν φανταστεί.




Ανάμεσα σε αυτούς τους πολιτικούς σαλτιμπάγκους που δηλώνουν ευθαρσώς πως δεν θα επιτρέψουν η κατάσταση αυτή να εξαπλωθεί στη δική τους χώρα, δεν θα μπορούσαν να μην βρίσκονται κορυφαία στελέχη της Ελληνικής Κυβέρνησης, όπως ο Άδωνις Γεωργιάδης, ο Κυρανάκης αλλά και εσχάτως ο ίδιος ο πρωθυπουργός. Είναι πασιφανές πως τρέμουν στο ενδεχόμενο οι καταπιεσμένοι/ές στη χώρα μας να ακολουθήσουν επιτέλους το παράδειγμα της Γαλλίας, της Αλβανίας, της Ιταλίας, του Βελγίου. Για αυτό και έχουν βάλει τα πιστά τους μαντρόσκυλα, τους πληρωμένους δημοσιογράφους, να τρομολαγνούν.




Δεν πιστεύουμε λέξη από όσα παπαγαλίζουν τα καλοταϊσμένα ΜΜΕ της αστικής τάξης.




Στεκόμαστε αδιαπραγμάτευτα δίπλα σε όσους και όσες αντιστέκονται, εξεγείρονται, επαναστατούν απέναντι στη βαρβαρότητα, την καταπίεση και την εκμετάλλευση του κρατικού-καπιταλιστικού συστήματος.




Είναι ώρα πια οι καταπιεσμένες και εκμεταλλευόμενες τάξεις και στη χώρα μας να ξεπεράσουν τις κοινοβουλευτικές και θεσμικές τους αυταπάτες. Οι ζωές μας γίνονται κάθε μέρα και χειρότερες. Ο πόλεμος μας χτυπάει την πόρτα και αυτοί που θα κληθούν να πεθάνουν για τα συμφέροντα των αφεντικών δεν είναι άλλοι από τους προλετάριους της κάθε χώρας. Η απάθεια και η αδράνεια πρέπει να σπάσουν. Οι εκλογές και οι προσευχές δεν φέρνουν κανένα αποτέλεσμα. Τίποτα δεν κερδίζεται με την παλάμη απλωμένη. Τα πάντα κερδίζονται με την γροθιά υψωμένη.




Και όπως ειπώθηκε χαρακτηριστικά από κάποιον διαδηλωτή στα Τίρανα:


“Αν είναι να ζήσουμε, ας ζήσουμε ελεύθεροι. Αν είναι να πεθάνουμε, ας πεθάνουμε όρθιοι, σαν τα δέντρα”.




Ή όπως λέει το γνωστό τραγούδι:


“Η δύναμη βγαίνει απ’ τις γροθιές κι όχι από πρόσωπα καλοσυνάτα”.

author: Mario Trujillo
title: Victory! Court Rules OPM Data Disclosure to DOGE Is Unlawful
content:
In a victory for data privacy, a federal court in New York definitively ruled that the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) violated the law when it disclosed millions of federal employee records to DOGE agents. In a summary judgment ruling issued on October 20, 2026, the court found that OPM violated two provisions of the Privacy Act—one restricting disclosure of personal records between agencies and another requiring agencies to protect the security and confidentiality of records.

Since the case was filed, many DOGE agents have left the government and OPM has rescinded their database access. However, OPM should still clean up the cybersecurity mess it created. The court will decide the remedy at a later date.

"By virtue of the Court’s summary judgment ruling, OPM’s decision to grant DOGE Agents broad access to its systems of recordings containing [personally identifiable information (PII)] has been held unlawful," Judge Denise Cote wrote.

"The record also provides no support for a finding that it was the pursuit of a modernization agenda that prompted OPM to grant sweeping and expedited access to a score of DOGE Agents to its systems of records containing PII," she added.

OPM maintains databases of highly sensitive personal information about tens of millions of federal employees, retirees, and job applicants. Starting in January 2025, OPM disclosed data to the U.S. DOGE Service, led by Elon Musk. This disclosure violates the federal Privacy Act of 1974, a watershed anti-surveillance statute that prevents the federal government from abusing our personal information.

EFF sued OPM and DOGE because this data disclosure violates the Privacy Act. We represent unions of federal employees – the American Federation of Government Employees and the Association of Administrative Law Judges – and individual employees. We seek injunctive and declaratory relief. We filed in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York.

Our co-counsel are Lex Lumina LLP, State Democracy Defenders Fund, and The Chandra Law Firm LLC.

title: Smart işçilerinden gece vardiyası eylemi: “Mutlaka kazanacağız”

author: Unknown
title: Nijerya'da ilk Ebola virüsü vakası tespit edildi
content:
Nijerya hükümeti, başkent Abuja'nın bulunduğu Federal Başkent Bölgesi'nde (FCT) ilk Ebola virüsü vakasının tespit edildiğini bildirdi.

Nijerya Sağlık ve Sosyal Refah Koordinasyon Bakanı Muhammad Pate, başkent Abuja'da düzenlenen basın toplantısında, laboratuvar testleri sonucunda ülkede Ebola virüsü vakasının doğrulandığını belirtti. Pate, Doğu Afrika'ya, özellikle Uganda'ya seyahat geçmişi bulunan kadın hastanın, 7 Ekim'de belirtilerle Nijerya'ya döndüğünü, belirtilerin 4 gün sonra ilerlediğini ve yapılan testlerin ardından kadında Ebola virüsü enfeksiyonunun doğrulandığını ifade etti.

Hastanın şu anda izolasyonda tutulduğunu ve tedavi gördüğünü kaydeden Pate, temaslı takibi çalışmalarının başlatıldığını ve şu ana kadar 44 temaslının belirlendiğini söyledi.

Sağlık Bakanlığı, FCT Sağlık Sekreterliği, Afrika Hastalık Kontrol ve Önleme Merkezleri (Africa CDC) ve diğer ortakların virüsün yayılmasını önlemek için koordineli şekilde çalıştığını bildiren Pate, ülkenin giriş noktalarındaki gözetim ve denetimlerin de artırıldığını vurguladı.

Pate, sağlık kuruluşlarına olası vakalara karşı yüksek düzeyde teyakkuzda olmaları çağrısında bulunurken, Nijeryalılardan da sakin ve dikkatli olmalarını istedi.

Halka hijyen kurallarına uymaları, ateş, halsizlik, baş ağrısı ve ishal gibi belirtilere karşı dikkatli olmaları ve halk sağlığı yetkilileriyle işbirliği yapmaları tavsiyesinde bulunan Pate, hükümetin 2014'teki Ebola salgınıyla mücadele deneyiminden ve yıllar içinde geliştirilen halk sağlığı mekanizmalarından yararlandığını kaydetti.

Pate, temaslıların takip ve gözetim altında tutulduğunu, hükümetin salgını kontrol altına alma çalışmalarına ilişkin kamuoyunu düzenli ve şeffaf biçimde bilgilendireceğini ifade etti.

author: Unknown
title: Borç, haciz, güvencesizlik, ağır çalışma: Metal işçisi mengenede
content:
Erdal Kılıç [email protected] Muzaffer Özkurt

Bursa’da hava ağır. Sadece bulutlu, yağmurlu olduğu için değil. Geçim sıkıntısı, borçlar, geleceği görememe, siyasi baskılar, ağırlaşan çalışma koşulları, işten atılma korkusu… Metal işçileri, her yandan mengeneye alınmış gibi. Hangi işçi ağzını açsa bu sıkışmışlık hissediliyor.

Bursa’nın üç ana fabrikası olan Renault, TOFAŞ ve Bosch’tan işçilerle görüşüyoruz. İşçilerin büyük kısmının kıdemi 10 yılın altında. Sayıları hızla artan, kıdemi 5 yıla kadar olan işçilerin ücretleri 35 bin lira ile 45 bin lira arasında. Herkesin gözünün üzerinde olduğu 10 yıl civarı işçilerin ücreti 70-90 bin lira. 1990’lardan bu yana çalışan az sayıda EYT’li işçinin emekli maaşıyla birlikte 200 bin liraya yakın geliri var. Önceki dönemin mücadelelerine şahit olmuş, deneyim sahibi ama elindekini kaybetmekten korkan en eski işçilerle; ücretleri düşük, geçmiş mücadelelerden bihaber ama öfkeli genç işçiler arasındaki bölünme her geçen gün derinleşiyor. Genç işçilere dair değerlendirmeler ise çoğunlukla “Telefon için işe girmişler, ne yapacakları belli değil” şeklinde oluyor. Bu sözlerin sonuna bir ama geliyor: “Ama bu fabrikalarda bir şey olacaksa onlar yapacak.”

Borçsuz işçi yok. Fabrika bünyesindeki kooperatiften markette ne satılıyorsa içinde olan kooperatiflerden veresiye mal alınabiliyor. Ücret alınır alınmaz da kaynaktan kesiliyor. Aylar geçtikçe, enflasyonla birlikte kesilen miktar artıyor. Kredi borçları nedeniyle hacizlik olan işçi sayısı da... Bekarlar evlenmekten korkuyor çünkü sürekli boşanma haberleri dillerde.

Genç işçiler arasında daha yaygın olmak üzere ekonomik sıkışmışlıktan çıkmak için kolay yol tercih ediliyor: Kumar! Fona para yatırmak, borsa oynamak da kumarın içinde sayılıyor. Zira son vurgunla birlikte eşinin bilezikleri dahil neyi var neyi yoksa kaybeden işçi sayısı az değil. İntiharların artma olasılığı sıklıkla dile getiriliyor. Açıktan, herkesin içinde para kaptırdığını söylemek işçiler için hiç kolay değil. Muğlak konuşulsa da temel gündem bu.

Fabrikalarda örgütlü Türk Metal’in ise bu kadar dikkate alınmadığı hiçbir dönem yaşanmadığını söylüyor işçiler. Sendikacıların sadece sosyal medyada paylaşmak için fotoğraf çektirmeye geldiğini, hiçbir soruya cevap vermediğini söyleyen genç Renault işçileri, Influencer diyor sendikacılara, “Şipşak” lakabı takıyor. 2015’te düşük ücrete karşı başlayan Metal Fırtına’nın ilk hedefi sendikacılardı. Şimdi ise sendikacılar için “insan kaynakları departmanı” tarifi kullanılıyor. Dolayısıyla gözler sendikacılardan çok patronda.

Patronlar işte bu bölünmüşlüğü, işçiler arası güvensizliği istedikleri çalışma düzenini hayata geçirmek için kullanıyor. İşsizlik ortamının da etkisiyle “Benim istediğim gibi olacaksın, yoksa güle güle” çok rahat söyleniyor. 57 saniyede bir arabanın üretildiği fabrikada, çay molasına 10 saniye erken çıkılamıyor. Çıkılması halinde üretim şefi bandın dibinde bitiyor. Üretimin 1 dakikanın üzerine çıkması ise kırmızı alarm demek. Ücretlerin avro karşısında eridiği dönemlerde TL dışında hesap yapmayan patron temsilcileri, kur baskısı nedeniyle şimdi ağızlarını dolar ve avroyla açıyor: “Ücret maliyetleri 2 bin 300 avro civarında, Fas’ta/Hindistan’da bu 450 avro.”

Ülke genelinde artan baskı nedeniyle “Şikayet etsek Silivri’de alırız soluğu” diyorlar. İşçilerin karamsar olmasının temel sebebi ülkenin içerisinde bulunduğu durum. 25-30 yaş arasında olup AKP’den ve Erdoğan’dan umudu olan işçi sayısı çok az. 25 yaş altı gençlerde durum daha da sert; “Zaten emekli olamayacağız. Çalışarak bir yere varmanın imkanı yok” diyorlar. Herkese öfkeliler. İktidara, muhalefete, yüksek ücretli işçilere hatta “tembellik edip” üzerlerindeki çalışma yükünü artıran yaşıtlarına… Aileleri de bu öfkeden nasibini alıyor. “Bu iktidarı getirdiler, gençliğimizi yaşayamadık” diyorlar: “Kaos çıksın”, “Yer yerinden oynasın”, “Benzin döksünler ilk ben kibrit çakarım.”

Kemalpaşalı, köyle ve tarımla bağları süren, hâlâ ekip biçmeye devam eden pek çok işçi, ürünleri para etmediği için köylü eylemlerinde de yer almış. Bir işçi, “Zarar ettiğim için 200 bin lira cebimden para verdim. Sadece toprağıma tutunmak istiyorum” diyor. Toprağını ekmeyi bırakan çok sayıda işçi var. Kemik AKP’li sayılan bu işçiler arasında da çözülme başlamış. Zarar arttıkça, iktidardan da uzaklaşıyor Kemalpaşalı işçiler. “Mahalle baskısı” diye tarif ettikleri genel hava nedeniyle alternatifi yine sağ partilerde arıyorlar.

Fransız tekeli Renault’da çalışmanın etkisiyle Fransa’da gençlik hareketlerini, grevleri izleyen, bu hareketlere öykünen genç işçiler var. Diğer tarafta “Türk her alanda geri düşürüldü. Göçmenler doktor oluyor, biz düşük ücretle gençliğimizi tüketiyoruz” diyen gençler de. Bu gençlerin adresi daha çok Zafer Partisi ve Anahtar Parti. Sayıları henüz çok olmasa da bu partilerin içinde giderek daha fazla genç işçi yer alıyor. Bu partileri “Sistem dışı” diye tarif ediyorlar. Mevcut iktidarı da ancak onların yargılayabileceğini düşünüyorlar. Milliyetçi görüşten etkilenen bu işçiler iktidarın “terörsüz Türkiye” dediği sürece de mesafeli. “devlet politikası” olduğunu söylüyorlar, ucunda devlet sopası olduğu için ses çıkarmıyorlar. Ama tepki var: “Ülkücü bıyığını kesen çok kişi oldu.”

Yeni Partiyi ise pasif kalmakla eleştiriyorlar. Kılıçdaroğlu’nun mutlak butlanı kabul etmesi, muhalefete dair umutları azaltmış. Bursa Büyükşehir Belediyesine operasyon da etkilemiş metal işçilerini. Daha belediye başkanı görevden alınmadan önce yerel medyada yolsuzluk belgeleri yayımlanmaya başlanmış. Tutuklandığı gün de tepki bu yüzden daha az olmuş. Yerel seçimde CHP’nin gelmesi ve sonrasında hayatın olağan akışında sürmesi üzerine gelişen “Demek ki değişirse yer yerinden oynamıyormuş. İktidar da değişebilir” fikrine ağır bir darbe olmuş operasyon. “Bu iktidar seçimle gider mi?” sorusuna “evet” diyen yok neredeyse.

Deneyimli bir metal işçisi, kendi güçleri hariç çözüm arayışlarının boşuna olduğunu söylüyor: “Şu anki durumda işçiler yalnız kalmak istemiyor ama tehlikeye de girmek istemiyor. Geçinemediğini ve daha fazlasının olabileceğini biliyor ama asgari ücrete ve borçlarına bakıp elindekini de kaybetmekten çekiniyor. Bu nedenle de hep bir kahraman ve kurtarıcı peşinde. Bu olmayacak. Aksine durum daha da kötüleşiyor. Anahtar, Zafer… Bugün isyan ettikleri düzenin sorumlusu bu partilerin başındakiler de değil mi zaten. İşçi olduğumuzu, işçinin zavallı olmadığını, birleştiğimizde herkesten güçlü olduğumuzu anlamadığımız, gücü kendi ellerimizde, yanı başımızdaki arkadaşımızda görmediğimiz sürece gerçekten kurtulma şansımız da yok. Ama metal işçilerinin çoğu kendi tarihini bilmiyor. Bu nedenle her seferinde en baştan deneye yanıla görüyor. Kendi tarihimizle buluşmanın yollarını bulmalıyız.” Türkiye’de işçilerin aslında sessiz olmadığını, ülke genelinde grev ve direnişlerin yaşandığını hatırlatan işçi, bu mücadelelerin birleşmesi halinde içinde bulunulan karamsarlığın da dağılacağına dikkat çekiyor.

Avrupalı otomotiv tekelleri savaşa hazırlanıyor. Renault’nun Fransa’daki fabrikasında da dron üretiliyor. Türkiye’de de savaş dönemi üretimine ilk uyum sağlayan Renault. Üretim baskısı her geçen gün artıyor.

Her yeni model çıktığında cumhuriyet altını dağıtılıyor. Yüz milyonlarca avroluk yatırım alınmasına karşın bu altın dağıtılmış değil. Her yıl dağıtılan erzakların gramajları küçültülmüş. Eldivenler otomatlardan sayılı alınıyor. İşçiler kazanılmış haklarının bir bir ellerinden alınmasına öfkeli. Her iki sözden biri verilmeyen altın. İşçiler için neredeyse onur meselesi haline gelmiş durumda.

Türk Metal’e olan güven de beklenti de yok raddesinde. “Vergi büyük dert ama bunun düzeleceğine, sözleşmede yüzde 15’le sabitleneceğine, sendikacıların talepler için bir şey yapacağına kimse inanmıyor” diyor işçiler. Tüm baskılara rağmen, işçilerin “Altınımız nerede” diye yüksek sesle sormasının altında da bu yatıyor. Altın verilmesi, ücretlere zam yapılmasından, verginin sabitlenmesinden daha olabilir kabul ediliyor.

“TOFAŞ diyor ki benim istediğim gibi olacaksın. Yoksa güle güle.” TOFAŞ işçisi fabrikadaki çalışma prensibini böyle özetliyor. Fabrikada borçsuz işçi yok. Hacizli işçilerin sayısı epey fazla. TOFAŞ’tan bir işçi “Ücretim 80 bin lira. Kredi kartına geri ödemem 50 bin lira. Ben iyi durumdayım. Kira vermiyorum” diyor.

TOFAŞ kooperatifinde yağ fiyatı 500 liradan 750 liraya çıkarılmış. İşçi tepki gösteriyor: “Ama benim ücretime yüzde 50 zam yapmadın ki.”

“Peki nasıl düzelir?” diye sorduğumuz işçi şu yanıtı veriyor: “Ben, eşim, annem, babam… 4 oyum var ne yapabilirim ki?”

Bosch fabrikasının gündemi işçi kıyımı. 1190 işçinin işten atılacağı söyleniyor. Kendi ayrılmak isteyenler, mevcut kıdem tazminatına ek olarak 6 aylık net ücret ve 2 aylık ihbar tazminatı ile teşvik ediliyor. Yüksek ücretli EYT’li işçiler hedefte. Hatta tek tek çağırılıp “Seni istemiyoruz artık” deniyor. Patronun direk işçi atmak yerine, teşvik ödeyerek böyle bir yola başvurmasının nedeni devletin teşviklerinden yararlanmaya devam etmek istemesi. Böylece kağıt üzerinde kendi işçi atmış olmuyor, işçiler kendi istekleriyle ayrılmış oluyor. İşçi ek para alıyor ama işsizlik sigortası ödemesinden yararlanamıyor. Dava açma hakkı da kalmıyor.

“Bosch teknolojiyi yakalayamadı” dedikodusu dolaşıyor. Elektrikli araçta gerekeni yapamadığı bu nedenle küçülüp işçi çıkardığı söyleniyor. Hatta “5 yıla kalmaz bu fabrikanın işi biter” diyenler var. Bir işçi bunu söyleyenlere tepki gösteriyor: “Neyi yakalayamadı, ne bitiyor! Geçen yıl geliri 91 milyar avro. 8 milyar avroluk ARGE’si var. Bak üretime düşme var mı, yok.” Endüstri 4.0 dönüşümü kapsamında bazı hatlarda robotlu üretime geçilmiş. 15-16 işçinin günde 2 bin parça ürettiği bir hatta, şimdilerde bir işçinin baktığı robotlu üretimle 4 bin parça üretiliyor. Tam bu nedenle işçi sayısının daha da düşeceği söyleniyor. İşçi devam ediyor: “Biz teknolojiyi yakalayamadı falan dedikçe daha çok işçi atılır.”

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

title: Bolu Belediye Başkanı Tanju Özcan’a 7 yıl 3 ay hapis ve 4 yıl siyasi yasak
content:
Bolu 3. Ağır Ceza Mahkemesi, Bolu Belediyesine yönelik soruşturmada 19 sanığın yargılandığı davada kararını açıkladı.




Mahkeme, görevinden uzaklaştırılan Belediye Başkanı Tanju Özcan, eski Belediye Başkan Yardımcısı Süleyman Can ve Bolu’yu Seviyorum Sosyal Yardımlaşma ve Dayanışma Vakfı (BOLSEV) yöneticisi Ali Sarıyıldız’a “zincirleme şekilde icbar suretiyle irtikap” suçundan 7 yıl 3 ay 15’er gün hapis cezası verdi.




Özcan ve Can'a 4'er yıl siyasi yasak getiren mahkeme, Sarıyıldız’ın da 4 yıl belirli hakları kullanmaktan yoksun bırakılmasına hükmetti. Üç sanığın tutukluluğu devam edecek. Karar için temyiz yolu açık. 




“Evde kedi gibi oturacağım”




Özcan, 19 Ekim’deki savunmasında suçlamaları reddetmiş, tahliyesini istemişti. İhlas Haber Ajansının aktardığına göre Özcan'ın talebi şöyleydi: 







“Serbest kalmak istiyorum. Oğluma kız istemek istiyorum. Suya sabuna dokunmadan evdeki kedi gibi oturacağım.”







20 Ekim’de karar öncesindeki son sözü sorulan Özcan yargılamanın kendisini siyasi olarak etkisizleştirmeyi amaçladığını öne sürdü:







“Bu yargılamanın, belediyeye yapılan operasyonların sebebi de Tanju Özcan’ı bitirmek. Bir plan ve senaryo var. Bu planı kim yaptı bilmiyorum.”







Özcan, “MASAK raporu herkesi akladı. Burada bir tiyatro sergileniyor,” diyerek mahkemeden beraatini istedi. Mahkemenin delillere ilişkin gerekçesi henüz açıklanmadı. Özcan salonda bulunan oğluna da “Babam bana haram lokma yedirmemiş diyeceksin” sözleriyle seslendi.




Rüşvetten beraat, dolandırıcılık cezalarına erteleme




Mahkeme, Özcan ve Sarıyıldız’ın rüşvet ve kamu kurumlarıyla dernek ve vakıfların ilişkilerine dair 5072 sayılı Kanun’a muhalefet suçlarından beraatine karar verdi.




Kurban bağışlarına ilişkin nitelikli dolandırıcılık suçlamasındaysa her mağdur yönünden ayrı ayrı 1 yıl 15 gün ile 1 yıl 8 ay arasında değişen hapis ve adli para cezaları verildi. Özcan’ın cezaları ertelendi; Sarıyıldız hakkındaki hükmün açıklanması geri bırakıldı. Bu suç yönünden verilen tahliye kararları, irtikap suçundan tutukluluğun sürmesi nedeniyle Özcan ve Sarıyıldız’ın serbest bırakılması anlamına gelmiyor.




Zabıta Müdürü Hakan Yılmaz’a irtikaptan 5 yıl 10 ay, Mali Hizmetler Müdürü Naim Ayhan’a rüşvetten 5 yıl 2 ay 15 gün hapis cezası verildi. Mustafa Altındal, nüfuz ticaretinden 2 yıl 11 ay hapisle cezalandırıldı ve tahliye edildi. Mahkeme 11 sanığın bütün suçlamalardan beraatine hükmetti.




Dava nasıl açılmıştı?




Soruşturma, Bolu’daki zincir marketlerin belediyeyle bağlantılı kuruluşlarla reklam sözleşmesi yapmaya zorlandığı ve BOLSEV adına toplanan kurban bağışlarında usulsüzlük yapıldığı iddialarını kapsıyordu. Özcan bütün suçlamaları reddetti.




Bolu Sosyal Bilimler Lisesinin spor salonunda yapılan karar duruşmasına Özcan ve Can cezaevinden Ses ve Görüntü Bilişim Sistemi (SEGBİS) aracılığıyla katıldı. Savcılık, esas hakkındaki mütalaasında Özcan için 217 yıla kadar hapis cezası istemişti.







Sığınmacılarla ilgili uygulamalara ayrı davada beraat




Özcan’ın belediye başkanlığı döneminde yabancı uyruklulara yapılan ayni ve nakdi yardımlar kesilmişti. Bolu Belediye Meclisi, 2021’de yabancılar için su ücretlerini dolar üzerinden hesaplama ve iki yabancı uyruklu kişinin evliliği için nikâh ücretini 100 bin lira olarak belirleme kararı almıştı. Özcan daha önce su ve bazı diğer hizmet ücretlerini on kat artırmayı savunmuştu.




Bolu İdare Mahkemesi, su ve nikâh tarifelerine ilişkin kararın yürütmesini durdurdu. Belediye Meclisi, yargı kararı sonrasında Ocak 2022’de ilgili düzenlemeleri yürürlükten kaldırdı. Türkiye İnsan Hakları ve Eşitlik Kurumu (TİHEK), 2022/175 sayılı kararıyla uygulamaları ayrımcılık yasağının ihlali sayarak Bolu Belediyesine 40 bin lira idari para cezası verdi.




Özcan, bu uygulamalar nedeniyle ayrıca “nefret ve ayrımcılık” suçundan yargılandı. Bolu Asliye Ceza Mahkemesi 13 Temmuz 2026’da Belediye Başkanı'nın beraatine hükmetti. 







(AEK)

author: Fundi Skweyiya-Gushu
title: Africa’s Cybersecurity Gap Is Not a Treaty Problem. It Is a Readiness Problem
content:
Africa’s digital economy is expanding faster than its ability to protect it. 

INTERPOL’s African Cyberthreat Assessment Report 2026

, drawing on information from 36 countries, found that artificial intelligence was involved in 55 per cent of reported cybercrimes across the continent. Reported losses rose from $192 million in 2024 to $484 million, while 72 per cent of surveyed countries reported scam centres operating within their borders.




The figures expose a growing vulnerability. Africa’s digital transformation is creating economic opportunities but also expanding the terrain on which criminals operate. The question is whether African institutions can respond collectively when attacks cross borders, exploit financial systems and use AI to target victims at scale.




Morocco Cybersecurity Week

, held in Rabat from 12 to 14 October 2026, placed regional cooperation firmly on the agenda. The emphasis was appropriate. Yet Africa’s challenge extends beyond convening officials and announcing strategies. It is making institutions cooperate effectively under pressure.




Africa does not lack legal frameworks. 

The African Union Convention on Cyber Security and Personal Data Protection

, known as the 

Malabo Convention,

 entered into force in June 2023 after years of delays. Morocco, meanwhile acceded to the 

Council of Europe’s Budapest Convention on Cybercrime

 in 2018 and signed its 

Second Additional Protocol on electronic evidence

 in 2022.




These instruments provide important foundations for criminal investigations, data protection and cross-border cooperation. But legal commitments cannot, on their own, ensure that investigators obtain evidence quickly, financial institutions exchange actionable intelligence or police services coordinate an effective response.




Cybercrime crosses institutional boundaries. A fraudulent transaction may involve a mobile-money provider, a bank, a telecommunications company, a cryptocurrency exchange and digital infrastructure spread across several jurisdictions. Each holds part of the evidence. When requests are delayed or responsibilities are unclear, investigators lose valuable time while criminals move money and erase their tracks. African institutions must therefore measure cooperation by what they can accomplish together, not by the number of agreements they endorse.




There is evidence that coordinated action works. 

INTERPOL’s Operation Serengeti 2.0

, conducted between June and August 2025, brought together law-enforcement authorities from 18 African countries and the United Kingdom. It resulted in 1,209 arrests, the dismantling of 11,432 malicious infrastructures and the recovery of $97.4 million. Private-sector partners contributed intelligence and technical expertise.




The lesson is not that treaties are unnecessary. Investigations still require lawful powers, admissible evidence and safeguards. Rather, Serengeti demonstrates the value of shared objectives, established channels and institutions equipped to act on intelligence together.




This is where Africa should look beyond calls by some of its leaders for a continental equivalent of 

NATO’s Article 5

. On 19 May 2025, Rwandan President Paul Kagame made these remarks in his keynote address at the inaugural 

International Security Conference on Africa (ISCA)

, held at the Kigali Convention Centre. Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni has also raised related questions at the 

African Defence Chiefs Conference on Military Operations

. While these calls reflect growing interest in collective African security, NATO’s experience offers a more specific lesson for cybersecurity governance. 

NATO recognises cyberspace as an operational domain

, and significant cyberattacks may, in certain circumstances, constitute an armed attack. However, invoking collective defence is not automatic: each case is assessed individually by the North Atlantic Council.







For African governments confronting cyber-enabled fraud, ransomware and attacks on public services, the more immediate lesson is not collective retaliation. It is collective preparedness.




Consider 

NATO’s annual Locked Shields exercise

, organised by its 

Cooperative Cyber Defence Centre of Excellence

. The 2026 exercise brought together approximately 4,000 participants from 41 countries to defend simulated digital systems against complex attacks. Participants tested technical responses while confronting the coordination challenges that emerge during a crisis. The winning Latvia–Singapore team also demonstrated the value of cooperation beyond NATO’s membership.




Africa should adapt this model to its own circumstances. A recurring continental cyber-resilience exercise could simulate ransomware targeting a regional electricity network, attacks on mobile-money platforms or the compromise of a government identity system. Police, computer emergency response teams, financial regulators, banks and telecommunications operators would have to investigate, communicate and make decisions together.




The objective should not be a staged demonstration in which everyone knows the answers. Exercises must expose weaknesses: who can isolate a compromised system, how evidence is preserved, when neighbouring countries are notified and how essential services continue operating. Participants should publish appropriately sanitised assessments identifying failures and corrective measures.




Morocco is well positioned to contribute. The 

International Telecommunication Union’s 2024 Global Cybersecurity Index

 placed the country in Tier 1, the highest performance category, with a score of 97.5 out of 100. In October 2026, Morocco also launched a 

Cyber Academy programme

 with the World Bank and Smart Africa Digital Academy to strengthen cybersecurity leadership across Africa.




Such initiatives are valuable, but executive training must complement technical capacity. Africa needs analysts who investigate malware, incident responders who contain attacks and digital-forensics specialists who preserve evidence. It also needs institutions able to retain these professionals and fund the systems they require.




Trust is equally important. Morocco’s cybersecurity directorate operates under its National Defence Administration. This arrangement does not, by itself, establish that information will be misused. However, any continental threat-intelligence mechanism must define who can access shared data, for what purposes and under what oversight. Banks and telecommunications companies will hesitate to share sensitive information if protections and accountability are uncertain. Citizens also need safeguards against the misuse of cybersecurity powers for unlawful surveillance.




Africa must improve how it measures the problem, too. The 

United Nations Economic Commission for Africa

 has cited estimates that cybercrime costs African countries an average of 10 per cent of GDP. This should not be treated as a verified annual loss across every country. Estimates differ in scope and methodology, while official incident data remain incomplete. Standardised reporting is essential to distinguish confirmed losses from broader economic damage and establish credible priorities for investment.




Four priorities should follow. First, establish common incident-reporting standards. Second, create a funded, recurring African cyber-resilience exercise open to all African Union member states and involving public and private institutions. Third, develop secure mechanisms for urgent cross-border evidence requests, consistent with domestic law and international obligations. Fourth, establish independent oversight, clear access rules and privacy protections for shared threat intelligence.




Artificial intelligence can strengthen detection and response, but it cannot compensate for institutions that fail to communicate or procedures that collapse during a crisis.




Rabat’s significance should ultimately be measured by what follows the speeches. By the next regional gathering, can agencies in different African countries rehearse a joint response, exchange evidence lawfully and report incidents using comparable standards?




If they can, cooperation will have moved from declaration to capability. If they cannot, Africa will remain vulnerable not because it lacks ambition or legal instruments, but because its institutions have not practised working together.




Criminal networks already operate across borders. Africa’s defenders must learn to do the same.




The post 

Africa’s Cybersecurity Gap Is Not a Treaty Problem. It Is a Readiness Problem

 appeared first on 

African Arguments

.

author: Mike Ludwig
title: Lawyers Accuse Trump of Building a “Deportation Assembly Line” for Children
content:
A new lawsuit argues that Trump administration policies are robbing migrant children of due process.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

The Trump administration has stripped protections from unaccompanied migrant children and undocumented minors to fast-track deportations, a new lawsuit challenging the administration argues. The administration’s policies have created harrowing scenes in courts across the country, where an increasing number of kids appear before judges without a lawyer or the legal support necessary to navigate a complex legal system that will determine their future.

One legal organization that is part of the suit described representing a child with a documented heart condition who applied for asylum based on her experiences of sexual abuse in her home country. She was forced into a hours-long virtual asylum interview one day after being hospitalized for a cardiac event. She requested to end the interview because she was experiencing pain in her chest, visibly crying and clutching her heart. The asylum officer insisted she continue; only after hours of subjecting this child to severe distress did the officer agree to reschedule.

In the lawsuit, filed in a federal court in Maryland on October 15, a coalition of immigration advocates and legal aid providers say the administration has ignored federal law to create a “deportation assembly line” for unaccompanied children and undocumented minors.

The number of unaccompanied minors removed from the U.S. has more than tripled compared to President Trump’s first term, according to ProPublica. Children who have parents or sponsors in the U.S. have been separated from them and denied due process within Immigration and Customs Enforcement’s (ICE) byzantine system of detention centers and jails, the lawsuit argues.

In some cases, children who crossed the border to seek asylum and, in many cases, to be reunited with family in the United States, could potentially be deported back to the dangerous conditions they attempted to flee, according to Cristel Martinez, an immigration attorney in Chicago.

“It’s basically sending the kids back to countries where their life is in danger, and may end up getting killed,” Martizen told reporters on October 15.

Martinez is herself an immigrant, and her law office has represented more than 400 unaccompanied minors in immigration court. That job has become increasingly difficult under a series of policy changes made by the Trump administration to fast-track deportations and cut off federal funding for nonprofits that provide legal support established by Congress for unaccompanied children. Attorneys previously had months to gather documents, perform psychological evaluations, and prepare a case. Now judges are setting asylum hearings and issuing removal orders at a speed never seen before.

Mickey Donovan-Kaloust, a director of children’s representation at the Immigrant Defenders Law Center, a plaintiff in the lawsuit, said she has worked with undocumented children for 15 years but has never witnessed the “chaos, cruelty, and disregard for due process that I’m seeing today.”

“The government is stopping at nothing to fast-track the deportations of these children,” Donovan-Kaloust told reporters on Friday. “Instead of promptly releasing children to their family members as the law requires, the government has been trapping children in government custody for months on end.”

Minimum standards for caring for unaccompanied migrant children were not established until the Flores Settlement of 1997, a consent decree resulting from years of litigation filed by human rights groups. Then, until the early 2000s, children who arrived at a U.S. border without a parent or guardian were often detained indefinitely in a prison system designed for adults and could not meet basic childhood needs such as education.

Pushing for a bill to reform these practices in 2008, Sen. Dianne Feinstein described witnessing a 15-year-old girl appear “shackled and in prison clothing” at an asylum hearing ostensibly about her seeking safety in the U.S.

“As she told her story to an immigration judge, she could not wipe away her tears because her hands were chained to her waist,” Feinstein said at the time.

A series of legal challenges in the 1980s and 1990s began to set new standards for unaccompanied children, culminating in provisions included in the Homeland Security Act of 2002 (HSA), and later in the William Wilberforce Trafficking Victims Protection Reauthorization Act of 2008 (TVPRA). Congress proposed these laws to help children fleeing violence and exploitation find safety in the U.S., the plaintiffs say.

“Together, the HSA, the TVPRA, and their implementing regulations try to account for the vulnerability of a child navigating a foreign immigration system alone — without a parent, without a lawyer, and frequently without English fluency,” the new lawsuit reads.

The laws established child-appropriate procedures for unaccompanied children, such as “affirmative” asylum interviews with specially trained officers, so that kids are not forced to recount the most traumatizing moments of their lives before an immigration judge.

However, the Trump administration is now violating these laws by denying migrant children due process rights and fast-tracking their removal from the country, according to the lawsuit.

“They are making it impossible for children to get competent representation, and they are accessible to the government [for maximizing deportations] because they are in their custody,” Beth Baltimore, interim managing director of legal services at The Door, a youth center in New York City, told Truthout. “It’s a very coordinated attack on children.”

Today, all unaccompanied minors apprehended by federal immigration police must be handed over to the Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR). ORR is not an enforcement agency and operates shelters where parents and potential sponsors can be screened to become caregivers for the children.

However, advocates for immigrants rights say the Trump administration is now rushing these same children — and others taken during chaotic ICE raids and separated from parents — through the legal proceedings in ways that deny them due process and put them in danger. ORR and other agencies under the Department of Homeland Security tasked with protecting their rights are instead dismantling them, according to the lawsuit.

“I’ve been in immigration court observing as well for the past few weeks, have seen firsthand kids getting removed, even when attorneys from the organization that is supposed to be helping them are present and not speaking up for the kids,” Martinez said.

The lawsuit specifically challenges two new policies that attorneys say have eroded due process, including requiring children to apply for asylum within weeks of entry and providing as little as one day’s notice before an asylum interview, which establishes whether they qualify as a refugee fleeing danger. The administration abruptly changed the asylum interview format and instructed judges to complete their detained child docket by January 2027 regardless of circumstance. This has left attorneys little time to prepare cases as children are mandated to appear in court multiple times a week.

Baltimore said many children arrive at the border unaccompanied but are trying to reunite with family in the U.S. The fear created by Trump’s violent mass deportation scheme has made this impossible for many families.

“Some of them, they are not unaccompanied. They are living with families, but because of an ICE detention on the street or criminal arrest where they are sent to ICE or ORR, they become ‘unaccompanied children,’” Baltimore said. “They are being placed into ORR custody and then there are these huge barriers for release, but they are already living with families and it was fine; there are no allegations of abuse or neglect with those parents.”

As Democrats in Congress have pointed out, federal law also requires special protections for suspected child victims of human trafficking, but the administration appears to be circumventing these rules to increase deportations.

Additionally, ORR is supposed to provide children with legal services, and traditionally did so by paying nonprofit legal aid providers. However, after a dispute with a nonprofit in which the Trump administration demanded sensitive personal information about defendants, the federal government let the contracts lapse on July 31, potentially leaving an estimated 26,000 children and teens without paid legal representation. Advocacy groups are digging into reserve funding to pay attorneys and are also challenging this in federal court.

Speaking to reporters on Friday, Donovan-Kaloust described another recent case.

“Last week, a 5-year-old child who had been abandoned by his family was ordered deported in a docket where [our organization] was present,” she said. “A five-year-old. That should stop this country in its tracks.”

This was a readership we painstakingly built over decades, and it vanished because Google chose corporate greed over a healthy democracy.

author: Erin Reed
title: Anti-Trans Ads May Be Backfiring on Republicans
content:
Elon Musk’s America PAC has committed $100 million to a midterm push heavy on anti-transgender ads.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

In the first few weeks of October, three national pollsters asked three different questions about transgender issues, and all three landed in the same place from different angles: the anti-transgender ads this year may be backfiring on Republican strategists. Navigator Research, AP-NORC and ABC News/Washington Post/Ipsos polls collectively found that voters trust Democrats on transgender issues and rank those issues as not very important to their vote, and that Republican and independent voters were less likely than Democrats to prioritize them. When the polls are contrasted with the massive amount of ad spend on transgender issues, there are signs, first seen in the Virginia gubernatorial election last year, that the high concentration of ads may turn voters off and could fuel, rather than suppress, a Democratic wave election in 2026.

The first poll to come out was the Navigator Research poll. In this poll, voters were asked to list up to five top issues, giving it a stronger signal than prior polls that only required voters to list their top issue. Even when voters were asked to list five, transgender issues ranked dead last among all 20 issues on the list. And Democratic voters were the most likely group to rank transgender issues a top issue, meaning many of those who did are likely voting to protect transgender rights, not to restrict those rights. Prior polls from Gallup have found similar results, although this poll is most notable due to its top-five format.

Then, another poll came out: AP-NORC asked Americans on a per-issue basis how important each issue was to their own vote. Whereas most issues asked about were considered “one of the most important,” such as the economy and the war with Iran, only 11% of respondents named transgender issues one of the most important to their vote. Furthermore, 51% of respondents said that transgender issues were “not an important issue” at all, the only issue to score higher than the teens on that question. And as we know from prior polling, Democrats are much more likely to answer that transgender issues are important to them.

Lastly, an ABC/Post/Ipsos poll has been released that outright asks Americans which party they trust to do a better job on transgender issues. Of those asked, 38% of Americans say they trust Democrats on transgender issues when compared to 29% who say they trust Republicans, a 9-point Democratic edge. Notably, Americans trust Democrats on a whole host of issues that the survey asks about, ranging from health care to the economy. Only on crime do respondents trust Republicans more than Democrats, a poor sign for the Republican Party in the lead-up to the 2026 elections.

These results are heavily contrasted by the money being spent on anti-transgender ads. According to AdImpact data, more than $100 million has been spent since Aug. 1 on more than 200 ads that use the phrase “sex change.” Meanwhile, Elon Musk’s America PAC has committed $100 million to a midterm push heavy on anti-transgender ads aimed at Democrats. EITM has received reports of mailers in several races ranging from state legislative to congressional campaigns that such data has no way of capturing, and many political pundits have pointed out that the anti-trans ad focus seems to be a defining issue in the 2026 midterms.

Republicans are starting to sound the alarm that the anti-trans ads are not working. The American Principles Project, one of the progenitors of anti-transgender ads, has admitted that such ads “may not be sufficient” on their own this election cycle for Republicans to win the midterms. And former Texas House Speaker Dade Phelan, a Republican, said last week that the ads are just “not resonating” with Texas voters. Now, these polls confirm the fears of Republican strategists about the effectiveness of the ads.

If all of this sounds familiar to EITM readers, it is because similar dynamics played out around the same time in 2025 in Virginia’s gubernatorial and House of Delegates elections. Voters, when asked who would better handle transgender issues, named Abigail Spanberger, the Democratic candidate for governor, over Winsome Earle-Sears, the Republican. Despite this, Earle-Sears kept pouring more and more money into anti-trans ads, with such ads making up a whopping 57% of Republican ad spending in the race. Even though polls showed a closer race, Spanberger took the contest by 15 points and Democrats scored a 64 seat historic majority in the House of Delegates. Not only did anti-transgender ads not work, but the sheer volume of them may have turned off voters who ultimately trusted Democrats over Republicans to handle such issues.

Could we see similar results in the 2026 elections? The signs are there. Polling shows Democrats running ahead, and forecasters favor them to win both the House and the Senate this year, while races in states normally far out of reach for Democrats appear to be floating into their grasp. Republicans, meanwhile, keep pouring money into targeting transgender people, perhaps unable to run on much else, even as their own strategists warn it may not be enough. This could be the year the gambit fails on a national scale. Voters will deliver their verdict on Election Day, Nov. 3.
