author: Sasha Draeger-Mazer
title: Texas Woman Sues Anti-Abortion Group Under Law It Helped to Pass
content:
The woman is suing Students for Life for the cost of raising the children of two unplanned pregnancies.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

A Texas woman is using a state law banning the transport of abortion pills to sue members of the anti-abortion organization Students for Life of America.

In the suit filed Tuesday in a Harris County district court, plaintiff Maria Puerto, a 26-year-old mother of two using a pseudonym to protect her family, alleges that four anti-abortion activists had ordered abortion medication on their phones in March 2026 outside of the Space Center Houston. The lawsuit cites, among other things, a now-expired social media post by one of the defendants captioned “Guess what we are doing? Ordering abortion pills undercover? Yep. Stay tuned.”

Known as the Woman and Child Protection Act, House Bill 7, which went into effect in December, prohibits providing an “abortion-inducing drug” to or from anyone in the state of Texas. The law is enforced by allowing almost any person, regardless of whether they have been impacted by the incident, to bring a civil suit against a provider of abortion medication. Plaintiffs may seek an injunction and a minimum of $100,000. If the person bringing the suit has no connection to the incident, the plaintiff receives $10,000, with the remainder of the award going to a charity selected by the plaintiff.

The lawsuit does not specify how the defendants violated HB 7. While the law does not explicitly bar the ordering of abortion medication, it does prohibit the transport of the drug within the state.

“What the statute says is that transporting abortion drugs from one location to another within the state is a violation of HB 7 … By the plain language of the statute, this would seem to be a violation,” Puerto’s attorney Molly Duane told The Texas Tribune. “This is the problem with writing such a confusing and vague law.”

While pregnant women cannot be prosecuted under HB 7 for actions taken to have an abortion, none of the four defendants — Kristan Mercer Hawkins, Lydia Taylor Davis, Jamie Curry and Megan Roos — were pregnant at the time, according to the lawsuit.

Duane, who is with Amplify Legal, the legal arm of advocacy group Abortion in America, said she and her client are hoping that the lawsuit will eventually surface more about what the defendants did with the abortion pills once they ordered them.

Hawkins is the president of Virginia-based Students for Life, which lobbied heavily for the passage of HB 7 last year. In a video posted to X on Tuesday, Hawkins called the lawsuit “frivolous” and a “publicity stunt,” and urged Texas Child Protective Services to investigate Puerto.

Puerto is suing for $459,782, “the average cost of raising two children from birth to age 18 in the state of Texas.” According to the lawsuit, both of Puerto’s pregnancies were unplanned and occurred despite the use of contraception, and she was unable to end the pregnancies due to the state’s abortion ban and the expenses associated with traveling out of the state. The suit also says that her first pregnancy directly resulted in her having to quit college and losing her job.

If she wins the lawsuit, Puerto would be entitled to $10,000 of the award, as she has no connection to the defendants. According to a Tuesday statement by Abortion in America, she plans to give the remaining award to Jane’s Due Process, a nonprofit that helps young Texans confidentially access abortion and birth control.

In an essay she published Tuesday, Puerto said Texas laws regulating her pregnancy effectively controlled her future, and described the financial struggle she has faced as a result.

“I’ve filed a lawsuit against those who helped build these horrible laws — and then had the privilege to break them in an attempt to trap women like me who still need help,” Puerto wrote. A statement by Students for Life Vice President Kristi Hamrick called the suit a “backhanded compliment” and vowed to fight it in court.

A request for comment from the defendants was directed to Students for Life’s initial statement on the lawsuit.

At least two other lawsuits have been filed using HB 7, and each of those lawsuits have targeted out-of-state abortion providers and alleged that women have actually taken the abortion pills they provided. A case filed by Texas resident Jerry Rodriguez and his daughter against California-based abortion care provider Remy Coeytaux alleges Coeytaux provided the medication used to end his girlfriend’s pregnancy on two occasions. In another case, Davis v. Cooprider et al., the plaintiff accused the organization Abortion Access of providing pills to defendant Christopher Cooprider, who used them to terminate the plaintiff’s pregnancy against her will.

The lawsuit filed Tuesday does not say if the abortion medication allegedly ordered by the defendants was actually consumed.

“Texas is a strange place filled with vigilante statutes, vigilante laws that seek to turn Texans against each other,” Duane, Puerto’s attorney, said. “But if anyone should be benefiting from these legal regimes, it’s people like our client. So it was putting those two things together that might be unusual, but this is the situation that Texas has put its citizens in.”

The Texas Tribune is a nonprofit, nonpartisan media organization that informs Texans — and engages with them — about public policy, politics, government and statewide issues.

Truthout is one of only a few platforms for justice-oriented, grassroots journalism. Today, we face an existential threat.

Due to Google’s launch of AI search, we’ve seen a drastic plunge in our site traffic and, as a result, our revenue. We lost 15 percent of our readership overnight. This was a readership we painstakingly built over decades, and it vanished because Google chose corporate greed over a healthy democracy.

We are fundraising right now to meet our basic operating expenses. If you can support Truthout with a one-time or monthly donation, you will make a significant impact on our work. Anything you can do makes a difference — we appreciate your support.

author: Randi Beers
title: The world is ending, and I feel fine
content:
A friend told me a story this summer about

 a smokey day in Minnesota, where she lives. When she complained about the haze to her 13-year-old nephew, he responded: “That’s just summer.”




It wasn’t long ago that wildfire smoke was a characteristic of summer mostly limited to western North America, where conditions are drier.




But, in just a few years, that has drastically changed. Evidence of climate change is everywhere: it’s in the sea ice of the North — much less predictable now — and unbreathable air across the south. (And 

parts

 of the North.)




When we think about and imagine the collapse of civilization, the conversation usually revolves around the world becoming uninhabitable due to climate change.




Nunatsiaq News reporter Miriam Lafontaine recently 

wrote about

 one recent study that predicts Arctic winters will be, on average, 10 degrees warmer by 2100. 

A change like that could bring Iqaluit’s mean daily temperature in January from -26 C to -16 C. 




For comparison, Iqaluit’s average daily temperature 

increased

 by one degree between 1991 and 2020. 




Even more recently, artificial intelligence has emerged as a potential threat, with leaders in the field warning AI could kill us all by the end of the decade.
















Of course predicting the end of the world — and being wrong about it — is a constant throughout history.




We braced ourselves for Y2K, in anticipation that computers wouldn’t understand the calendar flipping from 1999 to 2000. 

Before that, we thought global petroleum reserves would wane with demand still soaring. 

Before that, during the Cold War, the threat was nuclear.




In 1947, after the first nuclear weapons were developed, the Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists created the Doomsday Clock to assess risks to humanity. It was originally set to seven minutes to “midnight,” or the end of the world.




Today, it sits at 85 seconds to midnight.




Is the end of the world nigh? Nobody knows — not even ChatGPT. But it did acknowledge it’s a fair question.




No single person can control climate change or any other threats to civilization but we can control our own lives. Like Iqaluit’s Derek Allerton, who 

collects cans

 every day in the hopes the Nunavut government will reinstate a beverage recycling program.
















We can buy into renewable energy programs, compost, limit our consumerism, and do other small things to make our communities better.




Even if the path forward isn’t clear, I’m confident we will find ways to adapt to anything.




Except maybe an asteroid.

author: Unknown
title: Il terreno sta cedendo? Lo yen, il dollaro e l’autunno caldo in Francia
content:
Pubblichiamo la traduzione di questo interessante articolo di Andrée Dima apparso su 

Realité

 il 14 ottobre 2026

 

in vista della giornata di mobilitazione del 17 ottobre in Francia. 




Diciotto mesi fa, dopo la pubblicazione del nostro primo articolo, “

Su un terreno instabile”

, abbiamo ricevuto numerosi commenti da parte di lettori tanto benevoli quanto perplessi: che farsene di queste analisi e, in fin dei conti, a che pro tutto questo arrovellarsi il cervello? Nella prospettiva di un autunno di lotte sociali, vorremmo mostrare, in maniera più concreta, i legami tra congiuntura monetaria e lotta di classe e, soprattutto, che cosa cambi per chi intende intervenire nel movimento reale.




Da una trentina d’anni, i paesi ricchi vivono a ritmo di credito a basso costo, e gli Stati Uniti, la Gran Bretagna e la Francia hanno potuto mascherare, attraverso il debito, lo smantellamento della propria industria nazionale. È questo il contesto che ha plasmato le forme assunte dalle lotte e i «compromessi sociali» che ne sono nati; è questo il contesto nel quale ci siamo formati, abbiamo compiuto la nostra formazione politica e, forse, nel quale abbiamo acquisito delle cattive abitudini. La situazione sta tuttavia cambiando, e il 17 ottobre potrebbe assumere una portata ben diversa rispetto ai movimenti sociali ai quali ci siamo abituati, gilet gialli compresi: la posta in gioco non è più costringere il governo a fare marcia indietro su una legge o un provvedimento, ma mettere la borghesia francese con le spalle al muro, imponendole un’alternativa: la fine della guerra a Est oppure il sacrificio dell’euro. Due prospettive la cui portata supera di gran lunga i confini nazionali e che mettono in gioco gli equilibri mondiali. A condizione, però, che il movimento sia consapevole di ciò che ha tra le mani. 




Per rendere tutto questo più tangibile, occorre ripartire da una sequenza iniziata quest’estate, con un avvenimento apparentemente lontano, quasi esotico: nella torpida calura del mese di agosto, la Banca centrale del Giappone ha annunciato un’operazione congiunta con il Dipartimento del Tesoro statunitense, volta ad arginare la svalutazione della propria valuta, lo yen. Se vale la pena soffermarsi su questa iniziativa, è perché si trattava di un’operazione alquanto borderline. Innanzitutto, per il metodo adottato: in una situazione del genere, la prima reazione di una banca centrale sarebbe, in linea di principio, quella di aumentare i propri tassi di riferimento (che determinano gli altri tassi d’interesse). Poiché in Giappone questi figurano tra i più bassi al mondo, la banca centrale dovrebbe 

apparentemente

 disporre di ampi margini di manovra, ma il problema è che un intervento del genere avrebbe avuto conseguenze spiacevoli 

anche

 per il mercato del debito pubblico statunitense, e non solo. L’economia giapponese sta emergendo da trent’anni di deflazione, e i tassi d’interesse vi rimangono strutturalmente più bassi che altrove. Siccome il denaro costa poco, gli speculatori si indebitano in yen, per poi convertirli e investirli in titoli più remunerativi, come i buoni del Tesoro statunitensi. È un’operazione nota come 

carry

 

trade

, che contribuisce a indebolire il valore dello yen e, allo stesso tempo, ad alimentare la domanda di debito pubblico americano. Lo yen a buon mercato funziona come una macchina per fare soldi, non soltanto per gli speculatori, ma anche per lo Stato americano: basta però che Tokyo aumenti i propri tassi perché questo meccanismo che alimenta il debito pubblico statunitense rischi di incepparsi.




Per evitare di arrivare a tanto, l’adorabile Scott Bessent, segretario al Tesoro americano, si è dunque offerto generosamente di dare una mano: anziché aumentare i tassi d’interesse, la Banca del Giappone avrebbe potuto riacquistare la propria valuta, riducendone la quantità in circolazione e facendone così risalire il valore. E per evitare che il Giappone finanziasse l’operazione vendendo titoli del Tesoro americano, Washington avrebbe potuto persino farsene carico al suo posto, magari vendendo euro per coprire i costi. Il tutto per qualche centinaio di miliardi di dollari. Questa mossa ha lasciato di stucco gli osservatori. Segnala infatti che il mercato del debito americano, il più profondo e liquido del mondo, non è più in grado di assorbire uno shock dell’ordine di un centinaio di miliardi di dollari senza subire un aumento immediato, doloroso e intollerabile dei tassi d’interesse sul debito pubblico statunitense. Segno che il dollaro sta raggiungendo i propri limiti, entrando in maniera sempre più evidente in una fase di senilità monetaria.




Ritorno su 

Un terreno instabile




Per comprendere appieno la portata dell’evento, il lettore ci conceda una breve digressione sul contesto storico, che avevamo esaminato più approfonditamente in 

Su un terreno instabile

. Nel 1971, Nixon annuncia la fine della convertibilità del dollaro in oro e, con essa, la fine del sistema di Bretton Woods, che aveva strutturato il sistema monetario del dopoguerra attorno al controllo dei movimenti di capitale. In fondo, questo avvenimento non rappresentava altro che un adeguamento della struttura monetaria ai movimenti dei capitali più maturi, che già da un decennio ne mettevano alla prova i vincoli, ricorrendo a ogni sorta di espediente per aggirare le barriere imposte alla loro mobilità (in particolare attraverso il mercato degli eurodollari, ma questa è un’altra storia). Preso atto della fine di Bretton Woods, il nuovo sistema monetario si è dunque riconfigurato attorno a due grandi principi: da una parte, la progressiva deregolamentazione dei movimenti di capitale, che consentiva di investire liberamente all’estero e di rimpatriarne i profitti; dall’altra, il passaggio a un regime di cambi fluttuanti tra le principali valute. Principi che avrebbero costituito il quadro di una globalizzazione nella quale le potenze imperialiste si misurano le une con le altre attraverso i rispettivi tassi di cambio.




È così che, nei curiosi anni Ottanta, si è instaurata una singolare guerra valutaria «dall’alto» tra le potenze imperialiste: è l’epoca dei Volcker, delle Thatcher, dei Raymond Barre, che gareggiano nell’innalzare i tassi d’interesse, talvolta in maniera spettacolare, per sostenere le rispettive valute. Per gli Stati Uniti, era il prezzo da pagare per mantenere il dollaro al centro del sistema monetario internazionale; per gli altri, che faticavano a sostenere le proprie valute attraverso avanzi commerciali,in particolare la Francia e la Gran Bretagna, era l’unico modo per evitare il declassamento dei rispettivi capitali. Questa situazione è durata fino alla metà degli anni Novanta, quando le autorità cinesi, per evitare l’apprezzamento dello yuan, hanno avviato una politica di conversione sistematica delle eccedenze commerciali cinesi in buoni del Tesoro statunitensi. Un volume crescente di liquidità, indifferente ai rendimenti offerti, si è così riversato negli Stati Uniti, provocando una forte diminuzione dei tassi d’interesse (ricordiamo che questi riflettono i rapporti tra acquirenti e venditori sui mercati del debito). In questa nuova congiuntura, gli Stati Uniti e, al loro seguito, la Gran Bretagna e la Francia hanno cominciato a funzionare a pieno regime grazie ai «doppi deficit»: una combinazione di deficit commerciale, legato alla deindustrializzazione, e di deficit di bilancio, reso possibile dalle nuove facilitazioni all’indebitamento. Dal 1994, il debito pubblico si è moltiplicato per sei in Francia e per undici in Gran Bretagna.




Questo sistema confortevole, fondato sulla subordinazione della Cina nell’economia mondiale, non era tuttavia destinato a durare, e le prime crepe hanno cominciato a manifestarsi già negli anni Dieci del Duemila, sulla scia della crisi finanziaria. Nel pieno della crisi, il dollaro ha inizialmente confermato il proprio status indiscutibile di valuta rifugio e di maggiore liquidità internazionale, ma ha comunque mostrato segni di debolezza durante l’ondata di 

quantitative

 

easing

 varata dalla Federal Reserve (massicce iniezioni di liquidità a sostegno dell’attività economica). Il deprezzamento del dollaro rispetto all’euro ha giustificato, all’epoca, le forti pressioni esercitate sulla Germania affinché la BCE adottasse una politica analoga. La Cina ha risposto alla contrazione della domanda mondiale dapprima con un piano di rilancio interno (2009), e poi con un vasto programma di investimenti infrastrutturali all’estero (le Nuove Vie della Seta), che ha trasformato le modalità del suo inserimento nell’economia internazionale e, con esse, la convenienza di detenere un simile ammontare di riserve in dollari.




A partire da quel periodo, la Cina comincia a ridurre la propria esposizione e a disfarsi dei buoni del Tesoro USA che aveva accumulato fino ad allora. Il processo è stato graduale, ma resta il fatto che al picco del 2013 la Cina deteneva oltre 1.300 miliardi di dollari in buoni del Tesoro (l’11% del debito pubblico americano), mentre oggi ne possiede soltanto circa 600 miliardi (il 2% di quel debito). Per quanto le banche centrali vassalle di Washington ne abbiano assorbito una parte, ciò non è bastato a compensare contemporaneamente il disimpegno cinese e le nuove esigenze di finanziamento del Tesoro americano. Sono dunque subentrati gli investitori privati: la quota di debito americano da loro detenuta è passata dal 40% all’inizio degli anni Dieci a quasi il 60% di oggi[1]. Ed ecco un nuovo problema: questi investitori non acquistano titoli per il piacere di accumulare riserve valutarie, ma per diversificare un portafoglio il cui valore viene giudicato, in ultima analisi, in base al rendimento. In breve, i detentori del debito americano sono diventati sensibili ai tassi d’interesse, soprattutto perché dopo anni di investimenti insufficienti negli Stati Uniti il ciclo dell’intelligenza artificiale offre loro opportunità d’investimento alternative e decisamente più redditizie. Dopo vent’anni di culto del modello 

fabless

 e dell’«economia immateriale» (in altre parole, dell’esternalizzazione), l’alta tecnologia americana si è rimessa a investire in beni materiali con uno zelo da neoconvertiti. Supercomputer, reti in rame e reattori nucleari modulari costituiscono altrettanti attivi utilizzabili come garanzie (collaterali), offrendo alle imprese del settore la possibilità di finanziarsi attraverso il debito. Nella sua insaziabile sete di investimenti, il settore tecnologico, tradizionalmente finanziato sui mercati azionari, ha dunque cominciato a espandersi nel mercato obbligazionario, dove entra direttamente in concorrenza con i titoli di stato. Si stima che nel 2026 i giganti dell’intelligenza artificiale potrebbero raccogliere tra i 300 e i 600 miliardi di dollari sui mercati del debito[2].




Il quadro resterebbe incompleto senza tener conto della guerra. È infatti proprio nel momento in cui la domanda di titoli di debito pubblico americano si prosciuga che la guerra condotta su più fronti impone un’accelerazione del ritmo della spesa: il bilancio delle forze armate statunitensi è passato da 755 miliardi nel 2021 a oltre 1.000 miliardi nel 2026. Cina, intelligenza artificiale, guerra: questa traiettoria complessiva si traduce in un rapido aumento dei tassi d’interesse. Gli Stati Uniti stanno attraversando una brusca crisi d’astinenza, ed è questa situazione, inedita nella storia recente del dollaro, a fare da sfondo all’intervento di quest’estate: per assorbire 100 miliardi di buoni del Tesoro detenuti dai giapponesi, il mercato avrebbe imposto un ulteriore rialzo dei tassi, sempre più doloroso da sostenere a causa dell’aumento del debito pubblico statunitense. Da qui il colpo basso di Bessent, la cui eleganza è consistita nel far pagare il prezzo dell’aggiustamento alle economie europee: ognuno per sé e Dio per tutti.




Dall’altra parte dell’Atlantico, la «questione francese» ossessiona l’Eurozona




Se ci siamo soffermati così a lungo su questa ricostruzione, è perché ci sembra che questi elementi di contesto siano fondamentali per comprendere appieno la profondità storica di un eventuale movimento sociale che dovesse svilupparsi in Francia nel corso dell’autunno. La Francia occupa infatti, nel quadro che abbiamo appena delineato, una posizione singolare. Ovunque, sulla scia degli Stati Uniti, la nuova congiuntura monetaria internazionale spinge i tassi d’interesse verso l’alto, ma naturalmente non tutti dispongono degli stessi mezzi per attutirne l’impatto. I paesi che avranno maggiori difficoltà ad assorbire lo shock sono quelli in cui le imprese, e con esse l’occupazione, dipendono maggiormente dagli aiuti pubblici, e il cui tessuto industriale devastato non è più in grado di sostenere la crescita. In breve, le economie caratterizzate dai doppi deficit (commerciale e di bilancio) , tra le quali figura la Francia. I tassi d’interesse sul debito francese hanno infatti reagito con una rapidità stupefacente nell’arco di un solo trimestre: dal 3,6% prima dell’estate a quasi il 5% di oggi, il livello più alto degli ultimi venticinque anni[3]. Un brusco ritorno alla realtà: l’ultima volta che lo Stato pagava così caro il denaro preso in prestito, il suo debito ammontava a poco più di 500 miliardi di euro; oggi supera i 3.500 miliardi. Eppure, non si tratta soltanto della Francia: se questa dovesse fallire, l’intero sistema dell’Euro fallirebbe con lei. La Francia si trova sulla linea di faglia di questi movimenti tettonici monetari che mettono in movimento i grandi blocchi mondiali.




Il terreno, già instabile, sta cedendo, in un contesto sociale reso teso da dieci anni di macronismo incoerente e dall’aumento vertiginoso dei prezzi dei carburanti alla pompa: una situazione delicata per un governo ormai privo di margini di manovra sul piano del bilancio pubblico. Se dovesse esplodere un movimento sociale, il manganello sarebbe il mezzo migliore per rassicurare i mercati. Colpirebbe più duramente in quanto l’esecutivo in carica è ormai privo di prospettive elettorali e, pertanto, non ha più nulla da perdere. Ma qualora la repressione non dovesse bastare, la contraddizione potrebbe benissimo spostarsi a un livello superiore, quello di Bruxelles. Che il governo francese non riesca a far approvare un «bilancio di responsabilità», oppure che la BCE accetti, come ultima risorsa, di riacquistare titoli del debito francese per concedergli un po’ di respiro, la «questione francese» finirà per contagiare l’euro. Anzi, ha già cominciato a farlo: dalla fine di agosto, l’euro perde terreno rispetto al dollaro, con il problema che un euro debole rende anche più costose le importazioni di petrolio, fatturate in dollari. Per arrestare il deprezzamento, la BCE dovrebbe aumentare il proprio tasso di riferimento: una doppia pena per le imprese europee, strette nella morsa tra l’aumento del costo del denaro e quello degli idrocarburi.




È nella natura stessa di un’unione monetaria far ricadere sull’insieme dei membri le conseguenze delle difficoltà delle sue singole componenti. Si riproporrà dunque inevitabilmente la stessa questione sollevata negli anni Dieci, durante la crisi dell’Eurozona: perché i paesi «frugali» dovrebbero farsi carico delle conseguenze di un fallimento francese? Ma questa volta il film sarà diverso, perché è cambiato il cast. Nel ruolo del debitore disperato non troviamo più la piccola Grecia, bensì la Francia, 

too

 

big to fail

; in quello del lupo cattivo, una Germania che non è più quella di Schäuble, ma un paese nel quale l’AfD è diventata la seconda forza parlamentare. Lo scenario è più o meno lo stesso negli altri paesi frugali alleati della Germania, dall’Austria alla Finlandia, fino ai Paesi Bassi: nessun governo del Nord potrà firmare un assegno a favore di Parigi senza pagarne successivamente il prezzo alle urne. A questo punto, è vero, non possiamo che formulare delle ipotesi, ma un movimento sociale vigoroso in Francia potrebbe ragionevolmente aprire due possibilità.




La prima, probabilmente la meno dolorosa, consisterebbe nell’affrontare la causa dei problemi più immediati: la crisi dei carburanti. L’aumento dei prezzi non cade dal cielo: è la conseguenza cumulativa di due guerre imperialiste, in Ucraina e in Iran. Nel breve periodo, il modo più pragmatico per gestirla comporterebbe, per gli europei, l’avvio di un processo di pace sul fronte orientale, al fine di ristabilire la regolarità degli approvvigionamenti dalla Russia.                                                             La seconda possibilità consisterebbe nel gestire le conseguenze di un’insolvenza francese (vale a dire l’incapacità di imporre al proprio proletariato un nuovo piano di austerità) all’interno dell’Eurozona, forse al prezzo di una frammentazione negoziata dell’area monetaria. Piuttosto che assistere all’uscita fragorosa di una grande economia dall’Eurozona, si avrebbe una sorta di quiet quitting collettivo, che consisterebbe nel creare, per ciascun sistema nazionale, euro di qualità differenti, dotati di tassi di cambio variabili. Ciò restituirebbe flessibilità alle politiche monetarie nazionali, dispensando al tempo stesso i paesi frugali dal farsi carico dell’aggiustamento necessario a sostenere le economie più traballanti. In questo modo si isolerebbe il «problema Francia», sancendo al contempo, in maniera collettiva e negoziata, la fine della moneta unica.




Attraverso l’anello più debole?




Questa ricostruzione della questione monetaria mostra fino a che punto l’«anello francese» sia vulnerabile e quale portata potrebbe assumere un movimento capace di mettere alle strette la borghesia francese. Un movimento del genere, in ultima analisi, non le lascerebbe che due vie d’uscita: porre fine alla guerra imperialista a Est oppure sacrificare lo strumento monetario del proprio imperialismo 

lumpen

, l’euro. Per queste ragioni, non possiamo considerare il movimento attuale, capace di scuotere la struttura dell’imperialismo, come una semplice data nell’agenda militante, come l’ennesima ripresa autunnale delle mobilitazioni sociali, e nemmeno solo come un’occasione simpatica per fare casino. Perché, in queste circostanze, la cosa più disastrosa sarebbe che un movimento emergesse per poi lasciarsi risucchiare dalla consueta drammaturgia delle manifestazioni sindacali, dello sciopero del martedì e del 

cortège de tete

 (spezzone di testa  del corteo, n.d.t). Che si lasciasse così ricondurre alle rivendicazioni di routine: difesa degli «interessi del servizio pubblico» (intesi nel senso proprio del termine), tassazione dei ricchi, convergenza delle lotte e, perché no, un programma di noleggio agevolato per i veicoli elettrici, per finire docilmente relegato tra le voci del prossimo bilancio pubblico. Al contrario, è il suo potenziale di rottura che bisogna mettere in primo piano, convincendo i partecipanti al movimento della sua portata storica e portando lo scontro sulle questioni bandite dai dibattiti televisivi, quelle che contano davvero, perché hanno una portata sistemica e internazionale, cioè gli aiuti ad imprese che prosciugano le casse della previdenza sociale; la moneta forte che permette alle multinazionali francesi di arricchirsi all’estero mentre impoveriscono il tessuto economico nazionale e il finanziamento di una guerra imperialista di cui paghiamo il prezzo alla pompa della benzina. Tutte aspetti della configurazione esistente che un movimento del genere potrebbe rimettere in discussione.




Note




[1] Benn Steil, «America is losing its captive creditors» (L’America sta perdendo i suoi creditori vincolati), Financial Times, 10 settembre 2026.




https://www.ft.com/content/a441ea66-329a-4f42-8e50-3ff140958e53




[2] Euan Healy, Emily Herbert, Michelle Chan, «AI hyperscalers are transforming debt» (Gli hyperscaler dell’intelligenza artificiale stanno trasformando il mercato del debito), Financial Times, 28 settembre 2026.




https://www.ft.com/content/00f94018-e658-4545-b16e-1bc00e19b754?syn-25a6b1a6=1




Estratti selezionati:




«Il presidente della Federal Reserve, Kevin Warsh, e il segretario al Tesoro americano, Scott Bessent, sostengono che gli hyperscaler competono sul mercato dei capitali con quello dei buoni del Tesoro statunitensi, che vale 31.000 miliardi di dollari e sul quale, la settimana scorsa, i costi di finanziamento a dieci anni hanno raggiunto il livello più alto dal 2007».




«Questa frenesia nella raccolta di capitali sta trasformando il modo in cui il mondo prende denaro in prestito, influenzando dove, quando e a quale costo le imprese e i governi emettono titoli di debito. Alcuni hanno dichiarato che potrebbe trattarsi del più grande sconvolgimento dalla nascita del mercato delle euro-obbligazioni negli anni Sessanta».




[3] Questi tassi sono tassi nominali. Per calcolare il tasso reale, occorre sottrarre il tasso d’inflazione, poiché quest’ultima aumenta «meccanicamente» le entrate dello Stato e la sua capacità di rimborso. Se ci basiamo sulle previsioni dell’INSEE — 2,6% per l’anno in corso —, i tassi reali si attesterebbero attualmente intorno al 2,5%.

author: Marjorie Cohn
title: As Trump Sabotages the ICC With Sanctions, There Are Many Ways to Fight Back
content:
Trump officials now face a temporary restraining order for violating the First Amendment by sanctioning US groups.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

The U.S. government has long sought to incapacitate the International Criminal Court (ICC), the world’s first global court that was created to prosecute the most atrocious crimes. As the ICC seeks to provide accountability for Israeli crimes, the Trump administration has become increasingly aggressive in its attempts to hobble the court. On October 9, 2026, Team Trump imposed punitive sanctions against the court itself, which constitutes the gravest intensification of its war on the ICC. But there are several strategies available to mitigate the worst effects of these sanctions.

In February 2025, Donald Trump issued Executive Order 14203, which authorizes the imposition of sanctions against the ICC. The sanctions amount to illegal unilateral coercive measures because only the UN Security Council has the authority to impose sanctions.

The executive order prohibits U.S. persons from providing material support or services to certain designated persons and entities, including financial services. It exposes non-U.S. persons to secondary sanctions for engaging in conduct prohibited under the order. U.S. persons who violate it may face criminal penalties of up to 20 years imprisonment and fines of up to $1 million.

Trump’s 2025 order has led to the sanctioning of nine of the ICC’s 18 judges, three ICC prosecutors, the ICC president, and a senior ICC trial attorney. The Trump administration also sanctioned three highly respected Palestinian human rights organizations — Al-Haq, Al Mezan, and the Palestinian Centre for Human Rights — for their assistance to the ICC. Francesca Albanese, UN Special Rapporteur on Occupied Palestine, who wrote three courageous reports documenting Israel’s genocide in Gaza, was sanctioned as well.

In December 2025, a top Trump administration official told Reuters there was “growing concern” that “the ICC will turn its attention to the president, to the vice president, to the secretary of war and others, and pursue prosecutions against them,” adding that this was “unacceptable, and we will not allow it to happen.” He said the ICC had been warned that unless it amended the Rome Statute to ensure it would not investigate Trump and his top officials, new and very severe U.S. sanctions would be imposed on the court.

Sure enough, in an attempt to permanently paralyze the court, the Trump administration sanctioned the entire ICC on October 9, pursuant to Executive Order 14203. These harsh financial sanctions prevent the court from using U.S. dollars and U.S.-based financial services and technology companies. They bar U.S. citizens and companies from supplying the court with funds, goods, or services without a license from the U.S. Treasury.

U.S. sanctions have serious impacts on targeted individuals, whose bank accounts can be frozen or closed. Their financial transactions can be rejected, and they can be denied access to digital services and entry into the United States. Sanctions have a chilling effect on non-U.S. banks and other companies outside the jurisdiction of the United States; they themselves could lose access to the U.S. banking system. The ICC could lose access to companies on which it relies for its critical functions, including banking, information, technology, and travel.

Although the sanctions contain a six-month wind-down period and exemptions for certain services, they still pose significant risks. In the face of global reliance on the U.S. financial and IT systems, even non-U.S. service providers, including banks, might stop providing services to the ICC for fear of penalties or reprisals by the U.S. Treasury. This could affect the court’s ability to maintain a bank account, receive financial contributions from States Parties, pay staff, make payments, and maintain essential operations.

The imposition of these outrageous sanctions is the latest, and most devastating, chapter in the U.S.’s long campaign to undermine the ICC. Moreover, these sanctions were imposed on the same day that the Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to Navi Pillay, a South African lawyer who served as a judge on the ICC for five years and led the UN Commission of Inquiry in 2025 that confirmed Israel’s commission of genocide in Gaza.

The International Criminal Court, which became operational in 2002, is a permanent international court created to prosecute individuals for genocide, war crimes, crimes against humanity, and the crime of aggression. Nearly two-thirds of the nations in the world have ratified the Rome Statute, thereby becoming States Parties and taking responsibility for arresting and sending those under warrants to the ICC for trial. The court was established to complement, not replace, national criminal justice systems. It will assume jurisdiction only when national systems are unwilling or unable to prosecute.

Bill Clinton signed the ICC’s Rome Statute in 2000 as his presidential term was ending, but George W. Bush removed the U.S. signature from it in 2002. The U.S. Congress then enacted the “The Hague Invasion Act,” which says that if a national of the U.S. or its ally (which includes Israel) is detained by the ICC in The Hague, the U.S. military can use armed force to extricate them. The Bush administration effectively blackmailed 100 States Parties to the Rome Statute by forcing them to sign bilateral immunity agreements in which they promised not to turn over U.S. persons to the ICC, or the U.S. would withhold their foreign aid.

In November 2024, after an investigation lasting more than three years, the ICC issued arrest warrants for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and former Defense Minister Yoav Gallant. They stand charged with the war crimes of starvation as a form of warfare, and intentional attacks on civilians; and the crimes against humanity of murder, persecution, and other inhumane acts, for their actions in Gaza since October 7, 2023.

The U.S. contends that the ICC has no jurisdiction over Israeli (or U.S.) nationals since neither Israel nor the U.S. are States Parties to the Rome Statute. However, the statute authorizes the ICC to exercise territorial jurisdiction over crimes committed by non-State Party nationals in the territory of a State Party. Palestine is a State Party to the statute, so the ICC determined that it has jurisdiction over crimes allegedly committed by Israeli nationals in Palestine. Indeed, the U.S. has supported several ICC investigations and prosecutions of crimes allegedly committed by non-State Party nationals, including the arrest warrant that the court issued for Russian President Vladimir Putin.

On July 13, 2026, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio pledged to “dismantle” the International Criminal Court. He accused the ICC of “waging a war against our country, not with bullets or missiles,” but with “the force of so-called international law.” Venezuela and Chad announced their withdrawal from the Rome Statute following U.S. threats to reduce or withdraw assistance if they refused to do so.

On July 13, 2026, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio pledged to “dismantle” the International Criminal Court.

Meanwhile, the court faces a leadership vacuum following the firing in July 2026 of the ICC’s former chief prosecutor Karim Khan, who had requested the issuance of the arrest warrants against Netanyahu and Gallant. UN investigators said they “found evidence that Mr. Khan engaged in ‘non-consensual sexual contact’” with a lawyer who had worked as a special assistant to him in 2023. But after a three-month review of a 152-page report by the Office of Internal Oversight Services and of the 5,000+ pages of underpinning material, the Ad Hoc Panel of Judicial Experts unanimously determined that the facts did not establish evidence beyond a reasonable doubt of any wrongdoing on the part of Khan. Nevertheless, the Assembly of States Parties to the Rome Statute voted to fire him with no due process on July 24.

In December 2026, the assembly will elect six judges to fill one-third of the ICC’s 18 judicial seats. The U.S. will invariably endeavor to interfere with those elections.

On July 15, Democracy for the Arab World Now and the Taxpayer Alliance Against Genocide filed a lawsuit in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York, alleging that Trump’s EO 14203 violates the constitutional right to engage in Palestine-related human rights advocacy. They claimed that the sanctions violate the First Amendment by limiting what people in the U.S. can say to an international tribunal or to foreign advocates, and by limiting their ability to associate with sanctioned parties.

In December 2026, the assembly will elect six judges to fill one-third of the ICC’s 18 judicial seats. The U.S. will invariably endeavor to interfere with those elections.

U.S. District Judge Jesse M. Furman granted Democracy for the Arab World Now and the Taxpayer Alliance Against Genocide a temporary restraining order on October 13, which temporarily blocks the Trump administration from imposing civil or criminal penalties on the two organizations for supporting ICC’s investigations into alleged war crimes and crimes against humanity in Gaza. The judge said the two organizations were likely to prevail on their claims that Trump’s sanctions violated the First Amendment.

Democracy for the Arab World Now announced it would immediately resume its advocacy with the ICC for the prosecution of Israeli and U.S. perpetrators of grave crimes, and it will work with the three sanctioned human rights groups and the Special Rapporteur.

On August 11, the American Friends Service Committee, the Center for Constitutional Rights, Human Rights Watch, and the Open Society Institute filed a lawsuit in the same New York federal court, alleging that Trump’s executive order violates the U.S. Constitution; U.S. statutes; and international law, including the Genocide Convention, Geneva Conventions, and customary international law.

On October 12, the Coalition for the International Criminal Court (CICC), comprised of more than 120 organizations from over 60 countries representing all regions of the world, and dozens of legal experts, human rights defenders, and members of the EU, issued a joint statement, urging States Parties to act now to protect the ICC from unlawful U.S. sanctions.

The statement condemned “unequivocally and in the strongest terms the decision by the United States to impose unlawful sanctions on the International Criminal Court.” The CICC said, “This unprecedented measure represents a direct attack against the rule of law, the independence of the Court and international justice, ultimately undermining the rights of millions of victims and survivors of mass atrocities worldwide.”

The CICC listed 12 actions that States Parties should take, individually and collectively, to protect the court. They include the immediate adoption or activation of blocking measures at the national and regional levels; for example, the immediate adoption of the EU Blocking Statute and equivalent domestic legislation elsewhere. Blocking measures would shield those sanctioned, including the court and its officials, the UN Special Rapporteur, and civil society organizations, from the extraterritorial reach of the sanctions.

In addition, the CICC urges States Parties to guarantee that the court and those cooperating with it have access to banking and other essential services; to find concrete measures to mitigate the impact of sanctions on civic space, freedom of speech, and freedom of association; and to explore all possible diplomatic and legal avenues to challenge the sanctions and their legality under international law, including by supporting U.S. legal challenges and a referral to the International Court of Justice.

And the CICC implores States Parties to refuse, “without exception,” coercion by a non-State Party to influence votes, positions, or conduct within the Assembly of States Parties or any other body of the Rome Statute system.

The battle to save the ICC and its capacity to enforce accountability for the most heinous crimes is one struggle with many fronts: local, regional, national, and international.

Truthout is one of only a few platforms for justice-oriented, grassroots journalism. Today, we face an existential threat.

Due to Google’s launch of AI search, we’ve seen a drastic plunge in our site traffic and, as a result, our revenue. We lost 15 percent of our readership overnight. This was a readership we painstakingly built over decades, and it vanished because Google chose corporate greed over a healthy democracy.

We are fundraising right now to meet our basic operating expenses. If you can support Truthout with a one-time or monthly donation, you will make a significant impact on our work. Anything you can do makes a difference — we appreciate your support.

title: Öcalan: The future of the Middle East lies not in new wars but in building a democratic society
content:
A conference titled “Democratic Confederalism in Kurdistan: A Perspective for Peace in the Middle East” has begun in Turin, Italy.




The conference, organized with the support of the Kurdistan Information Office in Italy (UIKI) and the Verso il Kurdistan Association, is being held at the conference hall of the Metropolitan City of Turin on Corso Inghilterra.




The conference, attended by Kurdish politicians, Italian parliamentarians, local government officials, academics, and representatives of the women’s movement, is discussing a democratic solution to the Kurdish question and the prospects for peace in the Middle East.










https://1649452211.rsc.cdn77.org/20261017113704_2026-10-17-torino-demoktatik-konfederalizm-konferansi-acilis-1.mp4











The conference is attended by Davide Nicco, President of the Piedmont Regional Council; Michela Favaro, Deputy Mayor of Turin; Ayşe Serra Bucak Küçük, Co-Mayor of Amed Metropolitan Municipality; Antonio Olivieri, President of the Verso il Kurdistan Association; and Yılmaz Orkanda, Director of UIKI.




The conference consists of three sessions. The first session will address democratic confederalism as an alternative model for the Middle East, developments in Rojava, and the struggles in Iran and Shengal.




The afternoon sessions will focus on the Peace and Democratic Society Process in Turkey, Öcalan’s freedom, international solidarity, and the struggle for women’s liberation.




Kurdish leader Abdullah Öcalan sent a message sent to the conference, stating the following:




“Dear friends,




I greet you from İmralı with feelings of international solidarity and freedom. I hope your conference will contribute to equality and freedom among peoples and the establishment of lasting peace in the Middle East.




The Middle East is currently at a critical turning point. Wars, conflicts, nation-state solutions, and security-oriented policies have failed to bring peace and freedom to the peoples of the region. This is now clear. Therefore, our fundamental task is to abandon the politics of war, embrace democratic politics, organize society, and build a new era that guarantees the equal and free coexistence of peoples.




Democratic confederalism and the perspective of a Democratic Republic are among the central issues in this search for a solution.




The dissolution of the PKK and the end of its strategy of armed struggle should be seen as the beginning of a new era. This change also requires a new perspective on the issue.




It must be stated clearly that the end of armed struggle does not, in itself, mean peace. For peace to become lasting at the end of this process, the root causes of the conflict must be eliminated, Kurdish identity, language, and culture must be guaranteed, obstacles to democratic politics must be removed, and equal citizenship must be secured by law.




Democratic integration does not mean unilateral adaptation or unconditional participation in the existing system. On the contrary, it must be a democratic transformation in which differences are not denied, rights are recognized, and coexistence is established on the basis of equality.




The political expression of democratic politics is the Democratic Republic, while the guarantee of a democratic society is the rule of law. Without legal guarantees, democratic politics cannot become sustainable, nor can the peace process succeed.




The resolution of the Kurdish question cannot be considered separately from the democratization of Turkey. Likewise, Turkey’s democratization is inseparable from the emergence of a political will that enables peoples to live together freely and equally.




This is precisely where the significance of the democratic confederalism perspective for the Middle East lies. The solution is not to assimilate peoples into a single identity, turn borders and differences into sources of new conflicts, or create new forms of state domination.




What is needed today is this: democratic politics instead of the politics of war, recognition instead of denial, law instead of coercion, and free and equal coexistence instead of social fragmentation. This transformation requires states and political actors to assume responsibility, democratic institutions to be strengthened, and society to have a voice and decision-making power over its own future.




Dear friends,




I hope this conference will discuss the perspective of democratic confederalism in the context of today’s conditions and identify concrete paths toward a democratic solution.




The future of the Middle East lies not in new wars or new forms of domination, but in building a democratic society. Liberation lies in the free unity of peoples and the strengthening of democratic politics.




Politics must replace weapons, the rule of law must replace mistrust, and equality must replace denial. This is the path to lasting peace.




Once again, I extend my greetings to your conference with my unwavering belief in peace and freedom.




Abdullah Öcalan




İmralı”

Корреспондент газеты Avanti! из Йези, сообщая о публичном выступлении против принудительной ссылки[1], которую я провёл в этом городе, пишет: «… Он добавил (оратор), что огромная вина (за рабскую покорность, с которой народ терпел притеснения правительства и капиталистов) лежит на анархической партии и республиканской партии, которые, проповедовав столь долго революцию, осознают невозможность её совершить, поскольку народ, совершенно несознательный, за ними не пойдёт»[2].

Так оно и было – это действительно то, что я сказал; но курсив, разумеется, корреспондент добавил от себя, и этот курсив в социал-демократической газете служит для того, чтобы хорошенько отметить (и, возможно, похвастаться), что я, критикуя мою партию и республиканскую, исключал из критики социал-демократов.

Это требует некоторого объяснения.

В Йези я говорил о разочарованиях, последовавших за надеждами, возбуждёнными итальянской национальной революцией, и говорил о том, как, с одной стороны, экономическое положение пролетариата становилось всё более тяжёлым, а с другой – постепенно утрачивалась та небольшая свобода, которую завоевала революция, вплоть до возвращения в состояние, равное или худшее тому, в котором находились при павших правительствах.

И я старался объяснить этот факт двумя рядами причин.

Во-первых, тенденцией, которую имеют общественные учреждения развиваться в определённом направлении и производить свои естественные следствия: тенденцией политической власти всегда расширять свою сферу действия и становиться всё более угнетающей; и тенденцией частной собственности захватывать все средства производства, всё более усиливать эксплуатацию работника и обращать во вред пролетариату все новые достижения науки и общественного прогресса.

Во-вторых, отсутствием народного сопротивления. И в этом отсутствии сопротивления, оставляя в стороне другие причины общего порядка, не входившие в цель того моего публичного выступления, я обвинял республиканцев и анархистов.

И те и другие, сознавая коренную несправедливость определённых учреждений и те дурные последствия, которые они фатально должны были принести, заботились только о полном и внезапном разрушении этих учреждений, презирая всё, что могло бы смягчить эти дурные последствия, – более того, желая, чтобы они проявились как можно острее, в надежде, что это вызовет и ускорит падение учреждений.

Республиканцы, естественно враждебные монархии, все беды возводили к конституционному [монархическому] режиму и либо не считали возможным, либо по тактике делали вид, что презирают любое улучшение, любую реформу, отправной точкой которой не было бы упразднение монархии.

Анархисты, противники всякого правительства и, следовательно, монархии, и противники частной собственности, ждали – по идее, аналогичной идее республиканцев, – всякого блага от радикального преобразования общественной организации, презирая улучшения, к которым может быть восприимчив нынешний режим, и, может быть, желая – всё в той же надежде ускорить конфликт – роста угнетения и нищеты.

Так вся деятельность двух партий сводилась к проповеди революции. Что же касается того, чтобы сделать её возможной и подготовить её, то они не умели делать ничего другого, как только вербовать в соответствующие организации приверженцев, по необходимости немногочисленных, и собирать оружие, которое из-за отсутствия средств и бдительности правительства всегда было мало и плохо и в конце концов обычно либо конфисковывалось, либо ржавело и становилось непригодным. К этому, мадзинисты сначала, а анархисты потом, добавляли развлечение с той или иной более или менее безобидной бомбой.

Между тем приверженцы, оттого что ждали революцию, ничего не делая, в конце концов совсем засыпали; а массы народа – по крайней мере та их часть, которая имела хоть какое-то сознание и могла бы что-то сделать, – слыша постоянно, что без революции ничего нельзя добиться, позволяла правительству и хозяевам угнетать и эксплуатировать себя в своё удовольствие… а также ждала революции. Революционный дух, возбуждённый в Европе великой французской революцией и сохранявшийся живым в первой половине века в Италии более, чем где-либо, – теперь, когда, из-за изменившихся условий и изменившихся целей, революцию нельзя было больше делать старыми методами, – мало-помалу угасал; и правительство смогло наконец позволить себе всё, не встречая никакого серьёзного сопротивления. И более того, очень часто случалось, что рабочие, когда собственными силами умели организоваться и добиться какого-то улучшения, отдалялись более чем когда-либо от революционеров, чьи предсказания и чьи намерения противоречили достигнутым результатам; так что достигнутые успехи, вместо того чтобы служить, как должны были бы и могли бы, приближению полного освобождения народа, становились новыми элементами сохранения рабства.

Этим ошибкам, этому методу классических революционеров, которому мы долго следовали, я противопоставлял своё убеждение, которое теперь является убеждением почти всех наших товарищей: что буржуазные учреждения могут, вынужденные сопротивлением и народной угрозой, ещё многое уступить, прежде чем дойти до точки, когда они должны будут неизбежно пасть, более или менее насильственной смертью; что в интересах революционеров вырвать у правительства и хозяев все возможные уступки – как чтобы уменьшить нынешние страдания народа, так и чтобы скорее добраться до окончательной битвы; и что народ тем более способен к революции, чем лучше его материальные и моральные условия и чем больше он приобрёл сознание собственной силы и привычку и способность бороться в сопротивлении и в непрерывной борьбе за улучшение условий жизни. Поэтому я заключал, поощряя к сопротивлению против закона о ссылке на поселение, который будет первым опытом – надеемся, победоносным – того, что народ может уже теперь, даже мирно и законно, против правительственного произвола, если только сумеет показать свою волю.

Во всём этом я не упомянул социал-демократическую партию по простой причине: в тот период итальянской истории, к которому я относился, её не существовало. Она родилась в Италии как раз как следствие наших ошибок и упадка революционного духа народа; и она падёт или сведётся к партии простых политиканов в тот день, когда мы, наученные опытом наших прошлых неудач, сможем развернуть среди масс нашу деятельность, – и в итальянском народе пробудится уснувший революционный дух.

Впрочем, социал-демократы были бы неправы, если бы захотели похвастаться этими «признаниями анархиста», поскольку нашим ошибкам, общим для всех старых революционных школ, мы в значительной степени обязаны марксистским теориям, сторонниками которых все анархисты были когда-то – более логичными, если не более ортодоксальными, чем те, кто считал себя марксистом, и, возможно, чем сам Маркс, – и от которых мы избавлялись по мере того, как освобождались от ошибок марксизма.

[2] Avanti! (Рим) 1, №265 (17 сент. 1897).

[3] Под этим псевдонимом прячется Эррико Малатеста, который находился в Италии на тот момент нелегально.

author: Radikal Perspektif
title: Yabancılaşma
content:
Yazan: David Graeber




Çeviren: Gorthim




Çevirilen Asıl Metin




PDF Linki







Yabancılaşma kavramı oldukça sıra dışı bir kavramdır; zira bu kavram, bir yandan yaygın bir duyguyu —çok öznel, bir bakıma tanımlanamaz bir duyguyu— açıklamaya yönelik bir girişim, diğer yandan da bu duyguyu düzenli olarak üreten her türlü toplumun doğasına yönelik bir eleştiri niteliğindedir.




Bu her zaman böyle değildi. Kişinin dünyada kendini evinde hissetmemesi, çevresinden, kendinden ve diğer insanlardan yabancılaşma hissi, tarih kadar eski gibi görünmektedir; çoğu dünya dininde (Budizm, Hristiyanlığın çoğu mezhebi ve Taoizm, İslam’daki Sufi akımları) bu duygu, esas olarak insanlık durumunun gerçeğine dair derin bir içgörüyü yansıttığı şeklinde değerlendirilirdi. Keşişler, rahipler ve meditasyon yapanlar, daha yüce bir şeye ulaşmanın bir yolu olarak yabancılaşma duygularını sıklıkla aktif bir şekilde değer vermiş veya beslemişlerdir. Kalvinizm, izolasyon ve boşluk duygularını insanlığın lütuftan düşüşünün bir işareti olarak görerek modern kavrayışa daha çok yaklaşmış olsa da, bu terimin modern anlamı aslında ancak on dokuzuncu yüzyılda ortaya çıkmıştır. Bu kavrayış, geniş, kişiliksiz, endüstriyel bir şehirde yaşama deneyimiyle yakından bağlantılıydı. Yabancılaşma duyguları, özellikle önceki nesillerde melankolinin muhtemel kurbanları olarak görülebilecek kişileri etkilemeye meyilliydi: entelektüeller, sanatçılar ve gençler. Etkileri de hemen hemen aynıydı: depresyon, kaygı, umutsuzluk, intihar.




Modern yabancılaşma literatüründe iki ana akım ayırt edilebilir: Birincisi, deneyimin kendisini modern yaşamın şahsi olmayan, bürokratik doğasının kaçınılmaz (ancak muhtemelen hafifletilebilir) bir sonucu olarak vurgulayan ve bu deneyimi, dünya hakkında daha derin, daha gerçek bir gerçeğe ulaşmak için kullanma yeteneğinin yitirilmesini beraberinde getiren bir akımdır — zira Tanrı’nın ve geleneksel otorite yapılarının ortadan kalkmasıyla birlikte, bu gerçeklerin çoğunun kesin olarak yitirildiği kabul ediliyordu. Diğeri ise, daha eski teolojik geleneklerden yararlanarak, yabancılaşmayı modern (yani kapitalist, endüstriyel) düzenin kendisinin gerçek, gizli doğasının anahtarı olarak görür ve bunun, ancak o düzenin devrilip yerine kökten farklı bir şeyin getirilmesiyle çözülebilecek dayanılmaz bir durum olduğunu ortaya koyar.




İlk gelenek, Alexis de Tocqueville, Émile Durkheim veya Max Weber gibi sosyal düşünürlerde; Fyodor Dostoyevski veya Franz Kafka gibi romancılarda; ve Søren Kierkegaard veya Friedrich Nietzsche gibi filozoflarda görülebilir. Burada yabancılaşma, modernliğin tüm olumlu değerlerinin karanlık yüzüdür; topluluk, hiyerarşi, kutsal gibi önceki tüm anlam kaynaklarından kopmuş olanların deneyimidir. Bu, bireyciliğin yalnızlığa, özgürlüğün köksüzlüğe, eşitlikçiliğin tüm değerlerin yok edilmesine, rasyonalitenin ise demir bir kafese dönüştüğü noktadır.




Muhtemelen bu türdeki en ünlü kavram, Émile Durkheim’ın (1858–1917) anomi kavramıdır. Hem ekonomik yükseliş hem de ekonomik çöküş dönemlerinde intihar oranlarının artma eğiliminde olduğunu gözlemleyen Durkheim, bunun tek nedeninin, hem yükselişlerin hem de çöküşlerin sıradan insanların beklentilerini tamamen altüst etmesi olduğu sonucuna vardı; bu durum, insanların normlardan yoksun bir duruma düşmelerine, hayattan neyi bekleme veya isteme hakkına sahip olduklarını belirleyememelerine ve bunu yapabilecekleri bir zamanı hayal edememelerine yol açıyordu. Bu tür bir analiz, ya modern toplumdaki kamusal yaşamın asla gerçek anlamda yabancılaşmadan başka bir şey olamayacağına dair (sosyal muhafazakarlar tarafından benimsenen) bir varsayım olan boyun eğen bir karamsarlığa ya da yabancılaşmayı bir sapma biçimi ya da uygun entegrasyon eksikliği olarak gören ve politik karar vericilerin ideal olarak bunu hafifletebilmesi, hatta aşabilmesi gerektiğini savunan liberal bir yaklaşıma yol açabilirdi.




Diğer gelenek ise, teolojik kaynaklardan büyük ölçüde yararlanan Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel’e (1770–1831) kadar uzanır. Hegel için “yabancılaşma”, Ruh’un

1

 (Hegel’e göre Ruh, aynı anda hem Tanrı, hem Zihin, hem Ruh hem de İnsanın Özbilinciydi) gerçek özbilgiye ulaşacağı sürecin vazgeçilmez bir aşaması olan teknik bir terimdi. İnsanlık tarihi de aynı öyküyü barındırıyordu: Zihin kendini dünyaya yansıtarak, örneğin Hukuk’u, Sanatı, Bilimi ya da Devleti yaratırdı; daha sonra kendi yarattıklarıyla, kendisine yabancı ve garip gelen bir şey olarak yüzleşirdi; nihayetinde ise bu yabancılaşmış biçimlerin aslında kendisinin farklı yönleri olduğunu kavrayarak, onları yeniden bünyesine katar ve sonuç olarak daha zengin bir benlik algısına ulaşırdı.




Karl Marx (1818–1883) bu diyalektik yaklaşıma sadık kaldı, ancak emeğin maddi yaratıcılığına odaklanarak, kapitalizm altında sadece kişinin emeğinin ürünlerinin değil, emeğinin kendisinin, yani kişinin yaratma yeteneğinin —ve Marx için bu, kişinin insanlığının ta kendisidir— alınıp satılabilen bir meta haline geldiğini ve dolayısıyla işçiye “yabancı bir güç” olarak göründüğünü vurguladı. Marx, Hegel’in iyimserliğini paylaşıyor ve bu ikilemi yeni, devrimci bir topluma giden yolu açan bir unsur olarak görüyor; bu bakımdan tüm bunlar, yabancılaşmanın ne kadar acı verici olursa olsun kişinin dünyayla olan ilişkisinin gerçeğini fark etmesini sağlayan ve dolayısıyla bunu anlamanın yabancılaşmayı aşmanın anahtarı haline geldiği şeklindeki eski, teolojik anlayışla büyük ölçüde uyumludur. Ancak yirminci yüzyıl Marksistleri bu kadar tekdüze bir iyimserlik sergilememişlerdir.




Marksist rejimler kendi toplumlarında yabancılaşma sorununu ortadan kaldırdıklarını resmen iddia ederken, György Lukács (1885–1971) ile başlayıp Frankfurt Okulu ile doruğa ulaşan Batı Marksizmi, endüstriyel demokrasilerde devrimci bir değişimin yaşanmamasını açıklamak zorunda kalarak, modern yaşamdaki çeşitli yabancılaşma biçimleri (şeyleştirme, nesneleştirme, fetişizm vb.) üzerine uzun soluklu bir düşünce süreci haline geldi. Bu vurgu, yirminci yüzyılın ortalarında konuyla ilgili çok sayıda eserin ortaya çıkmasına zemin hazırladı; bu eserlerin hepsi Marksist değildi.




1950’lerde ve 1960’ların başlarında Fransa’da, izole olmuş birey için bir ahlak anlayışı oluşturmaya çalışan Jean-Paul Sartre ve Albert Camus’nun varoluşçuluğundan, çeşitli Marksist yaklaşımlara kadar uzanan, son derece zengin bir yabancılaşma teorisi külliyatı ortaya çıktı. Bu yaklaşımların en abartılı —ve en ilham verici— olanı, Situasyonist Enternasyonal tarafından geliştirilmiştir; bu örgütün üyeleri, modern tüketim toplumunu devasa bir “gösteri” olarak görmüşlerdir; bu gösteri, yalnızca medya imgelerinden değil, aynı zamanda piyasa mantığından, uzmanların egemenliğinden ve meta biçiminin doğasından oluşan geniş bir aygıttır; tüm bu unsurlar bir araya gelerek bireyleri kendi hayatlarının pasif ve izole edilmiş seyircileri haline getirmektedir. Ortaya çıktıkları birçok radikal sanat akımı gibi, Situasyonistler de kapitalist yabancılaşmanın “yaşayan ölümü”nü aşmanın bir yolu olarak, kendilerini gündelik hayatın kendisini devrimci bir şekilde dönüştürmenin yollarını hayal etmeye adamışlardı.




Fransa’da Mayıs 1968’de gerçekleşen başarısız ayaklanmanın ardından, bu yabancılaşma literatürü, öznenin kendisinin de bir söylem etkisi ve dolayısıyla toplumsal bir kurgu olduğu gerekçesiyle toplumdan ya da kendinden yabancılaşmış bir insan öznesinden söz etmenin imkânsız olduğunu savunan postyapısalcı eleştiriler karşısında hızla ortadan kayboldu. 1970’ler ve 1980’ler boyunca bu eleştiriler Fransa’nın dışına yayıldı ve sonuç olarak yabancılaşma teması, yirmi birinci yüzyılın başlarında entelektüel tartışmalardan büyük ölçüde kayboldu.




İki temel istisna bulunmaktadır. Birincisi, yabancılaşma kavramı, radikal ve kurtarıcı biçimiyle, büyük ölçüde akademi dışındaki sanatsal ve devrimci çevrelerde hâlâ canlılığını korumaktadır. Örneğin, Situasyonizm, her ikisi de büyük ölçüde “ana akım” kentsel, endüstriyel veya postendüstriyel yaşamın anlamsızlığına ve yabancılaşmasına karşı birer isyan niteliği taşıyan (giderek daha uluslararası hale gelen) anarşist ve punk sahnelerinin hâlâ tam merkezinde yer almaktadır. Bu temalar, “küreselleşme karşıtı” hareketin yükselişiyle birlikte aniden kamuoyunun dikkatini yeniden çekmiş olsa da, akademide hâlâ neredeyse hiç yankı bulamamıştır.




İkincisi, daha liberal ve iyileştirici biçimiyle yabancılaşma kavramı, sosyolojinin belirli dallarında yer edindi ve dolayısıyla giderek daha fazla “postmodern” yabancılaşma teorisi olarak adlandırılan akımda yeniden ortaya çıktı. Amerikalı sosyologlar 1950’lerde ve 1960’larda yabancılaşma temasını sistematik olarak ele almaya başladıklarında, öncelikle bunu nicelendirilebilir bir faktör haline getirdiler. Bireyin yabancılaşma derecesini ölçmeye yönelik çeşitli anketler ve tablolaştırma teknikleri geliştirildi; anketler daha sonra, pek de şaşırtıcı olmayan bir şekilde, öğrenciler dışında yabancılaşma puanları en yüksek olanların tam da yabancılar, göçmenler ya da zaten ana akım Amerikan yaşamının kenarında yer alan azınlık gruplarının üyeleri olduğunu ortaya koydu. 1990’lar ve yirmi birinci yüzyılın başlarında, bu sosyolojik çalışmalar, kimlik ve kimliğe dayalı toplumsal hareketlere duyulan ilgiyle birleşerek, yeni bir “postmodern” yabancılaşma teorisi külliyatı ortaya çıkardı.




Bireysel düzeyde, yabancılaşmanın, kişinin kendi kendini tanımlaması ile daha geniş bir toplum tarafından kendisine atfedilen kimlik arasında bir çatışma olduğu zaman ortaya çıktığı söylenir. Böylece yabancılaşma, çeşitli baskı biçimlerinin (ırkçılık, cinsiyetçilik, yaş ayrımcılığı vb.) mağdurlar tarafından fiilen deneyimlendiği ve içselleştirildiği öznel bir biçim haline gelir. Sonuç olarak, eski devrimci anlayış yabancılaşmayı “ana akım”ın temelde şiddet içeren, insanlık karşıtı doğasının vazgeçilmez bir parçası olarak görürken, postmodern teoriler yabancılaşmayı yeniden ana akımdan dışlanmanın bir ölçüsü olarak görmektedir. Toplumsal düzeyde, postmodern yabancılaşma anlayışının, özgürlüğün eksikliğinden ziyade fazlalığından kaynaklandığı söylenir; bu görüş, on dokuzuncu yüzyılın sonlarında “modern” yabancılaşma kavramları olarak adlandırılanlardan neredeyse ayırt edilemez görünmektedir. Şimdiye kadar, bu iki gelenek birbirleriyle neredeyse hiç temas kurmamıştır—belki de son zamanlarda ortaya çıkan “doğadan yabancılaşma” konusundaki çevreci fikirler hariç. Bu iki geleneğin nasıl temas kuracağı ya da kurup kurmayacağı ise hâlâ açık bir sorudur.

title: Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya’nın ablası büyükelçilik görevine başladı
content:
Fon vurgununda yaklaşık 2 milyar TL kazandığı ortaya çıkan ve malvarlığı dondurulduğu öne sürülen AKP'li eski Aile ve Sosyal Politikalar Bakanı Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya'nın ablası Ayşe Hilal Sayan Koytak, Helsinki Büyükelçiliğinde görevine başladı.

Cumhurbaşkanı Erdoğan’ın Helsinki’ye büyükelçi tayin ettiği Ayşe Hilal Sayan Koytak, güven mektubunu Finlandiya Cumhurbaşkanı Alexander Stubb’a önceki gün sundu.

Ayşe Hilal Sayan Koytak güven mektubunu Cumhurbaşkanına sunarak Türkiye’yi Finlandiya’da temsil etme hakkını elde etti. Koytak, Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya’nın bakanlık döneminde ise Aile Bakanlığı’nda müsteşar yardımcısıydı.

Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya’nın kardeşi Ömer Fatih Sayan, 8 yıl Ulaştırma ve Altyapı Bakan Yardımcılığı yaptıktan sonra Temmuz 2026’da EPDK Kurul Üyesi oldu. Kız kardeşi Nazmiye Sümeyye Sayan ise bir dönem İBB Meclis Üyesiydi.

author: heinhtetkyaw
title: The Last Defense of the Lake: From Environmental Conservation to Political Revolution
content:
For over seven decades, Myanmar was consumed by the world’s longest civil war, but the Intha (Insaku), the "Children of the Lake/The People of The Lake," remained a peaceful exception. Nestled among high mountain peaks in Shan State, they lived peacefully with nature on the still waters of Inle Lake, famous worldwide for their stilt houses, floating gardens (ye-chan), and iconic leg-rowing fishermen, or at least that's what the state and tourism agency’s narrative for their brand image. The iconic leg-rowing fishermen have become a brand of Myanmar's tourism campaign since 1996, when the military was promising market reform and democracy.

Although recognized as one of Myanmar's 135 distinct indigenous groups, the Intha remain a "minority within a minority" in Southern Shan State, distinct in language and history from their Shan, Pa'O, Lisu, Taungtha, Kareni, and Danu neighbors, and their language is a branch of Widely accepted theories suggest their ancestors migrated from Lower Burma, Dawei, a long time ago, or a group of Tibeto-Burman who were still left behind. At the same time, the rest moved forward to the Irrawaddy Valley. Applying James C. Scott’s concept of “Zomia,” which describes upland societies that historically avoided centralized state control, the Intha experience can be understood as a form of aquatic adaptation. Rather than escaping into mountains, they survived on an economically marginal lake environment surrounded by hills. Their oral histories and religious traditions contain accounts of resistance against local feudal authorities. Even during British colonial rule, the region was viewed less as a profitable administrative center and more as a scenic recreational area. This delicate socio-ecological balance began to shatter after the 2010 political reforms. Under President Thein Sein’s administration, military-tied tycoons and international investors targeted the lake's eastern shore for a massive "Hotel Zone" project. The infrastructure building has leveled hillsides, drained wetlands, and seized land with minimal compensation for the local population, leading to severe ecological damage, driving local fish populations toward extinction, and destroying traditional livelihoods. Although Inle Lake was designated Myanmar's first UNESCO Biosphere Reserve in 2015, the surrounding Inlay Lake Wildlife Sanctuary had already been recognized as an ASEAN Heritage Park in 2003. It was later designated Myanmar's fifth Ramsar Wetland of International Importance in 2018. Despite these international conservation recognitions, environmental degradation driven by deforestation, unsustainable agriculture, tourism development, and weak conservation governance has continued. One of the most controversial cases involved Myanmar Naing Group Co., Ltd., owned by U Tun Naing Shwe, son of former military ruler Than Shwe, which proposed to construct a luxury hotel on land that had previously been part of the Inle Lake Wildlife Sanctuary. The proposal sparked widespread opposition from local communities, environmental organizations, and government agencies, becoming a prominent example of the conflict between tourism development and environmental conservation around Inle Lake. Many farmers and fishermen lost their way of life; many were forced to migrate abroad for work. Those who stayed were pushed into minimum-wage work in construction and the hospital sector. Some local activists and scholars have criticized the commercialization of Inle Lake’s cultural practices, arguing that activities such as staged leg-row fishing and ethnic performances risk transforming living traditions into tourist spectacles rather than preserving their original social meaning. The commercialization of agriculture and watershed degradation has intensified the ecological crisis at Inle Lake. Historically, the lake’s unique wetland ecosystem allowed the Intha to develop floating-garden agriculture, with tomatoes becoming one of the region’s most important economic crops. However, expanding domestic and regional markets encouraged increased use of chemical fertilizers, pesticides, and commercial seeds, contributing to nutrient pollution and ecological stress. At the same time, state land policies allowed customary lands in Shan State to be classified as vacant or wasteland and allocated to large-scale investors and military-linked companies. Many Environmental organizations have documented how deforestation and resource extraction in Shan State’s watersheds contributed to soil erosion and environmental degradation. These processes have increased sedimentation, reduced water quality, and threatened the long-term sustainability of traditional Intha livelihoods. Interview with Nway La Nway La (in English meaning “The Summer-Moon”) is one of the indigenous peoples who have witnessed this timeline firsthand. Q: What was your life like before 2021? Nway La: "Before the 2021 military coup, while running a nature-based tourism business in the Inle region with my family, I observed and documented the various ways in which the Inle Lake environment was being degraded. Just as I was collaborating with partners to actively conserve the natural environment of Inle Lake alongside my nature-based tourism work, the military coup occurred, causing my dream to be shattered." Q: Can you elaborate on the root causes of Inle Lake's environmental degradation? Nway La: "As Inle Lake is both a natural freshwater highland lake and a socio-ecological system, the root causes of its degradation lie in factors both human-induced and natural, such as water pollution, the shrinking of the water surface area, siltation and shallowing, and socio-economic inequities. The deterioration of Inle Lake is primarily due to weak policy commitment regarding its management and conservation, as well as the pursuit of vested interests. The Inle region relies primarily on agriculture and tourism for its livelihood. Its deterioration stems from several factors: local administrators lack full decision-making authority, there is no full access to utilize locally collected taxes for regional preservation and protection, and residents, despite understanding the root causes of the issues, are denied the opportunity to take action." Alongside military-linked business interests and expanding luxury tourism networks, global fashion and travel companies have increasingly transformed Inle Lake’s cultural heritage into a high-value commodity. The commercialization of lotus weaving illustrates how local traditions can become premium luxury products within global markets. Italian luxury brand Loro Piana has promoted Inle Lake lotus fiber as one of the world’s rarest natural textiles, with garments that require tens of thousands of hand-harvested lotus stems and sell for several thousand US dollars. While such initiatives provide international visibility for local craftsmanship, critics argue that luxury branding often emphasizes romantic narratives of tradition and sustainability while obscuring the unequal distribution of value between global companies and local producers Similarly, high-end tourism operators have marketed Inle Lake through images of leg-row fishermen, floating gardens, and craft workshops, generating premium tourism experiences while raising questions about how much economic benefit remains within local communities and whether tourism growth contributes to long-term ecological protection. The final breaking point arrived with the February 2021 military coup. The Myanmar military brutally cracked down on peaceful anti-coup protests. The long-peaceful Intha were forced to make a historic decision. For the first time in history, they formed their own armed resistance organization to join the broader national struggle for federalism against the military regime. Q: How did you make the transition from conservation work to joining the armed movement? Nway La: "I never thought I would end up here. If I think back, politics and revolution were not familiar terms to me, but somehow I have been involved with the Inle People's Defense Force (IPDF) since its very inception. I have played the role of filling in the gaps wherever needs arose. My work involves coordinating with various members and minimizing errors in the unit's operations. I enjoy working alongside the youth and fostering a sense of unity among us. I have dedicated significant effort to serving in various roles and ensuring a smooth handover of responsibilities to successors over the past five years." Q: What is the organizational structure and political goal of your movement today? Nway La: "Now, I serve as the Relations Officer at the Inle Region Liberation Organization (IRLO), which was formed in response to the military coup, recognizing the necessity of armed revolution with the political objective of achieving a transformation toward a federal democratic union that is appropriate for the Inle region. It was an umbrella organization federated with the IPDF (Inle People Defense Force), IWU (Inle Women Union), IFDM (Inle Federal Movement), the Inle Medical Team, and BOE NS (Nyaung Shwe Education Board). Efforts are also underway to strengthen the organization by engaging unions and Civil Disobedience Movement (CDM) networks across the region. It is designed to ensure that the armed forces do not dominate the civilian sector and to safeguard values such as gender equality, bottom-up federalism, environmentalism, anti-fascism, and anti-extremism in race and religion, while providing services to the community. We welcome and support the emergence of a federal democratic system in Myanmar. With the establishment of a federal democratic union, we also look forward to a federal arrangement for the Inle region that is appropriate and well-suited to the area." Five years since the establishment of IPDF (P3-1009), the unit actively fights alongside its neighboring ally, the Karenni People's Defense Force (KNDF). Yet, the resistance operates under severe constraints. Heightened military oppression, severe economic collapse, and the devastation of a recent earthquake have strained local public support. At the same time, geopolitical backing from key regional actors, including China and Russia, has strengthened the junta's position. Q: How is the local community sustaining this effort amid these growing challenges? Nway La: "The IRLO and IPDF have sustained ourselves through local support and solidarity despite our small population since the inception of the Spring Revolution. We still face significant needs and continue to struggle. Everyone knows that the effort must come from us, yet we naturally desire substantial and effective assistance." For Nway La and his comrades, nature belongs to no single ethnicity or socioeconomic elite, but their identity, culture, and survival are inseparable from the waters of Inle Lake. As state-backed crony capitalism threatens to expand, the destruction of Inle Lake represents far more than environmental ruin. It threatens to erase a distinct culture that spent centuries living on the margins to evade state control and is now taking an unprecedented stand to ensure its future. Even in Myanmar's political context of resistance, the struggle is always built on ethnic nationalism against the Burman majority; the children of the lake, or Lake People, a minority within a minority, struggle to walk a different path toward bottom-up federalism with social-ecology consciousness. Myanmar Center for Responsible Business, Danish Institute for Human Rights, & Institute for Human Rights and Business. (2015). Sector-wide impact assessment of tourism in Myanmar.

The lotus weavers of Myanmar by Snapdragon

Cohen, E. (1988). Authenticity and commoditization in tourism.
