title: Groupe Révolutionnaire Charlatan - Will 1793 Take Place?
content:
Author

: Groupe Révolutionnaire Charlatan

Title

: Will 1793 Take Place?

Subtitle

: Destituent Remarks on the Chilean Uprising and the Yellow Vests

Date

: October 6

th

, 2026

Notes

: Translated by the authors and Ill Will

Source

: https://illwill.com/1793




 










 First published in French in August 2026, the present article argues that the 2018–19 Yellow Vests movement in France and the 2019 Chilean uprising form two instances of a single pattern. In each case, an insurrection begins with modest demands, such as a metro fare or a fuel tax only to then explode outward, outstripping its own stated goals, before ultimately being contained by constituent processes, referendums, and left-wing electoral projects. The authors treat the Constitution of 1793, with its famous article on the “duty of insurrection,” as the archetypal “act of capture” for such sequences: on the one hand, it was an attempt by ruling powers to absorb revolutionary energy into itself; at the same time, it served to embed a permanent insurrectionary principle into the political-legal system, one which the state has never been able to fully extirpate. Against the left’s push for new constitutional initiatives, the authors argue for a “revolution without power” grounded in the refusal of institutions and representation, crediting the Yellow Vests with developing new forms of assembly and fleeting affiliation in the absence of a distinct language or subject of its own. The key question, they suggest, is ultimately not whether 1793 will take place, but who will finish the job. 










 










 Then annihilate forever what may one day destroy your work. Consider that the fruit of your labors being reserved for your grandchildren only, duty and probity command that you bequeath them none of those seeds of disaster which could mean for your descendants a renewal of the chaos whence we have with so much trouble just emerged. At the present moment our prejudices are weakening; the people have already abjured the Catholic absurdities; they have already suppressed the temples, sent the relics flying, and agreed that marriage is a mere civil undertaking; the smashed confessionals serve as public meeting places; the former faithful, deserting the apostolic banquet, leave the gods of flour dough to the mice. […] One more effort; since you labor to destroy all the old foundations, do not permit one of them to survive, for let but one endure, ‘tis enough, the rest will be restored. And how much more certain of their revival must we not be if the one you tolerate is positively the source and cradle of all the others! —Marquis de Sade, 

Philosophy in the Bedroom

, 1795 










In Santiago as in Paris




 Chile, October 25

th

, 2020.

[1]

 After months of insurrectionary demonstrations, the government agrees to hold a referendum to elect a constituent assembly. The vote takes place on the 15

th

 and 16

th

 of May, 2021, and on July 4

th

 the assembly begins its work, which is to last for a period of one year. With the initiation of the constituent process, another quite distinct process draws to a close: the revolutionary process. The latter began on October 7, 2019 when groups of young people, dissatisfied with the rise in metro fares, decided to refuse to pay and to jump the ticket barriers en masse. Collective ingenuity, the joy of rebellion, the determination of the 

primera línea

 (frontline), the feeling of being on the verge of storming heaven, all gradually give way to self-serious protocols and democratic formalism. On two separate occasions, the newly drafted constitution is rejected in referendums and abandoned. The rest is history: the left wins the elections of November–December 2021 with an abstention rate of roughly 50 percent, taking power in March 2022. Yet the aftermath proves disappointing and, in December 2025, a far-right candidate, the son of a Nazi, is elected as the country’s leader against a backdrop of a spectacular rise in voter turnout (up thirty-eight percent in the first round, and twenty-nine in the second). Once again, hopes for a Chilean path towards a freer and more egalitarian society are dashed. Once again, counterrevolution succeeds in stifling the revolutionary process, by imposing upon it the timeframe and institutional forms of democratic power: the mirage of a referendum, a moment of national electoral unity, a left-wing government, and a breakthrough by the far right. 




 In France, the Chilean uprising enjoyed a certain resonance with the Yellow Vests movement. It was not the price of the metro ticket but rather the cost of fuel that sparked the unrest, dragging out into the open the aspirations and courage of hundreds of thousands of people confronting the rising cost of living, the unwavering contempt of those in power, constant disparagement in the media, and the extreme brutalization of law enforcement. The grievances of the Yellow Vests included the resignation of Macron, a reshuffling of government, and still more importantly, increased active participation among citizens in political life through the Citizens’ Initiative Referendum (RIC). In the absence of anything else to articulate, uprisings always begin with such demands. But the specific demands of the movement should not obscure the fact that, rather than simply opposing a particular tax or government, this was a struggle for the dignity of life. To put it another way, what the movement said did not fully reflect what it wanted. In the absence of a common language, its actions went further than its words, without ever truly finding a way to express its aims. This distinguishes it from the so-called Marxist revolutions, which inherited the language of their century, even though their substance may have differed from what their ideology implied (representative democracy, a mixed economy, parliamentarism, tax justice, agrarian reform, etc.). There is always a disconnect between the desires expressed and experienced during an uprising and what subsequently materializes: this “cunning of reason” is the crucible of the insurgents and their failed emancipation. 




...

author: Unknown
title: Groupe Révolutionnaire Charlatan - Remarks on the Ongoing Student Revolt
content:
Author

: Groupe Révolutionnaire Charlatan

Title

: Remarks on the Ongoing Student Revolt

Date

: October 9

th

, 2026

Notes

: Translated by Ill Will

Source

: https://illwill.com/remarks-on-the-ongoing-student-revolt










 The following remarks, forged in the heat of battle during a wave of student unrest that is now spreading to Belgium and Italy, were posted to 

x.com

 on October 6, 2026. For a longer position piece by the same authors, see their recent article, “

Will 1793 Take Place?

” 










1.




 The student revolt is the spearhead of the movement announced for October 17. 




2.




 The “gangs” [bandes] of students from working-class neighborhoods constitute the actual driving force both within and against the current youth movement. In a sense, this force is less a part of the student movement than it is a continuation of the Nahel revolt. It has neither demands nor representatives; it does not conform to the codes of the Left and rejects bourgeois politeness. It wants revenge. 




3.




 The universities have followed the high schools and joined the dynamic of the blockades. They, in turn, could bring about a qualitative leap by, for example, launching an occupation that could be taken up and spread by other sectors of society—whether students or not. This hypothesis, however, is oppposed by the overwhelming dominance of student union organizations, which leave little room for group spontaneity, collective ingenuity, and self-subversive practices. 




4.




 When one speaks of “blockades” at high schools, one is already engaging in a form of reduction and simplification of the practices of the student revolt. There are acts of sabotage (doors set on fire, gates knocked down, “e-blockades” against distance learning) and acts of revenge (against the school hierarchy and the police outside), urban guerrilla tactics (barricades) and wildcat strikes (work stoppages during breaks and staggered blockades), and finally something akin to a game aimed at ridiculing authority (slogans about Macron and his teacher, superhero costumes in contrast to the oppressors’ uniforms). 




5.




 The unions cannot come to terms with the idea of October 17, as it reminds them too much of the Yellow Vests. They must pretend to join the movement in order to gain better control over it—both through their monopoly on negotiations and by dictating the timeline. If the inter-union coalition called for action on October 6 alongside the students, it was only to better defuse the call for October 17, which they wish to reduce to an interim date ahead of their mobilization on November 5. 




6.




 In high schools, the left differs from other political forces in form, but not in substance. In form, the left pushes students into the role of victims, thereby allowing itself to present as the “responsible adults.” Consider the human chains of parents and teachers, or elected officials denouncing the police’s use of LBD weapons. It is striking, however, that batons, shields, helmets, and other standard components of the arsenal of democracy are far less frequently called into question. 




7.




 In terms of substance, the left aligns itself with the other political forces in their efforts to restore peace. This is precisely what happens when it puts forward demands that are consistent with its platform, thereby helping to separate the “good” students (those with demands deemed legitimate) from the “bad” students (these “rioters” without ideas or genuine political motives). 




8.




 Unlike the left, we have neither flags to wave, nor a tempo to set, nor lessons to teach. 




9.




 How should we deal with the enthusiasm for “October 17” and the way certain segments of the youth present it as an echo of the Yellow Vests movement? Even if a new generation seems to invoke its symbolic power full of hope, it is by no means certain that reusing the object will help us rediscover its spirit. Nevertheless, perhaps that is precisely what is expected of us: to don it and see if it—even if only temporarily—embodies a sense of belonging with which others can identify and to which they can align themselves, without appropriating it in the process. At the risk of appearing ridiculous and anachronistic, and discarding it again swiftly. 




10.




 The spectacular actions of the student revolt are the work of bands or gangs [bandes] that organize themselves and make their identity known in this way. Wearing Under Armour outfits fools no one: only to the extent that we reconnect with our emotions and our gang-like instincts will our actions resonate and have an impact, both offensively and tactically (distribution of masks, Phy-Serum, Anrirep flyers, lists of lawyers, food, sound and lighting equipment). By acting in this way, we hope to prolong the time we have fought to open for encounters, discussion, and conspiracy.

author: greensyndic
title: Speed Kills: Snuff Capitalist Acceleration - Jeff Shantz
content:
The elimination of jobs at the workplace now coincides with the elimination of former workers outside the workplace under snuff capitalism. And this elimination too must be done in accelerating rates. Time, as always, is money from capital’s perspective. From Anarcho-Syndicalist Review, 95, Fall 2026.

Whether we like it or not, capital is accelerationist. Speed up is built right into the very engine of capitalism. Capital’s drive for accumulation, in competition with other capital for profit, means that it must always go faster, must always accelerate exploitation and value extraction. This is the drive behind the ceaseless, permanent, push for technological advance, from motors to assembly lines to robots to computers, to AI, and beyond.

Speed is the means by which capital beats its competitors in extracting value. More surplus value in an ever-shorter period of time. Any worker knows the tyranny of the clock in the capitalist workplace. Marx suggests that this surplus value extraction is either absolute, the lengthening of the working say, so we work longer beyond the point that we produce the value equivalent to our wages or relative, narrowing the time it takes us to produce the equivalent of our wages. Relative surplus value is the logic of the speed up—using technology to get us producing more and faster. Both forms of extraction, though, dominate the worker’s lifetime. Denying us rest, breaks, mealtimes, or even bathroom breaks. Stealing our life times—time away from family, from loved ones, from ourselves.

Speed also, significantly, overcomes obstacles—first and foremost among them the slowness built into human labor by the physical and mental limits and frailties of our bodies. Technological acceleration is therefore about overcoming the human element in labor. It is about controlling us too, taking initiative away from us.

Reducing and then replacing our numbers, and our capacities to resist or control the labor process. Fundamentally it is about rendering our human labor irrelevant, while doing the same to the embodiment of that labor itself—us.

Capital has used speed to overcome the limitations posed by workers on value extraction and accumulation. But under current and emerging conditions of accelerating electronicization (AI and its ilk are exemplars), capital is accelerating, not with workers, but without us. The working class becomes an obstacle to be overcome, not only at work but increasingly outside of work. The living bodies of the working class slow down the circuits of capital in distribution (consumption) as well as in production. Capital moves quickly from stealing our life times to stealing our life itself.

The elimination of jobs at the workplace now coincides with the elimination of former workers outside the workplace under snuff capitalism. And this elimination too must be done in accelerating rates. Time, as always, is money from capital’s perspective.

From Social Services to Snuff Services

Those expelled from production and (simultaneously) from consumption are too costly for capital, too much of an obstacle to accumulation. As capital becomes more desperate it increasingly sees any supports that might sustain the unemployed, such as welfare, unemployment insurance, social housing, health care, as a transfer of wealth by the state away from capital and to the unproductive and unnecessary. They are, from capital’s perspective, expendable. They must be eliminated. This is the impetus, and organizing principle, of snuff capitalism.

Like production and consumption themselves, this elimination must be done quickly, at accelerating speeds. Every day the unneeded are kept around is an impediment to accumulation, a drain on capital.

This elimination must at least keep pace with the elimination of jobs, of workers from work, of consumers from consumption. Time, as always for capital, is money. First and foremost.

This is driving expansion of and innovation in snuff industries, innovation and expansion of murder infrastructures, innovation and transformation of capital’s states from neoliberal tools (of crisis) to democidal weapons (of extermination).

This is made to happen through the dual spheres of the state as usual, through law (legality) and force (police). Increasingly it will happen through what were once called social services—health care as assisted suicide and coercive detention, social assistance as death camp labor and medical experimentation.

One focus of democidal states has been the removal of laws and regulations that would impede capital or slow its circulation, such as environmental or workplace protections. While writing this piece the US Supreme Court gave a decision protecting Bayer from lawsuits over cancer related to glyphosate, the active ingredient in the company’s Roundup weedkiller. Ominously, it protects capital from having to warn about deadly ingredients in their products. Why worry about warnings when death is the point?

Snuff capital cannot even wait for people to die before treating them as if they are dead—killing them legislatively. The same month it was learned that the Trump administration had plans to falsely declare 2.7 million people dead as part of the government’s mass deportation efforts. According to a whistleblower, the White House planned to have people’s names and Social Security numbers added to the Death Master File which tracks when a person has died in order to stop government benefits.

While this was not implemented (this time) it shows us a workable model for future democidal policy under snuff capitalism. It can be done that quickly—with the stroke of a pen you are legally dead. Then, of course, literally.

This is the mindset of snuff. We must not be mistaken in the false hope that these experiments, intentions, innovations will stay at the level of the snuff fantasies of madmen.

In the realm of state force, we have already seen the death squads of ICE in action. Rapid and mobile murder infrastructures. Organized state gangsterism, the mode of the democidal state.

The litany of atrocities, and the ever growing roster getting set to launch from the starting blocks, come at us faster than we can enumerate. Every day, new horrors are announced to a reeling public. And that is as intended. We are meant to recoil in horror. Acceleration is the point and the way. It cannot be otherwise for capital desperate to accumulate, despairing for still more. It will not slow down. From the perspective of capital, it must not.

Acceleration itself is an attack on life. Humans (and other living beings for that matter) are not meant to live our lives at ever increasing speed. We are not built for it. It breaks us down mentally and physically. We cannot process, integrate, and act at the speed capital requires. We are built to live according to celestial time, not capital time.

The toll on life built into capitalist accelerationism is expressed in growing levels of physical ailment and disability (which have long been linked to capitalist time, like heart disease) and in epidemics of mental health problems, such as depression and suicide.

We see it too in the severe negative impacts on health, including deaths, associated with capital’s great rush to return to business as (more than) usual before COVID was over with and while it is still killing people. Capital moved with a speed that led many to forget COVID already, to act as if it is no longer dealing death. But for snuff capital, dealing death is the order of the day, so what does it matter?

What some refer to, rather cynically, as compassion fatigue, is not really about compassion at all. It is a reflection of people being overwhelmed psychologically and emotionally by the waves in which atrocities are unleased against us. The rapid streams of horrors we are faced with, even only as images and reports overwhelm the senses. We cannot properly process them. Our capacities for understanding are flooded.

Acceleration confronts us with new disasters, crises, atrocities, while we are still trying to analyze those that have already trampled us. At the same time democidal states cynically refer to compassion fatigue in justifying cuts to social services that might benefit the working class, especially the excluded sectors of the working class. People are tired of tax dollars going to support the “unproductive” they tell us. We can no longer afford sympathy for programs to help those who will not help themselves. Far from reflecting compassion fatigue among the working class broadly, these reflect the views of capital. Though we may recognize that some workers, having bought into the dog-eat-dog priorities of capital and its states, turning to fascist survivalism in the false hope of buying themselves some time.

Creating Roadblocks to Capitalist Accelerationism

One outcome, of course, is fatalism, demoralization, defeatism—what some today call “doomersim” or the all pervading belief that we are all condemned, no matter what we do. We have to avoid doomerism, but at the same time be honest about what confronts us. These are the realities we must face, and against which we must be fierce. Unfortunately, movements (anarchist as well as leftist) are still moving at the speed of a glacier.

Movements are still oriented towards literal dead ends. Social democracy, electoralism, “green new deals,” symbolic protests, demonstrations, making moral appeals to the immoral. Slow march politics that do nothing to stop the fast march to the graveyard.

Snuff capital is not open to reform. It has no interest in bargaining. And why should it, given the current imbalance of power in its favor. It is fully dedicated to the path it is, with full awareness and intent, pursuing. There is no reforming a system operated by and according to those who have determined that their existence is predicated on our extermination. In any event, you do not reform snuff.

We must be clear too that we cannot pursue our aims through the dominant, traditional structures of working class organizing—most notably through mainstream trade unions. Unions have been vehicles for negotiation with capital—vehicles for capitulation, accommodation, and containment within contracturalism.

We have long seen union responses to earlier forms of mechanization and automation—negotiated layoffs and severance packages. Union will cling to hopes of bargaining with snuff right up until the last worker is out the door. An illusion that you can slow the culling, while still allowing the culling to occur.

We need to remember once-familiar militant working-class methods from slow downs to sit downs, strikes and occupations. These are the great (often literal) roadblocks to capitalist speed. The sabotage that derails and dismantles. These are the exploited and oppressed pulling the emergency break. Not asking for capital to take its foot off the gas pedal.

Revolutionary rank-and-file action will be key as part of this, while we still have access to workplaces that we could win control of away from capital. And shut down as necessary. Before our place as workers is eliminated. Syndicalism, which has always taken a class-wide approach, is necessary as are its preferred tactics of militant direct action against (not in negotiation with) capital. To end the labor-capital structure. To snuff out capitalism before it snuffs out us.

author: Brian Hioe
title: Army Suicide Reminds of Recurring Issues with Bullying and Hazing in the Military
content:
A RECENT CASE in which a female Army first lieutenant committed suicide is being investigated as a potential case of bullying. The first lieutenant in question, surnamed Wang, jumped to her death from a building at the Army’s 206th Brigade base in Hsinchu County on September 30th. An audio recording that was posted on Threads on October 12th shows a man berating Wang for failing to heed instructions, leading to the bullying allegations.

The Ministry of National Defense has vowed that the case is being investigated and that Minister of National Defense Wellington Koo is attentive to its developments. This would not be the only case in recent years in which a suicide in the military has been linked to bullying.

In November 2020, a similar case emerged of a corporal surnamed Liu stationed in the Eighth Army Command’s 203rd Brigade in Danei District, Tainan, who died by hanging. Liu, too, was reportedly bullied by his superiors and peers.

The most famous case of a death in the military thought to have resulted from bullying in the military would be the death of cadet Hung Chung-chiu in July 2013. Hung is thought to have been bullied by his superiors and peers shortly before his discharge from mandatory military service, as a form of hazing or as retribution against him before his service ended. The lack of government transparency in the wake of the death, with allegations of a cover-up, led to the Citizen 1985 movement, one of the major predecessor movements of the 2014 Sunflower Movement.

The government is likely sensitive to the optics of bullying in the military. The Hung Chung-chiu case, as well as the military’s perceived lack of transparency, is thought to be a major factor in public distrust in the military. This proves an important issue for the government at a time when it seeks to boost recruitment numbers, so as to counter rising Chinese threats.

At the same time, one notes that the military was an authoritarian institution during the many decades of the White Terror. In the course of the White Terror, the military served as the enforcer of the KMT state, and it conducted many of the political killings during the purges that took place then. Deaths due to bullying or hazing, as well as the cover-up of such deaths, were a common occurrence during the authoritarian era. In fact, incidents such as the Hung Chung-chiu case were relatively common during the authoritarian era and were mostly covered up, such that a single death in post-authoritarian Taiwan would garner such attention.

To this extent, one notes that cases of workplace bullying in government that have resulted in suicides have received greater scrutiny. Cases in point include the suicide of a civil servant surnamed Wu who worked in the Ministry of Labor in 2024. After the death of deputy trade representative Yen Huai-hsing in March at age 53, allegations that Yen was bullied by her superiors also emerged. Though such issues regarding workplace bullying have not always been put in the same frame as deaths in the military, insofar as both are, in some sense, public sector workers

author: Peter Boyle
title: NSW Parliamentary Friends of the Kurdish people launched
content:
NSW Parliamentary Friends of the Kurdish People was launched in NSW Parliament House on October 13. It has an initial membership of 11 MPs, including co-chairs Abigail Boyd (Greens), Anthony D’Adam MLC (Labor) and secretary Tim James MP (Liberal).

Gulfer Olan, co-chair of the Federation of Democratic Kurdish Society Australia, said this was “an historical milestone”.

Boyd explained that it took seven years and the hard work of many people to get to the Parliamentary Friends of the Kurdish People officially established. “I resonate with the spirit of the Kurdish community, your commitment to grassroots democracy, your commitment to gender equality and economic equality, your love of nature, the environment.”

D’Adam said: “We are one in commitment to democracy and human rights, the right to self-determination and the right to cultural autonomy... [this is] another marker of the status that this community now holds in Australian society as an important part of our multicultural community.”

He added that it is “a very important thing to acknowledge our multicultural society where people aren’t asked to surrender their culture and become part of a monoculture”.

“We are all Australians and we’re able to maintain our cultural identity and that’s something that’s really important. It’s important that we defend that at this time when, as we know, there are dark forces rising in our community that are threatening those very values that we hold here.”

Parliamentary Friends of the Kurdish People

Federation of Democratic Kurdish Society Australia

author: Ella Gutteridge
title: Hundreds protest far-right conference in Brisbane
content:
High-profile racists and far-right leaders descended on the Brisbane showgrounds over the weekend of 10 and 11 October for the Conservative Political Action Conference.

One Nation leader Pauline Hanson headlined the event. She was joined by Liberal leader Angus Taylor, far-right podcaster Karl Stefanovic, and one of Britain’s least successful politicians, former Prime Minister Liz Truss.

Inside, it was a carnival of reaction. The ABC reported that 

Hanson was greeted with 

rapturous applause

 as she harangued the Coalition for signing up to net-zero and creating an eSafety commissioner, which she pledged to abolish on the grounds of free speech.

The leader of the National Party, Matt Canavan, cosplayed as a blue-collar worker as he took to the stage to extol the virtues of Australian manufacturing. Despite earlier criticisms, Hanson said that she’d be willing to work with the Coalition to “

throw out this wretched and corrupt Labor government

”.

Outside, hundreds of irreverent high schoolers, trade union activists and community members rallied, waving homemade signs, chanting and drumming. The crowd was a sea of keffiyehs, rainbow flags and signs, with many commenting on Hanson’s close relationship with Australian billionaire Gina Rinehart (“Pauline works for Gina!”).

“Migrants are welcome, racists are not!” was a popular chant, echoing across the showgrounds while conferencegoers streamed out for their lunch break. One Nation recently unveiled 

its policy to cut Australia’s immigration intake

 by 750,000 people over three years, including plans to cut visas for the family members of skilled migrants and international students to zero.

“Pauline Hanson wants net zero immigration, but my parents are immigrants, my friends are immigrants, and without them this country would be nothing and fuck Pauline!”, Sam, a high school student, told 

Red Flag

.  

The rally heard from Dave Pullen, an Indigenous elder from Inala who ran against Hanson in Ipswich in 1996. Draped in an Indigenous flag, Pullen opened with an acknowledgement of country and of Hanson’s long record of racism towards Indigenous people.

National convenor of the Socialist Party and teacher unionist Rebecca Barrigos highlighted the importance of posing an alternative socialist vision to One Nation and the broader right:

“Today’s rally isn’t just about sending a signal to those inside the conference; it’s about saying we know what you’re doing. They’re fighting for a more competitive, more brutal, more pro-billionaire, anti-worker vision of society, and to that we say, fuck your vision of society! We have an alternative vision.”

There is a long way to go to realise that vision. 

Hanson is currently the preferred prime minister to Anthony Albanese

 and is polling at 36 percent in Queensland. While the right has momentum, it still faces opposition. People who oppose One Nation’s vision for the world should rally to our side and put up a fight.

author: To be a name
title: In Gaza, even thinking has become a struggle
content:
I have thought carefully about how to write about my life in Gaza. Even speaking about what we experience requires caution. How can I tell the truth about my reality without putting myself at risk?

This question alone says something about what it means to live here.

My days have become a series of moments. in which survival takes priority over everything else.

At night, the sound of surveillance drones makes it difficult to think about anything beyond the possibility that we could be next. Even when the sky grows quiet, peace feels unreal. At night, closing my eyes no longer feels different from opening them.

Our homes are destroyed, yet we still hope to recover even one small belonging from the rubble.

We want something to carry from our past into a future we cannot imagine.

Sometimes, the movement of rats among the ruins makes us wonder whether danger has returned. Even animals seek shelter in the remains of our homes, while we cannot safely retrieve the things that once made those homes ours.

Then comes the daily search for drinking water.

In 2026, finding clean water should not be the greatest problem occupying a person's mind. Yet we wait in line, hoping to receive enough to get through the day. We think about studying, working, resting and finding moments of happiness, but every ordinary activity competes with the demands of survival. Even water becomes a calculation.

After a bombing, another family may enter the records of the dead. Their loss might become a headline for a few seconds, or pass almost unnoticed.

But those who knew them will remember their names, their voices and the lives they lived. Human beings should never have to meet an unspoken threshold of tragedy before their deaths are considered worthy of attention.

I see people carrying grief that no words can fully express.

I see destroyed homes, displaced neighbours and parents trying to comfort hungry children. I see people who have lost their work, their security and loved ones, yet still find reasons to smile. Their smiles do not mean the suffering has disappeared.

Sometimes, they are simply a way of remaining human.

Then, from far beyond Gaza, we see people raising Palestinian flags and speaking out against oppression and genocide. Their solidarity reminds us that we are not alone. It gives us a moment to feel pride, connection and hope.

We do not ask the world merely to witness our deaths. We ask it to recognise our lives: Our right to study, to find clean water, to enjoy ordinary moments, to protect our families and to imagine a future without fear.

I write not only for myself, but for the millions whose daily struggles may never become headlines.

Thank you to those who have not forgotten us. Your solidarity cannot undo our losses, but it reminds us that humanity has not abandoned us — and that we are still here, trying to live.

author: Josh Richman
title: In Memoriam: Barry Steinhardt
content:
Barry Steinhardt, a lifelong privacy champion and an early leader in the battle for digital civil liberties who served as EFF’s president in 1998-99, died last week at age 73.

 




A Connecticut native, Steinhardt led the Vermont and Pennsylvania affiliates of the American Civil Liberties Union before becoming associate director of the national ACLU. There, he helped spearhead the fight to overturn much of the Communications Decency Act, resulting in the U.S. Supreme Court’s landmark 

Reno v. ACLU

 

ruling in 1997.

 




When the internet was still young, 

Steinhardt 

became one of 

the first 

attorneys to 

specialize in the intersection of technology and privacy

. 

In early 1998 he took a leave of absence from the ACLU to become EFF’s president, and then returned to the ACLU in 1999.

 




In 2002 he founded the ACLU’s Program on Technology and Liberty. After retiring from the ACLU, he continued on as a senior advisor to London-based 

Privacy International

.

 




Steinhardt chaired the 2003 Computer Freedom and Privacy Conference and served on a wide variety of significant panels and boards, including the Department of Transportation’s Negotiated Rule Making on national driver’s license standards, the Advisory Committee to the US Census, and the Blue Ribbon Panel on Genetics of the National Conference of State Legislatures. He also was selected to be a member of the US delegation to the G-8 Government and Private Sector Tokyo conference on Cyber Crime and served as an advisor to the Czech Helsinki Committee. 

 




“Barry led many critical technology and civil liberties fights and was an important mentor to me and others in the field,” said EFF Executive Director Nicole Ozer. “Barry’s influential work across strategy to defend and advance privacy rights and safeguard people against surveillance has made its mark on the law and policy of our digital world and protected the rights and safety of people across the United States and around the world.”

author: labor4pal
title: Palestinian trade unions renew their solidarity with workers around the world who are resisting all forms of oppression and persecution, and call for global action to end all forms of complicity in Israeli crimes, starting from Friday, November 20, and continuing until the “International Day of Solidarity with the Palestinian People,” which falls on Sunday, November 29, 2026
content:
Palestinian trade unions renew their solidarity with workers around the world who are resisting all forms of oppression and persecution, and call for global action to end all forms of complicity in Israeli crimes, starting from Friday, November 20, and continuing until the “International Day of Solidarity with the Palestinian People,” which falls on Sunday, November 29, 2026

This coming November, we undersigned Palestinian trade unions and federations urgently renew our call to unions around the world to:

Uphold and defend the inalienable rights of the Indigenous people of Palestine as stipulated in international law, particularly the right of our refugees to return home and receive reparations, and

Escalate BDS pressure to end all state, corporate and institutional complicity in Israel’s illegal occupation, apartheid and genocide.

While approaching the third anniversary of the beginning of Israel’s ongoing genocide in Gaza and the International Day of Solidarity with the Palestinian People, and in light of Israel’s accelerating ethnic cleansing, annexation, settler violence and pogroms in the West Bank, anddepraved violent repression of our prisoners , we remind ourselves that an injury to one is an injury to all. Israel’s livestreamed genocide, coupled with the wars and threats of aggression by its imperialist partners in Washington, is leading to the collapse of respect for international law, human rights and workers’ rights, threatening humanity at large, not just Palestinians.

Today, the Palestinian struggle for justice is at the heart of the battle against a world order of “might makes right” that is being imposed by the US-Israel genocidal axis and enabled by colonial powers. As Israel’s wars of aggression against the peoples of the region expand from Lebanon to Syria and from Yemen to Iran, and as the US threatens the peoples of Cuba, Greenland, Venezuela , Oman, among others, it is clear that hardly anyone is safe from this descent to the abyss.

The Israel-US axis is waging its war for Greater Israel without any consideration for the global recession (maybe even depression) it is potentially creating and its impacts globally. This includes the exacerbation of the cost of living crisis, austerity measures, the housing crisis, food insecurity, among others. Military budgets are swelling at the cost of health, housing and education. The first to feel the brunt of all this are working people and their families. The demands for affordability, fair wages, more and better social services, and lower living costs are organically connected to the calls for an end to astronomical military spending, vicious privatization, and global complicity in Israeli crimes. This affects us all and therefore should unite us all. Where states fail to uphold international law and end their own complicity, workers and their unions must take the lead in acting to end this complicity!

Our struggle for justice in Palestine is inseparable from the global struggle against systemic racism, exploitation, climate devastation and all forms of oppression.

It is the duty of unions to ensure that the workers they represent—whether in ports, on ships, in businesses, or in government offices—are not involved, often without their knowledge and/or consent, in actions that involve complicity in atrocity crimes anywhere, including Israel’s war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide against our people.

The 2024 decisions of the International Court of Justice (ICJ) – that Israel is plausibly committing genocide , that its occupation is illegal, and its policies amount to apartheid – make ending all complicity in Israel’s crimes not only a moral but also a legal obligation. States, institutions (including unions) and corporations must impose targeted, lawful sanctions on Israel. We call on all union bodies and civil society organizations worldwide to organize, uplift and turn solidarity into concrete strategic action across the ten days leading up to the international day of solidarity with the Palestinian people from November 20th to November 29th 2026.

We, the undersigned Palestinian trade unions, call on workers and unions around the world to escalate their support for our liberation struggle by:

Organizing, joining and amplifying global peaceful actions to mark the International Day of Solidarity with the Palestinian People from Friday 20th to Sunday 29th November.

Adopting ethical procurement policies ( EPP ) and, where applicable, ethical investment policies ( EIP ) that exclude corporations implicated in grave human rights violations anywhere, including in Palestine.

Pressuring corporations and institutions they work in to end any complicity through ending contracts that directly or indirectly support Israel’s atrocity crimes, and adopting EPP and/or EIP.

Rejecting any racist agreement with Israel that facilitates the substitution and further oppression of Palestinian workers.

Escalating economic, academic, cultural, and sports BDS campaigns .

Peacefully disrupting and blocking the transfer of military, energy and other dual-use supplies to Israel, by:

Pressuring your governments to uphold their legal obligations following the ICJ rulings of 2024, as stated by UN human rights experts , by, at a minimum, imposing “a full arms embargo on Israel, halting all agreements, imports, exports and transfers, including of dual-use items that could be used against the Palestinian population under occupation,” as well as canceling or suspending “economic relationships, trade and academic agreements relations with Israel that may contribute to its presence and apartheid arms in the occupied Palestinian regime.” territory.”

Cutting all ties with Israel’s colonial Histadrut federation and expelling it and all similarly complicit Israeli unions and associations (academic, medical, etc.) from all international fora.

Declaring your union an Apartheid-Free Zone (AFZ) to end corporate and institutional complicity with systems of oppression, particularly Israel’s regime of apartheid and genocide against the Palestinian people.

title: Özlale: Taha Çakmak'ın istifası daha geniş bir ilişki ağının araştırılması gerektiğini gösteriyor
content:
Yeni Parti İzmir Milletvekili Ümit Özlale, fon vurgunu soruşturmasına ilişkin yaptığı açıklamada Türkiye Sigorta Genel Müdürü Taha Çakmak’ın istifasının daha geniş bir ilişki ağının araştırılması gerektiğini gösterdiğini söyledi.

Çakmak'la birlikte fon soruşturması kapsamında tutuklanan eski TCMB Başkan Yardımcısı Erkan Kilimci ve soruşturmada adı geçen eski bakan yardımcısı Bülent Aksu'nun Berat Albayrak'ın Hazine ve Maliye Bakanlığı dönemiyle bağlantılarının açıklığa kavuşturulması gerektiğini söyleyen Özlale, Borsa İstanbul Yönetim Kurulu Başkanı ve Türkiye Varlık Fonu Yönetim Kurulu Başkan Vekili Erişah Arıcan'ı da "yolların kesiştiği isim" olarak tanımlıyor. Özlale, Berat Albayrak'ın tezini Arıcan'la birlikte yazdığını hatırlatıyor.

Özlale, sosyal medya hesabından yaptığı açıklamada şu ifadeleri kullandı: "Bir istifa, onlarca bağlantı, milyarlarca liralık soru… Taha Çakmak kim? Erişah Arıcan’dan Türkiye Sigorta’ya, kredi derecelendirmesinden yatırım fonlarına uzanan ilişkiler bize ne anlatıyor? İsim isim, kurum kurum anlattım. Bir halka koptu diye zincirin geri kalanını unutturamazsınız. Taha Çakmak’ın istifası ve bir ilişki ağının anatomisi. Bir istifa çok sayıda bağlantı. İstifası bugün kamuoyuna yansıyan ve haberlerde malvarlığına tedbir konulduğu belirtilen Taha Çakmak sıradan biri değil. Kendisi, Şahap Kavcıoğlu’nun TCMB Başkanı olduğu dönemde başkan yardımcılığı yaptı. Daha önce, 2016–2018 yıllarında TCMB Başkan Yardımcılığı yapan ve sonrasında TERA yönetiminde yer alan Erkan Kilimci de fon soruşturması kapsamında tutuklandı. Kilimci ile Çakmak aynı dönemde başkan yardımcılığı yapmadı; ancak farklı dönemlerde kamu finans yönetiminde görev alan bu isimlerin daha sonra hangi kurumlarda buluştuğunun araştırılması gerekiyor. Fon soruşturmasında adı geçen eski bakan yardımcısı Bülent Aksu’nun da bulunduğu bu çevrenin Berat Albayrak dönemiyle bağlantıları açıklığa kavuşturulmalıdır. Yolların kesiştiği isim: Erişah Arıcan. Sayın Berat Albayrak tezini Erişah Arıcan ile yazmış. Erişah Hanım o kadar kıymetli biri ki kendisi hem Borsa İstanbul Yönetim Kurulu Başkanı hem de Türkiye Varlık Fonu Yönetim Kurulu Başkan Vekili. Lisans derecesini nereden aldığına dair çok bilgi yok ama sonrasında hep Marmara Üniversitesi’nde olmuş. Zaten kendisi aynı üniversitede öğretim üyesi olan Aydın Ayaydın’ın yeğeni. Erişah Hanım’ın çok başarılı tez öğrencileri var. Biri de yukarıda bahsettiğimiz Şahap Kavcıoğlu. Kendisinin başkanlık döneminde TCMB’de insan kaynakları genel müdürü olarak görev yapan Doğan Başar da Taha Çakmak’ın genel müdür olduğu Türkiye Sigorta’da genel müdür yardımcısı olarak görev yapıyor. Türkiye Sigorta’nın bir de teknik genel müdür yardımcısı var. Adı Çağrı Akpınar. Kendisi Marmara Finansal Bilimler Fakültesi Dekan Yardımcısı Özgür Akpınar’ın kardeşi ve Erişah Arıcan’ın da doktora öğrencisi. Türkiye Sigorta’nın parası nereye gitti? Peki, daha önce hakkında tedbir kararı alındığı ve bu kararın saatler sonra kaldırıldığı ileri sürülen Türkiye Sigorta A.Ş. neden önemli? Fon vurgununu konuşurken neden bu kurumun yatırım kararlarını sorguluyoruz? Çünkü topladığı primlerle, tasfiyesine karar verilen fonlara ve soruşturmaya konu hisse senetlerine yüksek tutarlı yatırım yaptığına ilişkin iddialar var. Türkiye Sigorta’nın ana hissedarı, sermayesinin yüzde 76,1’ini elinde bulunduran TVF Finansal Yatırımlar AŞ. Kalan yüzde 23,9’luk pay Borsa İstanbul’da işlem görüyor. Dolayısıyla Borsa İstanbul’un hissedar olmasıyla şirket paylarının borsada işlem görmesi birbirine karıştırılmamalı. Buradaki temel soru, bu ölçekte kurumsal kaynağın hangi yatırım kararlarıyla, hangi riskler üstlenilerek kullanıldığıdır. İşin bir de özel sektör tahvili tarafı var ki önlem alınmazsa ciddi bir piyasa riski doğurabilir. Sistemi, Adil Varlık Yönetim AŞ hakkında ileri sürülen iddialar üzerinden ele alalım. Şirketin ortaklık yapısı, Mustafa Yazıcı ve Ali Emre Ballı’yla bağlantıları, gerçekleşen tahvil ihraçları ve ihraç gelirlerinin kullanım yerleri birlikte ortaya konmalıdır. İncelenmesi gereken ihtimal şu: Bir şirket tahvil ihraç ederek topladığı parayı faaliyet veya yatırım yerine sorunlu fonlara yönlendirirse ne olur? Bu şirketin borçlanmaya erişiminde güçlü bir kredi notunun etkisi bulunabilir. İşte bu noktada devreye kredi derecelendirme kuruluşları giriyor. Bu alanda önemli bir yeri bulunan kredi derecelendirme kuruluşu JCR Eurasia’ya bakalım. Yönetim Kurulu Başkan Vekili ve Genel Müdür Prof. Dr. Feyzullah Yetgin bilin bakalım kiminle doktora tezini yazmış? Doğru bildiniz: Erişah Arıcan ile… JCR Eurasia’nın yönetim kurulu üyelerinden biri kim? Server Demirci. Kendisi de Erişah Arıcan ile aynı üniversitede çalışmış ve ortak yayınları var. Şimdi asıl soruya dönelim: Adil Varlık ve benzeri ihraççıların kredi notları, gerçek borç ödeme kapasitelerini ne ölçüde yansıtıyordu? Şirketlerin faaliyet nakdi, fon yatırımları ve bu yatırımların nakde dönüşme riski yeterince değerlendirildi mi? Tahvillerini Türkiye Sigorta satın aldıysa hangi tutarda, hangi tarihte ve hangi yatırım değerlendirmesine dayanarak aldı? Aynı kurumun soruşturmaya konu paylara ve fonlara yaptığı ileri sürülen yatırımlar da bu incelemeye dahil edilmelidir. Türkiye Sigorta’nın Hazine ve Emeklilik Operasyonları Genel Müdür Yardımcısı Gürol Sami Özer’in tahvil alımlarındaki karar, onay ve risk değerlendirme süreçlerindeki rolü de açıklanmalıdır. İhraç gelirlerinin TERA ve Pusula bağlantılı fonlara yönlendirilip yönlendirilmediği, tahvil satışı ile fon alımlarının tarih ve tutarları eşleştirilerek araştırılmalıdır. Burada Pusula ve Katılımevim çevresindeki iki isme dikkat edelim. Pusula’da genel müdürlük yaptığı belirtilen Ayşe Seher Aydın’ın doktora tez danışmanı Erişah Arıcan. Katılımevim Tasarruf Finansman AŞ’nin kurucu ortağı Serdar Turhan ise zamanında Erişah Hanım’ın başında olduğu programda yüksek lisans öğrencisi olmuş bir isim. Bilgi notundaki umre ziyaretine ilişkin anlatım da bu çevrenin sosyal temaslarına işaret ediyor. Yurt dışına hisse transferiyle ilgili belgenin ise hesap sahibi, talimatı veren kişi, alıcı kuruluş ve işlemin gerçekleşip gerçekleşmediği yönünden ayrıca incelenmesi gerekiyor. Bir transfer talimatından hareketle hesabı belirli bir kişiye atfetmek veya işlemin tamamlandığını söylemek doğru olmaz. Araştırılması gereken mekanizmayı sadeleştirelim: Şirket yüksek kredi notuyla borçlanmaya erişiyor; tahvilini Türkiye Sigorta gibi kurumsal yatırımcılara satıyor; elde ettiği parayı yüksek getiri beklentisiyle fonlara yönlendiriyor. Getiri borçlanma maliyetinin üzerinde kaldığında aradaki fark şirkete kazanç sağlıyor. Ama çark tersine döndüğünde fonun muhasebedeki değeri, tahvil ödeme gününde kullanılabilecek nakit anlamına gelmiyor. Fon payları satılamazsa veya değer kaybederse şirketin kupon ve anapara ödemesi zorlaşabiliyor. Şirketin faaliyet nakdi de yetersizse risk, tahvili taşıyan sigorta şirketine veya başka fonlara yayılabiliyor. Bu, belirli şirketler bakımından işlem kayıtlarıyla sınanması gereken bir risk zinciridir. Adil Varlık’a ilişkin ödeme aksaması iddiası da doğru tüzel kişi, vade, tutar ve ödeme bildirimi üzerinden netleştirilmelidir. Ekonomi yönetimine uyarımız açık: Fonlardaki sorunun tahvil piyasasına yayılmasını beklemeyin; ihraç gelirlerinin kullanımını, ödeme takvimlerini ve kurumsal portföylerin riskini şimdi inceleyin. O zaman şu soruyu da sormak gerekiyor. Bütün bunlar olurken Borsa İstanbul’da manipülasyon şüphesi taşıyan işlemleri rapor etmekle görevli birimler ne yapıyordu? Anlatalım: Borsa İstanbul’un genel müdür yardımcılarından biri Sayın Güzhan Gülay zaten Erişah Arıcan’ın doktora öğrencisi. Borsa İstanbul’da en önemli birimlerden biri olan Denetim ve Gözetim Kurulu’nun Başkanı Sayın Filiz Demirkıran. Kendisi bu senenin başına kadar kimin özel kalemiydi? Erişah Arıcan’ın… Tabii bir de Borsa İstanbul’da İç Kontrol ve Risk Yönetimi Birimi var kurum içindeki kontrol süreçlerinin yeterliliğini değerlendiren. O birimin başında da Sayın Elvan Altıkulaç var. Kendisinin doktora tez danışmanını söylemeye bilmem gerek var mı? Elvan Hanım’ın eşi Ertan Bey de Ziraat Bankası’nda Uluslararası Bankacılıktan sorumlu ve tabii ki kendisi de eşi gibi doktora tezini Erişah Hanım ile yazmış! Burada piyasa işlemlerinin gözetimi ile kurum içi kontrolün aynı görev olmadığını da ayıralım. Sorulması gereken, ilgili birimlerin hangi uyarıları hazırladığı, bu uyarıları kime ilettiği ve yönetimin hangi kararları aldığıdır. Tedbirlerin varlığı kadar zamanlaması, kapsamı ve sonuçları da incelenmelidir. Bugün istifası kamuoyuna yansıyan Taha Çakmak, açıklığa kavuşturulması gereken büyük bir ilişki ağının yalnızca bir halkası. Her şey herkesin gözü önünde yaşanırken bu kadar bağlantının, bu kadar yetkinin ve bu kadar sessizliğin nasıl bir araya geldiği açıklanmalıdır. Araştırılması gereken tam da şu: Vatandaşın parasına el uzatanlarla buna göz yumanlar, aynı ağın farklı noktalarında mı duruyordu? Hesaplaşma bir kişinin istifasıyla sınırlanamaz; parayı yönlendiren de kararı onaylayan da uyarıyı görmezden gelen de ortaya çıkarılmalıdır. Bir halka koptu diye zincirin geri kalanını unutturamazsınız."

title: Vahap Seçer'den TBB Başkan Vekili seçilen Ayşe Ünlüce'ye tebrik: Bu görevi başarıyla sürdüreceğine inanıyorum
content:
Türkiye Belediyeler Birliği, TBB Başkanı Vahap Seçer’in tutuklanarak görevden uzaklaştırılması nedeniyle başkan vekili seçimi yaptı. Eskişehir Büyükşehir Belediye Başkanı Ayşe Ünlüce, TBB Başkan Vekilliğine seçildi.

Tutuklu Türkiye Belediyeler Birliği ve Mersin Büyükşehir Belediye Başkanı Vahap Seçer, TBB Başkan Vekilliğine seçilen Eskişehir Büyükşehir Belediye Başkanı Ayşe Ünlüce’yi tebrik etti.

Belediyelerin gücünü temsil ettikleri kentlerin yurttaşlarından aldığını söyleyen Seçer, demokrasi ve milli iradeyi savunmaya devam edeceklerini ifade etti.

Seçer, seçimin ardından yaptığı açıklamada şu ifadeleri kullandı:

“Türkiye Belediyeler Birliği Başkanvekilliği görevine seçilen Eskişehir Büyükşehir Belediye Başkanı Ayşe Ünlüce’yi tebrik ediyorum. Benim de gururla üstlendiğim bu görevi başarıyla sürdüreceğine inanıyorum. Demokrasinin ve milli iradenin en doğrudan tecelli ettiği belediyeler, gücünü temsil ettikleri kentin yurttaşlarından alır. Ülke nüfusunun büyük bölümünü sosyal belediyecilik anlayışıyla kucaklayarak kurduğumuz gönül bağının gücüne inancım tam. Bu inançla, her nerede ve hangi koşulda olursak olalım, demokrasi ve milli iradeyi savunmaya devam edeceğiz.”

author: Isabela Dias
title: Eduardo Bolsonaro vive noite de celebridade na festa da extrema direita nos EUA
content:
Na noite de quarta-feira (14), empresários conservadores, influenciadores digitais e autoridades do governo dos Estados Unidos se reuniram no Andrew W. Mellon Auditorium, na capital Washington, D.C., para a festa de gala da Hispanic Heritage, organizado pela plataforma financeira Latino Wall Street.




O homenageado do evento foi Javier Milei, presidente da Argentina. Seu principal aliado no Brasil, Eduardo Bolsonaro, foi um dos convidados de honra.  




Na entrada, convidados trajados com roupas brilhantes e smokings cercaram Eduardo para tirar selfies e apertos de mão. Muitos perguntavam sobre o pai, Jair Bolsonaro, que cumpre em casa a pena de 27 anos de prisão por tentativa de golpe de Estado. Outros demonstravam entusiasmo com a liderança do irmão Flávio Bolsonaro no primeiro turno da 

disputa presidencial

 contra o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. 




Eduardo conversou com veículos de comunicação identificados com o movimento MAGA (“Make America Great Again”, um dos slogans de Donald Trump), como a ex-boxeadora Cara Castronuova, uma das 

correspondentes da Casa Branca

 alinhadas ao governo. Ele também 

posou

 ao lado de Javier Negre, comunicador espanhol apelidado de “Rei Midas da viralidade”. Negre é sócio de Fernando Cerimedo, marqueteiro argentino de extrema direita, 

detido

 em agosto na Bolívia, acusado de envolvimento em ataque a tiros contra a ex-companheira.    




Em determinado momento, na entrada do evento, uma mulher que parecia ser uma das convidadas segurou o braço de Eduardo e ambos olharam para baixo, compenetrados. Eles rezavam pelo Brasil. Quem também tietava Eduardo Bolsonaro era a autointitulada diplomata espiritual, consultora de direitos humanos e empresária gaúcha 

Luciana Pananos

, que mora nos EUA. 




Do lado de dentro, iniciada a cerimônia, os oradores no palco falavam sobre acabar com a criminalidade e derrotar o socialismo na América Latina. Na plateia, os convidados, que pagaram entre US$ 3 mil e US$ 10 mil para participar do evento, saboreavam almôndegas de wagyu (carne bovina de origem japonesa), pato defumado com amoras, abacate recheado grelhado e filé-mignon bovino defumado. 




“Vamos expulsar o ditador comunista do Brasil”, bradou o homenageado da noite, Javier Milei, após 

abraçar

 calorosamente Eduardo, que deu chutes no ar como se estivesse expulsando Lula do posto. O presidente da Argentina disse ainda que os conservadores “não podem ceder um centímetro em nossa reconquista do hemisfério”. 




“Um discurso inspirador”




Após a fala de Milei, Eduardo discursou. Ele ponderou que o resultado da eleição ainda não estava definido. Mas o tom era abertamente comemorativo. “Quando confirmarmos a vitória do meu irmão, o senador Flávio Bolsonaro, como presidente do Brasil, vamos entrar em uma nova era, que eu chamo de Era de Ouro da América Latina!”




O deputado cassado adotava um dos slogans de Donald Trump, que costuma dizer que o país vive uma nova “era de ouro” sob sua batuta. “Temos tudo para ser iguais aos Estados Unidos”, completou Eduardo.




Durante o discurso, ele também louvou outros presidentes de extrema direita na América Latina, como Nayib Bukele, de El Salvador, e o colombiano Abelardo de la Espriella.




“Amamos todos aqueles que dificultam a vida dos criminosos”, declarou, acrescentando que “pela primeira vez veremos todos os países [da América Latina] combatendo o narcoterrorismo”. O público aprovou e aplaudiu entusiasmado. Um empresário do setor imobiliário que atua em Honduras disse à reportagem que considerou o discurso “inspirador” e que o Brasil deveria adotar o “modelo Bukele”. 




Flávio e Eduardo já 

visitaram

 o CECOT, o megacomplexo penitenciário para onde o governo Trump enviou imigrantes que, segundo 

relatos

, foram torturados. Se a vitória de Flávio Bolsonaro se concretizar, o Brasil pode integrar a coalizão 

Escudo das Américas

, formada por 19 países da região e liderada pelos EUA.  




“O melhor ainda está por vir”, declarou Eduardo Bolsonaro, prometendo libertar o Brasil, começando por seu pai.




Mais que entusiasta da candidatura do irmão à Presidência, Eduardo é um dos nomes mais 

cotados

 para se tornar o próximo ministro das Relações Exteriores do Brasil em um eventual governo de Flávio. Desde que se mudou para os EUA, no início de 2025, o filho 03 de Bolsonaro perdeu o mandato de deputado federal por faltar a mais de 80% das sessões e também foi despojado do 

emprego

 como investigador da Polícia Federal por abandono de posto. 




No início de outubro, o ministro do Supremo Tribunal Federal Alexandre de Moraes 

expediu

 um mandado de prisão contra ele, após sua condenação a mais de quatro anos de prisão por fazer lobby junto ao governo Trump contra o Judiciário brasileiro. Mas, no universo MAGA, Eduardo é uma estrela e a eleição de seu irmão é tratada como um fato consumado.
















Obra de arte autografada por Eduardo Bolsonaro mostra a América Latina sob a bandeira dos EUA




Em conversa com jornalistas antes do evento, Eduardo descartou as preocupações com a ingerência dos EUA nas eleições brasileiras e voltou a repetir 

alegações sem fundamento

 

que já foram contestadas

: segundo ele, durante o governo de Joe Biden, a agência oficial de ajuda humanitária USAID, fechada por Trump em 2025, financiou ONGs e veículos de comunicação sob o pretexto de combater a desinformação, com o objetivo de impedir a reeleição de Jair Bolsonaro em 2022.




“O Brasil já sofreu uma interferência internacional. O que eu vejo agora é justamente o oposto”, afirmou. A primeira medida de um eventual governo de seu irmão seria “expurgar esse câncer chamado Alexandre de Moraes” do STF, disse ele, referindo-se ao ministro como um “tirano”. Caso contrário, seu irmão não conseguiria governar, na opinião do deputado cassado. Perguntado se voltaria para o Brasil mesmo com o pedido de prisão, Eduardo negou. “Eu não vou puxar uma cadeia sendo inocente, não”, afirmou.




Eduardo circulava pelo salão de baile acompanhado de perto pelo blogueiro de extrema direita Allan dos Santos. Foragido nos EUA desde 2021, quando teve prisão decretada pelo Supremo, o blogueiro é investigado em dois inquéritos sobre a criação de milícias digitais e propagação de fake news.
















Eduardo Bolsonaro cercado pelo blogueiro foragido por Allan do Santos e por membros da Revista Timeline




Presença frequente em eventos conservadores nos EUA, Eduardo também conversou informalmente com Matt Schlapp, presidente da Conferência de Ação Política Conservadora (CPAC), e sua mulher, Mercedes, que mencionou os Bolsonaro em seu discurso e previu que Flávio será eleito presidente do Brasil. “Colocamos a América Latina de volta nos trilhos”, afirmou ela.




Já no fim da noite, enquanto os convidados dançavam ao som de 

La Bamba

, 

Conga

 e 

Macarena

, a reportagem conversou com Lena Ruseva, que vestia um longo vestido vermelho estampado com o rosto de Trump e a frase “Drill, baby, drill” (“Perfure, baby, perfure”, slogan de Trump em alusão à exploração de petróleo).




Autodenominada artista 

America First

, Ruseva contou que Milei havia gostado tanto do retrato que ela fez dele especialmente para a ocasião que quis ficar com a obra. Ela também demonstrou orgulho do quadro que teria dado de presente a Trump em um de seus aniversários.







A artista trumpista Lena Ruseva em entrevista na chegada à festa







Algumas de suas obras estavam expostas no salão e seriam leiloadas, com lances iniciais de US$ 10 mil. Entre elas, havia uma representação da bandeira americana com o contorno da América Latina. Eduardo Bolsonaro assinou a obra com letras douradas.




“Disse a ele que ficaria com o quadro até que se tornasse o próximo presidente do Brasil”, contou ela.

author: Equality Now
title: Consent does not depend on one’s level of intoxication: The Cornell University Case in review
content:
15th October 2026










Consent does not depend on one’s level of intoxication: The Cornell University Case in review
















14 min read



















News and Insights




End sexual violence




United States


























































Image credit: Matthew Poveromo / Shutterstock.com




The allegations presented in the 

sexual violence case involving a Cornell University student

 describe egregious acts of sexual violence and profound violations of the human rights of the alleged survivor. The case returned to public attention two years after the alleged assault, when the accuser, known publicly as Jane Doe, filed a civil lawsuit in 2026, bringing renewed scrutiny to the handling of her allegations and the evidence surrounding them while simultaneously raising serious concerns about whether criminal justice systems are fit to conduct thorough investigations, prosecutions, and adjudications of sexual violence cases. 




In November 2024, 

a Cornell University student reported being sexually assaulted the month before by multiple men at a fraternity house

. According to her account and evidence subsequently reviewed by the University, she had consumed alcohol and drugs, including the dissociative drug ketamine, which left her severely incapacitated and unable to consent to sexual activity. She reported that multiple men entered the room at different points during the evening, and that several attempted to grope, kiss, or have sex with her despite her incapacitation. She also described gaps in her memory. During the alleged assault, one member of the fraternity shared messages on a group chat of more than 50 members, indicating that a woman was upstairs and available for sex, inviting others to join. Other members reportedly responded to and discussed the invitation in lieu of reporting the abuse. 




Cornell subsequently conducted a 

Title IX investigation

, resulting in disciplinary sanctions against several students. The local District Attorney’s Office declined to investigate, and so no criminal charges were pursued at the time. The criminal investigation has now been reopened, with New York Attorney General Letitia James appointed as special prosecutor.




All criminal investigations must be assessed on the evidence, and anyone accused of a crime is entitled to due process. Yet, too often, criminal justice systems approach sexual violence cases through assumptions about force, resistance, credibility, or a survivor’s conduct and behaviour, rather than applying the same scrutiny to whether a person was able to freely consent to sexual activity.




A person who is unconscious or otherwise incapable of freely consenting cannot consent to sex. At the centre of this case, regardless of its eventual outcome, is a fundamental question: whether the one’s capacity to consent to sex was properly examined at all.  




Gaps in sexual violence law can harm survivors




Reporting sexual violence can require a survivor to recount deeply personal experiences to officials, investigators, police, prosecutors and lawyers, often while facing intense scrutiny of their choices, conduct, and credibility. In this case, the student has spent nearly two years navigating university, criminal and civil proceedings in pursuit of justice.




The reopening of a criminal case, particularly when the adequacy of a prior investigation of sexual violence allegations is under question, 

has the potential to retraumatize survivors who will be forced to recount their experiences

 yet again. However, this case presents an important opportunity to examine how New York’s judicial system and the laws that govern it can become capable of delivering justice when survivors report sexual violence.  




In 19 US states, including New York, sexual assault laws distinguish between voluntary and involuntary intoxication

 in ways that can make prosecution for rape more difficult when a survivor voluntarily consumed alcohol or drugs. In these states,

 the law fails to recognise that a person who has become incapable of consenting is incapable of consenting, regardless of how they reached that state.




Under New York’s Penal Law, 

most sexual offences are defined by lack of consent based on either forcible compulsion or incapacity

, although certain offences, including rape in the third degree, also recognise when a person clearly expresses that they do not want s to engage in sexual activity, even in the absence of force or incapacity, as lack of consent. Circumstances including statutory rape where someone over 21 engages in sexual activity with someone under 17 are also considered rape in the third degree. 




A person is considered “mentally incapacitated” when they are temporarily incapable of appraising or controlling their conduct because of a substance administered without their consent, or due to another nonconsensual act. New York law also recognises that someone who is unconscious or physically unable to communicate unwillingness cannot consent. However, it does not address situations in which a person voluntarily consumes alcohol or drugs and later becomes too incapacitated to consent, but remains physically able to communicate.




This creates a significant gap in legal protection

. The key question the law should define is 

whether all parties freely consented to a sexual act, not whether someone made the “right” choices beforehand

. Just as voluntary intoxication does not amount to consent to being robbed or physically assaulted, it should never diminish a person’s right to protection from sexual violence.




Yet sexual violence laws in some states continue to make distinctions that shift attention away from the conduct of the alleged perpetrator and onto the survivor’s decisions prior to the assault.




A legislative response to drug-facilitated sexual assault in the United States

 




New York lawmakers have repeatedly introduced legislation to address this problem. 

Senate Bill S10632,

 which would prohibit the use of a victim’s intoxication as a defence in sex crimes, passed the State Senate in June 2026, but was not taken up by the State Assembly before the end of the legislative session on June 5.  




A separate bill, 

S4540/A5265

, proposed a broader, consent-based approach by defining consent to sexual contact as a knowing, voluntary, and mutual decision among all participants.  If New York is to properly address the issues raised by this case and strengthen protections against sexual violence, 

legislators must reintroduce both bills at the start of the 2027 Legislative Session.

 




Other US states have also taken steps to address these gaps. Texas enacted 

the Summer Willis Act in 2025

, which recognises sexual activity as nonconsensual where the perpetrator knows the other person is intoxicated or impaired to the extent that they are incapable of consenting. 




These reforms demonstrate that laws can and must evolve to better protect individuals from sexual violence. Sexual assault laws need to better align with 

international human rights standards of consent

, instead of forcing survivors to fit outdated legal definitions and understanding of rape.




The Cornell case raises questions about institutional responsibility




For years, 

the United States has repeatedly confronted allegations of sexual violence on college campuses

. Each time, there is a moment of public outrage. Universities promise reform. Task forces are established. Policies are rewritten. Training is announced. But the question regarding institutional accountability remains unresolved. 




The challenge of effectively addressing sexual volence are compounded by a shifting federal landscape that defines how colleges are expected to respond to sexual violence. The Department of Education’s Office for Civil Rights, which investigates alleged violations of Title IX, the law that governs how universities that receive federal funding investigate and respond to sexual harassment and sexual violence and other federal civil rights laws, has faced major staffing reductions and a shift in enforcement priorities. 

Reporting has documented a substantial decline in investigations into sexual violence, alongside a backlog of unresolved civil rights complaints

. In September 2026, the Department formally reinstated the 2020 Title IX regulations, which provide a narrower definition of sexual harassment than the 2024 rules. 




While changes to regulations are not uncommon, they can often lead to a shift in how institutions respond before there is sustained progress in how sexual violence is prevented, investigated, and addressed. Policies and procedures can only be impactful if institutions consistently apply them and provide a meaningful route to accountability for sexual violence.




Bystanders are part of the response to sexual violence




Effectively addressing sexual violence also requires confronting the attitudes, behaviours and responsibility of those who witness, enable or fail to intervene in situations where someone may be at risk. 




In the Cornell case, the reported messages shared in the fraternity group chat during the alleged assault, in addition to 

communications that appear to reflect efforts to manage its fallout

, hinge more on reputational protection than prevention of an irreparable harm against the alleged survivor. And following the filing of her civil suit, 

Doe has reportedly faced numerous threats and open hostility for coming forward

. 




Time and time again, 

we’re seeing the focus of sexual violence cases become about protecting a group

 or questioning the person who reports harm, which moves attention away from the conduct at the centre of the allegations. 




Research highlights that sexual violence has become normalised within some groups

, particularly when people treat another person’s vulnerability as entertainment, an opportunity, or simply someone else’s problem. Where people are aware that someone is at risk but fail to act, sexual violence has the opportunity to flourish, and a culture of silence and impunity can take hold. 




That is why sexual violence investigations cannot place the burden of prevention and accountability on survivors alone. 

Survivors already carry the consequences of what happened, as well as the burden of reporting

, recounting their experiences, and navigating systems that may question or scrutinise them. Expecting survivors to be the primary force confronting a culture that enables sexual violence leaves a fundamental part of the problem untouched.




Addressing rape culture means confronting multiple forms of apathy that enable impunity.

 The Cornell case should prompt universities and communities to examine how they can foster a culture of intervention, collective responsibility, and accountability before this happens again. 




New York and other jurisdictions must close voluntary intoxication loopholes and move toward consent-based definitions of rape consistent with international human rights standards.




All of us must challenge the attitudes that allow sexual violence to persist, including the notion that drinking, taking drugs, flirting, or merely existing can somehow amount to consent to sexual violence.

title: Resmi Gazete'de atama kararları: Hazine ve Maliye Bakan Yardımcılığına Bekir Bayrakdar atandı
content:
Cumhurbaşkanı Tayyip Erdoğan imzasını taşıyan atama kararları Resmi Gazete'de yayımlandı. Buna göre Hazine ve Maliye Bakan Yardımcılığına Bekir Bayrakdar, Devlet Opera ve Balesi Genel Müdürlüğüne Can Atilla, Milli Savunma Bakanlığı Personel Genel Müdürlüğüne Cüneyt Epcim atandı. Kararlarda ayrıca Dışişleri, Ticaret Bakanlığı, DSİ, Vakıflar Genel Müdürlüğü ve DHMİ'de de yeni görevlendirmeler yer aldı.

Kültür ve Turizm Bakanlığı Yaşayan Miras ve Kültürel Etkinlikler Genel Müdür Yardımcısı Vildan Satık görevden alınırken, yerine Pervin Oymak atandı.

Tarım İşletmeleri Genel Müdürlüğü Yönetim Kurulu Üyesi Yener Yıldırım görevden alınırken, boşalan üyeliğe kalan süreyi tamamlamak üzere Göktuğ Bağlı atandı.

Devlet Su İşleri Genel Müdürlüğünde ise VI. Bölge Müdürlüğüne Mehmet Akif Kaygusuz, IX. Bölge Müdürlüğüne Ömer Açıkgöz getirildi. Devlet Hava Meydanları İşletmesi Genel Müdürlüğünde açık bulunan Yönetim Kurulu Üyeliğine de Selami Yapıcı getirildi.

Devlet Hava Meydanları İşletmesi Genel Müdürlüğünde açık bulunan Genel Müdür Yardımcılığına ise Ertuğrul Karatay atandı.
