author: Anooradha Iyer Siddiqi
title: Reading List: Anooradha Iyer Siddiqi
content:
We are taught to think of a refugee camp as an object produced in an instant, only in response to an emergency — one brought on, perhaps, by those seeking refuge. We are taught that refugee environments are provisional and abject, moreover, to be naturalized as such within the African landscape — 

as

 the African landscape. We are taught to misread migrant spaces as lacking history or architectural expression. To counter these misdirections, 

Architecture of Migration: The Dadaab Refugee Camps and Humanitarian Settlement

 looks closely at the complex settlements, ecologies, domesticities, archives, and material aesthetics. In Ifo, Dagahaley, and Hagadera camps, established in 1991 by the Kenyan government and the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees at Dadaab, Kenya, in lands shared with Somalia and Ethiopia, the book finds African, Muslim, and Afro-Asian aesthetic worlds and a historical repository of partition, sedentarization, and migration. Dadaab forms a material afterlife of events long unfolding, through colonial and postcolonial time and space, and in multiple registers, aesthetic as well as social.

My book is grounded in 14 years of feminist and critical collective practice and research (see 

Cohabitations

, 

Dadaab Commons

, 

Feminist Architectural Histories of Migration

, 

Insurgent Domesticities

, and 

Settlement

). While researching in dozens of archives and libraries in Africa, Asia, and Europe, and interviewing hundreds of women practicing architecture and art, representing governments, cultural institutions, and nongovernmental agencies, or living life in refugee camps, I read many books! If the anticolonial thought in Frantz Fanon’s 

Black Skin, White Masks

 and Walter Rodney’s 

How Europe Underdeveloped Africa

 anchored my work, its everyday tugs and buoying came from feminists.

Ifo camp Chairlady Isnina Ali Rage. Photo by author, 2011.

My study of the handcrafted acacia camp environments and interviews with many of their builders — including Ifo Chairlady Isnina Ali Rage and shopowner Shamso Abdullahi Farah, and Dagahaley farmer Maganai Saddiq Hassan — gave shape to a consciousness rooted in the social and ecological worldmaking of African, Muslim, and Global South feminists. Let me begin with three. Sylvia Tamale not only insists on decolonizing master narratives that suppress multiplicity in 

Decolonization and Afro-Feminism

, but through her years of activism in Uganda and beyond, plants the working and thinking of African feminists on the ground, in the natural environment. This perspective is hardly limited to African feminists, as Radha D’Souza demonstrates in the 

Court for Intergenerational Climate Crimes

 — based on her book 

What’s Wrong with Rights?: Social Movements, Law and Liberal Imaginations

 — which foregrounds the workhorse labor and the place of the indigo plant (Comrade Indigo) within majority-world feminist intellectual commitment; she dispenses with reductive “West versus Rest” critiques through the perspectives of European underground and Third World intellectuals in the co-edited 

Decolonizing Knowledge: Looking Back, Moving Forward

 (

open access

). Further articulating the vitality of social difference to inform constructions of knowledge, Saba Mahmood argues that those constructions must assert against universalizing epistemes, secular as well as religious, in her foundational work on Cairo’s women, 

Politics of Piety: The Islamic Revival and the Feminist Subject

.

Store and shelters designed and built by Shamso Abdullahi Farah, Ifo camp. Photo by author, 2011.

From there, global Black feminisms were my north star. Yvonne Adhiambo Owuor’s 

Dust

 dwelt within the landscapes of Kenya’s Northeast, the erstwhile colonial “frontier” constituted of migratory lifeways and marabou storks; her habitations haunt my book’s histories of land, emergency territory, and sedentarized pastoralists. 

Lose Your Mother: A Journey Along the Atlantic Slave Route

, Saidiya Hartman’s attempt to fill in the blank slate of the historical record and her own life, helped me think with the stories of enslaved children freed from Indian Ocean 

dhows

, raised near Bombay, and resettled near Mombasa: the negotiation between rescuer and rescued in the East African abolitionist settlement of Freretown that forms Dadaab’s prehistory. My book stands on the shoulders of Mabel O. Wilson’s work on: (1) spatial agency, as rooted in the bodies of builders and the physical labor of construction, in an essay on the “provisional demos” of the African American protest camp in 

Design, Displacement, Migration: Spatial and Material Histories

, and (2) the inseparability of racial thought from modern subjecthood and the architectural discipline, which grew together out of Enlightenment reason and abstraction, in 

Negro Building: Black Americans in the World of Fairs and Museums

 and the co-edited 

Race and Modern Architecture: A Critical History from the Enlightenment to the Present

.

“Frere Town,” courtesy of National Museums of Kenya, Nairobi. Sibbie (née Bazett) Burns Photograph Album, Album II, c. 1892–late 1890s.

My book argues that the humanitarian environment, intended as temporary, paradoxically affects settlement. Architectural historians develop a feminist provincialization of their field in grappling with migration’s immanence to settlement. In 

Fallow Fields: The Remnant Landscapes and Residual Architectures of Imperial Germany’s Settler Frontier

, Hollyamber Kennedy articulates the displacement and unsettlement of people in German South West Africa (Namibia) and Eastern Prussia (Poland) together, within the nineteenth-century development of state policy to sedentarize and fix populations, eradicating migratory ways of life. 

Open Architecture: Migration, Citizenship, and the Urban Renewal of Berlin-Kreuzberg by IBA-1984/87

, Esra Akcan’s study of the International Building Exhibition (a historical landmark of both architectural modernism and social housing), is a story of migrant inhabitation. In 

The Remittance Landscape: Spaces of Migration in Rural Mexico and Urban USA

, Sarah Lynn Lopez tracks economic flows in built environments on either side of a fraught border.

My book argues that longstanding refugee settlements — aid environments long utilized to slowly confine migrants and police the border — are not de facto architectures to be understood teleologically, as if brought by people upon themselves, but instead predicated upon foundational partitions. This thinking draws on Vazira Fazila-Yacoobali Zamindar’s positioning of partition not as an event but as a concept, in 

The Long Partition and the Making of Modern South Asia: Refugees, Boundaries, Histories

. In it, the violence of a partition is not a vague consequence of border conflict, but the direct result of bureaucratic shaping, as states attempted to resolve political uncertainty — debunking the myth that India and Pakistan somehow emerged fully formed as partitioned states, but rather, partitioned through a process of urban shaping. This is so with Palestine, Ireland, and Somalia itself. Safia Aidid’s 

Pan-Somali Dreams: Ethiopia, Greater Somalia, and the Somali Nationalist Imagination

 shows a political imaginary of possible futures based on territorial unification, conceived in reaction to a colonial present; Greater Somalia was not merely a nationalist movement but, following Raymond Williams, “a structure of feeling.” My book argues in favor of such feeling, which overcomes the partitioning principle, toward a straddling collectivity.

author: Shams Eddin Essam
title: Will Supply Ministry’s wheat intervention really rein in cost of unsubsidized bread?
content:
As the grain and bakery industries petition the government for permission to increase bread prices in order to protect their profits, the Supply Ministry has 

announced

 it is injecting wheat onto the national commodity exchange to bring prices down and cut production costs.




The move came after calls for a government review of bread pricing guidelines in 

August

 and 

September

. Producers said they needed to increase consumer prices to compensate for rising production costs, particularly of flour. 

Despite talks between ministry and industry representatives, the government has held the price caps and loaf weight specifications 

steady

, announcing the supply release instead.




However, sources from the grain, milling and bakery industries who spoke to Mada Masr expressed doubt that the mechanism would meaningfully reduce production costs, indicating that the last time the ministry undertook a similar supply allocation in 2023, the move only fuelled profiteering on a secondary market that emerged in parallel to the commodity exchange.




The ministry has not said how much wheat it will offer via the commodity exchange, though ministry spokespeople 

explained

 that the extra supply would be enough to bring costs down across the supply chain.




Speaking on condition of anonymity, two grain industry sources told Mada Masr that the imported wheat is expected to be available via the Egyptian Commodities Exchange either this week or next. Sales are to be capped at 500 tonnes per mill, and, as per the agreement with the ministry, two trading sessions would be held weekly, the sources said.




The CEO of the commodity exchange 

told

 financial newspapers on Tuesday that trading had begun this week.




The ministry aims to sell wheat at LE16,500-LE16,700 per tonne. The sources said supplies will be available to all licensed mills, allowing more flour for bakeries that produce commercial bread, such as fino and “tourist” loaves.




However, the announced prices alone are not enough to convince mills to buy wheat through the exchange, said another grain industry chamber member.




A tonne of wheat currently costs LE16,800-LE17,200 on the open market, depending on quality.




But once the additional costs of participating in trading on the commodity exchange are factored in, the gap between the exchange price and the open market price narrows.




The source said that mills remain skeptical about the value of going to the exchange under its current system, given the registration and trading fees involved — costs they do not necessarily incur when purchasing directly from traders.




The source added that it would be difficult to assess whether the government’s price is competitive or not before learning more about the specifications and quality of the wheat being offered. When buying directly from private sector suppliers, mills can inspect a shipment before completing a purchase.




A mill owner said that there are questions beyond the immediate cost of the wheat: can the government ensure a steady supply of wheat through the commodity exchange to control costs and justify the cost of switching to the exchange?




Until the government’s mechanism proves capable of consistently meeting market demand, dealing with established suppliers is the more transparent option, he said. 




Global wheat prices have risen amid Russia’s escalating war on Ukraine, disrupting Black Sea shipping and ultimately pushing costs up in Egypt, the world’s largest wheat importer.




While the government says it has bought more domestically grown wheat, Egypt is still heavily reliant on wheat imports from both Russia and Ukraine. The cost pressures have become increasingly evident in Egypt’s domestic flour market over recent months. The price of a tonne of imported wheat stood at around LE12,500 in June, with a ton of unsubsidized flour at around LE17,000. Now, a ton of unsubsidized flour stands at around LE21,000.




Flour, in turn, accounts for between 60-70 percent of the production cost of commercial bread, according to an estimate from an anonymous General Bakeries Division source. This makes rising flour prices a direct strain on bakeries’ profit margins, particularly alongside 

increases

 in other operating costs.




A bakeries division member told Mada Masr that resuming wheat sales through the exchange would not be an adequate solution to the gap between the production costs of unsubsidized bread and the prices set by the Supply Ministry. The government used the same mechanism around three years ago, the source said, without adequately increasing the supply of raw materials available to bakeries to ease cost pressures.




Bakeries’ costs include various production inputs, all of which are impacted as the exchange value of the Egyptian pound continues to fall against the dollar, which is currently trading at LE53, up from less than LE49 at the end of August.




The Supply Ministry last 

offered

 imported wheat via the exchange from October 2023 until January 21, 2024. Then-Supply Minister Ali Meselhy attributed the trading suspension to price speculation on domestic wheat prices. 

At the time, sources who 

spoke

 to Mada Masr pointed not only to the small quantities offered by the ministry, which limited their impact on market prices, but also said that several mills that weren’t actively processing grain at the time registered as buyers on the exchange only to bull and then resell the government-offered wheat at higher prices in the free market.




The commodity exchange was 

established

 by prime ministerial decree in 2020 as an organized market for trading storable commodities through what the exchange itself describes as an “important” pricing mechanism.

 

Meselhy 

described

 it at the time as a way to regulate prices, saying it would promote market transparency and reduce price disparities across markets.

 

The post 

Will Supply Ministry’s wheat intervention really rein in cost of unsubsidized bread?

 first appeared on 

Mada Masr

.

author: Unknown
title: У политзаключённого анархиста Никиты Уварова умерла тётя: поддержите его письмом!
content:
На днях в семье Никиты Уварова случилось горе — умерла Татьяна, сестра его мамы Анны. По сообщению группы поддержки, семьи были очень близки, Татьяна поддерживала Никиту и вместе с его мамой приезжала к нему на свидания. Никита уже знает о её смерти.

«Мы выражаем глубокие соболезнования Никите, Анне и всем родным и близким Татьяны, - пишет группа поддержки. - Переживать потерю близкого человека особенно тяжело в заключении, вдали от семьи. Сейчас Никита находится в одиночной камере СИЗО-1 Красноярска. При этом возможности общаться с родными у него практически нет: из-за того, что следствие сделало его маму свидетельницей по новому уголовному делу, им запрещены свидания и телефонные разговоры».

8 октября суд в очередной раз продлил Никите содержание под стражей ещё на два месяца. Напомним, он должен был выйти на свободу 19 марта, полностью отбыв 5-летний срок по «делу канских подростков», но незадолго до освобождения против него возбудили новое уголовное дело. В августе обвинение ужесточили — теперь ему вменяют сразу две статьи за один и тот же разговор с другим заключённым.

Адрес для писем: 660075, РФ, г. Красноярск, ул. Республики, 72, СИЗО-1, Уваров Никита Андреевич 2005 г. р. Отправить письмо можно через сервисы «Ф-письмо», «Зонателеком» и PrisonMail.Online (для зарубежных карт).

author: Unknown
title: Ekrem İmamoğlu hakkında yeni bir soruşturma daha açıldı: Akın Gürlek'le telefon görüşmesini anlatmıştı
content:
İstanbul Büyükşehir Belediyesi Başkanı Ekrem İmamoğlu hakkında İBB Davası'nda kürsüde savunma yaparken soruşturma başlatıldı. Bakırköy Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığı tarafından başlatılan soruşturmada gerekçe olarak “kamu görevlisine görevinden dolayı aleni hakaret” gösterildi.

Soruşturma nedeninin İmamoğlu'nun savunması esnasında Adalet Bakanı Akın Gürlek ile telefon görüşmesini anlatması ve bunu anlatırken taklit yapması olarak gösterildi.

Başsavcılık tarafından yapılan açıklamada şu ifadelere yer verildi:

“İstanbul 33. Ağır Ceza Mahkemesi’nin 2026/208 Esas sayılı dosyasının sanıklarından olan Ekrem İMAMOĞLU’nun 15/10/2026 tarihli duruşmadaki, kamu davasına esas soruşturmayı yürüten yargı mensuplarını hedef alan ifadeleri nedeniyle, “kamu görevlilerine görevi nedeniyle aleni hakaret” suçundan, Bakırköy Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığınca resen soruşturma başlatılmıştır. Kamuoyunun bilgisine saygıyla duyurulur.”

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: David Venn
title: President, community director roles up for grabs in QIA election
content:
The Qikiqtani Inuit Association is looking for its next president.




It’s also looking for community directors in Iqaluit, Igloolik, Kimmirut, Sanirajak, Clyde River, Pond Inlet and Sanikiluaq, said a news release issued Thursday by Markoosie Qaunirq, spokesperson for QIA.




Each position carries a four-year term.




The nomination period for the election runs from Nov. 9 to 13.




Eligible voters must be Inuit, enrolled under the Nunavut Agreement; at least 16 years old; and have resided in the Qikiqtani Region for one year or more, according to the release.




The current QIA president Olayuk Akesuk 

won

 the 2022 election over Paul Okalik, with 61.2 per cent of the vote. He had served in the role since the fall of 2021, when he took over from P.J. Akeeagok, who resigned to run for MLA.




Election day is set for Dec. 14.

author: Chris Walker
title: Americans’ Confidence in Food Safety Plummets Amid Summer of Recalls
content:
Experts have expressed deep concern over Trump administration cuts to federal food monitoring systems.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

Americans’ confidence in the safety of the food supply has plummeted, as has their belief in federal food safety standards, according to a new poll from Gallup.

When asked about their confidence in the safety of food in grocery stores across the country, only 65 percent of respondents said they are either “very confident” or “somewhat confident.” While that figure represents a majority of respondents, it’s the lowest confidence rating that Gallup has recorded since it began asking the question in 2019, when 81 percent expressed confidence that the food they were buying was safe.

Additionally, the poll found that respondents are skeptical of how well the Trump administration is ensuring the safety of the food supply. According to the poll, only 47 percent of Americans have a “great deal” or “fair amount” of confidence that the federal government is making sure the food supply is safe, while 53 percent say their confidence levels reach the “not much” or “none” levels.

It’s the first time in the poll’s history that the confidence level in the federal government’s ability to keep food safe has dipped below 50 percent.

The lack of confidence in the government’s ability to monitor and keep food safe comes amid a spate of food warnings this past summer, including recalls of jalapeños, berries, beef, alfalfa sprouts, and more items. A record-breaking cyclosporiasis outbreak relating to lettuce sales sickened thousands with intense bouts of diarrhea, including at least two documented deaths.

One week in August this year saw recalls of 12 different food products. That number is four times higher than it was during a similar period last year, and six times higher than it was in 2024.

Some disease researchers have blamed the Trump White House for the increases in foodborne illness outbreaks and recalls, noting that cuts by the administration, stemming mainly from its so-called “Department of Government Efficiency” (DOGE) initiative, have made monitoring difficult and response time slower.

Indeed, the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) lost around one-fifth of its staff since President Donald Trump returned to office, and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) has lost around 25 percent, including most members of a food parasite-tracking team.

Microbiologist and founder of Food Safety Strategy Jennifer McEntire told Stateline earlier this year that there are “valid questions around the timing of the response” from the administration to the cyclosporiasis crisis, including “the time it took for agencies to recognize the outbreak and to start to investigate it.”

Susan Mayne, an adjunct professor at the Yale School of Public Health and former head of the FDA, has also questioned the Trump administration’s cuts to food safety standards.

“We had a national advisory committee, a committee that advised FDA and [the U.S. Department of Agriculture] on how to prevent microbial contamination in food,” Mayne said back in July. “That advisory committee was disbanded. We used to convene meetings with our Mexican counterparts on how we can work together to improve food safety. That entire team was let go.”

author: Jake Johnson
title: “Because of the Price of Oil … We’re Making a Fortune,” Trump Says at Rally
content:
Trump, who has profited massively from his second term in the White House, is a major investor in oil and gas companies.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

President Donald Trump attempted to spin high oil prices as a boon for the United States at a rally in Arizona on Wednesday, just hours after new federal data showed that inflation reached its highest level in months in September.

“Because of the price of oil, Texas and Oklahoma and North Dakota and all these places, we’re making a fortune,” Trump declared, referring to states that produce large amounts of crude oil. Those states are home to major fossil fuel companies that have reported windfall profits amid Trump’s illegal war on Iran.

Trump insisted that gas prices — currently at an average of $4.33 per gallon for regular gas and $6.32 for diesel — would tumble once the Iran war ends, but his administration has repeatedly given false timelines for the deadly conflict and has shown no indication that it is willing to reach a lasting diplomatic agreement.

Trump, who has profited massively from his second term in the White House, is a major investor in oil and gas companies. According to one recent analysis, the president’s investments in fossil fuel stocks have boosted his net worth by up to $15.5 million since January.

Working-class Americans, meanwhile, are struggling to make ends meet as high gas prices compound a broader affordability crisis that extends to food, housing, and other necessities. A tracker maintained by the Watson School of International and Public Affairs estimates that American consumers have paid an extra $135 billion combined in fuel costs since the start of the Iran war — roughly $1,030 per household.

Wage growth has not kept up with inflation, which rose to an annualized rate of 3.7% last month.

“Workers are losing the race between wages and prices,” Elise Gould, senior economist at the Economic Policy Institute, wrote on Wednesday. “Nominal wage growth continues to decelerate as workers lose bargaining power at work. Workers simply don’t have the leverage to bid up their wages. Reduced leverage and higher prices translated into falling [year-over-year] real wages for six months in a row.”

“Workers have seen zero progress on affordability compared to January 2025,” Gould added. “Real wages are essentially stagnant as workers’ leverage has declined and prices have risen. It’s no wonder workers feel left behind in the current economy.”

A Harris poll published by The Guardian on Thursday shows that three-quarters of US voters are concerned about a recession, and a “vast majority of Americans agreed that there is an affordability crisis, including 96% of Republicans.”

author: Maríangeles Guerrero
title: "Creemos en la potencia política de los feminismos para sembrar semillas de esperanza"
content:
Por Mariángeles Guerrero




Desde Córdoba




De todas las provincias, del campo y de la ciudad, llegan mujeres, lesbianas, travestis, trans. Viajan hace 40 años para encontrarse. Para compartir con otras lo que viven cotidianamente en sus territorios, para aprender de otras experiencias, para contar las propias. Este año, el 

39° Encuentro Plurinacional de Mujeres, Lesbianas, Travestis, Trans, Bisexuales, Intersexuales y No Binaries

 se realizó el fin de semana pasado en Córdoba capital. Los temas a debatir se organizaron por ejes. En el Eje Soberanía, la soberanía alimentaria tuvo su propio taller. Carina Vallejo, de la Unión de Trabajadoras y Trabajadores de la Tierra (UTT) de Santiago del Estero rescata “la fuerza de poner en común nuestras realidades y darte cuenta de que no estás sola”.




Y añade: ”Poder encontrarnos, escucharnos y ver que las problemáticas del agua, la tierra y el modelo de producción nos atraviesan a todas por igual en distintos puntos del país nos fortalece muchísimo. Nos permite 

salir del aislamiento del interior

 y llevar nuestras voces comunitarias a debates colectivos y asambleas de mujeres”.




Dhanna Moyano es travesti, productora caprina en Luján de Cuyo (Mendoza), integrante del Movimiento Nacional Campesino Indígena-Somos Tierra (MNCI-ST) y representante de Argentina en la Coordinadora Latinoamericana de Organizaciones del Campo (CLOC) - Vía Campesina. Fue una de las participantes del Encuentro y señala que la masividad que tuvo es una muestra del enojo que hay hacia el Gobierno. “

Hemos tenido travesticidios, femicidios, ventas de nuestras tierras

. Hoy estamos defendiendo la soberanía alimentaria porque es preocupante para nuestros cuerpos y cuerpas en todo el país. Este 15 de octubre tenemos que salir a defender que no nos vendan las tierras, porque venderlas es despojar a las familias campesinas, a las comunidades indígenas y al colectivo de la diversidad que está retomando ese camino”, denuncia.




Y agrega: “Nos abrazamos, lloramos, porque estamos mal en todo el país pero también estamos dando una gran lucha por un país soberano, libre y con igualdad de derechos para todos y para todas”.







Subraya que las diversidades sexuales son parte de la lucha campesina porque es un proyecto de vida concreto para ellas. “El Estado dice que las travestis nos morimos entre los 35 y 40 años por la calidad de vida que llevamos. Volver al campo implica que esa calidad de vida aumenta, porque es una vida más sana, más saludable”, explica.







Ante el desmantelamiento de las políticas para la agricultura familiar y las políticas de género, 

la presencia de la realidad campesina en los debates feministas se vuelve urgente

. En este Encuentro, por primera vez la UTT, el MNCI-ST y el Movimiento Nacional Campesino Indígena marcharon en una misma columna, representando a las organizaciones campesinas.




Carolina Llorens, del MNCI-ST y del Movimiento Campesino de Córdoba (MCC) remarca “la potencia política que tenemos los feminismos de articular luchas ante un horizonte tan fragmentado y sembrar semillas de esperanza y de organización”. Y apunta que ese es el rol que tienen los feminismos campesinos, indígenas y populares. Y que los encuentros son un espacio potenciador de esa presencia política, del protagonismo de las mujeres y las diversidades.




Graciela Salto vive a 60 kilómetros de la localidad de Quimilí (departamento Moreno, al este de Santiago del Estero). Es la primera vez que participa de un Encuentro. “Aquí se dice la verdad, uno no viene con invento, dice lo que conoce. En la vida del campo es muy importante la tierra. Y si la defendemos, es para algo bueno, para algo sano. Es para la familia, para nuestros abuelos, para nuestros hijos”, valora.




Salto participó del Encuentro con la bandera del MNCI en la espalda, junto a su hija y otras compañeras que viajaron con ella. Cuenta que el mensaje que fue a compartir con compañeras de otras provincias es lo que sucede en su territorio: las fumigaciones con agrotóxicos y los desalojos. “No podemos criar animales porque te los envenenan, no podemos poner una fruta o una verdura por el tema del veneno. Y si nos desalojan, ¿adónde vamos a ir? No queremos irnos, somos nacidos y criados en el campo”.




Al encuentro llevó su bandera y la realidad del lugar donde vive. Y vuelve a su casa, dice, “con muchos recuerdos de todo lo que se habló y de las compañeras que conocí”.




Encontrarse




Para poder viajar desde el departamento Figueroa (centro de Santiago del Estero), Vallejo y sus compañeras organizaron rifas y bingos para costear los pasajes, con premios que donaron los propios compañeros y compañeras. Además recibieron ayuda de la coordinación de la UTT para conseguir hospedaje y garantizar la alimentación. En su caso, también recibió la colaboración de ENI Argentina (Estrategia Nacional de Involucramiento de la Coalición Internacional por la Tierra - ILC). Los esfuerzos organizativos tuvieron el objetivo de llevar a Córdoba las dificultades que tienen las familias campesinas para construir soberanía alimentaria y producir agroecológicamente: la falta de políticas para el sector campesino y un contexto de beneficios al agronegocio y a las mineras.




Para ella, lo más significativo fue “poder poner en palabras y exponer nuestras vivencias como campesinas del interior del país, llevando la voz de la Secretaría de Mujeres Campesinas de la UTT”. Indica que fue clave mostrar que los 

problemas en el acceso a la tierra y al agua

 no pasan solo en Santiago del Estero, sino en las 20 provincias donde están organizadas. Además expusieron y pidieron apoyo para el proyecto de ley de Acceso a la Tierra que la UTT impulsa desde 2016. “Esto es indispensable para nosotras las mujeres, que somos las que menos acceso tenemos a la titularidad de la tierra”, remarca.




Mirtha Belizan también llegó desde Santiago del Estero e integra el MNCI. Vive a 50 kilómetros de Quimilí y se dedica a la producción de huevos. Considera que los encuentros las fortalecen para seguir más unidas. “Queremos nuestra tierra para tener nuestros animales y nuestros alimentos. Es la primera vez que venimos y al escuchar tantas tantas voces distintas, aprendemos y somos escuchadas”, expresa.




El deseo de ser escuchadas es también un mensaje para los gobiernos que hacen oídos sordos a la realidad de las familias campesinas y en particular de las mujeres y disidencias que trabajan la tierra. No solo porque desarticularon las políticas destinadas a la agricultura familiar sino también aquellas iniciativas que apuntaban a prevenir la violencia de género y a colaborar en la autonomía económica de las mujeres y disidencias sexuales.




“

El Gobierno quiere desalojar a los pobres y tirarnos lejos

. No le servimos a él, pero gracias a nosotros hay muchos pueblos que comen verduras, frutas. Así estamos y así estaremos: defendiendo nuestra tierra”, advierte. Agrega que viajó para estar más comunicada con “tantas compañeras luchadoras” y que aprendió también de ellas. Celebra la presencia de jóvenes que continuarán la pelea por el territorio.




Cristina Almirón también viajó desde Santiago del Estero. Este fue su primer encuentro. La motivó a asistir vivir la experiencia y tener nuevos aprendizajes.“Todas pasamos por lo mismo, traemos nuestras quejas y esperamos ser escuchadas”.




Si pudiera pararse frente a la multitud que asistió al Encuentro, en el escenario de cierre, la integrante del MNCI les diría a sus compañeras, las nuevas, las que conoció en estos tres días de vivencias compartidas: “Que tienen que tener firmeza, no tener miedo. Sentirse apoyadas, seguir la lucha y sobre todo no callar más”.




Si algo brinda cada Encuentro es la certeza de estar juntas en una cultura que apuesta cada vez más al individualismo. Es la posibilidad de saber que no se está sola ante la injusticia, que hay otras miles, anónimas, que desde los valles, la llanura o los ríos luchan contra el extractivismo, la precarización de la vida, la violencia que mata.




Lidia Furlani, campesina sanjuanina, es integrante de la UTT. Ve en los Encuentros de Mujeres y Diversidades la raíz de sus comienzos como militante organizada. Si bien participó en el Encuentro de San Juan en 2013, para ella los más significativos fueron los de Chaco (2017) y La Plata (2019). “En 2017 no participaba en ninguna organización y fui a Chaco medio sola, sumándome a un colectivo que iba desde San Juan. En La Plata, la masividad y el active me dio vuelta la cabeza y entendí que tenía que pertenecer a una organización que representara lo que yo hacía”, recuerda. Fue entonces que se sumó a la UTT.







“El encuentro genera una sensibilidad sobre participar de otras formas de organización. Cuando vas individualmente es una cosa. Al menos en mi experiencia, me hizo pensar que tenía que organizarme con otras personas”.







Llegó al Encuentro con la expectativa que genera la articulación con otras organizaciones campesinas. “Ese fue nuestro objetivo y volvimos con mucho entusiasmo por lo aprendido de las organizaciones hermanas. Y, en el caso específico de la soberanía alimentaria, dispuestas a seguir con acciones concretas en pos de esa lucha”, señala.




Se levantan las mochilas del suelo y poco a poco se desarma la ronda. El taller de Soberanía Alimentaria continuará más tarde, tal como lo prevé el cronograma. Mientras tanto, los pequeños encuentros del Encuentro continuarán en las ferias, en las actividades culturales, en el Pañuelazo por el aborto legal, en la Marcha contra los travesticidios, transfemicidios y transhomicidios y en la movilización de cierre. Allí habrá abrazos, charlas, nuevas compañeras y la complicidad de quien se sabe parte de un mismo movimiento. Un movimiento diverso y con tensiones que se encuentra para ponerlas en debate y para seguir proyectando el camino.




La soberanía alimentaria, del campo a la ciudad




Quizás lo más visible del Encuentro Plurinacional sea la marcha. Miles en las calles contra la violencia machista. Pero hay algo subterráneo, la raíz de cada Encuentro, que se forja en los talleres, donde se comparte la palabra de forma horizontal, donde se denuncian las injusticias pero también se piensan alternativas para enfrentarlas. En el Taller de Soberanía Alimentaria se discutió cómo hacer desde el campo y desde la ciudad para defender los derechos a la tierra, al agua, a la alimentación y la dignidad campesina.




Llorens indica que el hecho de que Córdoba haya sido sede del 39° Encuentro les permitió participar de la comisión organizadora (la que se ocupa de la logística en cada Encuentro), en diferentes comisiones y en representación de MNCI-ST y de la articulación de mujeres y diversidades de la CLOC. El MCC fue la única organización campesina que participó de la comisión organizadora. En ese marco, generaron pre-encuentros, por ejemplo en Serrezuela y en Cerro Colorado. “Fue muy potente para nosotras tener el encuentro en casa”, destaca.







Agrega que en el documento de apertura hicieron aportes sobre la sobre la necesidad de 

campesinizar la lucha feminista y sobre la importancia de la soberanía alimentaria para sostener otras soberanías

. “Tuvimos tensiones porque algunas organizaciones todavía no entienden lo que es la soberanía alimentaria. Algunos feminismos todavía son ‘negacionistas urbanocéntricos’ porque creen que la soberanía alimentaria no es algo que les toca, que es una lucha campesina y no del campo y la ciudad”.







Como MNCI-ST participaron por primera vez del Encuentro en Trelew, en 2018. Relata que se sumaron a talleres como el de Ecofeminismo, “pero a veces las discusiones eran muy urbanas”. También participaron en los talleres de Mujeres Rurales, “pero hablaban más de las problemáticas de las cooperativas y no tanto de la agricultura familiar”.




Fue en Jujuy (2024) donde desde el MNCI-ST se propuso hacer un taller específico sobre soberanía alimentaria. Al año siguiente, en Corrientes, funcionó el taller Soberanía Alimentaria y Agroecología. Este año, la soberanía alimentaria se ligó en un mismo eje con la soberanía de la tierra y de los territorios. “Históricamente la defensa de la tierra y de los territorios estaba en el eje de pueblos preexistentes. Y para nosotros era importante que hubiera un eje que integre la lucha de los pueblos preexistentes por la defensa de sus territorios ancestrales, pero que también ponga en discusión sobre la tierra en un sentido más amplio”, señala.







En el contexto de la disputa actual por la extranjerización de la tierra, el eje de la soberanía alimentaria y de los territorios generó debates que articulan los conflictos campesinos e indígenas con la necesidad de pensar un modelo agrario y un modelo de distribución de la tierra. Para Llorens, desde Jujuy (donde no había ningún taller) a Córdoba, hubo un gran avance. “La realidad de quienes producimos alimentos y no commodities estuvo mucho más presente”, asegura.







La soberanía alimentaria es, 

según conceptualizó La Vía Campesina en 1996

, “el derecho de los pueblos a alimentos saludables y culturalmente apropiados, producidos mediante métodos ecológicamente respetuosos y sostenibles, y su derecho a definir sus sistemas alimentarios y agrícolas“. Para eso es necesario el apoyo técnico y económico a las familias campesinas y el cuidado de la tierra y el agua.







Vallejo señala que ​la principal estrategia es generar conciencia sobre el consumo y la calidad de lo que comemos. “Tenemos que mostrarles a las ciudades que la comida y los productos artesanales con valor agregado que producimos las campesinas son totalmente sanos. Debemos hacer visible la diferencia entre nuestros alimentos agroecológicos y los productos ultraprocesados de las grandes corporaciones, que están llenos de conservantes, colorantes y saborizantes artificiales. Lograr que la ciudad apoye y elija al campesinado es clave para esta lucha“.







La falta de acceso a la tierra es uno de los grandes escollos para la soberanía alimentaria. Desde los desalojos con topadoras y quemas de casas en Santiago del Estero y en Misiones, hasta el costo del alquiler en el cordón hortícola de ciudades como La Plata a las dinámicas familiares que afectan particularmente a las mujeres en Cuyo. Así lo explica Furlani: “En San Juan no es tan típico el alquiler, sino que son tierras de familiares o de herencias viejas. Es una particularidad de la región cuyana. Pero las mujeres no somos titulares de esas tierras. En la línea familiar, terminan ocupando la tierra los varones, incluso aunque tampoco sean propietarios”.




La falta de acceso a la tierra hace que no sea posible sostener una familia solo con el trabajo en el campo, por eso las mujeres buscan otros empleos, como el servicio en casas particulares. Tampoco acceden a trabajos en grandes fincas de vid o de oliva porque son tareas culturalmente masculinizadas.




A eso se suma, en San Juan, la política estatal que desvaloriza la producción de alimentos que realizan las familias campesinas y prioriza la megaminería. Esta decisión política afecta el acceso a otro elemento indispensable para la producción y la subsistencia en el campo: el agua. “

Sin la tierra y el agua no hay soberanía alimentaria. Son necesidades estructurales para que podamos seguir sosteniendo la vida

”, señala.




De las conclusiones del taller, destaca la vinculación entre la soberanía alimentaria y el Buen Vivir. Pero marca que para eso es necesario gozar de derechos como la salud, la educación, la seguridad social. Y que el Buen Vivir no es algo individual, sino colectivo. Agrega que en el intercambio se vio con claridad que la soberanía alimentaria no es solo una problemática campesina. Mujeres que habitan las ciudades y que se acercaron al taller se involucraron en la necesidad de pensar estrategias para vincular la producción y el consumo creando nuevas redes de comercialización y consumo con mayor conciencia sobre un modelo alimentario justo, diverso y soberano.




De Córdoba a Capital Federal




La próxima sede del Encuentro será la ciudad de Buenos Aires. Así se resolvió por aclamación en el acto de cierre. “Veníamos desde el año pasado diciendo que teníamos que hacer un encuentro en CABA, disputarle a este gobierno hambreador y extranjerizador. Es estratégico porque va a generar una masividad de participación y es fundamental porque tenemos que ser muchas en las calles”, dice Llorens.




Vallejo se esperanza: “Espero que sea la oportunidad para que la gran ciudad finalmente mire al campo, entienda de dónde viene lo que consume y se solidarice con la lucha campesina por la tierra y la producción sana”.







La elección de la ciudad de Buenos Aires implica llevar el Encuentro más importante de las mujeres y diversidades sexuales al centro político del país en un año electoral, contra un Gobierno que es abiertamente antigénero. Furlani marca la necesidad de profundizar las demandas. “Algunos reaccionarios han dicho que las feministas nos pasamos tres pueblos. Creo que tenemos que redoblar la apuesta y pasarnos diez. 

Tenemos que imaginar cuestiones más grandes: una revolución

, básicamente”, manifiesta.







Y señala: “Son horizontes que tenemos porque nos dimos cuenta de que nuestras democracias tienen que pensar qué pasa cuando los fascismos toman el poder. Esa es una construcción que merece mucho más tiempo y dedicación por parte de las organizaciones. Si bien puede haber un objetivo para el 2027, hay que redoblar cualquier apuesta que nos hayamos planteado”.




Cuando se le pregunta cómo sueña esa revolución, responde: “Tiene que ver con lo que las organizaciones ya vienen haciendo, cada organización a su modo, pero lo quisiéramos para todo el mundo. Queremos poder vivir en el campo, disponer de agua para nuestros animales, cuidar los lugares donde vivimos y que se den las condiciones mínimas para hacerlo. Volvemos a lo del Buen Vivir: deseamos que cada compañera pueda realizar su Buen Vivir del modo en que lo desee. Y con eso seríamos muy felices”.







La entrada 

"Creemos en la potencia política de los feminismos para sembrar semillas de esperanza"

 se publicó primero en 

Agencia de Noticias Tierra Viva

.

author: Pauline Ertel
title: Brazil Abolishes Six-Day Workweek Ahead of Presidential Run-Off
content:
Brazil’s senate has approved a constitutional amendment ending the country’s six-day workweek, delivering a key pledge by president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva just days before an election run-off. 




The reform, passed on Wednesday, shortens the working week from 44 hours to a maximum of 40 hours and is set to 

improve working conditions

 for more than 37 million people. That includes 16 million who work six-day weeks and are now guaranteed two days of rest each week without a reduction to their wages.




The amendment primarily affects workers in low paid industries such as retail and hospitality, one of the groups from which Lula has 

lost suppor

t since defeating far-right incumbent Jair Bolsonaro in the 2022 election. Bolsonaro is serving a 27-year prison sentence for plotting a failed coup in the wake of his defeat. 




Informal and gig economy workers, including app-based drivers without employment contracts, will not be covered by the new law.




Lula, who will face far-right Flávio Bolsonaro, the jailed former president’s son, for a second round on 25 October, 

called the reform

 a “victory for the working class”. 




He 

said on X

 the vote was “a historic achievement for millions of workers, who will now have more time to rest, be with their family, take care of themselves and live,” 




The victory may give Lula a much-needed boost; the leftwing incumbent came second behind Bolsonaro in the first round of voting on 4 October and is still trailing him in the polls, albeit by a 

small margin

.




Brazilian trade unions and labour federations 

welcomed the amendment, 

which they said followed months of widespread

 strikes and protests by workers

. Advocates have been calling for the policy for years, but it gained

 more traction in 2023 thanks to a viral TikTok video by

 pharmacy clerk-turned-influencer Rick Azevedo.  




Bolsonaro long opposed the proposal, calling it an “opportunistic” attempt by Lula to appeal to working-class voters. But he reversed course shortly before the 4 October vote, 

telling journalists

 that “most Brazilian workers ‌want to ⁠see the end of the six-day workweek.” 




Seventy-five senators, including Bolsonaro allies, voted in favour of the amendment. The only one to vote against it was former vice-president Hamilton Mourão, who worked under Jair Bolsonaro.

author: Gustavo Faleiros
title: Povos da floresta e do mar contra a extrema direita
content:
Quer receber os textos desta coluna em primeira mão no seu e-mail? Assine a newsletter Ligando os pontos, enviada toda quinta-feira. Para receber as próximas edições, 

inscreva-se aqui

.







Em 1987, quando o Brasil acabava de sair das sinistras décadas de ditadura militar, surgiu uma união de forças sociais que até então pareciam distantes. Comunidades extrativistas e indígenas da Amazônia, vítimas históricas dos grileiros, 

criaram a Aliança dos Povos da Floresta

. O momento não poderia ter sido mais propício pois, deste grupo, que contava com lideranças como Chico Mendes e Ailton Krenak, saíram propostas que influenciaram a nova Constituição, promulgada em 1988.




O impacto político daquele encontro não pode ser esquecido neste momento em que a extrema direita, representada pela candidatura de 

Flávio Bolsonaro (PL)

, busca privatizar o patrimônio natural brasileiro. Se na década de 1980 a suposta direita conciliatória cedia terras públicas a empreendimentos agropecuários, hoje a direita quer privatizar as praias e abrir as terras indígenas para a mineração. 




A partir da união de seringueiros e indígenas, a luta dos povos da Amazônia foi projetada para o mundo, levando preocupação aos chefes dos bancos de desenvolvimento internacionais. O Banco Mundial e o Banco Interamericano de Desenvolvimento (BID) estavam liberando empréstimos para a criação de pólos de produção pecuária e financiando a abertura de estradas que cortavam os territórios tradicionais. Chico Mendes, em uma viagem emblemática a Washington, em 1987, conseguiu congelar alguns destes financiamentos e, como sabemos, pagou com a vida por sua coragem.




Mas sua luta sobreviveu: da profusão de ideias e da resistência criada surgiram outras lideranças, entre elas Marina Silva, a mais jovem senadora a ser eleita pelo Acre, na década de 1990, e depois a ministra de Meio Ambiente nas gestões de Lula. Ela levou a política ambiental para o coração do governo e conseguiu, com o apoio dos melhores cientistas e gestores, provar que é possível conter o desmatamento.




No momento em que escrevo estas linhas, saem notícias mostrando que, em 

2025, as taxas de derrubadas

 no Brasil atingiram nova baixa histórica. E o melhor, estes resultados já não estão se restringindo à Amazônia. Os dados do Deter, o sistema de alertas de desmatamento do INPE, mostraram 

uma redução de 30% em setembro

 no Cerrado. Uma notícia fantástica, uma vez que este é o bioma sob maior pressão, onde a ilegalidade e invasão de terras prosperaram nos últimos anos. 




Um dos alicerces da política de Lula e Marina para barrar a sanha destruidora é exatamente o combate à grilagem de terras e a promoção da regularização fundiária. 

Estudos de renomadas organizações não governamentais

 como o Instituto de Pesquisas da Amazônia (IPAM) têm mostrado que, nos últimos anos, com os embargos e a repressão ao desmatamento em propriedades privadas, os criminosos passaram a fazer mais queimadas e derrubadas em unidades de conservação e terras indígenas.




A grilagem de terras e a invasão de territórios indígenas definem muito o que é o Brasil. Nossa história colonial foi brutal contra os povos da floresta e seus efeitos sobre o nosso cotidiano perduram até hoje, como a persistência da violência no campo e as ameaças constantes sofridas por comunidades rurais. 

Nesta polarização tremenda que vive o país, temos falado muito do interior e como a cultura do agro tem ajudado a definir os votos. Mas somos um país atlântico, com identidade litorânea e com uma conexão muito forte com as praias. Por isso, enquanto alertamos para o que está ocorrendo na floresta, não podemos deixar de apontar a especulação imobiliária que pode vir a transformar a costa brasileira.




A Proposta de Emenda Constitucional para regularizar a venda dos terrenos da Marinha 

gerou enorme polêmica em 2024

. E agora, nesta eleição, voltou ao debate, pois ninguém menos do que Flávio Bolsonaro é o relator da proposta, que ficou conhecida como a PEC da Privatização das Praias. A ideia é permitir a venda de terras que ficam numa faixa que começa a 33 metros dos pontos mais altos de maré e que pertencem historicamente à União. O argumento dos defensores da proposta é de que isso levaria mais investimentos, em forma de condomínios e resorts, ao nosso litoral. Na prática, isso pode se tornar uma forma de fechar acessos e criar praias exclusivas para os donos do dinheiro.




Diante desta ameaça, fiquei imaginando se não seria o momento da Aliança dos Povos da Floresta voltar ao cenário nacional incorporando também os povos do mar. 

Assim como os extrativistas se tornaram guardiões de algumas das mais importantes reservas florestais do país, os pescadores artesanais, as marisqueiras e os catadores de caranguejo são os guardiões da nossa costa. 




O tema da proteção aos oceanos é especialmente importante. No ano que vem, o Brasil vai ser sede do 

encontro das Nações Unidas para a Década do Oceano

, que ocorrerá em abril no Rio de Janeiro. E não é difícil imaginar que, como seu pai, Flávio Bolsonaro – se eleito – vai banir as conferências da ONU sobre meio ambiente que estão marcadas para acontecerem no Brasil. Em 2019, um dos primeiros desmandos de Bolsonaro foi cancelar a realização da Cúpula de Mudanças Climáticas em solo brasileiro. Apenas em 2025 a conferência voltou ao Brasil, na icônica 

COP30 em Belém.

 




Agora me parece que seria o momento de ampliar essa aliança: floresta e oceano unidos contra a política da morte. E a aliança pelo mar não será apenas importante para um governo de extrema direita. Os impactos da exploração de petróleo, a concessão de novos blocos em alto-mar e as mudanças climáticas farão da nossa costa um ponto central para qualquer o futuro do país.

author: Gastbeitrag
title: Das Schweigen brechen – Wie eine Konferenz sexistischer Polizeigewalt den Kampf ansagt
content:
Am 18.10. findet in Berlin Kreuzberg eine Konferenz gegen sexualisierte Polizeigewalt statt. Die Organisator:innen sind vor allem politisch aktive Frauen aus unterschiedlichen Organisationen, wie ZORA oder der Prisoners Voice Platform (TSP). Wir haben mit ihnen über ihre konkreten Erfahrungen, das Programm der Konferenz und über die größeren Ziele gesprochen.




Interview: Osa Udushesheri







Könnt ihr euch einmal vorstellen und sagen, was euch dazu gebracht hat, die Konferenz gegen sexualisierte Polizeigewalt zu organisieren?




Erstmal lieben Dank für das Interview! Wir sind vor allem politisch aktive Frauen aus unterschiedlichen Organisationen wie ZORA und Prisoners Voice Platform (TSP – Tutsakların Sesi Platformu), aber wir werden in der Vorbereitung von vielen unterschiedlichen Genoss:innen und Organisationen begleitet, die schon in der Vergangenheit solche Konferenz z.B. in der Türkei gegen Vergewaltigung in Haft organisiert haben und im Kampf dagegen erfolgreich waren. Die Konferenz ist also ein Ergebnis vieler Genoss:innen, ein Ergebnis der Erfahrungen, die Frauen schon vor uns gesammelt haben.

Das hat uns aber vor allem dazu gebracht diese Konferenz zu planen: Auf Palästinademonstrationen in Berlin sehen wir auf fast jeder Aktion wie Frauen an die Brüste gefasst wird, wie Frauen der Hijab abgerissen wird, wie vor allem Polizisten ihre Macht gegenüber Frauen ausnutzen. Denken wir auch an die Aktionen des Rheinmetall-Entwaffnen-Camps. Auf der Großdemo 2025 wurden Aktivist:innen 12 Stunden im Kessel gehalten und die Polizei ging äußerst brutal gegen Frauen vor. Auch dieses Jahr bei den Blockadeaktionen des RME-Camps berichteten uns viele von Griffen in die Hose oder an die Brust, von sexistischen und abwertigen Kommentare und anderen Formen sexualisierter Polizeigewalt. Was besonders auffiel sind die Nacktdurchsuchungen die grundlos von Polizisten durchgeführt werden hier in Deutschland, es scheint fast so als solle das zur Normalität werden, in Fällen von Blockadeaktionen oder ähnlichem.




Vor allem nach den Veröffentlichungen im Dezember 2025 von Anna Liedtke zu der Vergewaltigung in israelischer Haft, kam es zu vielen weiteren Berichten der Flotilla-Aktivist:innen, die von sexualisierter Gewalt und Folter seitens der IDF berichtet haben. Auch während der People’s Caravan, die Anfang des Jahres nach Kobane reisen wollte, um von den Geschehnissen zu berichten folgten Veröffentlichungen zu körperlicher und sexualisierter Folter. Die Aktivistin der Föderation Klassenkämpferischer Organisationen Paula Maier machte im August dieses Jahres eine Veröffentlichung, bei der sie bekannt machte, dass sie bei der Jugenddelegation nach Bakur mit vielen anderen Aktivist:innen festgenommen wurde und dann in einer Einzelzelle von einem türkischen Beamten vergewaltigt wurde.

Das sind alles Fälle, die sich in den letzten Jahren gehäuft haben und zum Thema gemacht werden sollten. Wir sehen also wie unsere eigenen Körper als Waffe gegen uns selbst genutzt werden. Uns ist natürlich bewusst, dass überall da wo Frauen Widerstand leisten der Staat mit Repression antwortet. Obwohl das Thema jetzt aktuell ist, haben wir es als Frauenbewegung und linke Bewegung nicht geschafft, dass es Teil unserer Antirepressionsarbeit wird oder auch ein bewusster Kampf dagegen stattfindet.

Die Konferenz dient also als ein Ort, an dem wir als Bewegung zusammenkommen, uns austauschen über internationale Erfahrungen von Genoss:innen, über die Probleme, die wir aktuell haben und vor allem wie wir dagegen kämpfen können. Es soll für alle Menschen sein, die politisch interessiert sind, schon aktiv sind, Betroffene oder einfach jene, die was lernen möchten.




Was ist sexualisierte Polizeigewalt? Inwiefern spiegelt sexualisierte Gewalt die Strukturen der Polizei wider? Gibt es Unterschiede zu anderen Formen der Repression und der Polizeigewalt?




Die letzten Jahre haben uns deutlich gezeigt, dass die Polizeigewalt im Allgemeinen gegen alle, die gegen Krieg, Genozid, Ausbeutung und gegen dieses System kämpfen, sehr stark zugenommen hat. Der Staat hat vor allem auf eine starke Palästinabewegung mit brutaler Polizeigewalt und staatlicher Verfolgung geantwortet. Diese Repressionen, die wir in allen Bewegungen und Kämpfen erleben haben das Ziel durch Angst und Gewalt Einzelpersonen, aber auch ganze Kollektive von ihrem politischen Gedanken und Aktivismus abzubringen. Sexualisierte Polizeigewalt wurde bisher in Deutschland häufig auf eine Kontinuität der steigenden Polizeigewalt reduziert.  

Wir verstehen die Polizei als ein staatliches Organ, welches die Interessen der Herrschenden praktisch umsetzen soll: Bekämpfung von Widerstand, Kriminalisierung und Disziplinierung von Armen, Frauen, Migrant:innen, LGBTI+ und der Arbeiter:innen. Dabei scheut sich die Polizei nicht von hinterhältigen und menschenverachtenden Methoden: Schikane, Prügel, psychischer Druck, nicht selten werden persönliche Probleme gegen einen genutzt.

Die Polizei bedient sich dabei der gesellschaftlichen Scham, die uns Frauen auferlegt wird, damit wir uns gedemütigt fühlen. Sie setzen also praktisch die patriarchale und kapitalistische Unterdrückung direkt an.




Sexualisierte Polizeigewalt betrifft aber nicht nur Frauen. Auch erleben insbesondere migrantische Männer in Deutschland Nacktdurchsuchungen oder ihnen wird in die Hose gegriffen. Da spielt rassistische Polizeigewalt stark mit. Oder auch die unzähligen Berichte aus zionistischen Gefängnissen, die deutlich machen, dass brutale sexistische Polizeigewalt vor allem gegen palästinensische Männer genutzt wird. Hier dient sexuelle Gewalt zur Demütigung und Entmenschlichung nochmal besonders stark.

Sexualisierte staatliche Gewalt ist ein besonderer Angriff gegen die körperliche Unversehrtheit und Selbstbestimmung. Wenn ein Polizist von mir verlangt mich nackt auszuziehen, wenn ein Polizist mir Klamotten vom Körper reißt, wenn ich in Gewahrsam in Unterwäsche in einer Zelle stundenlang allein gelassen werde oder wenn mir internationalistischen Delegation von Beamten mit Tod oder Vergewaltigung gedroht wird. Das sind alles Realitäten und Erfahrungen, die wir als Frauen gemacht haben.




Gebt uns doch mal einen Einblick in die Konferenz? Wie wird sie ablaufen und was wird diskutiert werden?




Ziel ist es mit der Konferenz internationale Erfahrungen auszuwerten, Inspiration aus den geführten Kämpfen zu schaffen, aber auch eine Analyse der Entwicklungen in Deutschland zu diskutieren und mit welchen Methoden wir unseren Kampf dagegen organisieren möchten.

Die Konferenz ist gegliedert in zwei Teile: Das erste Panel wird internationale Erfahrungen von sexualisierter Gewalt durch den Staat diskutieren und hierbei auch insbesondere beleuchten, welche Formen des Widerstands dagegen entwickelt wurden. Auf diesem Panel spricht Sosyalist Kadin, Prisoners Dialogue über die Situation im Iran und eine Sprecherin zur Situation in Palästina. Darüber hinaus wird Nekane Txapartegi sprechen, eine baskische Aktivistin, die ihre Vergewaltigung in Haft öffentlich gemacht hat und von dort einen politischen Kampf dagegen geführt hat, sowie Rednerinnen zur Perspektive in den Philippinen.

Auf dem zweiten Panel möchten wir konkret die aktuellen Entwicklungen in Deutschland gemeinsam diskutieren und politisch einordnen: Anna Liedtke wird für die Frauenorganisation ZORA sprechen – im Dezember vergangenen Jahres hatte sie eine Veröffentlichung zur Vergewaltigung im israelischen Gefängnis gemacht, ein Betroffenenkreis aus Nürnberg wird über ihre Erfahrungen mit Würgegriffen durch die Polizei reden, sowie Paula Maier von FKO, eine Internationalistin, die Anfang des Jahres Vergewaltigung in Haft durch türkische Beamten erlebt hat, nachdem sie sich an einer Delegationsreise nach Bakur beteiligt hat. Darüber hinaus wird Ezwa sprechen, eine Solidaritätsstruktur, die Repressionsfälle der Palästina-Bewegung in Deutschland betreut und sich unter anderem mit Anwältinnen organisiert, um dagegen vorzugehen.

Hierbei wird es auch viel Raum für Diskussion geben, bei der Betroffene von Sexualstrafen die Möglichkeit haben ihre eigenen Erfahrungen zu teilen und eine politische Schlagkraft daraus zu entwickeln.




Was wollt ihr mit der Konferenz erreichen? Was wird uns danach erwarten und was braucht es noch, um sexualisierte Polizeigewalt zu bekämpfen?




Über das letzte Jahr hinweg sind unterschiedliche Organisationen erste Schritte gegangen, die Auswertungen und Erkenntnisse daraus wollen wir kollektivieren und die Bündnisse im Kampf stärken. Wir wollen Antworten auf die Fragen finden, wie ein organisierter Kampf geschaffen werden kann, welcher konkret sexualisierte Polizeigewalt zurückdrängt.

Würgegriffe und Nacktdurchsuchungen dürfen sich nicht ungehindert in alle unsere Proteste, unseren Widerstand und unseren Alltag einschleichen. Der direkte ideologische Angriff auf Frauen muss als dieser begriffen und ein gezielter Kampf als Organisationen und Bewegung gegen Methoden der Polizei geführt werden.  Das spontane Bewusstsein muss in ein organisiertes Bewusstsein und einen gemeinsamen Kampf umgewandelt werden, bei den betroffenen Frauen sowie der gesamten Bewegung. Wir halten es für notwendig eine Initiative zu gründen, die sich der Aufgabe stellt breit dagegen anzukämpfen. Wir wollen sowohl auf der Straße dagegen kämpfen, aber auch juristisch dagegen vorgehen. Kein Fall sexualisierter Polizeigewalt soll unbeantwortet bleiben!




Danke für das Gespräch!

title: İklim krizi ve kötü hava: Risk kuryede, kâr platform şirketlerinde
content:
14 Ekim’de ben de sahadaydım. Eminönü, Balat, Alibeyköy ve Maslak hattında teslim etmem gereken siparişler vardı. Hava bir bastırıyor, bir normale dönüyordu; ara ara sağanak geliyor, sonra kesiliyordu. Sağanağın en sert anına Sirkeci’de yakalandım. Ana arterler kullanılamaz haldeydi, her yer göle dönmüştü. Motosikletle yol almaktan çok suda yüzüyor gibiydik.




Haberleri takip etmek için bile sığındığımız benzinlikler motosikletçilerle doluydu. Duraklara sığınan insanlar bankların üstüne çıkmıştı. Bot da olsa yağmurluk da olsa, üzerimizdeki ekipmanın hiçbiri o yağmura dayanmadı. Bazı bölgeler tamamen kilitlenmişti. Motosikletin her zaman bulduğu dar aralar bile kapanmıştı ve suyun içinde kaldığımız çok an oldu. Böylesini ilk kez gördüm.




14 Ekim bize bir kez daha şunu gösterdi. Kötü havada kurye ya çalışıp canını riske atıyor ya da çalışamayıp gelirini kaybediyor. Her iki durumda da faturayı kurye ödüyor.



















Kuryelerin karlı havada çalışma koşulları: Tehlikeler, baskılar ve haklar




24 Şubat 2025










Sağanağı sele çeviren kent




Vali Davut Gül’ün açıklamasına göre İstanbul’da metrekareye 261 kilogram yağış düştü. Bu, Meteoroloji’nin ölçüme başladığı 1942'den bu yana kentte görülen en yüksek değer. Önceki rekor 200 kilograma yakındı. Valilik bugün 3 kişinin hayatını kaybettiğini, 2 bin 722 kişinin kurtarıldığını açıkladı.




Aşırı sıcaklar, ani sağanaklar ve fırtınalar artık istisna değil. İklim krizi bu olayları sıklaştırıyor. Ama aşırı yağışın sele, selin de afete dönüşmesi kaçınılmaz bir doğa olayı değil. Bunu büyük ölçüde kentin nasıl kurulduğu belirliyor. Betonlaşan kentte yağmur suyu toprağa sızamıyor. Dere yataklarına yerleşim alanları kuruluyor. Altyapı, büyüyen kentin gerisinde kalıyor. Ana arterlerde aşırı yağışa karşı alternatif tahliye sistemleri bulunmuyor. Sonuçta yollar dakikalar içinde göle dönüyor.




Bu tablo tek bir kurumun ya da tek bir dönemin eseri değil. İmar kararlarını veren merkezi yönetim de altyapıdan sorumlu yerel yönetimler de bu sonuçta pay sahibi. İklim krizi bir etken ama altyapı yeterli olsa, kent bu kadar betonlaşmasa ve dere yatakları yapılaşmaya açılmasa aynı yağış bu kadar büyük bir yıkıma yol açmazdı.




Kurye için trafik iş yeridir




Bu tablonun en ağır yükünü açık havada çalışanlar taşıyor. Kuryeler, inşaat, temizlik, tarım ve belediye işçileri… Çoğumuz için trafik, bir yerden bir yere gitmek için kullandığımız bir ulaşım alanı. Kurye için ise trafik iş yerinin ta kendisi. Ofiste çalışan biri için kötü hava, işe gidip gelirken katlanılan bir zorluk, kurye içinse ise iş yerinin baştan sona tehlikeli hale gelmesi demek. Görüş mesafesinin düşmesi, kaygan ve su basmış zemin, artan kaza riski, kuryenin iş yerindeki çalışma koşullarıdır.




Bu yüzden kötü havayı bir hava durumu haberi olarak değil bir iş sağlığı ve güvenliği meselesi olarak konuşmamız gerekiyor. Göle dönen bir cadde, kurye için su basmış bir iş yeridir. Yazın aşırı sıcak, kışın buzlanma da aynı meselenin parçası.




Uyarı vardı, tedbir gün içinde geldi




Kuryeler 14 Ekim’de gün boyu sağanak ve fırtına altında sipariş taşıdı. 

Kurye Haber

’e gün boyunca çok sayıda kaza ihbarı ulaştı. Beşiktaş’ta bir kuryenin motosikleti suya gömüldü. Bir başka görüntüde bir kurye, sele kapılmamak için devrilen motosikletine tutunuyordu. Kocaeli, Sakarya ve Antalya’daki kuryeler de benzer koşullarda çalıştıklarını gösteren video ve tanıklıklarını doğrudan Kurye Haber’e iletti.




Vali Gül ertesi gün, vatandaşların meteorolojik uyarıları dikkate almasının can kaybını ve zararları azalttığını söyledi. Bu açıklama, uyarıların önceden yapıldığını resmi ağızdan teyit ediyor. Meteorolojik veriler tedbirin çok önceden alınmasını gerektirse de motosiklet yasağı ancak gün içinde, hava çoktan kötüleşmişken, saat 18.30 sularında açıklandı. Yasak ise 21.00'de başladı. Kuryeler yasağın açıklandığı andan uygulanmaya başladığı saate kadar bile şiddetli yağış altında çalışmak zorunda kaldı. Önleyici tedbir, zorluklar yaşandıktan sonra değil, yaşanmadan önce alınmalı.




Ama sorumluluk yalnızca valilikte değil. Platform şirketleri, uyarıları herkes kadar bilmesine rağmen sistemlerini kapatmak için valilik kararını bekledi ve yasak gelene kadar sipariş almaya devam etti. Kuryelerin can güvenliği kuryeleri çalıştıran şirketlerin değil, valiliğin kararına bırakıldı.




Yasak geldiğinde de herkes uymadı. Kurye Haber’e özellikle mahalle aralarındaki işletmelerle ilgili şikâyetler ulaştı. Kısa mesafelerde denetim olmayacağını düşünen bazı yerel işletme sahipleri, kendilerine bağlı çalışan kuryeleri yasak saatlerinde sipariş dağıtmaya zorladı.




Üretim aracı kuryenin, sorumluluk da kuryenin




Resmi açıklamalarda kurtarılan insan, kapanan yol ve iptal edilen sefer sayıları var. Ama yasaktan önce çalışılan saatlerin bedeli bu rakamlarda yok. Sel sularında kalan pek çok motosiklette, başta elektrik aksamı olmak üzere ciddi hasar oluştu.




Motosiklet kurye için bir ulaşım aracı değil, üretim aracıdır. Platform şirketlerinin kazandığı her lira, bu motosikletlerin üzerinde üretiliyor. Ama esnaf kurye modelinde bu üretim aracının bütün yükü kuryeye ait. Motosikleti kurye alıyor, bakımını kurye yaptırıyor, arızasını kurye ödüyor. Tamir masrafı, değişen parçalar, ıslanıp kullanılamaz hale gelen ekipman ve motosiklet tamirdeyken çalışılamayan günler hep kuryeye kalıyor. Platform şirketleri ise bu konuda hiçbir sorumluluk almıyor. Keza 14 Ekim’in hasarı için de herhangi bir destek açıklamadılar.




Yasak günü, gelirsiz gün




Yasak başladığı anda kuryeler fiilen ücretsiz izne çıkarılmış oldu. Sabit maaşı olmayan, paket başı ücret alan bir kurye için tek bir gün çalışamamak bile ciddi bir kayıp. Kuryeler bütün giderlerini kendileri karşıladığı için güne zaten en az 1.500-2 bin lira ekside başlıyor. Önce gider için çalışıyor, ancak ondan sonra artıya geçebiliyor. Bu hesapla çalışılamayan bir gün, bir kurye için en az 3-4 bin lira kayıp demek.




Bu kayıp, zaten gerileyen bir gelirin üzerine biniyor. Giderler sürekli artarken paket ücretleri artmıyor, hatta düşüyor. Kira, kredi ve motosiklet taksidi ise yasak tanımıyor.




Çalışmaktan kaçınma hakkı kuryeyi neden korumuyor?




6331 sayılı İş Sağlığı ve Güvenliği Kanunu’nun 13. maddesi, ciddi ve yakın tehlike karşısında çalışana çalışmaktan kaçınma hakkı tanıyor. Bu süre boyunca ücretin ve diğer hakların saklı kaldığını da açıkça belirtiyor. Göle dönen yollar ve sıfıra inen görüş mesafesi, tam da bu hakkın tarif ettiği tehlike.




Motosiklet yasağı aslında bu hakkın idari karşılığı. Devlet tehlikeyi kabul ediyor ve trafiğe çıkışı yasaklıyor. Ama ortada ücretin saklı kalmasını sağlayacak bir mekanizma yok, çünkü platformlar kuryeyi “kendi nam ve hesabına çalışan esnaf” olarak tanımlıyor.




Oysa esnaf kuryeler kâğıt üstünde esnaf, fiiliyatta işçi. Platformun talimatıyla çalışıyorlar. Ücretlerini platform tek taraflı belirliyor. Paket zorunlulukları ve uyum kurallarıyla denetleniyorlar. Bu, bir işçi-işveren ilişkisidir. Yasa işçiyi korumak için yazılmışken, esnaf kurye modeli bu korumayı boşa çıkarıyor.




Kâr şirkette, risk kuryede




Kuryelerin talebi net. Olağanüstü hava koşullarında ücretli izin ya da gelir desteği. Bu talep pazarlık konusu yapılmamalı.




Şirketlerin “kaynak nereden bulunacak” sorusunun cevabı da ortada. Platform şirketleri kuryeler üzerinden milyarlarca lira kazanıyor. Paket ücretlerine yılda bir kez zam yapılıyor, ücret ve çalışma koşullarına dair kararlar tek taraflı alınıyor. Üstelik kuryeler logolu mont, yelek, çanta ve motosiklet sepetlerini kendi paralarıyla alıyor. Bu ekipman şehrin her sokağında dolaşan bir reklam panosu işlevi görüyor, ama kuryeye karşılığı ödenmiyor.




Motosiklet yasakları yılda sınırlı sayıda gün uygulanıyor. Şirketler bu günler için kaynak bulamadığını söylüyorsa, yapacakları ödemeyi kuryelerin yıl boyu yaptığı ücretsiz reklamın karşılığı olarak görsünler.




Kuryeler seçim yapmaya zorlanmamalı




Kasım’da iklim krizi Antalya’da konuşulacak. Hükümetler COP31'de, iklim hareketleri ise 14-18 Kasım’da Halkların İklim Zirvesi’nde buluşacak. ILO’ya göre dünyadaki işçilerin yüzde 70'inden fazlası iklim kaynaklı tehlikelere maruz kalıyor. Bu masalarda sokakta çalışanların iş güvenliği de konuşulmalı. Elimizde bunun için bir araç da var.




Uluslararası Çalışma Örgütü’nün (ILO) Haziran’da kabul ettiği 193 sayılı sözleşme, platform çalışanlarını statüleri ne olursa olsun koruma altına alıyor ve iş güvenliği güvencesi getiriyor. Türkiye bu sözleşmeyi gecikmeden onaylamalı.




Merkezi ve yerel yönetimler kentleri aşırı yağışa dayanıklı hale getirmeli, çünkü bu aynı zamanda sokakta çalışanların iş güvenliği meselesi. Valilikler meteorolojik uyarılar geldiğinde önleyici kararları zamanında, gerektiğinde bölgesel olarak almalı ve yasakların uygulanmasını mahalle aralarında da denetlemeli. Platform şirketleri kötü hava protokollerini şeffaf biçimde açıklamalı, valilik kararını beklemeden sistemlerini kapatabilmeli ve yasak günlerinde kuryelere ücret ödemeli. Kuryeler canları ile cebindeki para arasında seçim yapmaya zorlanmamalı!




(MS/HA)

title: Talabani receives Bakırhan, reaffirms PUK’s support for the peace process in Turkey
content:
Bafel Jalal Talabani, President of the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK), received Tuncer Bakırhan, Co-Chair of the DEM Party, in Dabashan.







The meeting on Wednesday was attended by Shanaz Ibrahim Ahmed and Dr Yousif Goran, members of the PUK Political Bureau, and Salar Lala Sarhad, Head of the Kurdistani Relations Board. Discussions focused on continuing joint coordination and cooperation and strengthening bilateral relations in pursuit of shared interests and greater regional stability.







The two sides also exchanged views on the peace process in Turkey. Bafel Talabani reaffirmed the PUK’s support for this historic initiative, stating: “We will continue to follow the same policy pursued by President Mam Jalal until this vital and decisive process succeeds. We believe that peace and coexistence enable us to serve our people, whereas war and division bring nothing but destruction. I therefore hope that everyone will turn a new page and work towards lasting peace.”







For his part, Bakırhan thanked Talabani and the PUK for their efforts to advance the peace process, saying: “We highly value your role and appreciate your steps in support of stability and peaceful coexistence in the region.”







Photos: PUKMEDIA

title: Savary-Borioli: If Turkey wants peace, it must release Öcalan
content:
Swiss politician and emergency physician Dr. Beppe Savary-Borioli believes that a lasting resolution to the Kurdish question is hardly conceivable without Abdullah Öcalan’s freedom and the fundamental democratization of Turkey. Speaking to ANF, the member of the Ticino cantonal parliament expressed serious doubts about the Turkish government’s willingness to secure the current peace process through binding political and legal guarantees. At the same time, he sees Öcalan’s concept of democratic confederalism as offering a perspective that extends beyond the Kurdish question.




Since Öcalan’s February 27, 2025, Call for Peace and Democratic Society, the Kurdish freedom movement has taken far-reaching steps toward ending the armed struggle against Turkey. According to Savary-Borioli, however, the future of this process depends crucially on whether Ankara is prepared to establish the political conditions necessary for a negotiated settlement on equal terms.










https://1649452211.rsc.cdn77.org/20261013215028_2026-10-14-habermerkezi-dr-beppe-savary-isvicreli-siyasetci-baris-icin-ocalan-ozgur-olmali-1.mp4













“If Turkey truly wants peace, it must release Öcalan”




Savary-Borioli described Öcalan’s continued imprisonment as a fundamental contradiction within the peace process. He stated that a government genuinely seeking a political settlement must allow the Kurdish side’s most important negotiating partner to fulfill his role freely.




“The crucial question for me is this: If Turkey truly wants peace, it must release Öcalan. As long as it fails to do so, everything else lacks credibility,” Savary-Borioli stated.




The politician criticized the authoritarian system of government under President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, comparing his approach to power to that of a sultan. By contrast, he described Öcalan as one of the most important figures capable of making a shared, peaceful future possible for the Kurdish and Turkish populations. Savary-Borioli also referred to the experience of South Africa’s peace process, noting that negotiations to end apartheid gained decisive momentum only after Nelson Mandela’s release. He sees a similar prerequisite for Turkey.




“We cannot speak of negotiations on equal terms when one side is represented by a prisoner and the other by a president who behaves like a sultan. That is simply impossible.”




Doubts about the Turkish government’s guarantees




Savary-Borioli considers the Kurdish freedom movement’s strategic decision to end the armed struggle in favor of political and diplomatic means an important step. However, he believes, a unilateral change in strategy cannot guarantee lasting peace. In particular, he doubts that the Turkish government will actually fulfill its obligations toward former PKK members. A state that disregards international legal norms must first demonstrate that its commitments are credible and reliable, he underlines.




In this context, Savary-Borioli recalled the symbolic burning of weapons by the Kurdish freedom movement in July 2025, which he had personally attended. He said the action had demonstrated the movement’s political will but had not prompted any immediate corresponding steps from the state.




“I remain skeptical. Will a state like Turkey, which does not respect international law, actually honor the guarantees it gives to PKK members after they lay down their weapons?” Savary-Borioli asked. He therefore continues to observe current developments with considerable caution. What matters, he stressed, is not political announcements but verifiable changes to the legal and democratic framework.




Democratization as the foundation for coexistence




Savary-Borioli sees the democratization of the Turkish state as another prerequisite for a lasting political settlement. He argued that the political system is heavily centered on the presidency, while parliament has only limited influence over fundamental decisions.




“Under these conditions, any peace agreement would remain politically uncertain, as its implementation would depend on the position of the country’s leadership at any given time. As long as Turkey does not become a genuinely democratic state, it is extremely difficult to imagine real peace between the Kurdish and Turkish peoples,” Savary-Borioli stated.




He explicitly distinguished between the Turkish population and the government or military. He remarked that the people of both societies could and should live together peacefully. However, this would require a democratic system that guarantees their rights and political equality, he added.




International responsibility for the Kurdish question




Savary-Borioli believes that responsibility for finding a solution does not rest with Turkey alone. He noted that the Kurdish question has been shaped by the historical partition of Kurdistan and the interests of international powers.




“Britain and France, in particular, pursued their territorial and economic interests during the political reorganization of the Middle East after the First World War. In the process, the Kurdish population and its political rights were disregarded. Even back then, the international community was not interested in the Kurdish question. On the contrary, it was interested in dividing Kurdistan. Western states were well aware of the region’s strategic and economic significance, including its natural resources,” Savary-Borioli said. He argued that this places a responsibility on them today to help overcome the historical consequences of those policies.




Democratic confederalism as an alternative model




Beyond the current peace process, Savary-Borioli also addressed Abdullah Öcalan’s political ideas. He argued that Öcalan’s concept of democratic confederalism is relevant not only to the Kurdish question but could also provide a foundation for social self-governance and democratic participation in other parts of the world.




At the heart of the concept is the transfer of political decision-making power to the people. Savary-Borioli associates this approach with a socialist understanding of democracy that prioritizes public participation in decision-making over centralized state authority.




“If we truly want to transfer power to the people, then it is clear that this democracy will have a socialist character. I believe this model could also serve as a good example beyond the Middle East,” he explained.




Savary-Borioli sees this as one of the reasons why authoritarian governments oppose Öcalan’s political ideas. He remarked that a model based on social self-organization and democratic participation in decision-making fundamentally challenges existing power structures. He argued that this opposition is not limited to the Turkish government. Savary-Borioli also pointed to the political systems in Iran and Syria, as well as the power structures in Iraq.




“It seems that despite all their differences, there is one point on which they all agree: They do not want democracy, nor do they want this model of democratic confederalism.”
