title: Imprisoned journalist Ahmed Polad’s father: Don’t leave him alone
content:
Journalist Ahmed Polad, who was abducted and detained by Hayat Tahrir al-Sham (HTS) on 18 January 2026 while covering events in Syria, was handed over to Turkey on 9 September 2026 after spending eight months in HTS prisons. Polad was subsequently arrested in Turkey. His father, Adil Aslan, appealed to the public to draw attention to his son's situation.




Ahmed Polad and Eva Maria Michelmann, who had been working as journalists in Rojava for many years, were abducted on 18 January 2026 during HTS attacks on Raqqa. Following a prisoner exchange on 11 April 2026, testimonies from people held in HTS prisons revealed that both journalists were in detention.




Once their whereabouts became known, campaigns demanding their release were organised in Turkey, Kurdistan and around the world. Following public pressure, HTS handed German journalist Eva Maria Michelmann over to Germany on 18 June 2026.




Eight months of torture in HTS prisons and a padded cell at MIT




Polad's whereabouts were finally confirmed on 9 September 2026. He was handed over to Turkey by HTS and subsequently remanded in custody by a court. In a report documenting his eight months in detention, Polad's lawyers stated that the journalist had been subjected to months of torture by HTS and had contracted scabies because of the unsanitary conditions and inadequate nutrition in prison.




The report also stated that immediately after being handed over to Turkey, Polad was interrogated for two days by the National Intelligence Organisation (MIT) and held in a padded cell for two days.




Polad described his experiences to his lawyers in the report: “On 18 January 2026, my German journalist colleague Eva Maria Michelmann and I were covering events in the Raqqa region of Syria when the building we were in was surrounded. We were detained after security forces entered the building. We were taken to a police station that I would describe as the Aleppo General Security Headquarters. The place where we were held was underground. It was a cell with no light, no fresh air and no ventilation. It measured one metre by two and a half metres. I was never taken outside. I never saw fresh air or daylight. The only exception was one week when I was held in a ward with around 190 to 200 people, including members of the Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF). For the first month, I was tortured every day. Three or four times a day, groups of people would enter my cell and start beating me. They tortured me by kicking me in the head, forcing me to the ground and crushing my head. Later, the torture became predominantly psychological. They would come at night and say things like, ‘Be ready in the morning, you will be executed,’ or ‘Be ready tomorrow, you will be beheaded.’”




Held in solitary confinement in Silivri




Polad is currently being held in a solitary cell at Marmara L-Type Prison in Silivri. His lawyers have said that his health is poor and that he urgently needs medical treatment. Polad's father, Adil Aslan, spoke to ANF about what the family had experienced over the past eight months and called on the public to show solidarity with his son.




‘We received no reliable information for eight months’




Adil Aslan said the family learned of Polad's abduction on 28 February and had lived in constant fear for his safety. Aslan also said: “He was detained by HTS gangs in Raqqa on 18 January, together with German journalist Eva Maria. We learned about it on 28 February, when the news became public. Naturally, we became extremely worried because the people who took them were truly brutal. If they had any humanity, we would not have been so distressed. We were constantly afraid. I kept saying, ‘These are barbaric people. They will murder our son. They will torture him to death or make him disappear.’ That fear was always with us, and we lived with it. For eight months, we received no reliable information whatsoever. Around 6 April, one or two eyewitnesses came forward. They claimed that Ahmed and Eva had been taken out of the same building together. We were told that they had been put into another vehicle and taken somewhere else. But those holding them refused to acknowledge it. They kept claiming, ‘We do not have anyone by that name.’ Despite repeated attempts by the lawyers, they never admitted holding him.”




‘They also interrogated our lawyer in Damascus’




Aslan said the lawyers submitted further official applications after an eyewitness reported seeing Ahmed Polad. He explained that the Syrian authorities had also interrogated their lawyer during the process of obtaining official approval for a power of attorney.




Aslan continued: “On 18 April, an eyewitness came forward and said, ‘I saw Ahmed in Aleppo Prison.’ The lawyers submitted another official application, but once again they claimed that Ahmed was not in their custody. Then, on 28 April, one of their ministers made a statement acknowledging that they were holding Ahmed. Some time later, we sent a power of attorney to our lawyer in Damascus. He went to the Ministry of Interior to have it approved, but they confiscated the document and told him, ‘We do not have anyone by that name.’ They asked him, ‘Where did you get this power of attorney?’ They took it from him and interrogated him for two or three hours. After that, we were back to square one.




We thought they must have done something to him, either executed him or made him disappear, and that was why they were denying everything. We were extremely anxious and distressed throughout that period, and there was very little we could do from here. It was incredibly difficult for me. I could not sleep at night. I would lie awake until morning, wondering where my son was, what he was doing and what they had done to him. For eight months, I lived with that anxiety. His mother, his siblings, all of us went through the same thing. Eight months later, on 11 September, at around 3 pm, I received a call from the Istanbul Police Department. They told me, ‘We have your son.’ I asked where he was, and they said he was at the Counter-Terrorism Branch (TEM). They told me, ‘We will call you if he is referred to the courthouse.’ I set off for the courthouse, but less than half an hour later they called me again.




They said, ‘Your son has been brought before the court, and they are taking him to prison.’ My son was supposedly being held at TEM. What did they do to him during those three days of unregistered detention? He was subjected to torture. In Syria, they tortured him for eight months while holding him in unregistered detention, without ever bringing him before a court or carrying out any legal proceedings. He was never brought before any judicial authority. Here, too, he was held for three days without any official record, blindfolded, with a sack over his head and his hands cuffed behind his back. That was how they kept him. Only afterwards did they call us.”




‘Ahmed’s health is poor, his internal organs have been damaged’




Adil Aslan said Polad became seriously ill on 10 September after being brought to Turkey, but police refused to follow doctors' recommendations for treatment and rushed him to court. He described what his son had experienced in Turkey and said: “On 10 September, he became seriously ill and was taken to hospital. The doctors said, ‘We need to admit him to intensive care for treatment.’ But they refused. Under pressure, they administered high doses of intravenous fluids, saying, ‘Let him recover a little, then we will take him to court and send him to prison.’ They forced him through the court proceedings and sent him to prison. His health is poor. He had been on hunger strike for five months, and his internal organs were damaged.




He was already wounded when they captured him. Once they brought him here, they kept him for two days in a closed, padded cell, blindfolded, with a sack over his head and his hands tied behind his back. They then took him to Ankara Police Headquarters. In fact, Ankara Police called me on 10 September. My phone rang once, but by the time I reached for it, the call had ended. Istanbul Police called me on 11 September. After bringing him from there to Istanbul, he became seriously ill. They took him to Taksim First Aid Hospital. The doctors there said, ‘His condition is poor. We urgently need to admit him to intensive care.’ But they refused. They administered high doses of intravenous fluids and medication.




Those high doses of medication also damaged his internal organs. This is how they treated someone who had been on hunger strike for five months. There is no medical justification for such treatment. We do not accept it. This amounts to an attempt to kill him, to eliminate him. That is how I see it. We cannot accept this. He was not treated like a human being. He is now being held alone in Silivri Prison No. 6. He has been diagnosed with scabies and is being held in a solitary cell. His health has still not recovered. He has open wounds that have become infected. He needs medical treatment, but he has not received comprehensive care. We are asking the public to raise awareness of his situation. We want my son to receive treatment at a fully equipped hospital as soon as possible.”




‘When I first saw him, I told my son to stand strong’




Aslan said he first saw Polad outside Metris Prison and described the moment they were reunited. Aslan continued: “The police called and told me they were taking him to Metris Prison. They said, ‘If you are at the gate, you will see your son.’ I turned around and went to the prison gate. I waited for half an hour but did not see anyone. I asked the officers, and they said, ‘We don't know.’ I also told his mother, who was on her way, to turn back. Then the same number called again and asked, ‘Where are you?’ I told them I was at the prison gate. They said, ‘They're coming in a white Renault Megane.’ When I first saw Ahmed, he was nothing but skin and bones.




His hair, his beard... No one who calls themselves human could reduce another person to that condition. Even if someone has committed a crime and you have taken them prisoner, no human being would treat a captive like that. But they are not human. They are remnants of ISIS. We know what a barbaric organisation ISIS is. They took someone who, until a year or two ago, was on the world's terrorist lists and made him president of a country. They have all grown beards, but faith is not found in a beard. They have nothing to do with Islam. They have no religion, no faith, no morality, nothing. They were gathered from different places and brought in to take control of Syria. They are all terrorists, all gang members. I do not recognise them as human beings. When Ahmed saw me, he cried. He told me, ‘Father, I have been tortured for eight months. I never gave in to them. I never gave them the satisfaction.’ I told him, ‘Stand strong, my son. I am by your side.’ He nodded, but he was exhausted and could barely speak to me.




The next day, when his lawyer visited him, Ahmed said, ‘Call my father. I was very exhausted last night, and my father was very upset. Tell him not to worry about me. I am fine.’ He was the one trying to comfort us. As a father, I was devastated. It is unbearable to see your child in that condition, his hair, his beard... They are holding thousands of people. I am appealing to everyone: Do not abandon these people to their fate. Please bring their situation to public attention. The world must pay attention. They are torturing people to death and leaving them devastated by hunger. They give them one sandwich every 24 hours. This is not compatible with human dignity. A person may be a prisoner, they may even have committed a crime, but no human being deserves such treatment.”




Aslan appealed to all journalists' professional organisations, lawyers, media workers and concerned members of the public to stand in solidarity with Ahmed. He said, “Do not leave Ahmed alone. He is a journalist who was working there to be the voice of a people.”

title: Cahit Berkay: Justice will strengthen trust in the peace process
content:
Artists continue to express their support for the Peace and Democratic Society Process through ANF. Musician Cahit Berkay welcomed the silencing of weapons and said swift, concrete steps were needed to advance the process. He stressed that justice was fundamental to peace and drew attention to the importance of freedom to use one's mother tongue.




‘The guns have fallen silent, now further steps must follow’




Musician Cahit Berkay told ANF: “The most important thing was for the guns to fall silent. This was a very welcome decision. Now further steps must follow. The way has been opened for that. It seems this process will be pursued more seriously than previous ones. I hope it achieves its goal.”




Berkay, who described love as his philosophy of life, continued: “My approach to these issues, my philosophy of life, is that love lies at the heart of everything. Peace is something that can be achieved by people who are capable of genuinely and properly feeling, building and experiencing love. Love begins with a person's respect and love for themselves. It then extends to their loved ones, friends, country, the world and the universe. Love also keeps our conscience alive.




When this becomes the foundation, every approach, every word you speak and every intention you feel is rooted in sincerity. As a result, nobody deceives anyone or sets traps for one another. Love is the foundation of everything. Since we are on the subject, let me ask: What was the central theme of Selvi Boylum Al Yazmalım (The Girl with the Red Scarf)? Love is effort. That energy, too, is a manifestation of the love a person carries within them. If you want that love to survive, you must make an effort. Nothing can be achieved without effort.”




‘Music brings people in Edirne and Batman together’




Berkay spoke about the powerful role music plays in bringing different peoples together.




Berkay said: “I have experienced this effect personally, and I still do. For example, I always play Al Yazmalım at every concert. I have played it in Batman (Êlih), Diyarbakır (Amed) and Edirne. I have also performed it in many European countries. Kurdish and Turkish people come together through the same song. They applaud the same notes. Twenty years ago, I performed at a voluntary event in Diyarbakır and Batman. As soon as the first notes of Al Yazmalım began, a wave of zılgıt (traditional celebratory ululation) erupted. I got goosebumps and started trembling. I cannot describe that feeling.”




‘Peace comes through justice’




Cahit Berkay also spoke about the relationship between art and peace: “Art makes an enormous contribution to building and sustaining peace. Most artists are thoughtful, sincere people who carry love within them and care about humanity. I believe peace is one of the central themes of art. Sculptors, painters and musicians all take peace as a theme in their work.




For decades, we have been struggling desperately, if you'll excuse the expression, to achieve peace. We must establish peace and restore our inner tranquillity as soon as possible. But of course, this can only happen through rights, the rule of law and justice. Without these, nothing else works.




Without justice, there will be plots and attempts to undermine peace, as well as crimes against humanity. That is why it is so important for the justice system to function properly. Justice will also strengthen trust in this process.




There are deeply rooted issues and memories surrounding the Kurdish question. This applies to all sides. Those memories are still alive. Justice and the law are also the remedies for the experiences that have left such deep wounds.”




‘Mother tongues must be free’




Berkay also spoke about the importance of freedom to use one's mother tongue: “Freedom to use your mother tongue is extremely important. If you cannot freely use the language you learned from your mother and grandmother, something fundamental is missing. That language is part of who you are. You can express your spirit, identity and love most fully in your mother tongue. Whether it is Kurdish or Laz, it makes no difference.




What unites us all is our humanity. Your beliefs, language or religion do not matter. If we approach one another with love, we will have taken the biggest step. Any remaining obstacles will be easier to overcome. Love and justice are also the foundations of peace.




Çetin Altan had a wonderful saying: ‘Never miss out on love.’ In relation to the issue we are discussing, that love must be nurtured throughout society and shared by everyone, hand in hand.”




‘

The process must be more transparent and move faster’




Musician Cahit Berkay also stressed that transparency was essential to ensuring that the process rested on solid foundations. Berkay said: “Swift steps must certainly be taken in this process, but we must not pretend that certain problems do not exist. Otherwise, the process will not rest on solid foundations. It is time to establish firm foundations. Everyone must put their cards on the table.




I have reached the age of 80. Someone else has reached 90, and then there are newborn babies. We need to think about all of them. This country urgently needs peace and tranquillity. Look at the country's economy, its political situation. Everything is there for everyone to see. There is no need to elaborate; we can all see what is happening.




I am concerned, but I am always hopeful. I have never lost hope. I always have hope because I love you and I love myself. It is that love that will resolve all these problems at their roots, without leaving any obstacles behind.”

title: Öcalan sends message to EUTCC conference: There is much that you, too, can do
content:
The following is the message sent by Abdullah Öcalan to the 20th Kurdish Conference, held this year at the European Parliament in Brussels, organized by the EUTCC:




“I extend my greetings to the participants and organizers of your 20th Conference, entitled ‘The European Union, Turkey, the Middle East and the Kurds.’




Undoubtedly, you have carried out—and continue to carry out—very valuable work, for which I offer my thanks and respect.




On 15 February 1999, I was brought to Imralı as a result of an international conspiracy. I am here today because of the influence of NATO’s Gladio network. I will not refrain from criticizing this at this point. They had said of me that ‘there is not a single patch of land in Europe where he could set foot.’ This conspiracy and these schemes were carried out in secrecy, hidden from the peoples of Europe. They were orchestrated according to the Gladio mentality. Undoubtedly, you are struggling against this situation. You are working to challenge it.




The European Union, which adopted this approach at the time, must today act in accordance with its own laws. It is of great importance that it take a constructive approach both to the democratization of Turkey and to the resolution of the Kurdish question. The fundamental way to resist the rising far right and the trend toward authoritarianism in Europe is to firmly uphold democratic values.




In particular, the support expressed through civil society and political initiatives such as your conference during the Peace and Democratic Society Process is support for peace and democracy. At the same time, your work and this conference need to become more enduring. New steps are needed. There is a need for internationalist cooperation. Such cooperation is important because it can bring together the democratic experiences and accumulated achievements of our regions and peoples, paving the way for a new paradigm of democracy and socialism.




The work we are carrying out in Turkey is valuable and important. We have launched a serious process aimed at finding political, fair and legal solutions to social problems in place of wars, massacres and the marginalization of others.




You can also discuss these issues at your conference. At present, there are many unanswered questions. Yet, despite these uncertainties, we are proposing a comprehensive model for a solution. This initiative represents a historic step for both Europe and the Middle East.




The success of our proposed Peace and Democratic Society project will make peace, stability and democratization in the Middle East possible. There is much that you, too, can do to help make this happen. I believe that valuable friends and comrades such as yourselves will help spread this initiative more widely.




Once again, I congratulate all those involved in the conference and send you my greetings and respects.




Abdullah Öcalan




Imralı




9 October"

title: PYD condemns the attack on party office in Hesekê
content:
The Democratic Union Party (PYD) condemned the vandalism of its office in the Xiwêran neighborhood of Hesekê and called for a comprehensive investigation into the attacks. In a statement issued on Wednesday, the party’s leadership described the attacks on Kurdish symbols and memorial portraits of fallen women as a threat to social peace, freedom of political activity, and coexistence among the different communities in northeastern Syria.




On Tuesday, unidentified individuals forcibly entered the PYD office, broke down doors, and vandalized the premises. Kurdish symbols, particularly memorial portraits of prominent women figures of the revolution, were targeted and stolen. Images of fallen women were subsequently desecrated in public, and footage of these acts was circulated on social media. According to the authorities, a suspect has since been arrested.




Connection with attack in Til Temir




The PYD recalled that the Center of the Council of Families of Martyrs in Til Temir had also been attacked just a few days earlier. The party views these incidents as part of a deliberate campaign targeting social coexistence. “The attacks in Til Temir and now in Hesekê, as well as the destruction of our office, indicate a systematic plan aimed at undermining coexistence,” the General Council stated.




PYD noted that the office in Xiwêran was not merely a party facility but also a center for community organizing and cooperation among different population groups. The attacks therefore threaten not only the PYD but also political organizing and coexistence in the region, it said. The party sees the attacks as reflecting a racist attitude reminiscent of the practices of the former Baath regime. “Its policies were based on the exclusion of other identities and the rejection of social diversity.”




Call for an investigation and protection of political institutions




The PYD called on the relevant authorities to ensure effective protection for party offices and civilian institutions, investigate the attacks, and hold those responsible accountable. It also demanded measures to prevent further attacks.




The party appealed to Syria’s political and social forces, as well as the wider population, to reject provocations and hatred and remain committed to dialogue.




“We call on everyone to uphold dialogue and coexistence and to protect social peace,” the statement concluded.

title: Kurdish Conference: No peace without democratization
content:
The 20th conference, organized by the European Union Turkey Civic Commission (EUTCC) and patronized by Nobel Peace Prize laureate and Iranian human rights advocate Shirin Ebadi, human rights activist Bianca Jagger, and Kurdish politician Leyla Zana, recipient of the European Parliament’s Sakharov Prize for Freedom of Thought, began with a reception on October 14 at the European Parliament (EP) in Brussels.




The conference entered its second day with a packed program. The second and third sessions of the morning focused on geopolitical changes in the Middle East and women shaping the future.




Second session




The second session of the conference at the European Parliament was held under the title “The Middle East at a crossroads: Geopolitical shifts, democratic transformation, and the pursuit of peace.”




Moderated by journalist Dilek Odabaşı, the session featured Doğu Ergil from Ankara University, journalist Amed Dicle, and Colin Starger from the University of Baltimore in the United States as speakers.




Doğu Ergil: The conditions for lasting peace cannot be established without democratization




Academic Doğu Ergil questioned why so much investment in security had produced so little peace, drawing attention to the deep crises facing policies built around security.




Assessing global military, geopolitical, and political changes, Ergil argued that the emerging situation was not one of multipolarity but rather of overlapping security spheres.




Referring to the ongoing process in Turkey, Doğu Ergil said: “Democracy is the capacity to manage social differences and existential conflicts through political means. It does not eliminate political disagreements entirely. It enables parties that cannot reach agreement to coexist peacefully despite their differences. Leaving political issues unresolved eventually becomes a persistent source of insecurity.”




Emphasizing that democratic reforms should not be regarded as a luxury to be considered only after stability has been achieved, Doğu Ergil added: “Democracy is not merely a consequence of sustainable stability but also one of its prerequisites. Why do I say this? Because we frequently hear the following argument: First, let the most important agreement be reached, and then democratic reforms can follow. However, the conditions for lasting peace cannot be established without democratization.”




Proposing three transformations, Doğu Ergil said: “The first is a transition from regime-centered security to human-centered security. The second is a transition from an exclusionary understanding of national sovereignty to a cooperative security framework.”




As a third transformation, he emphasized the importance of resolutions accepted and sustained by societies themselves rather than imposed from outside.




Amed Dicle: Europe should encourage a resolution




Drawing attention to the Peace and Democratic Society Process in Turkey, journalist Amed Dicle said: “Negotiating with a government to reach a resolution does not mean endorsing its approach to governance. To secure their rights and their future, the Kurds are engaging in talks with those who currently hold decision-making power. The opposition’s responsibility should be to build on this opportunity to advance the democratization of the country.”




Highlighting the responsibilities of the European Union and European countries, Amed Dicle stated: “If the European Union wants a political resolution, it must go beyond welcoming the decisions of the Kurdish movement and also raise the steps that the state needs to take. Maintaining trade, investment, and security relations with Turkey does not prevent the recognition of Kurdish rights. These relations can continue with a Turkey that has made peace with the Kurds, while direct and long-term relations can also be developed with the Kurds, who play a significant role in the region’s future.




What the Kurds expect from Europe is for the diplomatic influence gained through its relations with Ankara to be used to advance peace. The close relations that once made it possible to support policies of war can now also be used to encourage a resolution.




Because the outcome of this process will not be confined to Turkey’s borders. The Middle East is being reshaped, and the Kurds are at the center of this transformation. It is impossible to establish a new political order in the region without the Kurds. Both Ankara and European capitals must take this reality into account in their calculations. Postponing a resolution to the Kurdish question means postponing a fundamental issue that they will inevitably face in shaping the region’s future.




For this reason, neither Ankara’s decisions nor Europe’s position will only affect the current process. As the Middle East is reshaped, they will determine whether the Kurdish question becomes a cause of new conflicts or whether its resolution becomes the foundation for new relationships.”




Starger: It is time for change




Colin Starger from the University of Baltimore recounted the period during which he was held captive by the PKK. Stating that the United States should remove the PKK from its list of terrorist organizations and that his name should not be used to justify keeping the organization on the list, Starger said:




“When we consider that the PKK that abducted me in 1993 is not the same PKK we see today, and that the United States and its relationship with the Kurds have changed over time, I firmly believe that the US should remove the PKK from its list of foreign terrorist organizations. My name should not be used to support keeping the PKK on this list today. What happened to me 33 years ago cannot be cited as justification for keeping the organization on the list today. It is time for change.”




Starger continued: “As a legal professional, justice is extremely important to me. I am committed to achieving justice; that is what I am trying to do. The rule of law is not only intended to protect justice but also seeks to ensure that justice is achieved. Genuine peace is essential, but it requires more than just the silencing of weapons. True peace requires justice.”




Third session




The third session of the conference was held under the title “Women shaping the future: Democratic transformation, Kurdish unity, and peace in the Middle East.”




Moderated by political scientist Arzu Yılmaz, the session featured Atefeh Ramsari from Bielefeld University, former HDP MP and member of the Free Women’s Movement Sebahat Tuncel, and İlham Ahmed as the representative of Rojava.




Atefeh Ramsari: The independent will of the Kurds must be recognized




Drawing attention to the situation in the four parts of Kurdistan, Atefeh Ramsari stated the following: “The political will of the Kurds has historically been shaped by the interaction of territorial partition, competing state-building projects, cross-border Kurdish mobilization, and regional security strategies. Fragmentation is therefore not merely a geographical condition; it is continuously reproduced through political and institutional practices.




The fundamental contradiction here lies between the national framework within which the Kurdish question is managed and the regional relationships through which it is reproduced.




The institutions of each state assess Kurdish political demands primarily through their own understanding of sovereignty, territorial integrity, and national security. International diplomacy has also largely reinforced this state-centered approach.




However, the Kurdish question cannot be adequately understood as the sum of separate and independent minority issues. This is because the political conditions in each part of Kurdistan are shaped by relationships that extend beyond the territorial boundaries of the respective states.




This issue lies at the heart of any discussion about how peace can be achieved.




The resolution of the Kurdish question cannot be reduced to disarmament, the cessation of armed conflicts, or the integration of Kurdish actors into existing state institutions.




A lasting solution requires addressing the political relationships that reproduce the exclusion and subordination of the Kurds. This includes the distribution of authority, collective rights, democratic participation, and recognition of the Kurds’ independent political will.




Responsibility for achieving peace cannot be placed primarily on Kurdish actors. The conditions for a political settlement are shaped by the policies and strategic decisions of the four states, as well as by international actors that influence the regional balance of power.




The significance of these developments extends far beyond formal changes in political representation.




Women’s participation has generated political knowledge, organizational capacity, and new forms of collective action. These cannot be assessed solely in terms of whether particular institutions continue to exist.




This requires an important distinction between the reversibility of institutional gains and the long-term conditions for political change.”




İlham Ahmed: Without guarantees, peace will remain temporary




İlham Ahmed emphasized that peace cannot be sustained unless it is legally guaranteed, drawing attention to the problems encountered during the integration process. She particularly highlighted Arab chauvinism in the country and stressed the role of women.




İlham Ahmed said: “Women have played an important role in every sphere of life and in all aspects of social life. They have contributed to building a free life and social freedom. They have also played an important role in shaping Syria’s future. They have established democratic and social values. However, under the new political conditions emerging in Syria, it remains uncertain whether the gains achieved by the peoples in establishing their own systems of governance can be preserved.”




İlham Ahmed stated that approaches seeking to restrict women’s role in social and political movements and push them out of politics had emerged. “The issue is not merely that women should remain in the workforce, but that they should also be able to play an active role in political decision-making,” she said.




Addressing the situation surrounding the integration process, İlham Ahmed said: “We want lasting peace. However, the question of how integration will take place and how it will contribute to lasting peace has yet to be clarified. Peace may remain merely temporary unless the necessary guarantees are provided. If mechanisms and institutional safeguards to build peace are not established, there is always a risk that it could break down. This is why various problems are emerging.”




‘We want to be equal and essential

 

partners in Syria’




İlham Ahmed added: “The fundamental issue in relations between the Kurds and the Syrian government is this: The Kurds must be accepted as actors within this state, and their identity must be recognized.”




Stating that they intend to become partners in Syria, İlham Ahmed said: “We have decided to pursue integration, but this does not mean that we have agreed to take a step backward. We want to be genuine partners in this country. As Kurds, we want to be equal and essential partners. We have both the will and the determination to achieve this.




Therefore, it would be wrong to reverse the steps that have been taken or move the process backward. However, mutual acceptance and mutual recognition are also necessary. The state must also make greater efforts in this regard and establish a framework of reconciliation and governance that will make all components of Syrian society genuine partners in this state.”




Sebahat Tuncel: We must break the cycle of repetition and have our rights recognized




TJA (Free Women’s Movement) activist Sebahat Tuncel was the final speaker in the session. She warned that more difficult periods could follow if the necessary steps were not taken. Questioning how peace would be achieved and what form it would take, Tuncel particularly emphasized that the European Union is part of the Kurdish question and therefore bears responsibility.




Tuncel stated: “Europe is also part of the Kurdish question. If the Kurdish question has remained unresolved until today, the reasons do not stem solely from policies in Turkey or regional developments; there are also dimensions arising from Europe’s approach.




Today, we are still talking about a peace process. The PKK has announced its dissolution and disarmament. Despite this fact, the PKK remains on Europe’s list of terrorist organizations. As our American fellow speaker pointed out earlier, the PKK is also on the United States’ list of terrorist organizations. It is not realistic to regard this as an approach genuinely aimed at resolving the issue.”




Emphasizing that Europe’s approach so far has not been sufficiently positive, Sebahat Tuncel stressed that the Council of Europe has failed to take effective measures beyond issuing warnings, particularly regarding the implementation of the right to hope and rulings of the European Court of Human Rights (ECtHR).




“If we are part of this world, what is needed is a more effective stance. Otherwise, we will simply talk here and then disperse. I believe that if genuine change and transformation are to take place, they must happen everywhere,” she added.




The cycle of repetition must be broken




Sebahat Tuncel continued:




“I have spoken at the European Parliament before. Back then, we also discussed the Kurdish question and the situation of women. After that, I was away for a while, remained behind bars, and now, seven and a half years later, I am here again. Yet we are still discussing the same issues.




This has now become a cycle of repetition. I believe one of the most important observations in Mr. Öcalan’s February 25 message is the need to break this cycle. This is also one of the reasons behind the dissolution of the PKK.




The circumstances surrounding the founding of the PKK must be evaluated within their own historical context, rather than independently of state policies. At that time, the influence of the October Revolution, the international political climate, and the vision of an independent, united Kurdistan played a role in the emergence of armed struggle as a form of resistance.




However, global conditions have changed. The circumstances in Kurdistan, Turkey, and the Middle East are no longer the same. Therefore, it is believed that the strategic direction of the struggle must shift from armed struggle to democratic politics. It is also argued that the PKK must overcome its own deeply entrenched cycle of repetition. I believe this is an important observation.




However, the issue of repetition is not limited to the Kurds, Kurdistan, or Turkey. A similar cycle of repetition is taking place across the world. We must break this cycle.




Today, we see people taking to the streets demanding change, justice, and fairer governance. Why are young people in the streets? Because the demand for change is not ours alone; it is a demand shared by people around the world.




In addition to this, we have a specific demand: Extend to us the officially recognized citizenship rights enjoyed by citizens around the world. Because our existence is being denied.




This is the fundamental issue: The existence of the Kurds is not recognized. How can you guarantee the rights and legal protections of a people whose very existence is not recognized?




I believe that one of the key issues highlighted in Mr. Öcalan’s message is the question of recognition. He emphasizes the recognition of Kurdish identity and free identity, as well as the acceptance of the Kurds’ right to establish and preserve their own systems. This is the fundamental issue. Once these conditions are met, the other dimensions of the struggle can also be addressed within this basic framework.”




Lasting unity must be established




Emphasizing the importance of unity among the Kurds, Sebahat Tuncel said: “If the Kurds achieve unity among themselves, they can also establish unity with the peoples with whom they coexist. Unity is not merely about coming together from time to time or issuing joint statements. The real issue is to establish lasting unity through which the Kurds can collectively build their democratic future and a life in freedom.”




‘Abdullah Öcalan must be free’




Emphasizing that the parties involved must also be free for the process to move forward, Sebahat Tuncel stated that Abdullah Öcalan must be free.




Tuncel concluded her remarks by saying: “Demanding Mr. Öcalan’s freedom means demanding peace. He is struggling on behalf of the Kurds, and recognition of Mr. Öcalan’s status means recognition of the political status of the Kurds.”

title: Every so often, I think about how they told us back in 2009 that a $15 minimum wage would make…
content:
fabiansociety

:

dovesndecay

:

Every so often, I think about how they told us back in 2009 that a $15 minimum wage would make burger costs skyrocket & no-skill workers would be paid more than they’re worth, so they didn’t raise it.

But I guess the burger costs skyrocketing sounded … 

pretty good

! so they killed Dollar Menu and put Value Menu in its place like “no it’s totally the same guy” and a single 2026 burger now costs the same as 

four 

2009 burgers, but a 2026 worker is still only worth $7.25. 

a 2026 worker isn’t even worth 7.25 in 2009 dollars anymore. just to keep up with inflation, that minimum wage should have risen to 11.50 today. (thanks, 

cpi inflation calculator

!) a $1 burger would only have risen to $1.59 by inflation

FUN FACT: it’s now been so long since the dems were able to raise the minimum wage that today’s minimum wage is now functionally lower than than at any point since 

1949

. in fact, this is a chance to roll out my favorite radicalizing chart, the history of the minimum wage, adjusted for inflation:

This thing infuriates me almost beyond thinking. Look at it! American minimum workers haven’t had an actual raise since 

1968

. We’ve been steadily losing ground for 

58 years

. 2009 was the closest we’ve come, and even that only returned the wage to what it had been in 1983. Why is everything a catastrophe now? because a minimum wage worker in 2026 makes the exact same wage as one in 1939.

we haven’t had an actual raise since 1968, which was, not coincidentally, the only wage increase that happened after the passage of the civil rights act that made discrimination in wages illegal. the march on washington for jobs and freedom in 1963, the one where martin luther king jr gave the i have a dream speech, called for a $2/hour minimum wage. that would be the equivalent of $16.86 today. at the time of the march, that increase would have been a raise of about 60%. today it would be 132%. we’ve had so much stolen from us by the wealthy.

title: Karneya tenduristî û avhewayê ya welatan: Tirkiye di rêza 47em de ye
content:
Hevpeymaniya Avhewa û Tenduristiyê ya Cîhanî (

Global Climate and Health Alliance

 ,GCHA), karneya tenduristiyê ya 132 welatan parve kiriye ku wan welatan peyman û sozên neteweyî yên avhewayê di çarçoveya Peymana Parîsê de weşandine.




Di “Karneya Beyana Tevkariya Neteweyî ya Tendurist” (The Healthy NDC Scorecard) de karneya tenduristî û hewaya paqij a beyanên tevkariya neteweyî di heşt kategoriyan de hat nirxandin. Di analîzê de bandorên li ser tenduristiyê, qirêjiya hewayê, çalakiyên di sektora tenduristiyê de, fêdeyên din ên di qada tenduristiyê de, veguhestinên edîl, birêvebirina entegreyê, aborî û fînans, şopandin û pêkanîn hatin lêkolînkirin.




Tirkiye di rêza 47em de ye







Encam bi wê yekê re hatin berhevkirin ku bê ka armancên avhewayê heta çi astê bi îdia ne û li wî welatî rêjeya mirinên ji ber qirêjiya hewayê çiqas e. Di encama analîzê de Tirkiye bi 14 pûanan di nav 132 welatan de di rêza 47em de cih girt:







Li Tirkiyeyê rêjeya mirinên ji ber qirêjiya hewayê di her sed hezar kesî de weke 83,6 hat tomarkirin. Armanca giştî ya avhewayê ya wî welatî ji bo senaryoyeke ku di bin 4°C’yî de ye wekî gelekî kêm hat nirxandin.







Di raporê de ev xal derketin pêş:













19 welatên ku karîn di nav 20 welatên destpêkê de cih bigirin, welatên xwedî dahata kêm û navîn in.










Pûana Tirkiyeyê (14) nêzî pûana Kanada (16), Efrîqaya Başûr (13) û Yekîtiya Ewropayê (12) ye. 










Kolombiya bi wê yekê derdikeve pêş ku mijara tenduristiyê di plansaziyên xwe yên neteweyî yên avhewayê de bi awayekî herî berfireh entegre kiriye(pûana wê di ser 32an de 29 e). Nijerya (25 pûan) û Kamboçya (24 pûan).










Japonya û Hindistan ku tenê karîn 2 pûanan bistînin, di nav welatên ku pûana herî kêm stendine de cih digirin.










Welatên din ên ku emîsyona wan bilind e jî, ji ber ku erka dikeve ser milê wan bi awayekî adil bi cih neanîn, li paş armancan man. Di nav van welatan de Brezîlya (7), Awistralya, Çîn û Brîtanya (bi giştî 9 pûan) cih digirin.










Tê destnîşankirin ku tenê di pênc welatan de (Kamboçya, Şîlî, Kolombiya, Kosta Rîka û Paraguay) armancên kêmkirina karbona reş hene ku yek ji sedemên sereke yên guherîna avhewayê û qirêjiya hewayê ye û dibe sedema pirsgirêkên tenduristiyê yên giran.













Bandorên krîza avhewayê yên li ser tenduristiyê




Bandorên krîza avhewayê yên li ser tenduristiyê gav bi gav diyar dibin. Îsal tenê li Nepalê ji ber hilweşîna berfa qeşagirtî zêdetirî hezar û 400 kes mirin û zêdetirî 6 hezar û 600 kes hîn jî winda ne.




Ji ber bûyerên ku peywendiya wan bi guherîna avhewayê re hene li Afrîkaya Rojhilat û Başûr heşt mîlyon zarok bi xetereya birçîbûnê re rûbirû ne.




Her wiha tê zanîn ku li Ewropayê pêlên germê yên di havînê de bûn sedema mirina zêdetirî 35 hezar kesan.




Li gorî Rêxistina Tenduristiyê ya Cîhanê (DSO), krîza avhewayê dikare di nava salên 2030-2050an de her sal bibe sedema zêdeyî 250 hezar mirinên din.



















HEYAMA KU ÎKLÎM Û DINYA DIGUHERE... - 4




Bandora krîza îklîmê û sotemenîyên fosîlî li ser tendûristîya zarokan




10 Hezîran 2021










Ji sedî 92ê Tirkiyeyê hewaya qirêj dikişînin sîngê xwe




Li gorî Rapora Reş 2025an a Platforma Mafê Hewaya Paqij, ji sedî 92yê serjimêriya Tirkiyeyê li gorî pîvanên Rêxistina Tenduristiyê ya Cîhanê (DSO) hewaya qirêj dikişînin sîngê xwe.




Ew bajarê ku qirêjiya hewayê û rêjeya mirina ji ber qirêjiyê lê herî bilind e jî Colemêrg e.




Di raporê de tê diyar kirin ku heke qirêjiya hewayê dakeve asta ku DSO pêşniyar dike, li Tirkiyeyê di salê de dikare jiyana herî kêm 60 hezar kesî bifilite.




Ev nûçe bi hevkariya bianet û İklim Masasiyê(Maseya Avhewayê) hatiye weşandin. İklim Masasi servîseke nûçeyan e ku armanc dike agahiyên bawerpêkirî yên li ser krîza avhewayê di nav raya giştî de belav bike. Nivîskarên wê ji wan zanyaran pêk tên ku di mijarên dikin nûçe de xwedî pisporiyê ne.

title: "Hyperscale": Paris Marx on Excess of Big Tech Data Empires & His Critique of Bernie Sanders' AI Bill
content:
We speak with tech journalist Paris Marx about his new book, 

Hyperscale: The Ambition and Excess of Big Tech’s Data Empires

. In the book, Marx exposes the deceptive ways tech companies are taking resources from vulnerable communities in order to build massive AI data centers. “We have seen the tech companies that, back in 2019, 2020, wanted us to see them as climate leaders … completely throw their targets out the window in order to pursue generative AI and this data center buildout,” says Marx. He notes that after failing to connect to electrical grids in the locations where they were building data centers, some AI companies have pivoted to building “on-site gas plants,” further increasing dependency on fossil fuels.




Tech companies “want us to believe” that AI models are “starting to become so powerful that within 10 years they could decide that they want to wipe out humanity or a significant chunk of humanity,” says Marx. “That is a mix of science fiction and delusion … and it is also a very effective way to distract from the real harms that we’re seeing from these generative AI products.”

title: Flamingo-Revolution in Albanien gegen Jared Kushners Luxusresort im Schutzgebiet Vjosa-Narta betrifft längst mehr als Umweltschutz und Privatisierung
content:
Dossier




„

Eine Firma mit Verbindungen zum Schwiegersohn des US-Präsidenten will Hotelkomplexe in albanischen Schutzgebieten bauen. Der Regierungschef bestreitet eine Einigung. Bagger roden dennoch bereits Kiefernwald im Projektgebiet. Am Montag sind Tausende in Tirana, der Hauptstadt Albaniens, auf die Straße gegangen. Sie protestierten gegen ein Luxusresort-Projekt, das mit Jared Kushner, dem Schwiegersohn des früheren US-Präsidenten Donald Trump, in Verbindung steht. Das Investmentunternehmen Affinity Partners will küstennahe Feuchtgebiete in ein riesiges Ferienresort verwandeln. Das Projekt sieht Hotelkomplexe auf mehreren Hektar der geschützten Küstenzone Vjosa-Narta bei Zvernec und auf der unbewohnten Adriainsel Sazan vor

…“ 

Artikel von Anna Flori vom 02.06.2026 bei Euronews

 

 („Albanien: Tausende protestieren gegen Jared Kushners Luxusprojekt“) mit einem Video – siehe mehr Informationen:







„Die Zukunft gehört uns“: In Albanien schließen sich Studierendenproteste und Unterrichtsboykotte nun den 3. Tag der „Flamingo-Revolution“ an: Gegen Regierung und Polizeigewalt 







Studentenproteste, Stunde um Stunde




„… 

Schüler der Sekundarstufe in Korçë, Vlorë, Elbasan, Divjakë, Shkodër und Kamëz haben heute aus Protest den Unterricht boykottiert. 

m dritten Tag der Proteste haben Tausende von Studenten und Schülern der Tiranaer Gymnasien die Straßen der Stadt gefüllt und den Rücktritt von Ministerpräsident Edi Rama gefordert. Der Protest, zu dem für 10:00 Uhr vor dem Parlament aufgerufen worden war, begann bereits früher, als die Abgeordneten den Plenarsaal verließen, nachdem die Plenarsitzung abgesagt worden war. In einem Interview erklärte Ministerpräsident Edi Rama, er werde nicht zurücktreten

…“ albanischer 

LiveBlog der Redaktion von Citizens.al

 

 

 (Stand 15. Oktober 2026) mit Fotos und Videos (maschinenübersetzt)




Studentenprotest beginnt mit Boykott




„

Der heutige Morgen begann mit Protesten und einem Vorlesungsboykott an mehreren Universitäten und Gymnasien im ganzen Land als Zeichen des Widerstands gegen die Regierung.


Wie angekündigt haben die Studierenden der medizinischen Fakultät den Unterricht boykottiert und sind zu einem Marsch zum Bildungsministerium aufgebrochen, wo um 14 Uhr eine Protestkundgebung stattfinden soll.




Unter den Rufen „Rama ins Gefängnis“, „Berisha ins Gefängnis“ und „Die Zukunft gehört uns“ marschieren junge Menschen durch die Hauptstadt, und unterwegs haben sich ihnen weitere Studenten angeschlossen.


Dem Boykott haben sich auch Studierende der Polytechnischen Universität Tirana, der Wirtschaftsfakultät der „Alexander-Xhuvani“-Universität in Elbasan und der Universität für Rechtswissenschaften angeschlossen. Auch die Fakultät für Geschichte und Philologie sowie die Fakultät für Wirtschaftswissenschaften marschieren mit, nachdem sie den Unterricht boykottiert haben. Ebenso wurde der Unterricht am „Partizani“-Gymnasium in Tirana boykottiert.




Die heutige Demonstration findet einen Tag nach gewalttätigen Zusammenstößen zwischen Studenten und der Polizei in Tirana statt, die sich während der für den 13. Oktober vor dem Bildungsministerium einberufenen Demonstration ereigneten. Im Verlauf der Kundgebung kam es zu körperlichen Auseinandersetzungen, Stockangriffen und dem Einsatz eines Wasserwerfers, um die Menge zu zerstreuen. Demonstranten bewarfen das Gebäude mit Eiern, während die Polizei mindestens zehn Personen festnahm. Bei den Zusammenstößen wurden mehrere Menschen verletzt, und es gab Bilder von blutüberströmten Studenten

.“ albanischer 

Bericht von Arbjona Çibuku vom 14. Oktober 2026 in Citizens

 

 (maschinenübersetzt) mit Fotos




Nationale und internationale Organisationen reagieren auf die Polizeigewalt bei der Demonstration.

Das Regime des Zauns




„

Die Proteste gegen Privatisierung in Albanien dauern an. Das mit Stacheldraht umzäunte Naturschutzgebiet steht dabei für eine unhaltbare Ordnung.


Jahrzehntelang, unter der Diktatur Enver Hoxhas, war Albanien ein von Stacheldraht umgebenes Land. Dessen Grenzen wurden von Bunkern, Kontrollposten und Waffen bewacht, die nicht nur gegen die Außenwelt, sondern auch gegen die eigene Bevölkerung gerichtet waren. Der Zaun war das deutlichste Symbol eines Regimes, das nicht auf Vertrauen gründete, sondern auf Isolation, Kontrolle und Ausgrenzung. Heute errichtet zwar niemand mehr Stacheldraht an den Grenzen der Republik, aber die Logik des Zauns ist zurückgekehrt. Nur wird heute nicht mehr Albanien von der Welt abgeschottet, sondern gewissermaßen die Albaner*innen von Albanien selbst, von dem Land und seinen Ressourcen.


Der Zaun ist vielleicht das politischste Element des Bauens. Er umschließt Territorien, isoliert Räume, zerschneidet Landschaften und schafft Privilegien. Seit Jahren erleben wir, wie Bauzäune unsere Städte fragmentieren. Sie haben Gehwege blockiert, Parks zerstört, Bewegungsfreiheit eingeschränkt und die Orte reduziert, an denen Menschen einander begegnen und miteinander in Kontakt treten. Inzwischen hat die Einzäunung auch Strände wie Rrjolli, Manastiri, Palasa und Dhërmi sowie Schutzgebiete wie Vjosë-Narta erreicht – als wäre die Privatisierung des öffentlichen Raums das einzige Entwicklungsmodell für Albanien. Diese Zäune schützen private Interessen und mobilisieren dafür die gesamte Autorität des Staates. Das öffentliche Interesse wird vor dem Zaun gehalten, während sich der Staat in den Dienst jener stellt, die sich dahinter verschanzen. (…)


Jahrelang haben Aktivist*innen, Organisationen und Expert*innen diese Prozesse mit Argumenten, rechtlichen Mitteln und über Institutionen bekämpft. Als die Institutionen aufhörten zuzuhören und Argumente keine Wirkung mehr erzielten, übernahmen die Bürger*innen selbst die Verteidigung des öffentlichen Interesses auf Straßen und Plätzen. Deshalb ist der zivile Widerstand auf dem Boulevard nicht nur eine Reaktion auf einen Zaun in Zvërnec, sondern auf einen weit längeren Prozess der Zersplitterung des Territoriums, der Privatisierung des Gemeinwohls und der Konzentration von Vorteilen in den Händen weniger. (…) Vielleicht geht es deshalb bei diesem Konflikt nicht nur um ein Gebiet in Narta oder Zvërnec, sondern um zwei verschiedene Vorstellungen von Albanien: Die eine sieht das Land als Mosaik eingezäunter Räume mit begrenztem Zugang und reservierten Privilegien. Die andere sieht es als Republik, in der Territorium, Recht und öffentliches Interesse nicht durch Stacheldraht, sondern durch demokratische Institutionen geschützt werden

An der Veranstaltung nahmen Mitglieder des Europäischen Parlaments, Vertreter linker Parteien aus Ländern wie Portugal, Dänemark, Italien, Griechenland, Deutschland und anderen sowie zahlreiche Teilnehmer aus der albanischen Diaspora in Europa teil.




Tridico eröffnete die Diskussion mit dem Hinweis, dass dieses Treffen die Entwicklungen in Albanien unterstütze, wo Frauen, Männer und junge Menschen sich zusammengeschlossen hätten, um ihre Stimme zu erheben und deutlich zu machen, dass die albanische Umwelt nicht zerstört werden dürfe. Er erklärte, dass dieses Treffen den Europaabgeordneten dabei helfe, die Geschehnisse in Albanien besser zu verstehen. Der Europaabgeordnete erklärte, dass er die Bedenken der Albaner teile und daher beantragt habe, dieses Thema auf die Tagesordnung der Plenarsitzung bei der nächsten Tagung des Europäischen Parlaments zu setzen, die nächste Woche in Straßburg stattfinden wird. Dieser Antrag wird derzeit noch vom Präsidium des Parlaments geprüft, doch unabhängig davon sind sie entschlossen, sich weiterhin zu diesem Thema zu äußern

…“ albanischer 

Artikel der Redaktion vom 2. Juli 2026 in Citizens

Die „Flamingo-Revolution“ zieht am 19. Tag der Proteste zum Parlament – trotz immer mehr Strafverfahren und Haftbefehlen gegen Protestierende gegen den Ausverkauf 







Albanien: Proteste gegen Trump-Resort werden immer größer – Video




„… 

Das Projekt soll in Zvernec entstehen, rund 150 Kilometer südwestlich von Tirana, in einem der letzten unberührten Küstengebiete der albanischen Adria – einem Flamingo-Brutgebiet. Demonstranten rissen am Kakomes-Strand Absperrungen nieder und riefen: „Die Strände gehören dem Volk, nicht Oligarchen.“ Die Bilder gingen viral. Was dann passierte, hat selbst erfahrene Beobachter überrascht – das Video zeigt, wie sich die Lage seitdem dramatisch zugespitzt hat. (…) Albanische Behörden haben mittlerweile Strafverfahren gegen Dutzende Protestierende eingeleitet, zuletzt gegen 27 weitere Demonstranten. Auch Haftbefehle wurden beantragt. Es begann Ende Mai mit Zusammenstößen zwischen Polizei und Demonstranten an einem Strand in Südalbanien. Was daraus geworden ist, hat selbst erfahrene Beobachter überrascht: täglich Tausende auf den Straßen von Tirana, eine Protestbewegung, die ganz Europa aufhorchen lässt: die „Flamingo-Revolution“. Albaner aus dem Ausland reisen eigens in ihre Heimat, um mitzumachen. Am vergangenen Wochenende versammelten sich so viele Menschen wie noch nie zuvor

…“ 

Bericht von Christine Novotny vom 22.06.2026 in der FR online

 

 

 samt Video




Tirana: Erneute Proteste gegen Kushner-Bauprojekt in Albanien




„… 

Wegen neuerlicher Proteste gegen ein Luxus-Bauprojekt des Trump-Schwiegersohns Jared Kushner in Albanien sind Strafverfahren gegen 27 weitere Demonstranten eingeleitet worden. Den Verdächtigen werden Verstöße gegen die öffentliche Ordnung und Sicherheit vorgeworfen, erklärte die Polizei. Aus Protest gingen am Freitagabend erneut Tausende Menschen in Tirana auf die Straße. Anfang der Woche waren bereits Strafverfahren gegen 35 Demonstranten eingeleitet worden

…“ 

APA-Meldung vom 20. Juni 2026 in derstandard.at

 

 und 

im ORF

 

 mit einigen Fotos




»Eine sehr gewaltvolle Form der Herrschaft«: Albanien wird ausverkauft, aber es regt sich Widerstand!




„… 

In Wirklichkeit sind die Proteste getragen von Gruppen und Organisationen, die seit vielen Jahren politisch aktiv sind: Menschen, denen die Regierung ihr Land gestohlen hat; Menschen aus der Hafenstadt Durrës, deren Häuser von einem US-amerikanischen Unternehmen abgerissen wurden; Bäuer*innen in Dharda, denen der Zugang zu Wasser vom Betreiber eines Wasserkraftwerks verweigert wird; feministische Gruppen; Umweltschützer*innen; Menschen mit Behinderung. Außerdem beteiligen sich viele junge Leute, was eine neue, sehr positive Entwicklung ist – »Gen Z« war in den Protesten der letzten Jahre gar nicht vertreten. (…)




Im Rahmen der Berichterstattung über den geplanten Bau eines »Eco-Resorts« mitten in einem Vogelschutzgebiet wurde festgehalten, wie ein Umweltaktivist von Mitarbeitern eines privaten Sicherheitsdiensts verprügelt wurde. Das war anscheinend der Tropfen, der das Fass zum Überlaufen brachte, und die Proteste in Tirana begannen. Unter den Vögeln, die von den Bauplänen bedroht werden, sind auch Flamingos. So bekamen die Proteste ihren Namen. Wir haben kürzlich ein Editorial publiziert, in dem wir festhalten, dass es bei den aktuellen Protesten nicht allein um die Zerstörung der Naturschutzgebiete Vjosa-Narta und Zvërnec geht, sondern um die Art, wie in Albanien allgemein regiert wird. (…)




Wir berichten seit der Gründung von »Citizens.al« über den Feminismus in Albanien, einige unserer Kolleginnen sind auch selbst in der Bewegung aktiv. Wir alle in der Redaktion teilen einen feministischen Konsens, der sich in unserer journalistischen Arbeit auf unterschiedlichen Ebenen niederschlägt. Zum einen betrachten wir sämtliche Themen, über die wir berichten, durch eine geschlechterpolitische Perspektive hindurch. Das bedeutet konkret etwa, dass wir versuchen, Stellungnahmen insbesondere von Frauen einzuholen – etwa in Hinblick darauf, was in ruralen Gegenden passiert, die weit entfernt sind von der Hauptstadt. (…)




Die Tourismusindustrie ist extrem zentralisiert, es gibt wenige lokale, kleine Anbieter*innen, stattdessen riesige Resorts und Hotels. Außerdem gibt es viele private Villen von reichen albanischen Familien, die seit Jahrzehnten die Bevölkerung Albaniens ausbeuten und nun die Küste im Süden mit hässlichen Riesengebäuden bebauen. Nachdem sie die Städte zerstört haben, wollen sie jetzt eben ein Grundstück am Meer. Hier gibt es Gegenden, wo wirklich praktisch ausschließlich reiche Albaner*innen hocken, nicht das ausländische Kapital – aber das ist noch mal ein eigenes Thema. (…)




[Wie steht es denn in Albanien um die Arbeitsbedingungen, zum Beispiel in der Bauindustrie? In Deutschland ist das ein Niedriglohnsektor, in dem die Arbeiter*innen außerdem schlecht geschützt sind.]




Zuerst einmal: Es gibt zurzeit keine Gewerkschaften in Albanien. Die, die es im Sozialismus gab, wurden in den 1990er Jahren zerstört und die Leute hatten auch kein Vertrauen in sie. Gerade wird versucht, neue Gewerkschaften aufzubauen, aber da gibt es noch sehr viel zu tun, vor allem hinsichtlich der Vertrauensbildung unter den Arbeiter*innen. Die Situation in Bezug auf Arbeitsrechte ist sehr problematisch. Zum Beispiel arbeiten die Leute in der Regel viel mehr als vertraglich festgehalten, freie Tage und Arbeitszeitbegrenzungen werden missachtet. Alle Verträge sind individualisiert, Tarifverträge existieren nicht. Ganz oft wissen die Arbeiter*innen auch einfach gar nicht, was überhaupt in ihrem Arbeitsvertrag steht. Die Regierung ist regelrecht stolz darauf, dass es keine Gewerkschaften gibt und wirbt damit gegenüber ausländischen Investoren.




[Und wie sieht es mit dem Thema Arbeitsmigration aus?]




In Albanien sind, ebenso wie in Deutschland, in manchen Bereichen hauptsächlich Arbeitsmigranten beschäftigt. Das liegt hier allerdings vor allem daran, dass die albanischen Arbeitskräfte zu so großen Zahlen ihrerseits ausgewandert sind, zumeist nach Deutschland, England und Frankreich. Sie arbeiten in der Pflege und im Gesundheitssystem der westeuropäischen Länder, während diese Jobs in Albanien von Menschen aus Indien, Pakistan, Bangladesh und den Philippinen gemacht werden. Viele dieser Leute befinden sich allerdings gewissermaßen im Transit: Sie versuchen, über Albanien in die EU zu gelangen. Diese Tatsache trägt wiederum zur Verschlechterung der Arbeitsbedingungen bei, da die Arbeitgeber häufig die Pässe dieser Menschen einbehalten, obwohl das in Albanien eine Straftat ist. (…)




Ein ganz aktuelles Ereignis in der »Zusammenarbeit« mit einem EU-Staat ist die Errichtung eines Abschiebelagers auf albanischem Boden. Das Ganze basiert auf einem Abkommen, das der albanische Premierminister Edu Rama mit der italienischen Regierung geschlossen hat. Die Menschen sollen von Schiffen auf dem Mittelmeer direkt in dieses Lager gebracht werden, was verschiedene NGO als illegal und menschenrechtswidrig einstufen. Bislang ist dieser »Gefallen gegenüber Italien« (Rama) allerdings ein ziemlicher Fehlschlag: In dem Lager, das für über eine Million Euro errichtet wurde, befinden sich derzeit sage und schreibe 25 Personen, die außerdem laut richterlichem Beschluss wieder nach Italien zurückgebracht werden müssen. Es geht hier potenziell um die Schaffung eines gefährlichen Präzedenzfalls. 




 Rama hat übrigens auch behauptet, in dieser Sache seien keinerlei Gelder nach Albanien geflossen. Aber das finden wir schwer zu glauben, denn die albanische Regierung macht wirklich niemals Politik im Interesse der Bevölkerung, sondern nutzt den Staat für ihre persönliche Bereicherung. Es kursiert die Vermutung, dass die Bereitschaft Albaniens, solche Lager einzurichten, zumindest den EU-Beitrittsprozess beschleunigen könnte. Aber aufgrund der völligen Intransparenz der Regierung können wir das bisher nur mutmaßen

.“ 

Interview von Tanja Röckemann et. al. am 17.06.2026 in ND online

 

 mit dem progressiven Nachrichtenportal »Citizens« über die »Flamingo-Revolution«. Dieser Artikel ist die redigierte Fassung eines Gesprächs mit der Redaktion von »Citizens« mit Teilnehmenden der Bildungsreise »Tirana – Einblicke in Albaniens Wandel und Widersprüche« im Rahmen von Arbeit und Leben Sachsen-Anhalt.




Am 19. Tag zieht der Protest zum Parlament.




„

Hunderte Demonstranten beschlossen heute, die Demonstrationsroute zu ändern und zum Parlament zu marschieren, wo gerade die nächste Sitzung stattfand. Während des Marsches kam es zu Zusammenstößen zwischen den Bürgern und den Abgeordneten, die gerade das Gebäude verließen.




Inmitten von Revolutionsrufen warfen sie Abgeordneten der Regierungsmehrheit wie Blendi Çuçi und Mirela Kumbaro, die gerade das Parlament verlassen hatten, Korruption vor. Der einzige Abgeordnete, der vor den protestierenden Bürgern Halt machte, war Ardit Bido. Er näherte sich der Gruppe von Bürgern, stieß jedoch auf Widerstand, als er versuchte, mit ihnen zu sprechen. Die Demonstranten begrüßten ihn mit Rufen wie „Du Dieb“, während Bido entgegnete, diese Rufe kämen „von einer Menge mit öffentlicher Grausamkeit“. Abgeordneter Bido verließ den Ort unter Anwesenheit von Polizeikräften, ohne dass Zwischenfälle verzeichnet wurden.




Anschließend zog der Protest vor das Amt des Ministerpräsidenten, wo er seit nunmehr 19 Tagen stattfindet. (…) Die Flamingoschar reagierte auf Edi Ramas Aufruf zum Dialog mit einer einfachen Antwort in „Flamingo-Sprache“: „Rama, tritt zurück

.“…“ 

albanischer Artikel von Entenela Ndrevataj vom 18. Juni 2026 in Citizens

 

 (maschinenübersetzt)




Die „Flamingo-Revolution“ und die Grenzen des Tests für „hybride Kriegsführung“




„

Der als „Flamingo-Revolution“ bekannte Bürgerprotest ist eine der bedeutendsten zivilgesellschaftlichen Mobilisierungen der letzten Jahre in Albanien. Im Mittelpunkt steht die Unzufriedenheit mit der Funktionsweise des derzeitigen politischen und wirtschaftlichen Machtsystems sowie mit der Art und Weise, wie Entscheidungen über öffentliche und natürliche Ressourcen getroffen werden. Auslöser des Protests waren Bedenken hinsichtlich Eingriffen und des geplanten Tourismusprojekts im Zusammenhang mit Jared Kushner im Naturschutzgebiet Vjosa-Narta; inzwischen hat sich die Bewegung jedoch zu einer umfassenderen politischen Forderung nach einem rechenschaftspflichtigeren, transparenteren Regierungssystem entwickelt, das dem öffentlichen Interesse dient.




Obwohl die Proteste nun bereits seit 20 Tagen andauern, wurden die Anliegen und Forderungen der Bürger inhaltlich noch nicht aufgegriffen. Premierminister Edi Rama hat sich von Anfang an dafür entschieden, die Mobilisierung vor allem in einem anderen Rahmen darzustellen: als Ergebnis einer „hybriden Kriegsführung“, böswilliger ausländischer Einflussnahme, automatisierter Konten und der Instrumentalisierung durch Akteure wie den Iran, Russland, griechischsprachige Akteure oder andere ideologische und Anti-Trump-Netzwerke. Diese Darstellung verlagert die Debatte von den Ursachen der Unzufriedenheit der Bürger hin zum vermeintlichen Ursprung der Online-Verstärkung.




Medienberichten zufolge kursiert seit Kurzem ein vertraulicher Bericht von Blackbird.AI. Der Bericht analysiert Online-Beiträge zu Jared Kushners geplantem Projekt in Zvërnec und ordnet die Analyse in einen Datensatz mit dem Titel „Kushner-Investition in Albanien“ ein. Darin werden negative Äußerungen gegen das Projekt, Akteure, die diese verstärkt haben, sowie mögliche Anzeichen für Absprachen oder verdächtiges Verhalten im Internet identifiziert. Diesen Berichten zufolge wird das Dokument privat verbreitet, wobei nicht bekannt ist, wer es in Auftrag gegeben oder finanziert hat. Es wurde von keiner albanischen Institution offiziell vorgestellt, enthält keine detaillierte öffentliche Methodik, die eine unabhängige Überprüfung ermöglicht, und wurde keinem offenen Begutachtungsverfahren unterzogen. Genau aus diesem Grund mahnt der Bericht zu einer sorgfältigen Lektüre: Was wird darin tatsächlich gemessen, was sagt er uns und was beweist er nicht? (…)




Das Dokument stellt das Thema der Analyse als eine Debatte über die mit Jared Kushner in Verbindung stehende Investition in Albanien und die „negativen Darstellungen“ rund um das Projekt dar. Diese Unterscheidung ist von entscheidender Bedeutung. „Revolucioni Flamingo“ ist eine Bürgerbewegung, deren Tragweite über die Online-Reputation eines Investitionsvorhabens hinausgeht. Sie hat Bedenken hinsichtlich gesetzlicher Änderungen in Schutzgebieten, der öffentlichen Anhörung, der Transparenz, des öffentlichen Eigentums, der Qualität der Entscheidungsfindung, der Rolle von Institutionen sowie des Verhältnisses zwischen privaten Investitionen und dem öffentlichen Interesse geäußert. Der Bericht analysiert diese Themen nicht inhaltlich; er untersucht in erster Linie die digitalen Narrative, die rund um Kushners geplantes Projekt in Zvërnec entstanden sind. (…)




Der Bericht ist aufschlussreich, da er zeigt, wie ein lokaler Protest von seinem ursprünglichen Kontext abweichen kann, sobald er in den internationalen Online-Umlauf gelangt. Die „Flamingo-Revolution“ begann mit Bedenken hinsichtlich Schutzgebieten, öffentlichem Eigentum, Transparenz und Rechenschaftspflicht. Doch die Verknüpfung des Themas mit Namen wie Trump, Kushner oder Israel führte dazu, dass der Protest auch von Akteuren und Zielgruppen außerhalb Albaniens aufgegriffen wurde, die ihn vor dem Hintergrund ihrer eigenen politischen Interessen und Konflikte interpretierten. Diese Verschiebung ist bedeutsam, da sie das Verständnis des Protests verändern kann. Eine Bürgermobilisierung für die Verwaltung öffentlicher Güter kann im Ausland als Teil politischer Kämpfe dargestellt werden, die nicht denen der albanischen Demonstranten entsprechen. Der Bericht trägt dazu bei, diese Ebene der Debatte zu beleuchten: die Art und Weise, wie das Anliegen von Akteuren verstärkt, neu formuliert und instrumentalisiert wird, die nicht die Ursache für die zivilgesellschaftliche Unzufriedenheit in Albanien waren. (…)




Eine ehrliche öffentliche Debatte muss klar zwischen drei Ebenen unterscheiden. Die erste Ebene betrifft den Inhalt des Protests: Umwelt, öffentliches Eigentum, Konsultation, Recht und Rechenschaftspflicht. Die zweite Ebene ist das Informationsumfeld: Wie verbreiten sich Narrative, wer verstärkt sie, welche Inhalte sind problematisch und wo gibt es fragwürdiges Verhalten? Die dritte Ebene ist die politische Instrumentalisierung dieses oder anderer Berichte: Wie ein vertrauliches Dokument genutzt werden kann, um eine offizielle Darstellung zum Thema „hybride Kriegsführung“ zu untermauern. Eine Vermischung dieser Ebenen sorgt für noch mehr Verwirrung und bietet der Öffentlichkeit keine Klarheit.




Die „Flamingo-Revolution“ sollte anhand der Gründe beurteilt werden, die die Bürger dazu veranlasst haben, auf die Straße zu gehen, sowie anhand der Reaktionen, die die Regierung und die politischen Akteure auf diese Gründe zeigen. Die Verbreitung im Internet kann erklären, wie ein Protest Teil der internationalen Debatte wurde. Sie erklärt jedoch nicht, warum die Bürger ihren Protest mit solcher Beharrlichkeit fortsetzen

.“ albanischer 

Artikel von Blerjana Bino vom 19. Juni 2026 in Citizens

 

 (maschinenübersetzt)










Flamingos gegen Trump. Albanien: Zehntausende demonstrieren gegen Luxusresort aus Umfeld der Familie des US-Präsidenten. Der Umweltprotest ist zur Bewegung gegen Premier Edi Rama geworden




„

Unter dem Slogan »Albanien ist nicht zu verkaufen« sind Zehntausende Albaner den sechsten Tag in Folge auf die Straße gegangen. Der Grund: der Bau eines Luxusresorts durch das US-Investmentunternehmen von Jared Kushner, Trumps Schwiegersohn und Immobilienhai. Das Projektgebiet umfasst Sazan – die größte Insel des Landes, unbewohnt und jahrzehntelang militärisches Sperrgebiet – sowie mehrere hundert Hektar des Schutzgebiets Vjosa-Narta, eines empfindlichen Küstenfeuchtgebiets mit Robben, Nistplätzen von Meeresschildkröten und Flamingos. Gerade die Flamingos sind zum Symbol des Massenprotests geworden: Demonstranten versammeln sich auf dem Skanderbeg-Platz in Tirana und ziehen mit Flamingofiguren aus Pappe zum Regierungssitz. Aus dem Aufruhr gegen den Ausverkauf des Landes ist längst eine Antiregierungsbewegung geworden – die »Flamingorevolution«

…“ 

Artikel von Fabio Nacci in der jungen Welt vom 06.06.2026

 




In Albanien brechen Proteste gegen ein riesiges Resort-Bauprojekt aus, das mit Jared Kushner in Verbindung steht




„

In Albanien nehmen die Proteste gegen den Bau eines riesigen Ferienresorts zu, das mit Jared Kushner, dem Schwiegersohn von Präsident Trump, in Verbindung steht. Bereits im Jahr 2024 wollten Kushner und Trumps Tochter Ivanka Trump 1,4 Milliarden Dollar investieren, um eine verlassene sowjetische Waffenbasis namens Sazan in ein luxuriöses Inselresort umzuwandeln. Die Insel Sazan ist übersät mit nicht explodierten Kampfmitteln aus dem Zweiten Weltkrieg, darunter Artilleriegeschosse und U-Boot-Minen. Aktivisten äußern nun Bedenken, dass das Resort Auswirkungen auf die Tierwelt haben wird, insbesondere auf die Flamingos, Robben und Meeresschildkröten, die in einem Küstenfeuchtgebiet leben. Hier spricht ein lokaler Ökologe

…“ engl. 

Interview vom 4. Juni 2026 auf Democracy Now!

 

 

 (maschinenübersetzt)




Einkaufstour auf dem Balkan: Widerstand gegen Kushners Albanien-Pläne




„

Die Präsidentschaft von Donald Trump ermöglicht seiner Familie gute Geschäfte in der ganzen Welt. Sein Schwiegersohn Jared Kushner plant derzeit erneut ein großes Immobilienprojekt auf dem Balkan. Auf einer albanischen Insel soll ein riesiges Luxusresort entstehen, doch die Bevölkerung läuft dagegen Sturm. Auch in Serbien wollte Kushner gewinnbringend bauen, das Projekt scheiterte aber krachend. (…)




Zusammenstöße auf der Baustelle




Die Einheimischen aber gehen auf die Barrikaden. „Albanien gehört den Albanern“ und „Ivanka, go home“ lauteten die Botschaften von Tausenden Demonstrierenden am Montagabend in Tirana. Seit Ende Mai nun protestieren die Menschen, die einen Ausverkauf ihres Landes an reiche Investoren aus dem Ausland befürchten, gegen das Projekt. Den Auftakt für den Widerstand markierte ein Vorfall auf dem Baugelände in Zvernec. Dort wurden mit Stacheldraht bewehrte Zäune errichtet, um Einheimischen und Touristen den Zugang zum Strand zu versperren. Kürzlich tauchten im Netz dann Videoaufnahmen auf, die zeigten, wie private Sicherheitskräfte einen Demonstranten offenbar angriffen und anschließend eine Klippe entlang zerrten, wie unter anderem Politico berichtete. Andere Demonstranten, die die Zäune entfernen wollten, wurden bedroht. Die albanischen Behörden entzogen daraufhin zwei privaten Sicherheitsfirmen die Lizenzen, und ein Wachmann wurde festgenommen und inhaftiert. Ein örtlicher Polizeichef wurde suspendiert und Anklage gegen etwa 15 Demonstranten erhoben.

..“ 

Meldung vom 03.6.2026 im ORF

 







In Albanien nehmen die Proteste gegen Kushners 4-Milliarden-Dollar-Luxusresort zu




„

Verteidigt nicht die Oligarchen, das ist das Eigentum der Bürger!“, riefen die Demonstranten.




Tausende Menschen in Albanien gingen am Dienstagabend zum vierten Mal in Folge auf die Straße, um gegen ein von Jared Kushner vorangetriebenes 4-Milliarden-Dollar-Projekt für ein Luxusresort auf Albaniens größter Insel zu protestieren. Am Samstag, dem 30. Mai, kam es in der Nähe der Baustelle zu Protesten, nachdem Bauträger Stacheldrahtzäune errichtet hatten, die den öffentlichen Zugang zum örtlichen Strand und zur Küste versperrten. Demonstranten versuchten, die Bauarbeiten zu stoppen. Nachdem private Sicherheitskräfte einen Demonstranten wegzerrten, stieg die Wut weiter an.




Auf der Baustelle riefen Demonstranten: „Verteidigt nicht die Oligarchen, das ist Eigentum der Bürger!“ Am Montag und Dienstag weiteten sich die Proteste auf die Hauptstadt Tirana aus, wo Tausende auf die Straße gingen. Die Demonstranten skandierten „Albanien gehört den Albanern“ und hielten Schilder mit Aufschriften wie „Ich will kein Albanien wie Dubai“ und „Hände weg von Vjosa-Narta“ hoch – einem Schutzgebiet an der Küste, in das das Projekt eingreifen wird.  Das Projekt soll auf Sazan, Albaniens einziger Insel im Mittelmeer, realisiert werden. Kushner, Donald Trumps Schwiegersohn, kündigte an, die Insel im Jahr 2024 in ein Ferienresort umzuwandeln. Auch seine Frau Ivanka Trump hat sich zu der Insel geäußert; sie sagte, sie und Kushner hätten die Insel während eines Urlaubs in der Gegend entdeckt. (…)




Im Januar richteten 41 Umweltorganisationen aus 28 Ländern einen Brief an den albanischen Ministerpräsidenten Edi Rama, in dem sie die „sofortige Aussetzung“ des Projekts forderten, da es „ernsthafte Risiken für die Artenvielfalt und die lebenswichtigen Lebensräume in der Region“ mit sich bringe, von denen viele von gefährdeten Arten bewohnt werden.




Rama stimmte dem Projekt zu, um die Tourismuswirtschaft des Landes anzukurbeln
