title: Group from Zurich takes over the Freedom for Öcalan Vigil in Strasbourg
content:
The Freedom for Öcalan Vigil, which was launched on 25 June 2012, in Strasbourg, has entered its 746thweek.




The vigil, which continues in Strasbourg, where institutions such as the Council of Europe and the European Court of Human Rights are located, was taken over by Barış Çetin, Cihat Kalkan and Cesur Akar from Zurich.




Speaking on behalf of the demonstrators, Barış Çetin emphasized that they were protesting the conditions of isolation imposed for nearly 28 years on Abdullah Öcalan, who was imprisoned in 1999 as a result of an international conspiracy.




“We will continue until our leader’s physical freedom is secured,” Çetin said, adding, “We also want the international community to recognize the struggle taking place here and the reality of the situation. Our comrades have demonstrated their determination for 746 consecutive weeks. Our Leader’s physical freedom is of great importance to us.”




Calling on the international community to fulfill its duties and responsibilities, Çetin stated that stability and peace in the Middle East would only be possible through the freedom of Öcalan.

author: Unknown
title: YPJ Spokesperson: Any attack on the symbols of our martyrs constitutes an attack on every woman
content:
Ruksen Mohamed, spokesperson for the Women’s Protection Units (YPJ), made a statement regarding the attack that targeted the images of fallen female fighters in Hesekê.




The statement by Ruksen Mohamed reads as follows:




“In light of the recent events in Hesekê Governorate, which have witnessed acts of vandalism and grave assaults perpetrated by individuals operating outside the law, targeting the symbols and images of our fallen female martyrs, we strongly condemn and denounce these reprehensible acts, whether through tearing down their photographs, defacing them, or insulting their memory and sacrifices.




These unethical practices constitute a flagrant assault on our collective memory and conscience, as well as a violation of the humanitarian and national values embodied by our martyrs through their immense sacrifices.




Our female martyrs are symbols of struggle, dignity, and freedom. They gave their lives in defence of the land, justice, and gender equality, and their sacrifices will remain forever enshrined in the memory of our people.




We affirm that any attack on the symbols of our martyrs constitutes an attack on every woman who has struggled for freedom and legitimate rights. Such acts represent a grave moral and national offence that cannot be justified under any pretext. Accordingly, we call upon the Syrian government, represented by the Hesekê Governorate and its Internal Security Forces, to fulfil its responsibilities by holding those responsible for these assaults accountable and taking the necessary measures to prevent their recurrence.




We further emphasise that holding the perpetrators of these assaults accountable will serve as a genuine measure of the seriousness of the integration process, as well as the commitment to safeguarding rights, respecting shared values and principles, and upholding the dignity of women and the sacrifices of our fallen female martyrs.




We reiterate that these reprehensible assaults will not deter us from continuing our struggle to defend women’s rights, dignity, and freedom, or from preserving the legacy and sacrifices of our martyrs.”

author: Unknown
title: Kongra Star holds Damascus responsible for provocations in Hesekê
content:
The Kongra Star Coordination has strongly condemned the recent attacks on Kurdish symbols and memorial portraits of fallen women in Hesekê. The women’s movement views these acts as deliberate provocations intended to fuel hostility between the Kurdish and Arab populations. It holds the Islamist transitional government in Damascus responsible for ensuring security in the city and preventing further attacks.




The statement follows an attack on an office of the Democratic Union Party (PYD) in the Xiwêran neighborhood on Tuesday. An individual entered the premises, damaged portraits of fallen women, and stole Kurdish symbols. Other memorial portraits taken from the office were subsequently desecrated in public. The perpetrator shared footage of these acts on social media. According to the ANHA news agency, the man has since been arrested by the Internal Security Forces.




Attacks target women’s struggle for freedom




Kongra Star placed the incident in the context of increasing attacks on Kurdish values, symbols, and fallen fighters since the mobilization of Arab groups from Deir ez-Zor, Raqqa, Tal Hamis, and al-Shaddadi. The women’s movement warned of attempts to divide the population along ethnic lines, saying: “Kurds, Arabs, and other communities have lived together in Hesekê for centuries. Their shared interest lies in peace and coexistence based on mutual respect, rather than renewed conflict.”




Denouncing the desecration of portraits of fallen fighters, Kongra Star stated: “This reflects a patriarchal and misogynistic attitude that attacks women’s struggle for freedom, their leadership role in society, and their political self-determination.”




The coordination recalled that the Women’s Protection Units (YPJ) played a decisive role in the fight against the Islamic State (ISIS). The women fighters, it said, drew inspiration from the ideas and resistance of the women whose memorial portraits are now being targeted. According to Kongra Star, these attacks are therefore directed not only against the achievements of the Kurdish population but also against the memory of the struggle against ISIS.




Damascus must take responsibility




Kongra Star called on the transitional government in Damascus to take concrete measures to prevent further attacks and ensure the safety of the population. These measures, it said, should include monitoring groups that have arrived in Hesekê from other regions. In particular, the incidents in the Xiwêran neighborhood must be thoroughly investigated, and those responsible must be held accountable, Kongra Star demanded.




“Accountability must not be limited to words. It must be implemented transparently and credibly to ensure public trust,” the statement said.




At the same time, the women’s movement criticized the handling of the integration process between the Autonomous Administration and the transitional government so far. It noted that the Kurdish side has approached this process sincerely and constructively, adding: “However, an integration process that fails to recognize the political will of the Kurdish population and tolerates attacks on its social values would jeopardize coexistence.”




Kongra Star called on women’s organizations, democratic forces, and the people of Rojava to jointly confront these provocations through democratic and legal means. It vowed to continue its democratic resistance and protest actions against attempts to incite hostility between Kurds and Arabs and plunge the region into another war.




In conclusion, Kongra Star called for an independent investigation into the attacks: “We hold the government in Damascus responsible for preventing the provocations that have occurred in Hesekê and any further provocations. We will not tolerate any attack targeting the coexistence of peoples.”

author: Unknown
title: Court overturns environmental approval for Birsu hydroelectric power plant in Bingöl
content:
The Administrative Court in Bingöl has overturned the environmental approval for the planned Birsu hydroelectric power plant on the Sarim River. The judges unanimously ruled that the positive environmental impact assessment (EIA) decision was unlawful. The ruling was based on an expert report that identified significant scientific and technical deficiencies in the project’s assessment.




The hydroelectric power plant, planned by the company Silvan Elektrik Üretim, is to be built on the Sarim River in the border area between the districts of Lice and Kulp in Amed (Diyarbakır) and the district of Genç in Bingöl. Villagers have been challenging the project through legal channels for several years. They fear serious consequences for the region’s water resources, biodiversity, and agricultural livelihoods.




River flow and dry periods incorrectly assessed




According to the court, the deficiencies in calculating the available water volumes are particularly serious. The river flow data used in the project are not based on measurements taken within the affected river basin. Furthermore, the average river flow was overestimated, contradicting relevant scientific findings.




Accordingly, the pronounced dry periods between June and September were not adequately taken into account in the environmental impact assessment (EIA). As a result, there is no reliable basis for determining how much water could be diverted from the river by the operation of the power plant.




According to the experts, potential impacts on the groundwater system, as well as risks associated with geological faults and blasting operations, were also not examined using appropriate calculations and models. In addition, the region’s particular topographical conditions pose further challenges. Despite the steep slopes, the environmental impact assessment does not include adequate protective measures against landslides, erosion, and avalanches.




Habitat of rare fish species under threat




The Sarim River system is of particular ecological importance. The affected area is home to the Batman loach (

Paraschistura chrysicristina

), a fish species long believed to be extinct before it was rediscovered in the region. The protected Eurasian otter also inhabits the area. According to the experts, the minimum residual water flow planned for the operation of the power plant would be insufficient to preserve aquatic habitats, particularly during the dry summer months.




Furthermore, damage to forests and ground-level vegetation could harm regional beekeeping. Honey production is an important source of livelihood for the local population. The destruction of vegetation and nectar-producing areas could significantly undermine this source of income.




The expert report also criticizes the environmental impact assessment for failing to include a comprehensive examination of the cumulative impacts on the entire river basin. As a result, the combined effects of individual interventions were not adequately assessed. The court accepted the experts’ findings and ruled that the positive environmental decision was incompatible with both legal requirements and the public interest.




Years-long legal battle over the Birsu project




The latest ruling follows several years of legal proceedings. In January 2023, the Turkish Ministry of Environment initially decided that the project did not require a comprehensive environmental impact assessment. Villagers challenged this decision in court. In March 2024, the Administrative Court in Bingöl overturned a positive environmental decision. Following further appeals by the ministry and rulings by higher courts, the case was reviewed again.




In June 2026, another on-site inspection was conducted. The expert report submitted on August 11 concluded that the project was based on insufficient scientific evidence and should not be implemented in its proposed form. It had already emerged in June that the Turkish State Hydraulic Works (DSI) had terminated the water rights agreement for Birsu after the Energy Market Regulatory Authority (EPDK) revoked the project’s preliminary license because the company had failed to fulfill its obligations.




The Environmental and Urban Law Commission of the Diyarbakır Bar Association had described this as an important victory for the years-long resistance. With the latest ruling, the project’s environmental approval has now also been overturned by the court.

title: POV : Révolution
content:
Dimanche 4 octobre 2026, un premier ministre pince-sans-rire, Lecornu, annonce en catastrophe des chantiers pour «

 

préparer les lycées aux fortes chaleurs

 

». Depuis le 1

er

, rien ne semble arrêter les incendies de murs de poubelles, les assauts contre la police de la République, les déferlements suivis de pillages dans les centres-villes, les cris de joie quand on passe le portail de la captivité comme un lion saute à travers un cercle de feu. Plutôt que de lâcher des commentaires sur le fascisme, on met les slogans à jour : «

 

La jeunesse emmerde l'éducation nationale

 

».




Quand on veut qu'il se passe quelque chose, on a une chance de comprendre ce qui se passe dans les lycées. Les percées de ces derniers jours ont témoigné d'un niveau de courage, de détermination et d'euphorie qui apparaît de fait hostile à tout désir de réconciliation avec les forces du mépris, de l'humiliation et de l'enfermement. Si les revendications ne manquaient pas sur les premiers blocus, c'est en acte, dans tous les efforts déployés, que se traduit la profondeur des aspirations. Celui qui est humilié est vengé immédiatement. Lorsqu'un chef des 

RG

, face à un lycéen, puise au ruisseau son inspiration de tortionnaire, la réponse est univoque : rapport de force inversé, chacun est libre de tirer son penalty. Comme le précise une vieille amie, «

 

un flic n'est jamais lynché gratos

 

».




Tous ceux dont la fonction ou le réflexe est de perpétuer l'enrôlement républicain sont niés, et s'ils se mettent en travers, ils seront pris comme un obstacle à affronter sur la voie de la libération. «

 

La République, c'est moi

 

», il faut le dire beaucoup moins fort. Tous les volontaires à l'Enseignement Moral et Civique s'exposent aux injures et aux coups. Ce qu'ils professent, les flics le font. On ne demande plus une hausse des moyens pour les bahuts, on fait un battle d'incendie. On ne demande plus de meilleures conditions de travail informel, on ravage la boîte. Le gouvernement tente de rétablir l'ordre avec les appareils du covid (on avait 8 ans mais on s'en souvient

 

!), les cours en ligne sont désertés, on appelle à des e-blocus et à se rejoindre dans la rue pour continuer. Par suite rigoureuse, mardi 6, même les boulevards parisiens retrouvent le grand air de l'émeute après des années empuanties. On ne prend pas les mêmes et on recommence. Oui, l'application des consignes de retenue est pour beaucoup dans ce changement d'ambiance. Mais la modération vient après une phase de répression ouvertement coloniale, où la force lycéenne est traitée comme une foule à disperser au casse-bouche. Le répresseur dit qu'il est divisé entre le père et le flic, on n'a rien à rajouter. Le rapport de force a toujours quelque chose de politique (voir le préfet de Paris de 68). Si le retrait des grenades explosives est effectif, croyez-bien que nous saurons quoi faire de cette décision qui a coûté un avant-bras à une personne de 15 ans.




On le sait bien, tenir cette vision des choses n'a rien d'une évidence et demande un combat dans la durée, qui a toujours son versant interne. Les médias n'ont pas besoin de mentir, il leur suffit de donner la parole aux trous du cul du mouvement. En attendant, jour 1, c'est panique à bord. «

 

Le mouvement des lycéens semble hors de contrôle

 

». Garder le contrôle : le cœur du propos ennemi se passe de plus amples développements. Cela témoigne du vide de ce qui règne. Cela relève aussi d'une simplification un peu rapide des enjeux. Une fois hors de contrôle, on devra aussi se mettre hors de fonctionnement, hors de valorisation, hors d'identification. Quand les «

 

citoyens en devenir

 

» commencent à devenir autre chose, c'est le flip. «

 

Casseurs

 

!

 

» «

 

Barbarie

 

!

 

». «

 

Entre des lycéens qui ont des choses à dire-de-manière-pacifique et les violences urbaines, il y a un monde

 

» (Maud Bregeon, porte-parole du gouvernement). Alors, si on n'est pas du bon côté, c'est comment

 

? Tir à vue «

 

proportionnel

 

»

 

? S'il y a encore de la place pour de si vieilles opérations de division, ce n'est pas que «

 

la violence empêche de parler du fond

 

», mais qu'on ne parle pas du fond de la violence.




Si l'on s'en tient à la vision amère-radicale du lycéen Tiktoké, embullé, sommet de l'aliénation, ce mouvement est juste impossible. On comprend d'où sort la détermination lycéenne quand on voit avec quoi elle rompt. Elle rompt avec le défaitisme et le commentaire. Elle rompt avec le mode triste.




De quoi est faite notre époque entre deux âges

 

? De questions énormes, intimidantes, qui se dressent comme des silos. Une fois entré dans un silo, la pensée est prise dans un goulot d'étranglement. Gaza, climat, patriarcat, internationale réactionnaire, guerres mondialisées, techno-valorisation, techno-contrôle. Personne ne peut nier de tels problèmes. Personne ne peut non plus en faire un usage simultané et fort. À moins de retrouver l'arme qui fait sauter les silos : la question révolutionnaire.




À ceux qui désespèrent politiquement de l'époque, on ne dit pas qu'ils «

 

ne voient que les problèmes

 

», mais qu'ils en oublient au moins un, le principal, le plus gros, le plus tabou : la révolution. Sans l'enjeu révolutionnaire, pas moyen de briser la séparation des problèmes, le découpage des luttes, leur segmentation marchande.




À mesure qu'on devient révolutionnaire, on arrive peu à peu à lire la carte politique du monde. Comme l'emplacement des plus gros problèmes est aussi celui des meilleurs instruments de gestion de population, il s'agit d'apprendre à les tourner autrement. Autrement que des guerres et des solutions qui mobilisent, autrement que des impasses vertigineuses qui immobilisent. La pensée nouvelle se déploie seulement sur la base d'une immense fermeté de caractère, élaborée avec peine ou spontanée, qui ne cède pas à «

 

l'époque

 

», c'est-à-dire l'intimidation systématique. La seule chose au fond qui intéresse les tenanciers du monde, c'est la Dissuasion. Tout ce qui s'invente, marche et transite socialement, consiste à dissuader. De quoi précisément

 

? Ils s'en foutent. C'est très exactement notre problème.




Voilà ce que lycéennes et lycéens, à leur tour, se sont mis à ignorer avec éclat. Quand on passe outre à la Dissuasion, le temps politique fait retour. On retrouve peu à peu son caractère cumulatif, à l'opposé de la pratique normale. Tout le monde le dit, notre temps est saturé par la manie du commentaire, qui nous coince dans le présentisme. Celui-ci peut bien se payer tous les historiens et les futurologues qu'il veut : l'impuissance domine. Le présent politique, c'est autre chose. Ici, rien ne se perd tout à fait. La radicalité immédiate des 11 heures-Nation de 2016, le choix du terrain chez les 

GJ

 (2018-19), les feux de poubelles dans les manifs sauvages de 2023, choses qui se sont fait démonter en leur temps, les blocus de 2026 les «

 

remontent

 

» autrement. Après les émeutes pour Nahel les blocus ne reviennent pas à vide, mais chargés. Quand on renoue avec ce rapport cumulatif au temps, on reprend le chemin de la victoire. L'autre côté de l'impasse n'a rien d'un sens unique, tant ces rapports secrets entre les gestes font l'objet d'attaques constantes de la part de l'ennemi, des faux amis, des milices du déni.




Il s'agit d'en tirer toutes les conséquences. Finis les «

 

ouin-ouin le fascisme arrive

 

», arrêtez d'attendre après les élections, c'est maintenant 7 octobre 2026 qu'il faut tout arrêter pour se battre. Là où les questions ne sont pas séparées. Là où les gestes ne tombent jamais tout à fait dans le vide. Là où le souhait d'avoir la même vie que les parents n'est pas seulement une réalité rendue impossible, mais quelque chose dont on se délivre avec joie.




https://povcestlarevolution.wordpress.com/

title: Asociația Techsoup: Reclaiming Agency in the Age of AI

author: Monthly Review Press
title: New! “Grand Theft Capital”, by Fred Magdoff and John Bellamy Foster
content:
A 

New York Times

 headline in early 2026 announced what many workers have known for years: “For Many Cash-Strapped Americans, ‘Basic Living has become a Burden.’” Living paycheck-to-paycheck, with little or no savings for emergencies, workers are struggling to make ends meet. It should come as no surprise that, without a clear sense of the problem’s source, workers are left blaming easy targets: immigrants, people of color, religious minorities, or damaging decisions by a few, corporate bad apples.










But as 

Grand Theft Capital 

demonstrates, workers’ current conditions are the result of a deliberate, long-term effort by the corporate rich to increase their own wealth largely by extracting it from workers’ pockets. The evidence shows that workers’ wages have not kept pace with rising costs and that they’re feeling unhappy and stressed on the job. This partly reflects the weakening of worker power as union membership has declined over the past sixty years—reaching levels last seen before the major unionization wave of the 1930s. Regardless of what mainstream economists and the Consumer Price Index suggest, successive generations of young workers have been confronting difficult and precarious employment conditions. On top of it all, workers of all generations are alarmed at the possibility of job obsolescence given the looming threat of AI and automation.




In the face of this evidence, 

Grand Theft Capital

 offers a clear answer to the source of the problem and charts a clear way forward. What workers are facing is nothing less than a class war waged from above; the only solution is an equally determined class war from below.




Your copy is 

here







The post 

New! “Grand Theft Capital”, by Fred Magdoff and John Bellamy Foster

 appeared first on 

Monthly Review

author: Sharon Zhang
title: Trump Admin Killed Insider Trading Referral Probing Iran War-Related Oil Sales
content:
The incident raises alarm over officials’ moves to insulate insiders from anti-corruption enforcement.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

A Trump administration official intervened against an insider trading investigation into suspiciously timed oil sales made just minutes before a critical announcement by President Donald Trump related to the Iran war this March, new reporting finds.

Analysts within the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), the federal government’s regulator against abuses in derivatives markets, had made a referral to the agency’s Division of Enforcement on a series of advantageous large-volume trades made on March 23, Bloomberg reported this week.

These trades were highly profitable. That day, Trump announced that he was backing off, for now, on his threats to strike Iranian power plants — a move that would drastically escalate the war and undoubtedly cause Iran to double down on their closure of the Strait of Hormuz. Just 15 minutes before Trump’s announcement, traders made billions of dollars’ worth of transactions predicting that oil would fall and the S&P 500 would rise. These bets paid off nearly immediately.

CFTC workers in the Division of Enforcement are typically responsible for determining whether the agency would launch a full insider trading investigation that could potentially lead to an enforcement action. But, breaking with precedent, an official within the agency told the Division of Market Oversight to retract the referral. Instead, the official — Mel Gunewardena, a top adviser for Trump-appointed CFTC chair Michael Selig — said that further investigation into the incident would be done under his purview.

The incident, reported by Bloomberg on Wednesday, raises concerns about Trump administration insiders using non-public knowledge to make trades related to the Iran war. It also raises questions about whether the administration is installing Trump-friendly figures within agency watchdog roles in order to grant impunity for illegal activities like insider trading.

The trades were among a few of numerous well-timed trades made in March and April that agency officials have flagged, with a particular focus on the March 23 transactions. Analysts scrutinized those trades in particular because, in just two minutes, traders sold 8.5 times the volume of oil that had been traded in the same time over the prior week.

The forensic analysts are still looking into the trades, but they are siloed off from the rest of the agency as a result of Gunewardena’s intervention, Bloomberg found; the supervisor who Gunewardena ordered to retract the referral left the agency, and other members of that team resigned or were reassigned. Instead, Gunewardena “assembled his own team to conduct a new analysis of the trading,” the publication found.

The incident is another instance of the Trump administration’s interference in the CFTC’s regulatory role. The agency only carried out 13 enforcement actions in fiscal year 2025 — a major decline from 58 actions in 2024 and 96 in 2023.

author: Brian Bienkowski
title: Report Finds “Forever Chemicals” Pollute 83 Percent of 1,602 US Waterways Tested
content:
“If anything, the report dramatically understates the problem,” said a co-chair of the Great Lakes PFAS Action Network.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

If you swam, fished or paddled a lake or river in the US over the past couple of years, there’s a more than 80% chance the water contained toxic “forever chemicals,” according to a new report.

The report, published today by Environment America Research & Policy Center, found hotspots for the toxics, including the Mississippi River and Lake Ontario, and warns that this widespread pollution is likely “just the tip of the iceberg,” as it represents only a sampling of US waterways tested for per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS).

“The report underscores what is really a much bigger problem than what most people realize,” said Tony Spaniola, co-chair of the Great Lakes PFAS Action Network. “If anything, the report dramatically understates the problem.”

The findings come as the Trump administration rolls back policies aimed at reducing PFAS in drinking water. Critics say such moves will only worsen people’s exposure to the chemicals, which are linked to some cancers, high cholesterol, decreased immune response to vaccines, liver damage, thyroid problems, reproductive issues and other health issues.

In the new report, researchers analyzed federal, state and non-profit data collected between 2022 and 2024 and found that PFAS were detected at 83% of the 1,602 US lakes, rivers and streams that were tested. There were over 114 different types of PFAS found across the waterways.

Surface water monitoring varies across the country, said John Rumpler, report co-author and the clean water director and senior attorney at the Environment America Research & Policy Center. PFAS pollution was ubiquitous in lakes and rivers that had a lot of monitoring. For example, PFAS was detected at all 39 monitoring locations on the Mississippi River in Minnesota and Wisconsin, and at all monitoring locations on and around Lake Ontario.

There were also huge PFAS spikes in some locations, with the highest levels recorded in Brunswick, Maine, near an executive airport that suffered a PFAS firefighting foam spill in 2024. State testing found a nearby surface water retention pond had PFOS — a particularly toxic type of PFAS — at 1,040,000 parts per trillion. The US Environmental Protection Agency’s (EPA) current maximum level allowed in drinking water is just 4 parts per trillion.

The report builds on several previous reports that have looked at PFAS in drinking water. For example, an Environmental Working Group (EWG) analysis from March found that roughly 176 million people in the US drink PFAS-polluted tap water.

However, it is important to also look at surface water alone, Rumpler said.

“For one, many communities draw their drinking water from surface waters,” he said, adding that even if state or federal policies reduced PFAS in drinking water this report shows “we are still stuck with these highly toxic chemicals in our rivers, lakes and streams.”

“And it’s there that they contaminate the fish that we eat and other wildlife,” he said.

Spaniola echoed the concerns of PFAS buildup in fish. He became involved in PFAS advocacy after learning his family’s home in Oscoda, Michigan, was in the epicenter of one of the country’s first major PFAS contamination sites due to military use of PFAS-firefighting foam for decades at the nearby Wurtsmith Air Force Base. In 2012, Oscoda put in place the first fish consumption advisory in the nation for PFAS contamination.

“The fish take in the water and PFAS, the PFAS biomagnifies within their bodies,” Spaniola said, adding that the community is “defined by water.”

“In 2016 I received notice of the contamination. I thought: if my water is not safe to drink today, it hasn’t been safe to drink for a long time,” he said. “You realize how much of a role water plays in your life every day.”

The report comes as the Trump administration has weakened or rolled back several protections meant to prevent PFAS water pollution.

The Biden administration previously set limits six types of PFAS — PFOA, PFOS, GenX, PFBS, PFNA and PFHxS — which have been linked to a variety of health harms, including cancer, heart problems and birth defects. The drinking water limits were considered landmark regulations after years of research and testing found PFAS chemicals are widespread in Americans’ drinking water.

But in May, The Trump administration proposed to rescind the limits for GenX, PFBS, PFNA and PFHxS, alleging that the Biden administration failed to follow the requirements of the Safe Drinking Water Act by not allowing for proper public comment. The EPA will leave in place the limits for PFOA and PFOS, chemicals known to be particularly harmful.

The administration has also approved three pesticides that health advocates say fit the definition of a PFAS, and scrapped a scientific review of PFAS-contaminated sewage sludge that is often spread on farm fields as fertilizer.

Rumpler said “federal drinking water standards are, of course, essential, but they are not enough.”

“We need to turn off the toxic tap,” he said. “We need to stop using these forever chemicals.”

In the meantime, he said, he hopes the reports prompts policymakers to take concrete steps such as bolstering Clean Water Act permits to require filtering out PFAS chemicals before they are discharged to a waterway, and banning the application of sewage sludge that contains PFAS.

“All of these things can dramatically reduce the flow of these chemicals into our environment,” he said.

author: David Venn
title: QIA funds $15M wellness centre in Igloolik
content:
A wellness centre planned for Igloolik’s core will be a positive addition to the community, says a hamlet leader.




Last week, the Qikiqtani Inuit Association announced $15 million for the Saviruut Building, which will house hamlet wellness initiatives and a federally funded early childhood development program.




“It’s good to see that we’re getting more infrastructure, because the need is there,” senior administrative officer John Ivey said in an interview with Nunatsiaq News.




The hamlet asked QIA to fund a wellness centre a few years before Ivey joined its administration.




The regional organization, responsible for just over 51 per cent of Nunavut’s Inuit population, allocated the money from its Indigenous Community Infrastructure Fund.




QIA selected Arctic Fresh Projects Inc. as the contractor and expects materials to ship to the hamlet next year, said a news release issued last week by the Inuit organization.




Once built, the facility will support “initiatives that promote healing and the transfer of Inuit traditional knowledge and worldview to future generations,” said QIA spokesperson Markoosie Qaunirq.
















It will also be home to the Aboriginal Head Start early childhood program, to which the Public Health Agency of Canada provided $3.2 million.




Ivey said he’s unsure when Arctic Fresh plans to complete the building.




“The blueprints are very, very impressive,” he added.

author: Publicación Abierta
title: 12 de octubre: la conquista remata ahora la vida
content:
12 DE OCTUBRE: LA CONQUISTA REMATA AHORA LA VIDA




Por Rafael Bautista S.







La colonización ahora se propone 




aniquilar al mundo entero, pues si no todos somos iguales, 




la rebelión de las víctimas es el pecado 




que hay que escarmentar, 




porque dice Occidente: “toda la culpa la tienen las víctimas. 




El verdugo es siempre inocente”.




Para los fines de la conquista, fue preciso, necesario y estratégico cercenar las memorias y ceremonias antiguas de los indios, porque en esos residuos de resistencia se reproducía su modo de vivir. La inversión religiosa la describe muy ben Guaman Poma de Ayala cuando señala que “les quitaron su ley antigua y les pusieron temor y culpa donde antes había justicia”. Para arrebatarles y despojarles de humanidad, no bastaba con reducirlos a la miseria sino acabar con su memoria y sus costumbres, con su historia y su cultura.




Pero lo que las armas habían pretendido terminar, sólo logró su aplazamiento, pues la memoria comenzó a renacer, una y otra vez que la amenaza del exterminio prendía sus terruños, pero también su rebeldía. Las armas jamás pudieron doblegar el espíritu de liberación que atravesó, hasta el día de hoy, todas las formas que adquirió la dominación, el despojo y el robo de su tierra sagrada.




Hoy la liberación se expresa como 

restauración

. El “progresismo” no entiende que el progreso es un mito, que la alternativa ya no es aferrarse al tren del progreso sino ponerle un freno y proponerse, con mayor denuedo, despertar y 

conservar

 los valores que la tradición de nuestros pueblos nos ha legado, frente al desastre y el desmoronamiento de los valores moderno-occidentales. Pero 

restaurar

 no es volver sino 

recrear

, 

actualizar

 lo que hemos perdido: una existencia más digna, libre y justa, re-ligada a lo natural y espiritual, a la simpleza que significa vivir en plenitud; lejos del dinamismo, ritmo y la inclemencia del tiempo inhumano del capital y el mercado (una vida válida para todos, donde ya no gobierne la ambición de unos cuantos).




En el siglo XV, el Abya Yala estaba atravesando una época de esplendor civilizatorio, superior, en muchos casos, a la Cristiandad latino-occidental (porque Europa recién se estaba reconociendo como nueva entidad ontológica y geopolítica). En realidad, en 1492, 

quien se descubre no es América sino Europa

 y lo hace no a partir del “encuentro” con el otro sino negando su humanidad, para afirmarse como superioridad absoluta, una vez que ha diezmado la capacidad de resistencia de los pueblos dominados. El Abya Yala no fue reducida civilizatoriamente por vivir en el atraso histórico, en la barbarie (que es una pura leyenda negra que está siendo desmentida, cada día, por los nuevos hallazgos y argumentos antropológicos, arqueológicos, demográficos, tecnológicos, etc., etc.).




No nos vencieron por astucia, inteligencia o superioridad sino por una incompatibilidad radical. La 

cultura de la vida

 (en todas sus expresiones) respeta los límites éticos que manifiesta la idea del bien. Una cultura de muerte, basada en la culpa infinita, el sacrificio, la aniquilación del 

humanismo del otro hombre

, no admite límite alguno. Como en la actualidad, cuando el Imperio y Occidente, en su decadencia, desatan la política del odio, desatan un poder sin límites. Salah ad-Dîn o Saladino lo expresaba así, refriéndose a los cruzados cristianos: es casi inhumano luchar contra ejércitos tan hambrientos de sangre y muerte. Si el monje Bernardo de Claraval estimulaba a los cruzados con el perdón de los pecados y el paraíso eterno, por cada moro que se aniquile, se comprende la crueldad que despierta el odio al “infiel”. Como hoy en Gaza, el Imperio y Europa jamás abandonaron esa brutalidad sin coordenadas morales. Los pueblos expulsados a ser periferia del “primer mundo”, fuera de las fronteras del 

humanismo liberal-moderno excluyente y selectivo

, aun cargan con la interrogante: ¿cómo puede ser posible vivir en un mundo sin respeto por la vida?




Occidente nunca fue superior. Su moralidad los retrata en la figura de aquél que afirma que “lo único que puede detenerme es 

Mi propia moral

, 

Mi propio pensamiento

. 

No necesito

 del derecho internacional”, Trump dixit. Occidente es el nicho de la tradición imperial, que siempre debe retornar, como dice Dostoievsky, al lugar del crimen. Es su condena y, por eso mismo, debe acallar a los vencidos, para dejar de escuchar el clamor de los muertos que deja su progreso y desarrollo.




La invasión y la conquista venció un continente lleno de pueblos, culturas y recursos que hicieron posible que Europa financie la administración de su centralidad mundial. Pretendieron destruir todo pero, para generar la acumulación pre-originaria del capital, la conquista y la invasión de la subjetividad de los dominados hizo posible la justificación de un mundo basado en la desigualdad, la exclusión y la injusticia. La “extirpación de las idolatrías” significó dejar al indio sin alma, sin ningún resguardo espiritual desde el cual sea posible reconstruir su mundo y su vida y existir sin identidad, ni tradición, ni historia ni futuro y, hoy en día, es lo que se propone el evangelismo sionista. Primero fue el miedo, luego el terror, el infierno desatado como maldición, según fines estratégico-militares, como el dotar a los nativos de mantas contaminadas con viruela, que fue una práctica frecuente, tanto por militares ingleses como por holandeses; así sucedió en Fort Pitt en 1764, diezmando pueblos enteros con la diseminación de la viruela, bajo órdenes del comandante en jefe de las fuerzas británicas, Jeffrey Ahmerst.




El comercio desigual e impuesto a la fuerza a los nativos, hizo posible la generación de una economía basada en un “libre mercado” para los vencedores, pero injusto para aquellos, que eran víctimas, de lo que se llamó después “ventajas comparativas”; que no es más que la legitimación jurídica del despojo y el saqueo de aquellos no admitidos en las fronteras de los humano; así como la traición se hizo sistema pragmático, así también el despojo y el robo, la explotación y la dominación del trabajo humano y la naturaleza, originaron una economía liberal, que hacía aparecer los intereses particulares como interés general, cuya “acción racional” definía que los fines se traduzcan en beneficios, sin importar los medios adoptados.




La oposición no se expresó en los términos superior-inferior. Ni siquiera hubo superioridad militar (sólo la ausencia de humanidad, ética y respeto al vencido, podría considerar a la guerra biológica de superior). El conquistador cargaba, en su subjetividad, siglos de violencia. El 2 de enero de 1492 se terminaba la engañosa “reconquista”, permitiendo a los reyes Isabel de Castilla y Fernando de Aragón, expandir el Imperio cristiano al sur y expulsar al sultán Boabdil y los moros en la rendición de Granada y, con ello, dar fin a Al-Ándalus y generar las condiciones de la creación del Reino de España. La cristiandad por vez primera podía expandirse más allá del enclaustramiento civilizatorio en el que se encontraba y lo hacía por la Mar Océano, para llegar a las Indias e integrarse al mundo que, hasta ese entonces, siempre fue oriental.




Las Cruzadas tampoco fueron episódicas, sino que fueron constitutivas de la pretensión expansiva de la Cristiandad imperial (encerrada por el cerco otomano, hasta 1571, cuando el poderío naval español, financiado por la plata del Potosí y Zacatecas, vence a la flota otomana, en la batalla de Lepanto), que encontró en la invasión al Abya Yala, las posibilidades empíricas de su finalismo universalista. En ese sentido, la dominación imperial (más aun cuando posee el argumento de salvación universal y se coloca a sí mismo como el ejecutor de ese propósito) tiene carácter exponencial y su política está diseñada como “legítima dominación”. Por eso ningún recurso le es suficiente y puede llevar, hasta sus últimas consecuencias, sus pretensiones ontológicas: el ser es, el no-ser 

no es

, ergo, 

no debe ser

. La cultura de la vida es incompatible con esta pretensión unilateral, exclusivista y excluyente.




Dos formas de humanidad estaban enfrentadas, pero sólo una estaba dispuesta a la aniquilación total y absoluta. Sólo una podía proponerse negar toda la vida, destruirla, sin el más mínimo respeto, para cumplir sus propósitos estratégico-instrumentales. Inevitablemente iba a vencer, teniendo además el control de los medios de vida de los otros. La afirmación del proyecto moderno pasaba y sigue pasando por la negación y el aniquilamiento de toda otra forma de vida, de toda otra alternativa. Una vez impuesta la modernidad como la sociedad del bienestar y el progreso (ocultando siempre los desastres que ocasiona aquello, en la condición humana y la capacidad reproductiva de la naturaleza) puede afirmarse, como una fatalidad del destino, su invariable curso histórico.




Todos los mártires por la liberación de nuestros pueblos, desde 1492, alzan su voz, no por una melancólica súplica por un pasado cancelado sino por un reclamo universal que desnuda a Occidente y su moderna pretensión imperial que, desde Washington, amenaza al mundo al MAD (mutual assure destruction): ¿qué tipo de humanidad es capaz de aceptar un mundo basado en la aniquilación del otro como principio de vida, un concepto del derecho que legitima el robo y el saqueo a nivel global, una racionalidad económica que hace principio de vida la competencia salvaje, que hace de la salud un negocio, de la alimentación un nicho de enfermedades? ¿Qué mundo es aquel que su política admite como “racionales” el traicionar, mentir, saquear y borrar la existencia del que discrepa? ¿Qué de “racional” tiene la aniquilación del otro para existir?




Es por reiteración pedagógica y disciplinamiento cultural que la modernidad se mantenga en pleno desmoronamiento global. Las elites locales y su base de reclutamiento, la clase media, se constituyen ahora en los agentes aduaneros de vigilancia de un mundo que ya no admite la inclusión. El nuevo orden global ya no es para todos. Nunca lo fue. Pero la mentalidad colonizada y la consciencia periférico-satelital de la sociedad aun cree que puede ser parte beneficiada del nuevo orden postindustrial, transhumanista y dominado por la IA. No en vano la sabiduría de nuestros ancestros se preservó hasta ahora. La resistencia popular debe limpiar ese olvido y entre las capas de encubrimiento de cinco siglos, debemos ahora cosechar la savia subterránea que nos legaron. Ya no se trata de un pueblo sino de toda la humanidad que se encuentra confinada en el mito de la caverna.




En 1492, comenzó la invasión ordenando “por la santa corona imperial y su brazo armado, que aceptéis al único Dios del amor, para tu propio beneficio; porque es 

por derecho natural

 que el indio obedezca a su señor, la mujer a su marido, lo bruto a lo humano, la miseria a la riqueza, lo peor a lo mejor, para el bien de todos. Y si no lo hiciereis, te haré la guerra como jamás te hubieses imaginado, sembraré tus campos con miseria, tus cielos con llanto, tus noches con miedo y tus sueños con pesadillas eternas”.




Después vino el genocidio que no ha cesado hasta el día de hoy, en todas las latitudes: “El infierno que te imponemos es por tu propio bien, para que ya no oses igualarte a quienes debes obediencia. Porque nuestro Dios nos ha creado para mandar y a ustedes para servirnos. La democracia sólo puede ser la sumisión absoluta a nuestro derecho divino, que nos ha concedido todo, hasta robar, que nos ha permitido todo, hasta matar. Ni la justicia ni la injusticia te corresponde, ni el bien ni el mal. Porque nuestro orden divino y su moneda predilecta, el dólar, nos ha hecho a nosotros para ser libres y a ustedes para ser nuestros esclavos”.




Ahora en pleno 2026, cuando Sudamérica ya se encuentra en remate, el fascismo ha tomado de rehén a la misma democracia que dice defender y ha desatado la política de odio, como último recurso de restauración imperial: “Y haré libres a mis 

cruzados

 y les daré, de nuevo, licencia de matar, para desalmarlos y extirparles todo resto de humanidad. Y en donde florezca la desobediencia a mis mandatos divinos, sembraré infinitas Gazas, con fuego, dolor y sangre. Y te extirparé tus idolatrías y salvaré tu alma para que te inclines, para siempre, al único Dios de este mundo, al cual serás sacrificado para recibir el perdón de tus iniquidades, del pretender un mundo entre iguales”.




La Paz, Chuquiago Marka, 12 de octubre de 2026




Rafael Bautista S., autor de:




El ángel de la historia. vol. II




La disputa del arco sudamericano 




y la geopolítica del reinicio global. 

2024




Dirige “el taller de la descolonización”

author: Amy Goodman
title: Israeli Forces Raid Palestinian NGOs in the West Bank Ahead of Israeli Elections
content:
The raids come four years after the forced closure of multiple NGOs that Israel designated as “terrorist” organizations.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

Israeli forces have raided what they say are the offices of several Palestinian NGOs in the occupied West Bank. Palestinian officials say a child was injured from Israeli gunfire, while others suffered from tear gas inhalation. At least one journalist was reportedly detained in the raids, which come four years after the forced closure of multiple NGOs that the Israeli government designated as “terrorist” organizations.

“This is part of the whole propaganda show that this government is actually implementing just before the Israeli election,” says human rights lawyer Sahar Francis. “They just wanted to cause harassment, and this is the main message: the persecution and the collective punishment for the whole Palestinian community.” Francis was formerly the general director at Addameer Prisoner Support and Human Rights Association, one of the organizations that Israel claims to have raided this week despite the fact that it was already forced to close its West Bank offices in 2022.

This is a rush transcript. Copy may not be in its final form.

AMY GOODMAN: This is Democracy Now!, democracynow.org. I’m Amy Goodman.

In the latest crackdown on human rights defenders in the occupied West Bank Tuesday, Israeli forces raided what they say are the offices of several Palestinian NGOs, confiscating legal files, court records, valuable equipment. Israeli forces also deployed snipers around the entrances to Ramallah’s Palestine Medical Complex, the largest government medical facility in the occupied West Bank. At least one journalist was reportedly detained. Palestinian officials say a child was injured from Israeli gunfire; others suffered from tear gas inhalation.

For more in these last few minutes, we go to Ramallah, where we’re joined by Sahar Francis, human rights lawyer, previous general director at Addameer Prisoner Support and Human Rights Association, which is one of the groups that Israel just raided.

Sahar Francis, welcome back to Democracy Now! We had you on when you were the head of Addameer, which is the prisoner support and human rights group in the West Bank. I was watching overnight when Israel was raiding, because Al Jazeera was showing the raid live. But these offices, in fact, of your group, your previous group, Addameer, and others, the Palestine Women’s Association, were already closed — is that right? — years ago, because the Israeli government classified these organizations as terrorist. So, what were they raiding?

SAHAR FRANCIS: Exactly. Good afternoon, and thanks for inviting me again to join you in this important discussion.

As you just said, these offices actually were raided in 2020. We were, too, forced closure after the decision to designate the six Palestinian organizations as terrorist organizations. They confiscated property and stole files and equipments at that time.

So, what happened yesterday, I would claim that this is part of the whole propaganda show that this government is actually implementing just before the Israeli election, couple of weeks before the Israeli election, to send a very clear message to the whole Palestinian society, and especially to the Palestinian Authority, because the offices they raided is very close to the official governmental offices and other ministries in Ramallah city, that “We are the masters. We decide what we will do. You cannot interfere. You cannot protect nothing to do with your sovereignty in even Ramallah city, that is supposed to be an Area A.”

And what happened yesterday, they were not confiscating property for illegal organization, claiming that this property is used to support terrorism. And I’m sure you all saw in the videos that were presented by the different media, local or international, that they mostly broke and destroyed the files and the equipment, even the windows. The refrigerator in this office that they claimed it belongs for Addameer, they were throwing it from the second floor down to the ground. They just wanted to cause harassment, and this is the main message: the persecution and the collective punishment for the whole Palestinian community. The raid onto the city center Ramallah is not a lonely activity. It happens every day that they raid different villages, different cities. They arrest people, including journalists and human rights defenders.

And what’s most important to highlight in our case, that the office they raided yesterday, claiming that it’s for Addameer, basically it’s a legal office led by lawyers who are representing Palestinian prisoners, which means if you claim that this is illegal or a terrorist action, this means, at the end, that the legal representation for the Palestinian prisoners in front of the Israeli military courts is considered a terror act. Seriously? This is the message that they wanted to highlight. Actually, this is very, like, bizarre and disgraceful, I think, even for their image. And the other organization they claim that they raided, this organization was closed back in 2022. Since then, it doesn’t exist there at all, not even as —

AMY GOODMAN: Sahar, we only have 30 seconds, but I want to ask what message you think Israel is sending, at the same time the U.S. is sanctioning the International Criminal Court, overall, as an institution.

SAHAR FRANCIS: That we don’t respect the international law, we are not respecting the treaties and the institutions that implement and protect international human rights law, and we don’t care, because we are not accountable. And this is the time for sanctions.

AMY GOODMAN: I want to thank you so much for being with us, Sahar Francis, human rights lawyer, previous general director of Addameer Prisoner Support and Human Rights Association, speaking to us from occupied Ramallah.

That does it for our show today. A very happy birthday to my favorite news hound, Zazu! I wish her a happy birthday, as well as her brother Kasha as they turn 6 years old today.

Oh, and this news: Steal This Story, the documentary about Democracy Now!, is viewable online for the first time. If you live in the U.S. and Canada, you can watch the film in your own home. We did it live last night with a post-screening Q&A with me and the Oscar-nominated filmmakers Carl Deal and Tia Lessin, moderated by Pulitzer Prize-winning journalist Maria Hinojosa. Well, it’s now there at Eventive. You can get information about it at StealThisStory.org. I’ll be in Woodstock at 2:00 on Friday. Check our website at democracynow.org, at the Woodstock International Film Festival, and beyond. I’m Amy Goodman.

author: Stephen Prager
title: Mike Rogers’s Wealth Soared as His Wife’s Firm Won Billion-Dollar Contracts
content:
Despite concerns about conflicts of interest, Rogers was named chair of the House Intelligence Committee.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

Former US Rep. Mike Rogers, the Republican Senate candidate in Michigan, saw his personal wealth soar after he was named chair of the House Intelligence Committee in 2011, thanks in large part to his marriage to the CEO of a powerful military contracting firm.

Financial disclosures reviewed by Drop Site News as part of an investigation published Tuesday show that Rogers had just $4,000-$60,000 worth of investment holdings in fiscal year 2008 after he divorced his first wife of 17 years.

But that all began to change in 2010, when he married Kristi Clemens, a senior executive for the British-founded private security contractor Aegis, which has a major US subsidiary that she helped to establish.

Mike Rogers did what? This is pretty crazy even by DC standards https://t.co/OJhYJuyf4j

During the 2000s, the company won multiple Pentagon contracts worth hundreds of millions of dollars to support US military operations in Iraq, where it was put in charge of coordinating other private contractors.

Less than a year after his marriage, Rogers was named chair of the House Intelligence Committee — one of the nation’s most powerful oversight posts, which gave him access to highly classified intelligence.

Within seven months — despite concerns about conflicts of interest — Aegis was awarded a contract worth more than $1 billion to protect the US embassy in Kabul, Afghanistan. In a since-deleted online biography for a law firm she joined after leaving Aegis, Kristi took credit for leading a “two-year pursuit and capture strategy” to secure the contract.

In the meantime, Rogers’ financial assets — now merged with Kristi’s — grew substantially. Up from between $136,000 and $391,000 during the first year of their marriage, the pair now held anywhere from $230,000 to $925,000 three years later.

Rogers’ potential conflicts of interest became a subject of scrutiny even among fellow Republicans, who accused him of slow-walking an investigation into the killing of four Americans at a US compound in Benghazi, Libya.

Aegis had been heavily active in Libya since 2011, when NATO launched its operation to overthrow President Muammar Gaddafi, which plunged the country into civil war in the following years.

Rogers’ handling of the Benghazi investigation would later draw a scathing rebuke from longtime right-wing operative Dick Morris, who accused him of “obstructing and delaying the Benghazi investigation in order to shield his wife, Kristi, from scrutiny.”

Amid this controversy, Rogers announced that he would not run for reelection. In 2015, after serving 14 years in Congress, he returned to the private sector.

Rogers went on to profit from the national security and surveillance industries he’d helped to oversee — taking board positions with military contractors and cybersecurity firms.

According to Business Insider, financial disclosures showed he received nearly $2 million in payments from technology and cybersecurity companies between January 2022 and late 2023.

When he left Congress in 2015, Mike and Kristi Rogers’ combined net worth was about $1.7 million. As of 2026, it is estimated to have climbed to between $7 million and $14 million.

Dr. Abdul El-Sayed blasts Mike Rogers: “He hasn't been serious about providing healthcare his entire career. What he has been serious about is monetizing his time in office.” $14 MILLION, two yachts, and a Florida McMansion. That's quite a payday! pic.twitter.com/X6XCsjaeKX

Rogers is currently in the midst of a battle to reenter Congress as Michigan’s US senator, in a close race that could decide whether Democrats retake the chamber next month.

His Democratic opponent, Abdul El-Sayed — a former Detroit public health official — has run as a staunch opponent of President Donald Trump’s aggressive wars abroad, including in Iran, and his support for Israel’s assaults on Gaza and Lebanon, which Rogers has backed.

With less than a month before polls close on November 3, El-Sayed has hammered on Rogers’ support for legislation that expanded government spying powers in the wake of the 9/11 attacks. He’s also zeroed in on the Republican’s lucrative personal ties to the military-industrial complex.

“[Rogers] hasn’t been serious about providing healthcare his entire career,” El-Sayed said during last week’s contentious Senate debate. “What he has been serious about is making sure that he can monetize his time in public office — $14 million, two yachts, a McMansion in Florida.”

El-Sayed highlighted Drop Site’s findings in a social media post Tuesday: “STUNNING, [Mike Rogers’] deep state grift includes massive contracts for his wife’s firm,” he said.

A spokesperson for Rogers said on Wednesday that “the accusation that Mike used his position in Congress to protect his family in any way, shape, or form is patently false.”

author: Mada Masr
title: Protests at several prisons, detainee ‘banishments’ surround delay to Criminal Procedure Code
content:
A wave of protests has swept through several prisons over the last three weeks, as prisoners who were hopeful that the new Criminal Procedure Code would bring an end to their prolonged remand detention had their hopes dashed at the eleventh hour when the law’s implementation was postponed, according to several lawyers acting in defense of detainees held at different prisons who spoke separately to Mada Masr over the same time period.




The postponement pushed back what many detainees saw as a window of opportunity for authorities to release dozens of them held in remand after the law’s awaited implementation on October 1.




With that window now firmly shut until October 2027, a wave of demonstrations in detention centers has been met by security forces with measures that the lawyers say include the punitive transfer of detainees to prisons farther away from their families, a practice known as “

taghreeb”

 (banishment).




As cries and claims about the demonstrations and the security forces’ response made their way to social media, the Interior Ministry issued repeated denials that protests and abuses are taking place within prisons, most recently in an October 2 

statement

. The Public Prosecution, meanwhile, was yet to issue a statement regarding the claims at the time of publishing.




The state’s National Council for Human Rights (NCHR) intends to pay visits to a number of prisons about which it has received complaints, the council’s deputy head, Mohamed Anwar al-Sadat, tells Mada Masr. Sadat adds, however, that the council has received “assurances” from the prosecution and the Interior Ministry that conditions inside prisons are “normal.”




But lawyers and human right defenders, who continue to hear from concerned families and document the incidents, have raised calls for an independent investigation into possible violations against detainees.




***




Among those subjected to “banishment,” is journalist and researcher Ismail al-Eskandarany, according to human rights lawyer Mahienour al-Massry.




Massry received information on October 1 that Eskandarany, whom she represents, and other detainees had been transferred from the 10th of Ramadan Correctional and Rehabilitation Center “violently, resulting in injuries to some detainees,” as per her 

telegraph

 to the public prosecutor, in which she demanded the disclosure of Eskandarany’s place of detention.




Massry tells Mada Masr that Eskandarany’s family was able to confirm independently that he had been moved from 10th of Ramadan center’s prison 6 to the Wadi al-Natroun prison in what is known as a “banishment.”




Massry called, in her telegraph to the prosecution, for an urgent investigation into the circumstances of the transfer and any violations or assaults that may have been committed against Eskandarany or other detainees, noting the investigation should include their referral for forensic medical examination or to other relevant medical authorities to document their condition.




Another human rights lawyer representing prisoners in political cases says that some of his defendants, too, had been transferred from the 10th of Ramadan prison to the Gamasa prison against the backdrop of protests, according to information the lawyer received from three of his clients’ families. Demonstrations had taken place at 10th of Ramadan center’s prison 6, with large numbers of prisoners chanting slogans in protest against their detention conditions and refusing to return to their cells after their recreation time, according to the lawyer. Riot police intervened in an attempt to disperse the gatherings and return the prisoners to their cells, after which prison authorities began transferring a number of detainees to other facilities, the lawyer adds, citing accounts from detainees’ families. The lawyer says he was also informed of an incident in which a prisoner was placed in solitary confinement as a disciplinary measure after going on hunger strike.




The human rights lawyer, two other lawyers and a human rights source confirm to Mada Masr that detainees’ families have complained to them of security forces’ mistreatment of prisoners at the same facility following protests in several cells over recent days, including chanting and banging on cell doors, disabling surveillance cameras in several cells and refusing to leave their cells for recreation time. Prison authorities have also conducted extensive searches of cell contents, according to the lawyers.




The same three lawyers, who have all heard complaints from detainees’ families, say they fear that the protests could spread and that violence could escalate in several prisons.




The human rights source, speaking on condition of anonymity and asking that some details be withheld out of concern for the safety of detainees and their families, says that documentation through lawyers and detainees’ families has also confirmed the occurrence of protests at the Minya and Badr prisons. They describe protest actions varying between prisons and even between wards within the same facility and including hunger strikes, shutting cell doors and attempting to cover surveillance cameras. The source says prison authorities responded differently to the protests, with some seeking to defuse tensions and others resorting to more forceful measures.




The source tells Mada Masr that detainees in Minya staged various protests last week, refusing to accept meals or to leave their cells for recreation time. A group also refused visits, while many prisoners chanted and banged on cell doors. The source says they received complaints about the use of violence against a group that went on hunger strike which led other prisoners to bang on cell doors to protest the assaults. Security forces only intensified the pitch of their violence in response, before transferring the striking detainees to another prison.




Protest actions have also been recorded by 10 different rights organizations, which published a joint 

statement

 on October 9 noting that in recent weeks they have documented protests at prisons in 10th of Ramadan, Badr, Minya, Abu Zaabal and New Valley. The organizations cited reports of security forces entering detention areas to bring them under control and said they have documented “the confiscation of personal belongings from detainees and the transfer of detainees participating in the protests to other cells within the same prisons or to other prisons far from their original places of detention,” among them Eskandarany.




The rights organizations, which include the Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights, the Egyptian Commission for Rights and Freedoms, the Al-Nadeem Center for Rehabilitation of Victims of Violence and the Egyptian Front for Human rights, expressed “grave concern” over these reports and demanded that an investigation be opened into any potential abuses or use of force against detainees.




They also demanded “an end to retaliatory measures, arbitrary transfers, and restrictions on visits and communication, and for detainees to be guaranteed medical care.”




Detainees’ families also issued a collective 

statement

 on October 2 expressing their concern, especially given they are unable to communicate with their relatives directly. The move has garnered expressions of support from lawyers, public figures, human rights defenders and political 

parties

.




***




Signs of tension in prisons emerged toward the end of September, as the new Criminal Procedure Code’s implementation date neared.




According to the sources and to previous 

alerts

 from defense lawyers, 

thousands

 of detainees held in remand detention and their relatives had pinned their hopes on a “breakthrough” on October 1 that would have seen mass release decisions for the thousands of prisoners who are being held in excess of the legal limits on remand duration.




Article 124 of the new 

law

 specifies that “it is not permitted for the duration of remand detention during the preliminary investigation phase and other stages of the criminal case to exceed one-third of the maximum custodial penalty.” It explicitly puts in place a maximum limit of four months’ remand for detainees facing misdemeanor charges, with limits of “12 months for felonies and 18 months if the prescribed punishment for the crime is life imprisonment or the death penalty.”




Though they were not adhered to, the old criminal procedure law also stipulated limits on remand detention periods. But in 2025, as the new law was under debate and passing through Parliament for approval, it was presented in government statements as a step that would further 

guarantee

 defendants’ rights and reduce authorities’ reliance on, and resort to, remand detention.




One of the lawyers who received complaints from detainees’ families, the human rights source and a second source in the human rights field say that detainees and their families had received “reassuring” messages from the authorities in this regard.




“The hope was the situation would be brought in line with the law allowing for the release of large numbers of prisoners who have exhausted the terms of their detention periods,”says another lawyer whose clients were brought to the Badr Court at the Badr Prison Complex for remand detention review sessions in September.




Toward the end of September, three of the lawyers told Mada Masr that hunger strikes were already being called for the first week of October, in case the anticipated releases did not take place.




NHRC delegations paid visits to the 

10th of Ramadan

 prison in August and the 

Badr

 prison in September. According to the council’s statements, the delegations conducted meetings with inmates and toured the departments and facilities. The statements did not mention any complaints of violations.




The council is one of the only state bodies with access to oversight of detention facilities, the other being the Public Prosecution. The two agencies seldom point to any shortcomings or violations based on their access and visits. While the council law stipulates its 

jurisdiction

 to “visiting prisons and other places of detention, treatment facilities and correctional institutions, and listening to prisoners and residents of the aforementioned places,” in practice, council members’ visits are conducted only based on prior coordination with the Interior Ministry and under its supervision.




Independent human rights organizations, meanwhile, are not allowed to visit prisons and observe conditions inside.




Speaking to Mada Masr about the ongoing reports of protest action and harsh security response, Sadat says that the NCHR committees and leadership are actively working to ascertain the truth over what is being published and circulated about protests or strikes in some prisons and is in “continuous consultation” to do so with the Public Prosecution and the Interior Ministry’s human rights and social protection departments, which deal with correctional and rehabilitation centers.




Sadat tells Mada Masr that, so far, authorities have reassured the council that the situation is “normal and regular.”




However, he notes that the council intends to organize new visits to some of the prisons where it has received complaints about the authorities’ treatment of detainees, adding that the complaints include instances of bans on recreation time, lack of healthcare and difficulties faced by detainees’ families during visits, including exhaustive inspections and delays.




The Interior Ministry, meanwhile, has maintained its denial that these events are taking place. On September 26, it 

denied

 that prisoners were going on hunger strike in response to abuses in a prison in Minya. On 

September 28

, it denied the existence of messages from inmates describing protests and hunger strikes at several prisons. It affirmed again on 

October 2

 that “conditions are normal inside all correctional and rehabilitation centers, and the inmates are receiving their legally scheduled visits.” It denied “protests and hunger strikes among inmates of correctional and rehabilitation centers, the prohibition of visits, dealing with them using gas, and the attempt by some of them to commit suicide.” The ministry’s statements further described these claims as completely unfounded, saying they were formulated within the framework of  “ongoing, desperate attempts by the terrorist Muslim Brotherhood organization to stir unrest by fabricating lies and distorting facts to obtain legally unmerited benefits for its members inside correctional and rehabilitation centers.”




***




The lawyers describe the protests as arising from accumulated frustration with detention conditions in addition to a general state of tension and despair, all exacerbated by the hopes attached to the new law’s unrealized implementation.




With multiple claims that the court system is not ready for the law’ coming into effect, a last-minute amendment to delay the law was submitted to Parliament, which approved it in an 

emergency session

 on September 30.




A second lawyer whose clients were due for detention review sessions at the Badr court at the end of September recounts to Mada Masr an event which took place at the Badr criminal court on September 26, as tensions were mounting. When the court denied a defendant’s request to contact his relatives, other detainees who were being held together in the courtroom’s glass dock reacted spontaneously to the decision and began chanting in solidarity.




In the days following that court session, similar 

protests

 took place at the Badr criminal court, with defendants chanting and banging violently on the dock walls in protest to the court’s renewal of their remand detention. These protests reached their peak in a September 28 session, during which the presiding judge asked the detainees and their lawyers to halt the protests in the dock, ultimately issuing a three-year prison sentence to one of the protesting detainees for contempt of court. The sentence was later reduced to one year.




Those court sessions saw presiding judges issue detention renewal decisions for defendants who have been held in remand for over seven years, says the lawyer.




Lawyer Nabih al-Genady also previously 

described

 to Mada Masr a series of at least three detention renewal sessions at the Badr court that saw detainees protest, bang against the glass dock and smash surveillance cameras inside.




Lawyers who attended sessions at the Badr court in the same week confirm that the wave of court protests was unprecedented and that the following week, authorities reduced the number of defendants who were brought before the court in each session, in what appeared to be a step to contain the demonstrations.




“What we saw in the protests in the court was from detainees from more than one prison. They have a lot of hope and have been waiting for a long time” a third lawyer with defendants whose sessions have taken place at the Badr court tells Mada Masr. The lawyer says that families have asked him not to submit pleas for any further procedures in their relatives’ cases, conveying the detainees’ hope that  “when October comes we’ll be out.” The lawyer adds, “this wave of hope is strong and real, because it has been building since the law was being debated.”




“The postponement led to a sense of disappointment,” says the second lawyer who attended the Badr court sessions, adding, “The hope for release was big, and conditions seemed favourable for a large number of detainees whose time in remand had surpassed its full term.”




Commenting on the longevity of the issues around extended remand detention, which was a key point petitioned by advocates who called for changes in the new Criminal Procedure Code, the lawyer says, “there is a will to not engage or deal with the issue of remand detention.”

The post 

Protests at several prisons, detainee ‘banishments’ surround delay to Criminal Procedure Code

 first appeared on 

Mada Masr

.
